author: ssukhpinder
body:
## Article

**ASP.NET Core 10 PipeReader JsonConverter: Stop Losing Split JSON Tokens**

## Sample

- Folder: `041-pipereader-json-converter`
- Demonstration: sends one fixed JSON document through a contiguous stream and a deliberately segmented `PipeReader`. The broken `ValueSpan`-only converter loses the split value; the sequence-aware converter preserves it and decodes JSON escaping.
- Expected runtime result: five deterministic checks pass, including direct verification that `Utf8JsonReader.HasValueSequence` was observed.

## Validation

- `dotnet restore .\041-pipereader-json-converter\PipeReaderJsonConverter.csproj` — succeeded.
- `dotnet format .\041-pipereader-json-converter\PipeReaderJsonConverter.csproj --verify-no-changes --no-restore` — succeeded with no formatting changes.
- `dotnet build .\041-pipereader-json-converter\PipeReaderJsonConverter.csproj -c Release --no-restore` — succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- `dotnet run --project .\041-pipereader-json-converter\PipeReaderJsonConverter.csproj -c Release --no-restore` — succeeded with `Verifier: 5/5 passed`; ten repeated runs produced identical output.
- `dotnet list .\041-pipereader-json-converter\PipeReaderJsonConverter.csproj package --include-transitive` — no package dependencies found.
- `dotnet list .\041-pipereader-json-converter\PipeReaderJsonConverter.csproj package --vulnerable --include-transitive` — no vulnerable packages found.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## Limitations

The fixture covers one JSON string converter and forces segmentation with a long fixed token. Numeric, binary, and nested-token converters need separate semantic tests. Performance-sensitive converters may prefer segment-by-segment processing over copying `ValueSequence`.

## Credentials

No credentials, database, external service, or paid API is required. The sample makes no runtime network calls.

author: andrewkschug-hash
body: ## Problem After initial page load, bottom tab clicks could stop working and the UI felt stuck. Reload could also hang abnormally long. ## Root cause (updated after user reported fix #1 still freezing) Two compounding issues: ### A. Initial load thundering herd (fix #1) `lazy: false` mounted all tabs at once with concurrent AsyncStorage/cloud hydration. ### B. Focus refresh loop on every tab switch (fix #2 — the remaining bug) Each tab's `useFocusEffect` depended on a `refresh` callback from data hooks. Those callbacks included **state in their `useCallback` deps** (`progress`, `target`, `chapterStatuses`, etc.). Every AsyncStorage read returned new object references → `refresh` identity changed → **`useFocusEffect` cleanup + re-run** → another refresh → repeat. This created a focus storm on every tab switch, blocking the main thread with: - Duplicate mount + focus refreshes - Full `useReadingProgress()` on Vocabulary (chapter statuses + bundle) - `buildAdaptiveProfile()` + parsing up to 8000 reading events - Stories secondary loads (`loadBeforeRome` + `loadA2Plus`) firing before navigation completed ### Execution chain when stuck (tab switch) ``` Tab click → useFocusEffect runs refresh() → AsyncStorage read completes → setState → refresh callback recreated → useFocusEffect deps changed → cleanup + re-run refresh (LOOP) → buildAdaptiveProfile + JSON.parse(localStorage) on main thread → Tab press handler starved → UI appears frozen ``` ## Fixes **Round 1:** lazy tabs, getAccount/hydrate dedup, buildProfile persist:false, refresh guards **Round 2 (this commit):** - Stable `refresh` callbacks (refs for cache checks, no state in deps) - `autoRefresh: false` default — tabs refresh on focus only, not mount+focus - `usePeekProgress` for Vocabulary tab (no chapter status scan) - `deferAfterNavigation` for Stories secondary loads (after transition) - Coalesce concurrent `getContinueReadingTarget()` calls - In-memory cache for reading events after first parse - Stale-while-revalidate loading (no spinner when cached data exists) - `freezeOnBlur: false` on tab navigator ## Verification - `npm run typecheck` passes - 462 unit tests pass - Dev `[Navigation]` logs should show single focus/refresh per tab switch, not loops ## Files changed See commit history on this branch.

author: jamespagetbutler
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: gbodegas
body:
The application could only start when the process working directory was the
repository root. `blossom/static`, `blossom/templates` and `data/synthetic`
were hardcoded as relative paths, so `StaticFiles` raised at import time from
anywhere else. Separately, the three `BLOSSOM_*` variables in `.env.example`
were documented but never read by any code.

Changes:

- blossom/settings.py: a frozen `Settings` dataclass built from the
  environment, exposing absolute paths for fixtures, the database and the
  Chroma index, plus package-relative properties for the static and template
  directories. Two decisions are documented in the module docstring: package
  assets are deliberately not configurable, and relative values resolve against
  the repository root rather than the working directory, so the paths written
  in `.env.example` denote one fixed location regardless of launch directory.

  No settings library is used. Three paths do not justify a dependency, and
  `uv run --env-file .env` loads a `.env` file without one.

- blossom/app.py: `create_app` takes an optional `settings` argument so a test
  can point the app at a different fixture set without mutating the
  environment, and mounts static files from the resolved absolute path.

- blossom/routes/student.py: templates and the fixture root come from settings.

- .env.example: documents the real defaults and how to load the file.

- tests/test_settings.py: covers default resolution, environment overrides,
  blank-value fallback, and repository-relative resolution. The final test is
  the regression guard: it chdirs to a temporary directory and asserts
  `/student/due-this-week` still returns 200, which the previous code could
  not do.

author: wooshala
body:
## Problem

Production에서 통화 수집이 반복적으로 수십 시간 정지하고 operator 개입 전까지 복구되지 않는 문제.

확정된 구조 결함:

- process-bound CallLog ingestion
- wall-clock lookback 의존
- non-durable relay
- recording 3-strike `failed_upload` tombstone
- reboot recovery 부재
- heartbeat/main 불일치

## Solution

### CallLog

```
CallLog
→ cursor scan
→ Room durable outbox
→ relay worker
→ server ACK
→ ACKED
```

Primary recovery is cursor + idempotency (`source_event_id = call-log:{id}`). 15-minute overlap is a secondary dedup safety net only.

### Recording

```
pending
→ uploading
→ synced

failure
→ retryable
→ backoff
→ retry

auth
→ auth_blocked

local unrecoverable only
→ failed_permanent
```

### Recovery

- BOOT_COMPLETED
- cursor backfill
- persistent Room state
- periodic worker
- heartbeat

FGS는 도입하지 않음.

## Tests

```
6h process death        PASS — loss 0
24h network outage      PASS — loss 0
12h backend 500         PASS — loss 0
reboot without app open PASS
6h WorkManager delay    PASS — cursor backfill
duplicate retry         PASS — duplicate 0
```

```
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest
BUILD SUCCESSFUL

./gradlew assembleDebug
BUILD SUCCESSFUL
```

## Legacy failed_upload (intentional freeze)

```
Existing legacy failed_upload rows: 83
Automatic recovery in this PR: NO
Reason: intentionally frozen pending adb errorMessage inspection.
```

이번 PR이 배포되더라도 기존 83건을 자동으로 다시 보내지 않는 것이 **의도된 동작**이다. `failed_upload` 행은 drain 대상이 아니며, `MIGRATION_6_7`은 `retry_pending`만 `retryable`로 바꾼다.

## Room migration

- **v5 → v6**: `call_log_outbox` 테이블 생성 (CallLog durable outbox).
- **v6 → v7**: `nextAttemptAt` 컬럼 추가 (outbox + recordings). `FAILED_RETRYABLE` → `RETRYABLE`, `retry_pending` → `retryable`.
- **failed_upload 83건**: 상태 불변, pending 전환 없음, 삭제 없음.

## DO NOT MERGE

Production GO 조건은 아직 충족되지 않았다.

남은 조건:

1. adb Room failed_upload 83건 errorMessage 확인
2. QA APK 실제 기기 설치
3. device soak
4. cursor/outbox/heartbeat 실기 검증
5. Production rollout decision

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

author: bnest95
body:
## Summary

Lane 2 of Input Integrity: the pdf.js binding, the graphics-state walker over `getOperatorList`, the eleven detectors, and the machine verification the Phase 0 probe matrix lacked. No UI, no route, no API surface, no upload — that is Lane 3.

Lane 1 is untouched. `reader-result.js`, `FINDING_CLASSES`, `reader-check-vocab.js`, `file-result.js`, `file-templates.js` and `file-vocab.v1.json` have no diff; every detector finding is constructed through the Lane 1 schema or refused by it.

## What's here

**`file-intake-pdfjs.js`** — the only module that binds to a parser. `pdfjsLib` is injected rather than imported so node and a Lane 3 Web Worker can resolve different entry points without two implementations. `standardFontDataUrl` is a required argument, not a default, because omitting it does not fail — it degrades: pdf.js resolves f13's tag block to the low seven bits behind a warning nobody reads, and a walk that produced that answer would look exactly like one that did not.

**`file-graphics-walker.js`** — CTM, text and line matrices, fill/stroke colour, `ca`/`CA`, render mode, clip regions (clip arrives before its `constructPath`, minMax is pre-CTM), Form XObject `Matrix`/`BBox`, marked-content stack with OCG ids, image placement, per-glyph reconstruction with exact codepoints, effective size after CTM, and advance from per-glyph widths. No `node:` imports, no DOM, no `window`, no `fs`, and no import of `pdfjs-dist`.

**`file-detectors.js`** — the eleven Lane 1 classes, each emitting only the typed fields its template declares.

**`pdfjs-dist` is a devDependency pinned exactly to `6.2.108`.** `dependencies` is still `{}` and nothing under `api/` references it.

## The bug the new coverage caught

Operator coverage for `Tm`, `TJ`, `Tz`, `Ts`, `Tc`, `Tw` and `T*` was the brief's item 3, widening "advances are exact" from n=1. Seven hand-authored fixtures, uniform-width font so the expected advances are not derived from the thing they check.

`Tm` failed on its first run. pdf.js hands `setTextMatrix` a single `Float32Array` in argument zero while `transform` receives six loose numbers; reading one shape with the other's accessor does not throw, it yields a length-1 array holding an object, and every downstream coordinate becomes `NaN`. **Not one of the 25 probe fixtures uses `Tm`**, so the entire corpus passed straight over it. Fixed with a shared `matrixArg` normalisation used by both call sites.

## Mechanical re-verification

All 25 probe fixtures and `ground_truth.json` vendored byte-identical, every sha256 pinned. `test/file-intake-ground-truth.test.mjs` enforces three properties by test rather than by comment:

1. Every assertion is `actual == expected` on values. Nothing formats two things into strings and asserts they look alike.
2. Every ground-truth key is checked, exempted with a stated reason, or pinned as a divergence. Mutation-tested: removing one checker fails three tests rather than passing quietly.
3. Every disagreement pins both sides and the mechanism, and asserts the divergence still holds — so one that silently resolves fails and forces a re-ruling.

**All 16 ground-truth entries verify**, including `large_synthetic` end to end (82 pages, 3772 runs, exact).

### Five divergences, reported not softened

| field | ground truth | walker | mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| `glyph_box_pdf` (f07) | `[50,100,166.004,108.604]` | `[50,100,166.004,112]` | The probe's top edge is baseline + 12pt × Helvetica's 0.717 ascent, read from a font table out of band. An operator list carries no ascent, so the walker reports the em box top. Other three edges agree exactly. |
| `annotations[0].rect` (f08) | `[200,120,220,140]` | `[200,118,222,140]` | pdf.js enforces a minimum size on Text annotations and rewrites 20×20 to 22×22. The fixture's bytes carry the authored rect; the public surface does not return it. |
| `attachments` (f09, c5) | 1 | 0 | Catalog, Filespec, EmbeddedFile and xref offsets all checked and sound. pdf.js 6.2.108 returns empty. Not one of the eleven classes, so no detector depends on it. |
| `image.name` (f15) | `Im0` | `img_p0_1` | pdf.js assigns a synthetic per-page id; the resource name does not cross. Placement, pixel dimensions and CTM agree exactly. |
| `page_media` (all) | authored | not exposed | MediaBox is not on pdf.js's public surface at any version. f04 proves the boxes differ, so reporting `view` under that name would be a claim the parser never made. |

### c8b, the never-probed control

c8a and c8b carry byte-identical text and geometry and differ only in the order of the two halves of the content stream. The probe ran c8a and never ran c8b, so the covered-text finding rested on one arrangement with no control. Both operator lists are now asserted, along with the identical box, colour and rectangle — leaving z-order as the only difference, which is the whole finding.

### The cross-check

`getTextContent` appears in one test file as a comparator and nowhere else. It now demonstrates the ruling rather than restating it:

- **Agreement** where both surfaces carry the run: position and advance match to 1e-3 on f01, f07, f14.
- **Cf deletion**: six format codepoints vanish on f11, four on f12, five tag-block on f13. `encoding_control_structures` would be silently empty on the barred surface — the difference between a finding and no finding.
- **Fabrication**: op02's content stream shows exactly three glyphs; `getTextContent` returns `"A BC"`, a space no `Tj` painted and no font measured.
- **A third divergence, not named in the ruling**: f04 shows three runs and the comparator returns two. The missing one is `OUTSIDE-CROPBOX`, precisely the run `offpage_text` exists to find.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — **1719 tests, 1706 pass, 0 fail, 13 skipped**
- [x] The 13 skips are the pre-existing `IMBAS_WAVE0_ROOT` environment skips, unchanged
- [x] 50 new tests: 26 ground-truth, 15 detector, 9 operator-coverage
- [x] Lane 1 files have no diff; only `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are modified
- [x] `dependencies` is `{}`; nothing under `api/` imports the new modules
- [x] Walker and detectors import nothing but each other and the Lane 1 schema

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: mtrifilo
body:
## Summary

Revision history is cached with **no viewer dimension in its query key**, so an admin who opened a venue's History panel while signed out kept the *masked* payload for the whole 15-minute `staleTime` after logging in, rendered next to a Rollback button that acts on the real stored value. Login only refetched `auth.profile`; nothing else in the cache ever learned the viewer had changed.

This adds `refreshViewerTierQueries` to `frontend/lib/queryClient.ts` and calls it from every transition into an authenticated session, through one shared `refreshCachesForNewSession` helper in `useAuth.ts` (login, registration, magic-link sign-in, email verification, and both account-recovery paths — 6 sites, verified against current code; the ticket estimated ~5). Passkey sign-in and sign-up establish their session with a raw `fetch` rather than a mutation, so they call the helper directly.

The mirror-image `resetViewerTierQueries` runs on logout, before the existing `queryClient.clear()`. See below — this ordering is load-bearing and not what it looks like.

Per the ticket's own recommendation this is **invalidate-on-auth-change, not a viewer-id key segment**. A key segment would churn every call site in eight families; invalidation is one line per handler and matches the existing `createInvalidateQueries` pattern. The audit below found no family where invalidation is insufficient.

### Direction of travel matters

**Login uses `invalidateQueries`.** On the way *up* the cached payload is a subset of what the new viewer may see, so keeping it painted during the refetch is a seamless upgrade rather than a loading flash.

**Logout uses `resetQueries`.** On the way *down* the cached payload is data the new viewer must not see, so it has to leave the screen rather than keep being painted until an anonymous refetch lands.

Verified that `invalidateQueries` cannot reject (`refetchQueries` `.catch(noop)`s each fetch and returns `Promise.all(...).then(noop)`), so the deliberate un-awaited `void` calls cannot produce an unhandled rejection — noted in the doc comment so it does not get "fixed" later.

### Viewer-tier query-family inventory

Derived from an audit of every backend read route registered on an `optionalAuthGroup` (the only routes that can see a viewer at all — `rc.API` has no auth middleware, so those payloads cannot vary). Recorded in full in the `VIEWER_TIER_QUERY_KEYS` doc comment so it does not have to be redone.

**Invalidated on login** — payload varies by tier, key carries no viewer segment:

| Family | What varies |
| --- | --- |
| `revisions.*` | `address`/`zipcode` values replaced with `(hidden)` and the summary dropped entirely on unverified venues (PSY-1717); a non-approved show 404s its history for non-admin/non-submitter viewers, and the row filter applies to `total` too (PSY-1715). A tier flip changes both the values and which rows exist. |
| `comments.*` | `user_vote` on every node |
| `tags.entityTags` | `user_vote` per tag (scoped to this branch; the rest of `tags` is unauthed) |
| `collections.*` | private collection 403s for non-creators, `user_likes_this`, `is_subscribed`, the entity-collections list unions in the viewer's own private collections, nested tag `user_vote` |
| `contributor.*` | per-field owner-vs-not gating: stats, last-active, sections, contributions, rankings, following each collapse to a count or vanish; a private profile 404s |
| `requests.*` | `user_vote` per row |
| `community.leaderboard` | `user_rank` appended for authenticated viewers |
| `contribute.opportunities` | the `followed_artists_missing_links` category is omitted entirely for anonymous viewers (which also changes `total_items`), and item order is per-viewer |

**Exempt, with reason:**

| Family | Why exempt |
| --- | --- |
| `savedShows.count` / `countBatch`, `follows.entity` / `batch` / `libraryCounts` / `libraryFollowing` / `user` | Already carry a viewer segment (`isAuthenticated` + user id). An auth change re-keys them, so the previous viewer's entry can never be served in the new viewer's place. |
| `shows.detail` | The only viewer-dependent behaviour is a 404 on a non-approved show for non-admin/non-submitter. On a show page the viewer can already see, the bytes are identical. |
| `artists.graph` | `/artists/{id}/graph` **is** optional-auth and its payload carries a `user_votes` map, but nothing in the UI reads it. Listed in the code comment so it gets added if that changes. Its siblings `/related` (no consumer), `/bill-composition` and `/relationships/{id}/provenance` are optional-auth too but read no viewer. |
| `field-notes` | `GET /shows/{id}/field-notes` reads no viewer at all, so the `user_vote` its comment-shaped rows can carry is never populated. |
| `admin.*`, `contributor.own*`, `collections.my`, personal `charts`, `passkeys`, `mySubmissions`, `calendar`, `savedShows.list` | Signed-in only, with no anonymous variant to be confused with. Logout drops them wholesale. |
| `tags` list/detail/search/entities, public `charts`, venue / release / label / festival / scene / radio / graph / explore | Served by routes registered without auth middleware; the backend cannot see a viewer. |

**`follows.followers`** deserves a footnote: unlike its siblings it has *no* viewer segment and it is served by an optional-auth route. It has **zero consumers** in the frontend today, so it is dead key surface rather than a live cache. Not added, to avoid implying it is wired up — but the code comment says so explicitly, since "all follows keys are viewer-keyed" would be a false reason for the next reader to trust.

### The logout ordering, which is the opposite of what it looks like

`resetViewerTierQueries` must run **before** `queryClient.clear()`, not after. Measured, not assumed:

| Ordering | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `resetQueries(families)` then `clear()` | correct — panel ends re-masked with no external re-render |
| `clear()` alone | **stale** — panel keeps painting the privileged payload until something else re-renders it |
| `clear()` then `resetQueries` / `invalidateQueries` | **no-op** — the cache is already empty, nothing matches |
| `invalidateQueries` then `clear()` | **worse** — the in-flight refetch is orphaned and the privileged value stays painted |

The load-bearing detail: **`clear()` empties the cache but does not notify query *observers*.** It destroys each query and notifies cache-level listeners, while a `useQuery` observer is subscribed to the query itself. A still-mounted observer therefore goes on rendering the payload it last saw. Running the reset first pushes it into a pending state, and *that* notification is what re-renders the component and rebuilds its query once `clear()` has destroyed the old one.

My first pass argued no logout change was needed, on the theory that the logout state change always re-renders the panel. `/code-review` correctly pushed back. That theory only holds where an **ancestor consumes `useAuthContext`** — true for `VenueDetail` and `ShowDetail`, which is why the manual repro below looked fine. `ReleaseDetail` and `LabelDetail` also render `<RevisionHistory>` but read auth through `useIsAuthenticated`, which is a `useProfile` *query observer* — orphaned by `clear()` in exactly the same way. On those two pages an admin who signed out kept seeing unmasked revision rows for as long as the page stayed mounted. Now fixed and covered by a test that deliberately performs no manual re-render.

Cost: logout issues the viewer-tier requests twice (once from the reset, once from the post-`clear()` rebuild). Acceptable for a rare action; avoiding it would mean replacing the unfiltered `clear()`, which is a much larger blast radius than this ticket warrants.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd frontend && bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `cd frontend && bun run lint` — 0 errors, 136 warnings, **exactly** the count on `origin/main` (verified by stashing and re-running); no warning in a touched file that is not already on m

author: kkimdev
body:
## 🚀 What

Keep generated Rust operation sources in build-owned output trees and close the native FFI cancellation/result race while retaining the Smithy-generated ABI boundary.

## 🤔 Why

Fresh Bazel builds may use an immutable source checkout. Every `smithy_operations.rs` artifact must therefore stay in the configured generated output directory, and a cancellation published as definitive `Canceled` must never be followed by mutation execution or overwrite a definitive worker result.

## 🔧 How

- Route the Rust API and every generated Rust operation output through Cargo’s `OUT_DIR`, passing a generated output root to the generator while keeping the generator as the sole owner of generated sources.
- Make FFI admission and completion transitions atomic: pre-admission cancellation remains definitive `Canceled`; cancellation after admission preserves the documented `UnknownMutation` boundary; definitive completion wins over later cancellation and repeated terminal calls remain idempotent.
- Keep generated result discriminators and language adapters projection-driven, including the empty `SYNC` result mapping.
- Keep the public production tree free of test-only regressions and generated artifacts.
- Rebase the ABI/generator branch onto public `main` at `4b710dc268a04f69ef0596c9a957bed236260600` after #340.

## 💥 Breaking Changes

The native ABI version is 6. Consumers must regenerate Smithy bindings and use the generated contract header. Async request handles own copied input buffers and must be released exactly once; result payload pointers remain borrowed until the result handle is freed, and borrowed child views must not outlive their parent. Cancellation of a transmitted mutation reports `unknown_mutation`.

## ✅ Validation

- `OPENKACHE_GENERATION_CHECK=1 nix develop -c bun openkache/clients/generate.ts` (pass after deterministic regeneration)
- `nix develop -c bazel build --lockfile_mode=error @openkache_public//clients/rust:openkache_client` (pass)
- `nix develop -c just check-protocol-contract` (pass; disposable all-language contract generation)
- `git -C openkache diff --check` (pass)

## 🔗 Related

- Builds on request engine #337: https://github.com/openkache/openkache/pull/337
- Builds on canonical key and Item ID mapping #342: https://github.com/openkache/openkache/pull/342
- Builds on value protection boundary #339: https://github.com/openkache/openkache/pull/339
- Dependency foundations: #335 https://github.com/openkache/openkache/pull/335, #336 https://github.com/openkache/openkache/pull/336, #334 https://github.com/openkache/openkache/pull/334

Final public branch tip: `4de509fcf2c0b7f3cb817c8f3b4d41abd70f8c0a`.

## Known limitations

- The public repository intentionally contains no tests; downstream integration validation remains private.
- Generated output is ignored and produced by package/build workflows; no generated artifacts are committed.
- Required public CI and review status are not yet available; do not merge until they are present.

Closes #792

author: basilechretien
body:
## Why

Two sentences stopped being accurate when the offsite copy moved to the controller's own machine in #355. Both are fixed across **all ten locales**.

## 1. `sharing` — where the data actually lives

It said *"Your account and CV are stored in the EU."* True of the live service, but backup copies now also sit in Japan on the controller's machine.

> Your account and CV are stored in the EU. **Backup copies are also held by the controller in Japan on encrypted storage, and are not shared with anyone else**; the controller is based in Japan, and transfers between Japan and the EU are covered by the 2019 Japan–EU mutual adequacy decision.

"Held by the **controller**" is the load-bearing phrase: no sub-processor is involved. That's precisely what made the previous Google Drive copy a problem and makes this one fine, and the existing adequacy sentence already covers the transfer. "On encrypted storage" rather than "encrypted backups" because BitLocker encrypts the disk, not the files — claiming otherwise would overstate it.

## 2. `retention` — the fix that wasn't in the brief

This one matters more. It promised that deleting an account *"permanently removes your profile, CV, and any research records"*. But a deleted account survives in backups for up to 14 days. That's normal and defensible — a notice that doesn't allow for it is not, and it's exactly what a data-subject request or an IRB reviewer would land on.

> Deleting your account removes your profile, CV, and any research records from the live service **immediately**. Encrypted backups are kept on a rolling schedule and **overwritten within 14 days**, so a deleted account disappears from them within that window; **we do not restore deleted accounts from backup.**

That last clause is what makes the delay acceptable rather than a loophole.

## Code follows the promise

`pull-backups.ps1` had `KeepDays = 30`; it's now **14**, matching the notice. A privacy notice shouldn't commit to a window the tooling doesn't enforce.

## Verification

- The edit script **aborts unless every anchor matches exactly once per locale**, so no locale can be silently skipped — 20 replacements, 2 fields × 10 locales
- All ten locales independently confirmed to state a 14-day window (`14 days`, `14 天`, `14 días`, `14 jours`, `14 Tagen`, `14 日`, `14 dias`, `14 giorni`, `14일`, `14 дней`)
- `tests/privacy-i18n.test.ts` passes; `npm run format:check` passes repo-wide

## Note

Translations are mine, matching each locale's existing register and terminology (e.g. *responsable* / *Verantwortliche* / *titolare* / *контролёр* for the controller). Worth a native read before this reaches production if you want belt and braces — it is user-facing legal text.

author: murdore
body:
Rule 15 flagged imports from `../src/lib/` but permitted anything under `../dist/` at any depth. Rewriting `../src/lib/x.js` as `../dist/lib/x.js` therefore satisfied it without changing what a suite proved — the same internal shape, asserted through a different copy of the module.

Nothing under `dist/` beyond the entry point and the subpaths declared in `package.json` `exports` is reachable by a consumer, so `dist/lib/...` is exactly as internal as `src/lib/...`.

## The change

The permitted set is **derived from `exports`** rather than hand-listed — 16 entry points plus the `./processors/*` and `./adapters/*` wildcards, the wildcards matched one segment deep only. Anything else under `dist/` reports with a distinct message explaining why depth is the signal: `../dist/index.js` is the package, `../dist/lib/anything` is its inside.

## Sixteen suites are grandfathered in the same commit

This is not optional. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `npx eslint test/continuous-test-suite*.ts --max-warnings=10` inside the **`test` job, a required check**. Tightening the rule without the allow-list entries would turn a required check red on every open PR simultaneously, including four that are already blocked for unrelated reasons.

| | |
|---|---|
| `continuous-test-suite.ts` | `provider-descriptors` |
| `auth` | `provider-structure` |
| `context` | `provider-wiring` |
| `credentials` | `providers-mocked` |
| `error-classification-e2e` | `providers` |
| `memory` | `skills` |
| `observability` | `tool-dedup` |
| `ppt` | `voice` |

An earlier count put this at nine, from searching only `dist/lib/`. The real set also reaches `dist/utils/`, `dist/factories/`, `dist/providers/`, `dist/core/`, `dist/constants/`, `dist/cli/commands/`, `dist/cli/factories/`, `dist/features/` and `dist/services/`.

**That block is debt, and the code says so.** It carries a comment stating it is not a clean bill of health, that each entry should either gain a real public surface or be converted, and that new suites must not be added to it — they go above, with their own stated reason.

## These suites were not evading the rule

They were following local precedent. `provider-structure.ts` predates all of this and greps the **source text** of `providerRegistry.ts` with `fs.readFileSync` — considerably more unit-shaped than importing a compiled constant. Lint encoded the corpus rather than the prose, so the deep-`dist` form became the default path for anything with no public surface.

The value of this change is that the rule now bites for every **new** suite, which is where the pattern was spreading.

## Verified in both directions

- The exact CI gate command exits **0 with no output**.
- A scratch file importing `../dist/lib/models/manifestRegistry.js` **is reported**.
- `../dist/index.js`, `../dist/cli/index.js`, `../dist/rag/index.js`, `../dist/processors/pdf.js` and a type-only `../src/lib/types/index.js` import all still **pass**.

## Known follow-up

Some grandfathered suites pin invariants that genuinely have no public surface — nothing exported from `dist/index.js` reveals which lookup key a model resolves to, for instance. Rule 15's own wording says that signals a surface worth building rather than a licence to unit-test. Those conversions are larger than this change and are deliberately not attempted here.

author: spooderinbed
body:
Docs-only. The build plan required a written spec pass before PR 5B could be carved, and predicted it would split again. It splits in two — and the pass also found **two stale premises in the plan's own 5B entry**, both of which change what gets built.

## The two corrections

**"case-scoping the three existing routes" — already done.** MV-157 §G case-scoped `upload`, `[id]/view` and `[id]`; each authorizes the case before any Storage call and then filters by `case_id`. The real gap is narrower: all three resolve *the actor's own* case via `resolvePersonalCaseId`, so a counsellor cannot name a student's case. That is the standing **F-8** finding, and 5B closes it for these three routes only.

**"replacing the one-per-kind model" — the wrong verb.** The spec keeps `documents_case_kind_idx` and puts the model *beside* the vault. Three reasons, sharpest first:

1. supabase-js compiles `.upsert()` to `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, and the arbiter index must exist and be FULL — so dropping it breaks every upsert on `documents` **at plan time**. Same `42501` class measured three times (MV-155, MV-168).
2. `documents` is the student product's vault. "The current file for this kind on this case" is a fact `lib/checklist/generator.ts` and the profile sections depend on.
3. The consultancy model needs *history* and *review*, which are facts about a request — not about the vault.

So the uniqueness is not dropped in this lane at all. MV-182's header sentence ("the uniqueness has to go once, on purpose") is superseded, in writing, with the cost analysis attached.

## The carve

| Card | Ships |
|---|---|
| **MV-185** | `case_document_versions` + `case_document_reviews`: additive tables, RLS, column-scoped grants, MV-182's two forbidden-grant assertions. Request resolution **derived** from the newest version's review, never a second source of truth. No Storage, no routes, no UI. |
| **MV-190** | `case/<case_id>/<version_id>` prefix + its `storage.objects` policy; short-TTL signed downloads authorized **before** the URL is minted; the three routes accept a named case. |

MV-190 runs after MV-185 and **before** MV-186 — the number is higher only because the plan had already reserved MV-186–189.

## Two decisions worth stating plainly

- **Existing owner-keyed vault objects are not migrated.** They are live student PII, and a copy-and-rewrite of `documents.file_path` is a data-loss-shaped operation with nothing to gain. Counsellors reach them through the signed-URL path instead.
- **5B does not depend on Stage 5.** Nothing in it reads `student_user_id`, so an unclaimed case supports the full request → upload → review walk.

## Also in here

The build plan itself, which had been sitting **untracked** while MV-183's and MV-184's dossiers already cited it.

## Board

MV-184 trued to done for its merge (PR #150, `1160770`); MV-185 and MV-190 appended as Ready. 186 cards, no duplicates, `npm run board` green.

**Gate:** `npm test` 3598 passed / 375 files, 0 failed.

author: edwinang003
body:
SPEC §5 calls list ⇄ board "the core idea of the product, and the thing neither
reference app does". This is the slice the touch-drag spike was paying for.

It is a rendering choice and not a data choice, so it is **one component with
two layouts** rather than two components: one `onDrop`, one `describe`, one
place the undo-toast rule lives. `groupBySection` and `resolveDrop` were
already pure and reason about group membership rather than geometry, so the
board needed no second data path at all.

## What ships

- Sections become columns, tasks become cards, at every width.
- A header toggle, per project, remembered per device. A project you have never
  toggled opens as a list on a phone (SPEC §8 rule 6) and honours
  `default_view` above `lg`.
- Done is the last column, so completing a task by dragging it there — the
  two-way binding SPEC §4 calls the product's whole thesis — reads as a gesture
  rather than a drop onto a collapsed strip.
- `projects.default_view` lands on the row, closing a SPEC §15 gap before P1
  has to close it under sync.

## Three things only the browser could find

1. **Scroll snap and drag fight each other.** A mandatory snap refuses the
   intermediate scroll positions dnd-kit's autoscroll moves through, so a slow
   scroll became a jump to the far end and *every* drop landed in the last
   column. Snap is a swiping affordance; it comes off while a card is in the
   air.
2. **85vw columns hid their neighbours,** making every cross-column drag wait
   on autoscroll to reveal a target you could not see. 78vw shows the next
   column past the edge, and a short drag reaches it.
3. **A fifth word in the header** truncated the project's own name to `P…` on a
   390px screen. The toggle is a glyph below `lg` and keeps its name through
   `aria-label`.

## Database version 3

`default_view` is not indexed, so version 3 declares no `stores` — only an
upgrade that backfills `'list'`. It deliberately writes **no outbox entries**,
unlike v2's upgrade, which enqueued tasks because those rows had never been
enqueued at all (SPEC §9.1). The value written here is the column's own default
on the server; there is nothing for a server to learn from being told it.

## Verification

- 196 unit tests, 19 files (was 180/18). Clean `tsc -b`, clean oxlint.
- Browser-checked at 390 × 844 and 1280 × 800: toggling, persistence across a
  reload, per-project memory, no toggle on Today, cross-column drag, a drop into
  Done completing a task with no toast, a checkbox tick on the board likewise,
  and the list still raising its toast. Zero console errors or warnings.

**Known unrelated failure:** the Cloudflare Workers Builds check fails on every
PR branch in this repo, including a docs-only one (#9), and has since #4. It is
not caused by this work.

author: yzxcj797
body: ## Problem Issue #345's scanned PDF reports `page_count: 0` and rejects conversion with `OCR is required`. The file is linearized and has more than 512 bytes of padding after its final `%%EOF`. The document has two classic xref tables: - an early table whose trailer contains `/Root` and `/Prev`; - the final table, which completes the object list but has no `/Root` in its own trailer. lopdf cannot find the final EOF through the padding, so container repair runs. The old repair selected the newest classic xref without inspecting its trailer. That loads the rootless final table, leaves the catalog unreachable, and produces a zero-page result even though the root-bearing table and its `/Prev` chain are intact. ## Change - Enumerate validated classic xref starts from newest to oldest. - Prefer the newest table whose own trailer names `/Root`, which also recovers the rest of the chain through `/Prev`. - Keep the newest valid table as a fallback for unusual trailer layouts. - Add a synthetic, stdlib-only linearized PDF regression with two xref tables and 600 trailing NUL bytes. It fails on main with `page_count == 0` and now returns one text page containing `Hello World`. The sample from the issue was also checked locally: it now reports four scanned pages (still requiring OCR) instead of zero pages. ## Tests - `cargo test --lib` — 987 passed. - `cargo test --test integration_tests test_process_pdf_repairs_padded_linearized_xref_chain -- --nocapture` — 1 passed. - `cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings` — clean. - `cargo fmt` — clean. Fixes #345 --- ## Summary by cubic Recover linearized PDFs with padded EOF by preferring a root-bearing classic xref and requiring standalone token boundaries for `xref`/`trailer`. Previously repair always chose the newest classic xref and could pick a rootless final table, producing page_count: 0; now it selects the newest xref whose trailer has `/Root`, or keeps the newest rootless table only when its `/Prev` points backward, preserving revisions and restoring a reachable catalog. - Scans classic xref tables newest→oldest; bounds trailer searches to before the next xref; enforces leading/trailing token boundaries for standalone keywords. - Parses trailer dictionaries for top‑level keys only; ignores comments, strings, and nested dictionaries; reuses a whitespace/comment scanner; guards short inputs. - Retains the newest rootless table only if `/Prev` points backward; rejects forward `/Prev` and falls back to the newest root-bearing table; keeps the newest valid table when no root-bearing trailer exists. - Adds a stdlib‑only regression PDF with 600 trailing NULs and unit tests for commented “trailer”, nested/commented `/Root`, backward/forward `/Prev`, and keyword boundary checks; the sample in #345 now reports four scanned pages instead of zero. Fixes #345. Written for commit 9ddc2a9ee085d466c34e1c1b9d2956c84adf47be. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
## What & why

Fixes the landing page looking "messy on MacBook", where the mess got worse the wider the screen. I rendered the page in a headless browser at 1280/1440/1512/1728px and measured element positions to find the actual causes (not eyeball-patch them).

## Root causes → fixes

**1. Hero drifted left of the whole page, more so on wider screens.** The hero `<section>` was full-bleed (`max-width:none`) with `vw`-based side padding, while every other section uses `max-width:1180px; margin:0 auto`. Measured hero-headline left edge vs the section column:

| width | hero left (before) | section column | drift |
|------:|-------------------:|---------------:|------:|
| 1280 | 58 | 78 | 20px |
| 1440 | 65 | 158 | **93px** |
| 1512 | 68 | 194 | **126px** |
| 1728 | 78 | 302 | **224px** |

Fix: put the hero content in the **same 1180px centered container** (28px side padding). It stays left-aligned but now shares the exact left edge with the navbar logo, every section heading, and the footer — at all widths (78 / 158 / 194 / 302).

**2. One heading a whole tier too small.** "Kenapa Pilih 20FIT" hardcoded `font-size:32px` while every other section heading uses `clamp(30px,4.5vw,44px)` — so it rendered 32px vs 44px. Fix: use the shared clamp and center it to match the other content-section headings.

**3. Uneven spacing.** Section vertical padding was ad-hoc (events `60px…8px`, why-choose `56px`, others `64px`) and card-grid gaps were `14/16/18/20`. Fix: content sections to a uniform `64px` top/bottom, all card grids to a single `20px` gap.

## Verification (headless browser, all 4 widths)

- **No horizontal overflow** (`scrollWidth == innerWidth`) at any width.
- Hero headline + **all** section headings + footer now share one left edge.
- Every section heading computes to the **same** font-size.
- Sections stack contiguously — no overlap, no gaps in the box flow.

author: gopinaidu
body:
## What changed

- use the configured structured LLM to generate one concise, free-tier-safe research query before calling Serper
- keep deterministic query construction as a fallback if the LLM helper call fails or emits restricted search operators
- filter Serper results through ReelAgent's authoritative-domain trust policy before any LLM ranking
- use the structured LLM to rank only trusted official candidates by relevance to the factual claim
- prefer the strongest ranked official pages for fetching and evidence extraction
- keep deterministic Serper order as a fallback if ranking fails
- reuse the same configured Gemini/OpenAI structured client for retrieval assistance and final claim verification

## Why

Manual verification showed the architecture is sound but evidence quality varies by technology: Kubernetes worked well, while Kafka and CPython sometimes surfaced generic or weak official pages. Hand-written ranking heuristics would keep growing and still miss semantic relationships such as GIL vs Global Interpreter Lock.

This PR lets the LLM handle semantic query formulation and candidate relevance while ReelAgent keeps deterministic control of source trust.

## Trust boundary

The LLM does **not** decide which domains are authoritative. Serper results are first restricted to exact HTTPS hosts from ReelAgent's trust registry. Only those trusted candidates are sent to the LLM for ranking.

## Failure behavior

Both helper stages fail soft:

- query-generation failure -> existing deterministic concise query
- ranking failure -> original trusted Serper order

Final claim verification remains fail-closed and unchanged.

## Scope

Three files only: Serper adapter, verification runtime wiring, and Serper unit tests. No technology-specific ranking rules and no change to verdict semantics, CLI, Topic Intelligence, rendering, or publishing.

## After merge

Run the existing four verification checks:

```text
python -m reelagent verify --claim "PostgreSQL supports SKIP LOCKED for queue-style worker coordination."
python -m reelagent verify --claim "Kafka preserves message ordering within a partition."
python -m reelagent verify --claim "A Kubernetes Deployment manages ReplicaSets."
python -m reelagent verify --claim "CPython's GIL limits concurrent execution of Python bytecode."
```

If those produce relevant official evidence and sensible verdicts, Verification v1 can be considered functionally complete.

author: theagenticguy
body:
Implements #44: tasks now enter the store from evidence the corpus already sees, not only explicit `task add`. Builds directly on #45's batching kernel and state planes.

## What ships

**Shared minting discipline** (`packages/sleep/src/mint.ts`)
- Identity: a new `memhtml-finding-key` head meta, `<detector>:<sha256-prefix-16>` over a detector-owned canonical fingerprint. Tasks are carved out of content-hash dedup by design, so the finding key is their only stable identity; a malformed key degrades to a vocabulary warning and projects as absent (a typo'd meta never makes a task vanish from `task list`). Projected to `files.finding_key` (migration 0011) with a partial index over open detected tasks.
- Dedup at mint: exact key always; a claim-Jaccard restatement arm (0.6 floor) opt-in per detector — free-text commitment claims opt in, templated pair claims stay out (two distinct pairs sharing an endpoint measured 0.78–0.90 and would false-dedup).
- Caps: 10 new mints per detector per night; overflow counted; capped findings still enter `presentKeys` so closure attestation is cap-independent.
- Closure: close-by-absence only under a truthful `universeComplete` attestation (model ran, zero isolated batch failures, zero truncation at every cap on the candidate path, enumerated per phase) and only while the task is still `todo` — a human-touched task is never machine-closed by absence.

**Surface 1 — sleep phases emit tasks instead of counters**
- entity-resolution: below-floor clusters decompose to pairs; those plus undecided review-band pairs mint `confirm:` tasks with similarity, per-name counts, and centroid cosine as evidence.
- dedup-merge: true vetoes (re-applying `mergeVetoed` per undecided pair, separating them from the residual) at/above the 0.92 floor mint `review:` tasks quoting both sides.
- edge-typing: single-detection contradictions below the two-night gate mint `resolve:` tasks; closure is never by absence — an explicit closer runs every night (including no-model nights): promoted to edge / endpoint gone / evidence gone, with `evidence gone` respecting a human's `doing` status.

**Surface 2 — trace-consolidation extracts commitments**
- The consolidator contract gains `commitments` and `resolutions` (optional-with-default on the wire, so an older agent build decodes clean); grounding extends to both, and the client verifies every quote against the mounted transcript — accepting raw bytes or any single JSON-decoded string, so an honest quote carrying `"` or an internal newline cannot refuse the turn (that refusal livelocked the batch: never watermarked, re-selected nightly).
- The phase mints `commitment:` tasks through a four-arm deterministic gate (confidence ≥ 0.7, user actor, sessionId in the intersected batch, non-empty quote), fingerprinted session-free so a restated promise recognizes its open task. Resolutions close open `todo` commitment tasks at 0.6 Jaccard, compared with the pinned prefix stripped.

**Review surface**
- `task list --detected` filters to machine-detected tasks.
- `memhtml doctor` gains a report-only `staleQuotes` check: every open detected task's `<q cite>` evidence must still exist in its cited source (archive-chased), whitespace-normalized. Excluded from `healthy` for the same reason overdue tasks are.
- Evidence is `<q cite="/path">` inside a paragraph — `blockquote` is outside the closed vocabulary and its text never reaches citations. Quotes are cut from `body_text`, the projection doctor reads.
- Docs: `docs/tasks.md`, `docs/design.md` §10.2, and the published sleep-pipeline page.

## Guards from the issue, as shipped
- Detected task = proposal with verbatim evidence; doctor verifies file-borne quotes; the consolidator client verifies transcript quotes (session-cited quotes are outside doctor's coverage — accepted residual, documented).
- Author separation: `memhtml-author: agent:sleep` + tag `detected` + `--detected` filter.
- No self-referential loops: tasks stay excluded from every phase's candidate SQL (per-phase lock tests unchanged); the full-run exclusion test now distinguishes minting a new task from touching an existing one, whose byte-identity stays pinned.
- Closure is also detected: resolutions close commitment tasks; edge-typing's closer catches the human-fixed contradiction via `evidence gone`.

## Deferred (follow-ups)
- Surface 3 (batched corpus detection pass) — reuses the batch kernel; issue notes it can ship last or never.
- Doctor-recurrence minting (needs a night-over-night findings ledger).
- Embedding-based mint dedup (needs a query-embed port in PhaseEnv); restatement noise is bounded by the cap meanwhile.
- `dueHint` parses to body prose only, never `memhtml-due` (needs a reference clock).

## Verification
- `mise run check` green (58/58 turbo tasks): lint, typecheck, ~1900 unit tests, integration, eval, a11y, budget.
- Every new guard was mutation-verified — broken deliberately to prove its test fires; several mutations found real holes that are now pinned (vacuous truncation tripwire, quote-source mismatch, in-run path collision).
- A pre-push adversarial review (idempotency, state-over-time, archive handling, silent degradation) produced five findings, all fixed test-first in the final commit.

author: gene-png
body:
Records Gene's Option A decision on #87 as **D-050**, and the three obligations that come with confirming it.

## The decision

**The exported document uses the contracted target from intake, not the `/gap-analysis` selector.** The deliverable is a contractual artifact, not a snapshot of exploratory UI state. The rejected alternative produces output that silently depends on ambient screen state at the moment of a click — two consultants reviewing the same assessment could produce different documents, and neither could reproduce the other's.

**No behaviour change.** This confirms what D-049 already shipped. The value of deciding it explicitly is the obligations below, which were invisible while it was implicit.

## Asked to flag a business reason to prefer Option B — there isn't one, but A has a gap

I tried to construct the strongest case for B rather than assume there wasn't one. The best is legitimate: an engagement re-scopes mid-flight (contracted S4, both parties agree to a phased S3 for year one) and the consultant wants a deliverable reflecting the agreed goal.

**That doesn't argue for B.** It argues a re-scope should be a *recorded deliberate change to the contracted target* — the opposite of "whatever the selector said when someone clicked Finalize."

But it exposed a real gap, filed as **#90**. There is **no consultant-side write path to the contracted target anywhere in the codebase**:

```
app/routes/csf.py:664   sr.csf_target_tier  = body.target_tier
app/routes/zt.py:1186   sr.zt_target_stage  = body.target_stage
```

Both are in the **client self-assessment submit**, both gated on `DRAFT` (re-submit → 409). `admin.py:154-156` only reads. So the value governing every deliverable is: set at intake → amendable exactly once, **by the client** → frozen forever, consultant-immutable.

**This re-weights #85.** Filed as narrow and API-only, it is in fact the *sole amendment path* for that value, and it accepts `target = 1` where intake enforces `>= 2` — producing a document reading `0 gap(s) at target T1` with no gaps at all. Should be fixed with #90, not separately.

## Required follow-up — #89, not optional

Per Gene: the selector must be marked exploration-only, because with A confirmed it **affects nothing but the screen**. A consultant who moves it to discuss a phased goal, leaves it, and finalizes gets a 12-gap S3 screen and a 37-gap S4 document with nothing explaining the difference. The behaviour is correct; the silence is what makes it read as a permanent bug.

The load-bearing part of #89 is surfacing the divergence **at Finalize** — labelling the selector alone leaves it discoverable only by whoever already reads carefully before clicking.

## #84's severity restated where it gets scoped

Gene flagged that CSF's half is worse than the issue conveyed. Now stated in `DELIVERY_PLAN.md`'s W1 Risk section, in D-050, and on #84 itself:

**For a tier-4 client this is total silent omission, not a miscount.** Every subcategory at tier 3 is a real gap generating **zero** risk findings. The Risk Register doesn't under-count them — it doesn't mention them, and nothing on any surface indicates the omission.

The framing matters for scoping: *"the Risk Register is silent about a class of real risk for most clients"* and *"an off-by-one in a target comparison"* justify very different amounts of care, and the second is the reading that gets deferred.

## Still owed, and recorded as owed

**No test pins either reading of the policy.** One asserting the document follows the contracted target and *not* the selector should land with #89, or this drifts back the first time someone "fixes" the mismatch by wiring the selector into finalize. An unpinned decision is the same class of thing as an untested fix — which, given this repo's nine instances of that pattern, is worth writing down rather than assuming.

## Test plan

Docs only — no code changes.

- `prettier@3.9.5 --check` repo-wide — clean
- Every claim about write paths verified by grep against the current tree, not inferred: two writes total, both client-side, both `DRAFT`-gated, `admin.py` read-only

author: minsky-ai[bot]
body:
## Summary

`cli-mcp-substitution` (mt#4144) watches for the agent concluding Minsky's MCP surface is gone and
rebuilding the work out of CLI calls — which routes around every PreToolUse guard bound to the MCP
tool names. Its suppression was **monotonic**: `hasSucceededMcpCall` returned true on the first
successful `mcp__minsky__*` call found anywhere in the transcript window, and never un-set.

So the guard's entire reachable window was the interval **before** a session's first successful MCP
call. The class it exists to catch — mem#707 R10/R11, *MCP worked, then stopped, and the agent
rebuilt the surface out of CLI calls* — happens strictly **after** a success, i.e. strictly inside
the muted region.

Measured over the whole fire corpus (`.minsky/cli-mcp-substitution-calibration.jsonl`, 11,063
records, 2026-08-14 → 08-19):

| outcome | count |
| --- | --- |
| `clean` | 10,544 |
| `suppressed-mcp-in-use` | 514 |
| `matched` (fired) | **5** |

All 5 fires were `commandId: memory.get`, and in **5 of 5** sessions the fire was that session's
**opening record** while every later record in the same session was suppressed. That is the
predicted signature of a monotonic suppression, measured rather than inferred.

Found while discharging mt#4290's SC1 (classify the accumulated corpus). That task's rung decision
is recorded separately as **keep** — the rung was never the binding constraint.

## What the guard now does

It fires when a Minsky-CLI call has a registered `mcp__minsky__*` equivalent AND any of:

1. **no `mcp__minsky__*` call has succeeded** in the session — the original mt#4144 predicate;
2. **a call ERRORED since the last success** — unmutes immediately (R2);
3. **it is the SECOND or later substitution since the last success** — the run counter (ask#9452).

A permission DENIAL is none of these: the operator refused one call and the request reached the
harness, so the surface is demonstrably up.

## Key changes

- **`readMcpSubstitutionState`** replaces the bare boolean — one ordered walk returning
  `{ succeeded, substitutionsSinceLastSuccess, failedSinceLastSuccess }`. Suppression is
  `succeeded && run === 0 && !failed`. `hasSucceededMcpCall` stays exported and unchanged in
  meaning (its 7 existing assertions still hold); it is now a thin wrapper.
- **Both transcript shapes are read** (R1). `toolUsesOf` normalizes the top-level
  `type: "tool_use"` line and the assistant-embedded block, mirroring `transcript.ts`'s
  `findToolUseInputs`. A top-level line advances the run but can never prove success or failure —
  that shape carries no correlating id, which is now an INVARIANT documented on the type.
- **The three firing branches assert different facts and none may claim another's.** Ordered
  never-succeeded → errored → run-length, matching the calibration `reason` field's own
  precedence. Fires carry `reason` (`no-mcp-success` | `mcp-failed` | `substitution-run`),
  `substitutionsSinceLastSuccess` and `failedSinceLastSuccess` so a future pass can rate them apart.
- **`scripts/replay-cli-mcp-substitution.ts`** (new) — replays real transcripts through both rules.
- **Posture correction** in `hook-observers.mdc` and the detector's doc page: this guard **injects**
  and always has (`run()` returns `additionalContext`; `dispatcher.ts:1068` pushes it with no gate on
  declared `effects`). Both said "calibration-first (log-only, never denies)" — *never denies* is
  true, *log-only* never was (mt#4290).

## Why not the obvious fix

A failure trigger alone would not have caught the originating incident: in R11 the agent **stopped
calling MCP** rather than getting errors, so there is no failed call in the transcript. (It is still
worth having on its own merits, which is R2 — not catching one incident is no reason to skip a
trigger that catches others.)

And a matcher on the harness's disconnect notice **could never fire**: that notice is injected into
model context and never written to the transcript the hook reads — **0** non-assistant entries
carrying it across the 120 most recent transcripts. Shipping it would have been mem#704's
can't-fail probe. Checked before writing it, not after.

That leaves the substitution **run** for the R11 case, which means a threshold — an
enforcement-posture change, so it went to the operator rather than being chosen here.
**ask#9452: fire from the second substitution.** A success resets the run, EXCEPT when that call is
itself the substitution (`session_exec` running the Minsky CLI is both), which would otherwise let a
rebuild burst clear its own counter at every step.

## Measurement before shipping

The calibration log **cannot** size this change: it records substitution events but not the MCP
successes that reset the counter, so it yields only an upper bound (467 of 529, 88%) that assumes
every reset away. Replaying transcripts — which carry both — gives the real delta.

`bun scripts/replay-cli-mcp-substitution.ts --dir <this project> --limit 60`, run
2026-08-20T07:10Z:

```
transcripts replayed:        60
substitution calls seen:     385

fires under BOTH rules:      44  (no MCP success yet — unchanged)
suppressed under BOTH:       153  (first substitution after a success)
NEWLY firing under mt#4353:  188

total fires: 44 (old) -> 232 (new)
sessions with >=1 new fire:  19 of 60
```

**The absolute delta drifts between runs, and that is a property of the corpus, not of the rule.**
"The 60 most recent transcripts" is a moving window over live sessions: the same command returned
141 newly-firing before the R1 parsing fix, 147 just after it, and 188 twenty minutes later as
other sessions' activity entered the window. Reporting one figure as stable would be wrong. What is
stable across every run is the SHAPE:

- fires under both rules stay pinned at **44** — the change adds no fires to sessions that never had
  a successful MCP call;
- the new fires are heavily **concentrated** — the top 4 transcripts carry 144 of the 188, and
  19 of 60 sessions see any at all.

The heaviest sessions were read by hand and are the target class outright — sustained
`minsky tasks spec get` / `tools asks list` / `refs status` / `memory get|patch|create` bursts, i.e.
the whole surface rebuilt through the CLI, every one of which the old rule suppressed. The increase
is the guard reaching its target population, not noise.

(This measurement predates R2's failure trigger, which can only ADD fires — in sessions where an
MCP call errored. It does not change the shape above.)

## Testing

Execution evidence:

```
$ bun test --preload ./tests/setup.ts ./.minsky/hooks/detect-cli-mcp-substitution.test.ts
 46 pass, 0 fail, 75 expect() calls  [58.00ms]

$ bun scripts/run-tests-gated.ts        (pre-R1 tree)
 63 pass, 0 fail — Ran 63 tests across 4 files. [347.00ms]
 run-tests-gated.ts: all test steps passed.
```

typecheck: 0 errors across 8 projects (`validatedWorkspace` = the session dir).
lint: 0 errors / 0 warnings, 3836 files.

Negative control — the original rule, reverting the predicate to `if (state.succeeded)`:

```
(fail) AT6 > R11 ordering: MCP succeeded, then went quiet — the SECOND substitution fires
(fail) AT6 > a session_exec substitution does not reset its own run
(fail) AT6 > the run-length warning does not claim MCP never succeeded
 37 pass, 3 fail
```

Negative control — R1, with the top-level shape ignored:

```
(fail) AT6 > a top-level tool_use line advances the run (PR #3186 R1)
 41 pass, 1 fail
```

Negative control — R2, with `failedSinceLastSuccess` dropped from the suppression condition:

```
(fail) AT6 > an MCP call that ERRORED since the last success unmutes immediately (PR #3186 R2)
 44 pass, 1 fail
```

Negative control — R3, with the failure branch checked before the never-succeeded branch:

```
(fail) AT6 > an errored call with NO prior success does not claim one (PR #3186 R2)
 45 pass, 1 fail
```

All restored → 46 pass. The remaining AT6 cases pass under both rules by design: they are the
regression floor (first-subs

author: kjanat
body:
Audited the full `v4.1.1.post1..v4.2.0` upstream diff (5 source files) against `packages/pykeepass-stubs/`.

**4.2.0 itself needed almost nothing.** The headline changes alter behavior, not signatures: `add_entry`/`Entry` now accept `None` for title/username/password (the stubs already declared `str | None`; 4.2.0 makes that declaration true at runtime, 4.1.1 raised `TypeError`), and `save()` now rotates seeds without a signature change. The new `kdbx_parsing` symbols stay outside these partial stubs.

**The audit surfaced pre-existing drift, now repaired:**

- `find_entries`/`find_groups`/`find_attachments` and `xpath`/`_xpath` get `Literal` overloads over `first`/`cast`/`path`; the old three-way unions forced casts downstream (two `cast(Entry, ...)` in the e2e harness became reportUnnecessaryCast errors and are removed).
- `Attachment.data` is a read-only property aliasing `binary`, `expires` returns `bool | None`, `icon` setter rejects `None`, `deref` returns `str | None`.
- `icons` is a declared class with `Final` literals (was `SimpleNamespace`, so every access typed `Any`).
- Missing members added: `payload`/`kdbx` as `construct.Container`, the 12 deprecated `find_*_by_*`, Entry string-field helpers, module loggers, `BLANK_DATABASE_*`. `Entry.history` stays read-only: the runtime setter always raises `NotImplementedError`.

**Dependency side:** constraint widens to `pykeepass>=4.1.1.post1,<4.3`, lock moves to 4.2.0 (new transitives `importlib-metadata`/`zipp` replace the dropped `pkg_resources`). This supersedes the pykeepass part of #55; after a Dependabot rebase #55 shrinks to the `@bitwarden/cli` 2026.7.0 + Vaultwarden 1.37.0 bumps needed for issue #53.

**Verification:** mypy stubtest clean against 4.1.1.post1 and 4.2.0; a 27-assertion `typing.assert_type` consumption script passes basedpyright and ty; full gates (ruff incl. forced `--preview`, basedpyright, ty, stubs smoke, 21 pytest adapters, dprint) green with pykeepass 4.2.0 actually installed.

## ADR-041 A41-11 — `dump-composition` (the composition dump)

A41-11 has several parts (profile files, layered overlays, a replaceable loop-driver row, and **`--dump-composition`**). This PR lands the composition dump — cheap now, because A41-7 turned "what is registered" from hand-maintained lists into **registries you can read**.

### What lands

author: dat999zx
body:
`knowl decide` with no AI provider printed:

```
⚠️ No AI provider configured or API keys found. Falling back to direct insertion without conflict detection.
✅ Recorded decision successfully! ID: e3614f5719...
🔄 Superseded older decision: cbb8c5d0e4...
```

Both cannot be true. It's the warning that's wrong.

Same-subject reconciliation is deterministic and runs regardless — rules 1–5 in `docs/reference.md`, keyed on significant-token overlap of the title. What an AI provider adds is contradiction detection **across** subjects, where the new atom doesn't name the same thing it invalidates.

Now:

```
ℹ️ No AI provider configured. Same-subject writes still reconcile; cross-subject contradiction detection is off.
✅ Recorded decision successfully! ID: d1bb99a41e...
🔄 Superseded older decision: 8581609edf...
```

**Why it matters beyond wording.** This line is the loudest thing in `docs/assets/demo.gif` — it appears twice in a seven-line recording that exists to demonstrate conflict resolution. And it cost an evening in one session: a single failing case (a *claim* used as a title, which misses the two-token floor) was read as "supersession needs an API key", and that misreading reached the README before being caught.

Dropped from ⚠️ to ℹ️ since nothing is degraded on the common path.

No test asserted the old string. Suite green: 344 files, 3210 passed, 5 skipped.

author: krisarmstrong
body:
## Summary

`biome.json` excluded `**/dist`, `**/build` and `**/coverage` — patterns that match a directory of that name **at any depth**, not the build and report directories they mean. A source directory called any of those three is then silently unlinted and unformatted: it passes `npm run lint` by not being looked at, and reports "these paths were provided but ignored" if you check it directly.

Found in trellis while building its Coverage page — `ui/src/components/coverage/` was invisible to Biome — and the identical pattern is in all four repos. Fixed there in MustardSeedNetworks/trellis#76; this is the same change here.

The other excludes in the list (`.next`, `storybook-static`, `playwright-report`, `playwright/.auth`, `node_modules`) are left at any-depth: nobody names a source directory after them, so the ambiguity is theoretical.

## Linked Issue

Closes #1981

(Fleet-wide; found and fixed first in MustardSeedNetworks/trellis#76, tracked there as MustardSeedNetworks/trellis#71.)

## Type of Change

- [x] Defect fix
- [x] CI / release / packaging

## Risk

- [x] Low

Lint configuration only. It can newly *report* on files that were previously skipped; verified below that it does not, because no such directories exist here today. That is the point — the fix is cheap now and stops the trap before someone falls into it.

## Testing Evidence

```text
$ find ui/src -type d \( -name dist -o -name build -o -name coverage \)
```

author: kibarik
body:
Closes #73

## Что и зачем

Дорогие стадии Issue — разработка агентом OpenHands и круг правок по ревью — исполнялись обычными Temporal-активностями **внутри** родительского `IssueLifecycle`. Два следствия:

1. **Своего WorkflowId у них нет** — ни строки в `temporal workflow list`, ни следа, переживающего завершение. Операционная история собиралась логами контейнера и `docker ps`.
2. **Одна активность на всю стадию** — её ретрай повторял ВСЕ внутренние шаги. На живом прогоне `poh-demo-checkout#39` падал только `git push` на последнем шаге, а заново шёл двадцатиминутный прогон агента, и контур трижды объявил о передаче задачи.

Ветка вводит правило: стадия с тремя свойствами — минуты работы, недетерминизм, денежная стоимость — исполняется дочерним воркфлоу с детерминированным id, а её шаги становятся отдельными активностями со своими политиками ретраев.

## Целевая модель наблюдаемости

| Поверхность | Отвечает на вопрос |
|---|---|
| GitHub Issue | что просили — требования, подзадачи, решения человека |
| **Temporal** | **что и как делала система — операционная работа** |
| GitHub PR | что получилось — код и ревью |

Средний слой ветка и достраивает.

## Идентификаторы прогонов

| Прогон | Идентификатор | Статус |
|---|---|---|
| Родитель Issue | `issue-<repo>-<n>` | был |
| Аналитика | `analysis-<repo>-<n>` | был |
| Оценка | `estimate-<repo>-<n>-<marker>` | был |
| **Разработка** | **`develop-<repo>-<n>`** | **введён** |
| **Круг правок** | **`prfix-<repo>-<pr>-<round>`** | **введён** |

Все форматы — только в `shared/workflow_ids.py`.

## Честное ограничение

Единого дерева всех прогонов в UI не будет: родитель делает continue-as-new при 800 событиях, RunId меняется, дочерние прогоны остаются у прежнего. **Полнота восстановления держится на идентификаторе, а не на дереве.** Выявлено в архитектурных дебатах и записано в README.

## Безопасность выкладки

Оба переключения стоят под маркерами патча (`issue-lifecycle-develop-child`, `issue-lifecycle-prfix-child`). Прогоны, начатые на прежнем коде, идут прежним путём через `trigger_openhands_resolver`; `_run_linear` не тронут. Финальное ревью проверило неизменность прежнего пути построчно.

Выкладка **двумя этапами**: сначала разработка и проверка живым Issue, затем круг правок.

## Что нашло финальное ревью — и это чинилось отдельно

Три дефекта, которых задачные гейты увидеть не могли:

- **Ретрай публикации не мог удаться и давал ложный диагноз.** После падения пуша коммит уже создан; вторая попытка не находила staged-изменений и возвращала `None` — контур докладывал «агент не изменил ни одного файла» вместо настоящей причины. То есть на ровно том сбое, ради которого всё затевалось, диагноз становился хуже прежнего.
- **Обработка `WorkflowAlreadyStartedError` крутила родителя вхолостую** — возврат текущей фазы замыкался в `_enter` без единого `await`, и при автостарте цикл спинился до continue-as-new и заново.
- **Все сбои разработки схлопнулись в один отпечаток Sentry** — `_failure_reason` разворачивал один `.cause`, а дочерний воркфлоу добавил уровень.

Плюс потом: разворот `.cause` не должен проходить сквозь таймаут — иначе доложилась бы пережитая ошибка вместо настоящей причины.

## Проверка

703 теста, покрытие 84.43% (порог 83.0%). Новые тесты закрепляют свойства, а не факт прохождения: ретрай публикации гоняется против настоящего bare-origin с подменённым первым пушем; тест коллизии реально занимает канонический id; тесты на одну попытку роняют сам шаг агента.

## Аналитика

Цепочка SA-helper — [`sa_documentation/FNR/FNR_6/`](https://github.com/po-helper-org/poh-issue-agents/tree/research/issue-73/sa_documentation/FNR/FNR_6) в ветке `research/issue-73`: постановка, концепты с дебатами, системные требования, валидация.

План реализации — `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-fnr6-develop-as-child-workflow.md`.

author: 2eha0
body:
## Summary

FreeForm plugin forms have always written a hardcoded `null` for an empty/unset field. This adds a `FormConfig.emptyFieldValue` option (`'null' | 'undefined'`, defaults to `'null'`) so host apps can opt into `undefined` instead, while keeping every existing plugin's behavior unchanged by default.

## What changed

- **New config**: `FormConfig.emptyFieldValue` on `Form`/`PluginConfigurationForm`/plugin `formConfig`.
- **Two distinct helpers**, since one bug was easy to introduce here:
  - `getEmptyOrDefault(path)` / `field.emptyOrDefaultValue` — **initialization** only (new array item, new map entry, hidden-field reset). Still forces required-field structure (`[]`/`{}`) and an explicit `schema.default` back in.
  - `getEmptyValue()` / `field.emptyValue` — **user actively clears a field**. Always the plain configured sentinel, never re-injects a default or forces structure. Using `emptyOrDefaultValue` here would make a required field with an explicit default impossible to empty (every clear would snap back to the default).
- Routed the shared field components (String/Number/CredentialSecret/Foreign/Enum/Array/Map/Json) through the new helpers instead of a literal `null`.
- Also centralized several plugin-specific custom fields that had their own hardcoded `null` for clear actions: ACL mode switching, OpenID Connect principals/lookup settings, Datakit CA certificates, and the rate-limiting-advanced/service-protection request-limit row initialization.
- Left two spots (`service-protection`/`rate-limiting-advanced` `RedisField.vue` and Datakit's `FlowEditor.vue`) on a hardcoded `null` intentionally, with a comment explaining why: the plugin entity form *merges* free-form data with VFG data, and only `null` (not `undefined`) actually clears an existing `partials` value there.
- **Bug fix**: `StandardLayout.vue`'s template referenced an undefined local `formConfig` instead of `props.formConfig`, so `formConfig` was silently dropped for every plugin using the default layout — meaning the new config (and any other `formConfig` option) couldn't reach the form at all until this was fixed.
- Documented all of this in the FreeForm README (`Empty Field Values` section).

## Test plan

- [x] `vue-tsc` typecheck clean (only a pre-existing, unrelated `metadata.ts` error remains)
- [x] `eslint` clean (only pre-existing warnings in `EnumField.vue`/`useMapField.ts`)
- [x] `vitest run` — `schema.spec.ts` unit tests (10/10) covering the new config resolution and the `auto`/`schema.default` exclusions
- [x] Full `free-form/**/*.cy.ts` Cypress suite — 330+ tests, 0 failures, including the plugins that exercise the `StandardLayout` bug-fix path (JwtSigner, OpenidConnect, Governance, MeteringAndBilling)
- [x] New dedicated Cypress specs per field type (String/Number/CredentialSecret/Foreign/Json) plus extended existing ones (Array/Map/Enum) covering both the default and `emptyFieldValue: 'undefined'` behavior, and a regression test for the required+default bug this design avoids
- [ ] `CaCertificatesField.vue`, both `RedisField.vue`/`RequestLimitsForm.vue` copies, and `FlowEditor.vue` have no existing Cypress coverage (pre-existing gap) — verified by typecheck/lint only

## Summary
- make WebSocket registration atomic with the shutdown snapshot
- reject connections that finish upgrading after shutdown begins
- add a deterministic lifecycle regression test for the late-registration path

A hijacked WebSocket could previously finish registration after shutdown had already captured its connection snapshot. That connection was no longer managed by net/http and would miss the 1012 restart close frame.

## Résumé

## Backend

- `GET /recordings` (liste publique) — n'existait pas avant cette phase. Filtre texte naïf (`ILIKE`) en attendant l'indexation Meilisearch de la Phase 4.
- Jointure `users` sur toutes les routes de lecture (`authorHandle`/`authorDisplayName` dans `recordingSchema`) pour afficher "Recorded by {auteur}" sans aller-retour supplémentaire.

## Frontend (`apps/web`)

- Composants partagés suivant le design system : `Header`/`MobileTopBar`/`BottomTabBar` (bascule desktop/mobile 100% CSS, pas de composants "Mobile*" dupliqués), `PlayButton`, `Waveform`, `RecordingRow`/`RecordingCard`, `ExplorerMap` (placeholder SVG documenté comme tel — la vraie carte MapLibre/pmtiles est Phase 4), `ExplorerSelection`/`RecordingSummaryCard` (panneau flottant desktop + BottomSheet mobile, contenu partagé).
- Lecteur audio à instance unique partagée dans toute l'app (`apps/web/lib/audio-player.tsx`).
- Flux Ajouter en 3 étapes (Sound → Place & details → Publish) branché directement sur l'API existante (presign → upload → création → job de publication).
- Polices Public Sans / Source Serif 4 auto-hébergées via `next/font/google`.

## Décisions et simplifications documentées

Détaillées dans `plan/TASKS.md` (section Phase 3) et `plan/MEMORY.md` :

- **Géocodage** (Photon) reporté en Phase 4 — l'étape 2 du flux Ajouter capture les coordonnées via la géolocalisation navigateur en attendant.
- **`BottomTabBar`** garde toujours les 4 mêmes items (jamais un 5ᵉ pour Profil), suivant la règle explicite du handoff plutôt qu'une incohérence ponctuelle d'un mockup mobile.
- Pas de champ `featured`/date de prise de son en base : entrée mise en avant = la plus récente, date par défaut = date d'upload.
- Filtres "location/tag/duration" de l'écran Recherche affichés en texte inerte (pas de contrepartie serveur avant Meilisearch) plutôt qu'en liens trompeurs.

`pnpm build`/`typecheck`/`lint`/`test` verts sur les 9 packages. Vérification en conditions réelles avec la stack complète (Docker Postgres/Redis/MinIO + API + Web) : base seedée, session injectée directement en Redis (pas de cérémonie WebAuthn automatisable en navigateur headless), les 6 écrans comparés visuellement aux mockups en desktop et mobile (390px), et **un cycle d'upload complet exécuté réellement dans le navigateur** (presign → upload MinIO → création d'enregistrement → redirection vers la fiche publiée). Détail complet dans le journal de session de `plan/TASKS.md`.

Ajoute `CLAUDE.md` à la racine — sources de vérité du dépôt, conventions déjà en place, et procédures de fin de session pour `plan/TASKS.md`/`plan/MEMORY.md`/`README.md`.
