body:
## 무엇을 하나

러너(`tools/harness/execute.py`)에 테스트가 **0건**이다. `docs/status.md` 가 「지금 하네스의 가장 큰 빈칸」이라 적었고, [ADR-030] 파일럿 B 를 죽인 것도 러너 결함(`TimeoutExpired` 미처리)이었다. 그 빈칸을 **4축으로 갈라 워크트리 병렬**로 채우기 위한 **착수 준비**다. 이 PR 자체는 테스트를 쓰지 않는다 — lane 정의와 진입점만 얹는다.

| lane | 대상 | 새 테스트 파일 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runner-ac` | `_run_ac` 판정 (`:264-281`) | `tests/harness/test_execute_ac.py` |
| `runner-retry` | codex 호출 · 재시도 · 출구 (`:241-262`, `:302-352`) | `tests/harness/test_execute_retry.py` |
| `runner-commit` | 2단 커밋 · 브랜치 · 상태 인덱스 (`:140-193`, `:283-300`) | `tests/harness/test_execute_commit.py` |
| `runner-boot` | 시작 거부 · 형식 계약 (`:96-120`, `:197-204`) | `tests/harness/test_execute_boot.py` |

## 왜 이 순서인가 — 공유 파일 하나가 병렬의 유일한 구조적 비용이다

`phases/index.json` 은 모든 lane 이 갱신하는 단 하나의 공유 파일이다(`execute.py:290-300`). lane 브랜치를 먼저 판 뒤 각자 항목을 배열 끝에 추가하면 같은 위치를 고쳐 머지 충돌한다. **워크트리를 파기 전에 4항목을 전부 등록해 두면** 각 lane 은 서로 다른 줄의 `status` 값만 바꿔 3-way 자동 병합된다. `apps/api/tests/harness/__init__.py`(레포 관행)도 같은 이유로 여기 넣었다.

## 착수 전 실사 (전부 코드·upstream 대조)

- **AC 판별력 사전 측정**(`harness.md` §C-5d): 4 lane 전부 pytest AC **rc=4**(대상 파일 부재) · collect-count AC **rc=1**. 테스트를 실제로 쓰지 않으면 어떤 lane 도 초록이 날 수 없다.
- **upstream `jha0313/finsight` 대조**: `scripts/test_execute.py` 는 클래스 11개를 갖지만 **`_run_ac` 커버리지가 없다**(원본은 AC 를 러너가 안 돌린다 — 우리 수리 ①). 우리 수리 4종 영역은 전부 신규 작성이다. **finsight 에 병렬·워크트리 개념은 없다**(`threading` 은 progress spinner 전용).
- **`evals/harness/*` 는 러너 테스트가 아니다** — `judge`/`responder`/`reviewer`/`rules`/`triager` 로 이루어진 LLM eval 하네스다. status.md 가 「미이식 3종」으로 묶은 것을 갈랐다.
- **샤드 파티션 게이트**(`test_pytest_shard_partition.py`)는 살아 있지만 샤드 `c` 의 `paths:["tests"]` 가 `tests/harness/` 를 이미 덮는다 ⇒ `shards.json` 수정 불필요, lane 간 겹침 0.
- **⓪ 표의 하네스 적합 후보 9건이 전부 「트리거 미도래」**였고, 그중 [BL-661]·[BL-671]·[BL-639] 는 **잔여 작업 자체가 없다**(각각 [BL-669] 이관 완료 / 원장이 「값 0」 근거 셋을 적어 둠 / `account_exclusivity.py:31-46` docstring 이 이미 결정·구현했다고 명시). 원장 정정은 회차 마감으로 넘겼다.

## 검증

```
✓ runner-ac       steps=2  ac=[3,3]
✓ runner-retry    steps=2  ac=[3,3]
✓ runner-commit   steps=2  ac=[3,3]
✓ runner-boot     steps=2  ac=[3,3]
```

author: jacintalama
body:
Three things a client could not read off the Delivery page.

## 1. NO TRACKING was a number with nothing behind it

> "I don't understand what orders has no tracking at the moment, there is no way for me to press the no tracking to actually see which orders are missing tracking"

Underneath that sat a smaller copy of the 155-against-8 bug fixed last week. The tile counted every `NO_TRACKING` order; the section below held only the ones **also past their promise**. Two sizes for one idea, and the rows in the gap were reachable from nowhere on the page.

The section now takes exactly the set the tile counts — keyed on the same `state` `deliveryStats` reads, so the two agree by construction rather than by agreement — and the tile is the button that opens it.

The widening makes "Days over" the wrong column: most of these orders are still inside their promise, where it is zero row after row. It is now **Waiting** (days since the order was placed), longest first, with overdue rows marked in words rather than by colour alone.

## 2. "Available" meant two things at once

`AVAILABLE` is `['READY_FOR_PICKUP', 'DELIVERED']` in `milestones.ts`, and `src/lib/dhl/map.ts` maps only ever to `DELIVERED`. So every DHL order badged **"Available"** beside a DHL tracking page reading **"Delivered"** — the system looked like it was contradicting the carrier.

Both facts were already stored; only the state failed to tell them apart:

- `collectedAt` set → **Delivered** (all DHL deliveries, Bring once collected)
- `availableAt` alone → **Ready for collection** (Bring parcel at a pickup point)

**Deliberately not moved:** the clock still stops at `availableAt`, so the median, the on-time rate and `stats.delivered` measure to the pickup point exactly as before. A customer who takes a week to walk to the shop is not a late delivery — that is the whole reason `READY_FOR_PICKUP` stops the clock.

## 3. The strip had the same conflation, one level up

"Where everything is now" ended in a segment counting `delivered`, so an uncollected parcel was reported as delivered six inches above a badge now saying it is not. Waiting at the pickup point is a real position on that journey and gets its own. The two **split** `delivered` rather than recomputing it, so an arrived order cannot be counted twice.

## Verification

- Every behaviour red first. The route tests initially passed because the route was already changed, so they were re-checked against the old filter: 3 of 4 failed, as they should.
- Full suite: **225 files, 2417 tests, 0 failures**.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint` clean on all 11 files; `next build` succeeds.

## Notes

- The branch still carries `0801668`, the pre-squash version of #32. Those files are **byte-identical to main** (`git diff origin/main <branch>` over them is empty), so merging changes nothing for them.
- Not in this PR, and not code: the tracking-from cutoff. Setting each already-tracked shop to `2026-08-19` on `/settings/delivery` is what drops the 45 to only the days the warehouse has actually filed for. Shops whose field is blank must stay blank — blank means "not tracked at all".

author: michaeltaylor3d
body:
## What changed

Both GitHub Actions workflows in this repo were copied from another crate's repo and never renamed. `release.yml` re-locked a package that does not exist here, and `publish.yml` described this crate as something else entirely.

## Why it matters, and why the second half is the worse half

The release run for **0.3.0** failed:

```
error: package ID specification `dig-did` did not match any packages
```

So no tag was cut, nothing published, and `dig-mirror-coin` is absent from crates.io despite PR #1 having merged. That is the visible failure and it is the cheap one — it is loud.

The quieter defect is in `publish.yml`, which would have **succeeded**. It titles the GitHub release `dig-did vX.Y.Z`, describes this crate as *"a pure, key-free, network-free SpendBundle-builder for Chia Decentralized Identifiers"*, and gives the reader an install snippet telling them to add `dig-did` to their `Cargo.toml`. A release that ships correct artifacts under the wrong name with the wrong instructions is more expensive than one that fails, because nothing reports it and the reader has no reason to doubt it.

## The fix

- **`release.yml`** derives the package name from the manifest instead of hardcoding it:
  ```yaml
  run: cargo update -p "$(cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq -r '.packages[0].name')"
  ```
  This removes the defect class rather than this instance of it — the next repo to copy this file is correct on arrival instead of red on its first release.
- **`publish.yml`** release notes now describe `dig-mirror-coin`: what it does, and an install snippet naming the crate that is actually being published.

## How verified

- The derived expression resolves to `dig-mirror-coin` locally, and `cargo update -p` accepts it (`Locking 0 packages`).
- Both workflows parse as YAML.
- Checked for control bytes in both files and found none — an earlier attempt at this edit went through a shell heredoc that silently turned a `\1` backreference into a literal `0x01`, which `cat -A` caught but a diff would not have.
- Confirmed the only remaining occurrence of the old crate name is inside a comment quoting the error message, which is intentional.

## Version

**0.3.0 → 0.3.1**, patch: CI-only, no library behaviour changes.

## Blast radius

Workflow files plus the version. No `src/` change. Blast radius established by direct read and grep across `.github/` — gitnexus was not used for a four-line CI change.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators whose credentials were already migrated to SQLite would find OpenClaw completely unusable because a retired `auth.json` or `auth-profiles.json` file was still sitting in the agent directory. Every credential read failed with `AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`, and `openclaw gateway start` / `restart` refused to run at all, so all channels and providers stayed offline until Doctor was run — even though the working credentials were right there in the store.

Two adjacent operator-facing defects on the same surface:

- The duplicate-`agentDir` error told operators to "copy auth-profiles.json" to share credentials. Following that advice does nothing (runtime never reads the file) and lands the second agent in a migration-required state.
- `openclaw migrate plan codex --item auth:openai` reported a destination file that is never created, and the `openclaw secrets configure` picker labelled candidates with a filename that no longer exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fail-closed behaviour existed to prevent a stale token from overwriting a fresh one. That risk does not exist once the store is populated: Doctor's importer (`mergeImportedAuthProfiles`) never replaces a usable stored credential, it only fills empty slots. So the guard was over-broad — it punished the healthy migrated case it was never protecting.

A legacy file is now only fatal when the canonical store cannot serve credentials for that owner. Populated store plus leftover file means unarchived bytes: warn once, keep serving, let Doctor archive it. Empty store plus a credential file still fails closed and still never falls through to environment auth. Startup degrades that owner to configured-unavailable rather than refusing to boot, which is what `docs/gateway/secrets.md` already specifies — and that makes the gateway lifecycle preflight obsolete, so it is deleted.

The vocabulary cleanup follows the same invariant: the store moved to SQLite years of releases ago, but the operator-facing language never did. Genuine legacy-filename uses in Doctor, the security fixer, and migration fixtures are deliberately untouched.

The plugin SDK's `resolveSecretPlanTargetByPath` / `ResolvedSecretPlanTarget` are removed rather than deprecated: they have zero callers in core, plugins, or tests, and the symbols are absent from the latest stable tag, so they carry no compatibility obligation. Their inline parameter type was the only thing putting the retired filename on the public SDK surface.

## User Impact

- An install with a leftover credential file keeps working instead of hard-failing; the gateway starts, and one warning names the file to clean up.
- A genuinely unmigrated store behaves exactly as before: fail closed, no environment fallback, `openclaw doctor --fix` as the named next step.
- Operators following the duplicate-`agentDir` remediation, the migrate plan output, or the secrets picker are no longer pointed at a file that does not exist.
- The device-code sign-in prompt now warns about the actual phishing shape (someone else giving you a code), unconditionally rather than only when an expiry is known.
- No config changes, no migration required, no new operator action.

## Evidence

Live, on a built CLI against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, same state dir before and after:

- Populated store + stale `auth.json`, **before**: `Auth profile store …/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration` and no profiles listed.
- Same state, **after**: one warning — `retired auth profile files are ignored by runtime; run Doctor to archive them` — then `anthropic:default [anthropic/api_key]` listed and usable.
- Empty store + `auth.json`, **after**: still fails closed with the same migration error and the Doctor hint.
- The legacy file is byte-identical afterward in every case; runtime never reads or removes it.

Automated:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets src/plugin-sdk` — 233 files, 2295 passed.
- Auth/session/CLI suites for the changed surfaces pass; regression tests fail on pre-fix code.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — exit 0 across all gates (typecheck, lint, dead-export scan, database-first guard, import cycles).
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` — passes with no API digest acknowledgement required, confirming the deleted symbols were not part of the pinned public contract.
- Codex autoreview over the full diff — clean, no accepted or actionable findings.

Not covered: the gateway lifecycle preflight removal is proven by its unit test rather than a live `gateway start`, since that path installs a launchd service.

Production LOC is roughly net-neutral: the deleted preflight and SDK exports (−63) offset the new invariant, the phishing warning, and the corrected operator text.

author: dreamlx
body:
Closes #227.

## What

One-line fix: add `REFERENCES` to `VALID_EDGE_KINDS` in `export_reader.py`.

## Why

codeindex GH #128 introduced a 4th edge kind `REFERENCES` (Pass 4 import-ref + Pass 5 type-ref, connecting non-callable exported symbols like `const` / `interface` / `type_alias` that `CALLS` cannot reach). The drift was **one-sided** — loomgraph's read side, storage, and `graph --relation-type` flag already accepted REFERENCES and the edges were being stored — but the import gate's `VALID_EDGE_KINDS` set lagged, so every import spammed one `unknown kind 'REFERENCES'` schema warning per edge (638 on codeindex's own repo).

The surrounding comment already stated the intent ("Keep it in sync with codeindex so legitimate kinds ... don't spray false positives"). This completes the sync to the current codeindex edge vocabulary.

## Scope note

REFERENCES is **not TS-only**. Pass 5 type-ref runs for every language with type annotations — dogfooding codeindex's own repo (`languages: [python, java, php, typescript, javascript]`) produced 637 REFERENCES edges, **627 from `.py` type annotations**. So every Python+TS indexer hits this, not just TS repos.

## Verification

- **TDD red**: reverted `VALID_EDGE_KINDS` to the 3-element set → new test fails with the exact warning (`line 4 edge: unknown kind 'REFERENCES'`).
- **Green after fix**: `test_reader_references_edge_not_flagged_unknown_kind` passes; full `pytest` suite **852 passed, 2 skipped**.
- **Re-dogfood A/B**: `loomgraph import-export <codeindex artifact> --dry-run` schema_warnings **638 → 1** (the remaining 1 is the unrelated `#156` test-pollution hint, not an unknown-kind warning).
- `ruff check` clean on both changed files.

## Test

`test_reader_references_edge_not_flagged_unknown_kind` mirrors the existing `test_reader_imports_edge_not_flagged_unknown_kind`: feeds an NDJSON with a `REFERENCES` edge, asserts zero `schema_warnings` mentioning REFERENCES, `edge_kinds["REFERENCES"]` incremented, and the edge mapped through to storage (`edge_data["keywords"] == "REFERENCES"`).

author: poli0981
body:
## What this is

HANDOFF item 3's **prerequisite with code attached** — the one it says must land *before*
`presents / batch` is published anywhere. Item 3 needs no more counter code; what it needed
was this, a decision, and a measurement.

## The defect

`FgWindow.BucketFactors` splits the window into eight buckets and refuses a factor when one
departs from the whole. It divides by `Σ fgEvaluations`, which is **zero on every record** on
the one route a real title has been measured on — `slEvaluateFeature(kFeatureDLSS_G)` is never
called. So every bucket matched, and `RefusalFor` returned at the data-gap clause before
uniformity was ever considered.

Meanwhile `presents / batch` **was** printed, unconditionally, and it is the number a
verification run actually reads. Measured 2026-08-16: an alt-tab mid-capture produced an
achieved ratio of **1.84** against a title configured for ×2 — wrong by 8%, with nothing in the
report saying so.

A guard keyed on a quantity that is zero on the route that runs is not a guard.

## What changed

- **`FgWindow.BatchRefusal`** — the per-bucket `presents / batch` check §S30 named as a
  prerequisite. Same refusals the factor lives under (`swapchainId 0`, multiple streams,
  too-short window) plus the uniformity check, over the batch weight.
- **`FgWindow.PresentsPerBatch`** — the arithmetic moves out of the renderer, where it was
  inline.
- **`BucketsOf` takes a weight selector**, so there is one slicing and two weights rather than
  two copies of the bucket maths.
- **`SessionReport`** prints the verdict on the line *under* the ratio, so the number cannot be
  read without it, and prints `span=` — computed since it was written and never printed, which
  is why §S30's draft reconstructed the span from a **different** window and got a rate that
  moved across 78.6–83 on window choice alone.
- **Focus, in the host and not in the hook.** Each 10 Hz drain tick samples whether the target
  owns the foreground window; the session carries `(DrainTicks, ForegroundTicks)`.
  `ForegroundWindowProbe` lives in `Infrastructure` (two documented Win32 calls, §Solution
  layout puts every P/Invoke there), costs the hook path nothing, and needs no record byte.
  §S30 suggested doing this in-process; that would have bought nothing.

**The pair, because zero is not a finding.** A process owning no top-level window is unfocused
on every tick of every run — `hook-harness` presents to a composition swapchain and has none —
so collapsing "never had focus" into "lost focus" would fire on every integration run and teach
the reader to ignore the line. Same could-not-look / looked-and-found-nothing collision
`FlRtTier` and `upscalerQuality` already exist to avoid.

**Focus is attribution, never the guard.** `BatchRefusal` refuses a mixed window from the
records alone, so a caller that never wires focus still cannot publish an averaged ratio. Focus
is what lets the report name the cause.

## Proven both ways

A canary returning `null` from `RefusalForBatches` was compiled (build exit code read **first**
— §Traps) and run:

- **RED**: `AnAltTabMidCaptureIsCAUGHTByTheBatchGUARD…`, `AWindowTooShortToBucketRefusesTheProxyToo`
- **GREEN**: `AUniformWindowPUBLISHESTheProxy…`, `TheProxyRefusesOnTheSameATTRIBUTIONFacts…`,
  `NoBatchAtAllIsNotARatioOfZero`

so the guard is neither always-red nor keyed on something that cannot vary.

`ForegroundWindowProbeTests` asserts the value the probe reads **is a live process id** —
reading `GetWindowThreadProcessId`'s *return* value (a thread id) instead of its out parameter
compiles, type-checks, and would make `IsForeground` answer false for every pid forever, which
reads exactly like the legitimate headless answer. Verified on this machine that the positive
branch runs: the out-parameter pid is a live process and the return value is not.

## Also fixed, all found while touching this

- **Four comments still carried the pre-2026-08-14 subtraction** `F_app = presents − Σ
  fgEvaluations`, which `fl_shm.h` explicitly retracts — `ShmLayout.cs`, `MeasuredFactsTests`,
  `stub_sl_common.cpp`, `fl-probe-interposer`. The mirror also said the count is "3 at ×4"; it
  is 1 per application frame at every multiplier. The decoy stub's arithmetic argument was
  reversed by the same correction.
- **`HANDOFF.md` item 3 contradicted itself inside one entry** — one block recorded three
  oracles tried and fallen, a later bullet said neither cheap measurement had been run.
- **`HANDOFF.md`'s "`./build.ps1 check` cannot go fully green here" is no longer true**, and it
  is the first thing a new session reads. Measured 2026-08-20: fully green, 20/20 native.
  Nothing here fixed it — the machine moved from Insider build 26300/29639 to **29648** and
  WARP's D3D12 path was fixed upstream. **Dated rather than deleted**: the durable fact is that
  this dependency broke and healed under the machine without a code change, twice giving the
  native suite a colour that said nothing about `main`.

## Docs updated in this PR

`03_METRICS` §Frame Generation (the guard and why the old one could not be it), `04_CAPTURE`
§Ring draining (the focus sample, and why out of process), `HANDOFF` (prerequisite struck, two
stale claims corrected), `CHANGELOG`.

## Not in this PR

No hook change, no layout change, no new `FL_MEASURED_*` bit. `presents / batch` is still a
**proxy** and is still never published as `fg_factor` — deciding that needs the PresentMon
`FrameType` measurement, which is the next item.

## Gate

`./build.ps1 check` with no switches: green — 20/20 native tests, 285 managed, only the
documented `resx-audit` skip.

author: digigull
body:
BACKLOG item 17. Three asks on the Analysis tab: it only updated from the Finder, the UI needed adjusting, and a refresh button would help.

## Why only the Finder fed it

The Finder is the only scanner that keeps `timeLeft`, and the tab's whole method rests on it — a listing that vanished counts as *sold* only if less time passed than its last-seen countdown bucket guaranteed it had left. Every other search (Buy, Sell, More) runs through `AtrSearch:AnalyzeResultsPage`, which reads `GetAuctionItemInfo` but never `GetAuctionItemTimeLeft`, so there was nothing downstream to feed the analysis with.

## The feed

That loop now collects the raw listing for **watched items only**, and the set is banked on the search and handed over in `Finish` — not observed per page. A listing being absent is what "sold" *means*, so observing half a scan would report every listing on the not-yet-fetched pages as bought, into a saved database where nothing afterwards could tell it from a real sale.

So completeness is asserted, never assumed. `anComplete` is set only where the batch loop sees a short page. Four routes get their bank discarded:

- the **>3000 results** early-out,
- the **duplicate page** bail,
- the two **watchdogs** in `Atr_OnUpdate`, which finish a stalled search with pages outstanding,
- any **level-filtered** compound search — it returns a subset of an item's listings, and since gear scales per instance on this server, one item's listings carry many required levels; the ones outside the filter would read as sold.

Broader than asked: **any** completed search now feeds the tab, so Sell and More scans count too. Same rule, not a wider one — a complete result set for a watched name is valid whichever tab asked for it.

## Rescan button

One exact search per watched item in the current group, in sequence, progress beside the button, second click stops. It drives `gAnalysisPane` through the ordinary search machinery rather than calling `QueryAuctionItems` itself — one pump owns the auction API, and a second racing it is how duplicate pages and disconnects happen. The cost of that choice is in the button's tooltip: the pump only advances the **current pane's** search, so leaving the tab stops the run. Each item uses `rescanThreshold` 0, because a cache hit would compare a snapshot against itself.

**Trap worth knowing:** `gCurrentPane == gAnalysisPane` is not the way to ask whether this tab is being pumped — `gCurrentPane` is a file-local in `Auctionator.lua` and reads nil from another file. The selected tab is what assigns it, so `An_TabIsCurrent` asks `Atr_IsTabSelected` instead.

## UI

Headers and row cells were two separate coordinate lists that had drifted apart: headers sat at the left edge of centred and right-aligned columns, `Low`'s value ran under the `Gold/day` header, `Gold/day` ran under the per-row delete button, and the summary line had no width so it ran off the panel. Both now come from one `AN_COLS` table, the delete button has its own lane past the last column, the summary wraps, and rows gained the Ledger's hover tooltip.

## Verification

- `luac5.1 -p` clean across the addon.

body:
Fixes the `findMostOverlappyType` fallback gap pinned as the `#[ignore]`d fence `fresh_union_property_target_cross_arm_tests::all_discriminators_failing_uses_most_overlappy_member` (ClaudeDE-fb0cry's #17798 handoff residual 2, re-verified still red by ClaudeT-83mttu at 2026-08-20T05:33Z).

**Structural rule 1 (most-overlappy fallback):** when a fresh object literal fails against a union target, no discriminant selects an arm, and some constituent lacks a written property's key, tsc's `getBestMatchIndexedAccessTypeOrUndefined` has an undefined indexed access over the union and falls back to `getBestMatchingType`, whose final `findMostOverlappyType` step selects the single arm sharing the most `keyof` overlap with the source (ties to the LAST written arm; primitive/nullish arms never score) — the property elaborates against that arm alone. tsz does this through the solver's existing `select_union_target_best_member` (which already models discriminant → generic-base reference → key-overlap-last-wins), exposed as a free function behind the `query_boundaries/assignability` gateway and consumed by a new `unnarrowed_union_object_literal_property_target` derivation in the checker's per-property elaboration. Witness: `{ kind: "zz", n: 2 }` against `{ kind: "a"; n: 1 } | { kind: "b"; n: 9 } | { kind: "c" }` — the `n` leaf now renders `'9'` (arm `"b"`), byte-matching 7.0.2; the `kind` head (exposed by every arm) keeps the cross-arm union `'"a" | "b" | "c"'`.

**Structural rule 2 (written target leads the include-walk):** tsc's `discriminateTypeByDiscriminableItems` pre-excludes primitive and nullish constituents itself, so a written `A | B | C | undefined` with a discriminator set counts as DISCRIMINATED down to `A | B | C` even when no discriminant value matches — the per-property target is then the indexed access over the surviving object arms (undefined when a survivor lacks the key, skipping that property's drill-in), never the most-overlappy single arm. tsz's include-walk (#17798) already implements the pre-exclusion but only ever saw the nullish-STRIPPED target; the written (pre-nullish-split) type now leads the narrowing candidate list. Witness: `NU = A | B | C | undefined` with `kind: "zz"` — exactly one diagnostic (`kind` cross-arm union), no `n` diagnostic, matching 7.0.2.

Owner layer: solver (member selection) + checker per-property elaboration target derivation (display routing only — no relation verdicts change).

Adjacent matrix (each byte-compared to `scripts/conformance/oracle.sh --strict`, pinned typescript@7.0.2):
- witness: `n` leaf `'9'`, `kind` head cross-arm union ✔
- tie breaks to the LAST written max-overlap arm (arm order flipped → `'1'`) ✔
- higher key overlap beats later position (3-key first arm beats 1-key last arm) ✔
- alias-wrapped arms resolve for the overlap scan ✔
- argument position (TS2345 call) takes the same fallback ✔
- nullish arm: discriminates to object arms, `n` drill-in skipped (1 diagnostic) ✔
- primitive (`number`) arm: same via the pre-exclusion (1 diagnostic) ✔
- negative controls: all-arms-expose keeps the cross-arm union; discriminant-matched narrowing keeps the matched arm; no-overlap sources stay with TS2353/outer error (existing fences)
- pinned `#[ignore]`d residual (distinct owner, #17696 written-arm-order family): instantiating `GU<T>` re-interns the substituted arm so the evaluated member list loses declaration order and last-best-wins picks the wrong arm (`'1'` vs 7.0.2 `'9'`) — the order half, not the fallback half

author: zacxdev
body:
A queued test run's output was captured through a **pipe**. Node makes a child's stdout synchronous when it refers to a regular file and **asynchronous when it refers to a pipe**, so a child that calls `process.exit()` discards whatever is still queued — before the parent ever receives it.

## The measurement that picked the fix

Head-to-head: the **same child**, in the same process, through the old mechanism and the new one. Two separate runs would not be a comparison.

```
consumer=slow  PIPES received= 172 missing=4828  |  FILE received=5000 missing=0
consumer=slow  PIPES received= 172 missing=4828  |  FILE received=5000 missing=0
consumer=slow  PIPES received= 172 missing=4828  |  FILE received=5000 missing=0
consumer=fast  PIPES received=1473 missing=3527  |  FILE received=5000 missing=0
consumer=fast  PIPES received=5000 missing=   0  |  FILE received=5000 missing=0
consumer=fast  PIPES received=5000 missing=   0  |  FILE received=5000 missing=0
```

The lines are **numbered**, which is what makes this readable: a bare count cannot tell truncation from sampling, and here every missing line is a **contiguous tail** — that is what identifies the mechanism rather than just confirming loss.

It also **ruled out both fixes the ticket proposed**:

- *"the daemon detects a short read on child exit"* — it cannot. The daemon sees a clean EOF and has no signal to compare against, because the bytes never reached the pipe.
- *"flush child stdout before exit"* — not ours to call. The child is vitest.

A file needs no cooperation from the thing losing the data.

## A second, independent defect on the same path

With **every byte delivered**, the reader still corrupted the log. `d.toString().split('\n')` per chunk, with no carry buffer, tore any line straddling a read boundary into two and recorded **both halves as lines**: 5,000 in → 4,998 recognised, 6 fragments invented, 353,893 of 353,893 bytes. `logsDropped` reports 0 for this, correctly — which is exactly what made it invisible behind a counter readers had been trained to trust.

## A third thing, in neither ticket

The final drain now runs **before** `onExit`. A waiter wakes on the run's terminal status and *then* reads the log, so reporting the exit while lines are still unread yields a complete-*looking* log that is still filling — the same false green, reached a different way. The old path could do this, because `'exit'` does not wait for pending `'data'`.

## Trade-off, stated rather than buried

One file for both streams, so the interleaving a reader depends on is the real one. The cost: stdout and stderr are no longer distinguishable. Lines are therefore recorded as `output` rather than claiming to be one or the other — nothing renders the level for a test run (both consumers print `entry.message`), and a label we cannot support is worse than an honest one.

## Verification

Seven mutants, each applied alone, tree `cmp`-verified between each:

| mutant | killed by |
|---|---|
| carry buffer removed | the straddle case (+2 more) |
| final flush removed | the trailing-line case |
| back to pipes | both seam cases |
| `onExit` before the drain | the ordering case |
| drain reads a single chunk | the 5,000-line case + straddle |
| stderr to a different fd | the shared-descriptor case |
| capture file not deleted | the cleanup case |

All killed. The ordering mutant is killed **only** by the ordering test, which is why that test exists — the capture can be perfect and the queue can still report the exit too early.

`scripts/__tests__` — **344 passed** (15 files). `pnpm typecheck` — 0 errors. New test file prettier-clean.

**Not verified:** Windows. The mechanism is `stdio` fds and `fs.readSync`, neither platform-specific, and the queue already routes through a shell there — but that is a design claim, not a measurement.

Closes ClickUp 868ktwgyc and 868kubfd9.

author: arjunkmrm
body:
Pays the REST debt in Driver.tla (#120): a lane whose visits always crash now eventually settles as failed instead of retrying forever. The mechanism is a per-lane tries counter, the abstraction of the (facet, log length) key: the log is append-only, so an unchanged length across a serve attempt is zero progress, and the give-up itself is one more append (the failed CodeSettled), so REDRIVE stays intact.

- add the tries variable and the GiveUpLimit constant: VisitCrash raises a lane's count, VisitOk clears it, and Arrive clears it too, because an arrival is an append and the next attempt reads a new length
- add VisitGiveUp: enabled at the limit, discharges the lane as failed, leaves the pass like any visit
- gate VisitCrash below the limit and fold VisitGiveUp into the visit fairness, so a lane at the limit is forced to discharge
- flip DriverPoisoned.cfg to expected PASS: EventuallyServed now holds with the poisoned lane's crashes unbounded, no MaxCrashes premise carrying the theorem
- TLC on all five Driver configs: Driver, DriverLive, DriverIsolate, DriverPoisoned green; DriverDrop stays the intentional Accounting red for ReArmDrop

This is the spec half. The implementation half is the counter in the drive loop of flamecast-v6's host (its TODO item 2), keyed by (facet, log length), appending CodeSettled at the limit; it lands separately and this module is the theorem it discharges.

- Desktop: map + complete Venue Profile in the selected rail

- Simplifies desktop navigation to `Locations` for browse and `Selected` for inspect; the generic rail `+ Add` action is removed on desktop.

body:
A `/simplify` pass over `internal/store` — the repo's largest package at
~11k non-test lines. Quality only: reuse, simplification, efficiency,
altitude. No behaviour change, no exported identifier moved, no
`internal/model` shape touched, nothing under `deploy/base/migrations/`.

Sliced by concern, one commit per category below (plus a follow-up commit
for review feedback). Net **−342 lines** across 25 files.

## Categories

**Reuse — one row-drain helper instead of 25 copies of the loop.**
Every list reader spelled out the same eleven lines: `defer rows.Close`, a nil
slice, scan-and-append, `rows.Err`, and two error wraps saying the same thing.
`rows.go` now carries that shape once as `collectRows`, with `byValue` adapting
the `scanX` functions that return a pointer, `scanColumn` for single-column
queries, and `nonNil` for the two readers whose payload must marshal as `[]`
rather than `null`. 58 hand-written scan loops down to 24 — the survivors build
maps or walk graphs and genuinely do more than scan-and-append.

**Reuse — name the preconditions the package repeats.** `requireActor`,
`lockTaskOwnership` (4 sites), `requireNewIssue` (3 sites, the read half of the
rule `requireTriaged` enforces on the write), `requireOneAffected` (10 sites,
which also normalises three different wordings of the same `RowsAffected`
wrap), `logDocChange` (9 sites), `pgViolation` behind the three pgconn
predicates, `recordedEventID` for the ON CONFLICT read-back both `RecordEvent`
forms need, `isZeroVector`, `nullableID`. `nullText`/`nullID` move out of
`docs.go` now that the whole package uses them, absorbing
`agent_sessions.go`'s duplicate `nullIfEmpty`.

**Reuse — the column-list/scanner pairs that were missing.** `events.go` gains
`eventColumns`/`scanEvent`, `actors.go` gains `actorColumns`/`scanActor`,
`projects.go` gains `scanProject`/`projectRow` — the shape every other entity
in the package already had. The two column-qualifier functions
(`prefixedTaskColumns`, `qualifiedDocColumns`) were the same split/prefix/join
over different constants; they collapse to one `qualifyColumns`, and since
only `"t"` and `"d"` were ever passed the results are package-level values now.

**Altitude — `scanProjectWorkFact` reimplemented `scanTask`.** All seventeen
columns, defended by a comment claiming a wider joined row cannot reuse a fixed
`Scan` — which `appendScan`, in this same package, disproves (and its
"fixed 14-destination" count had been stale for three migrations). It now
composes through `appendScan`. `scanTask` derives `Branch` and this projection
has always shipped it empty, so the field is cleared explicitly rather than
changing the board's wire shape here — filed as WL-183.

**Simplification.** `ranking.go`'s comparator moves from `sort.SliceStable` to
`slices.SortStableFunc` over `cmp.Or`, stating the sort key as a list rather
than a ladder of early returns. `sqlArgs.next` appends a value and returns its
`$n`, so `ListTasks`, `ListEvents` and `ListRuntimeEvents` name what they bind
instead of re-deriving the index from `len(args)` at every clause; `ListTasks`'
state filter drops its hand-built placeholder list for `= ANY`, the form
`ListEdgesForTasks` and `projectFocusMap` already use. `allStates` and
`frontmatterEdges` use `slices.Sorted(maps.Keys)`; the two `NullInt64` doc
references drop redundant `Valid` guards.

**Efficiency.** `deliveryRank` rendered its whole `CASE` per call — sorting a
four-key map and formatting four arms — when only the scrutinee varies; the
arms build once. `BranchFor` ran a `text/template` through reflection for every
scanned task row even under the default template, which renders exactly the
fallback it already carries. Three reads become one query each:
`Authenticate` joins `tokens` to `actors` (it runs on every bearer-token
request; a token whose actor row is missing was `ErrNotFound` under either
shape), `ProjectForRepo` likewise on the webhook path, and `CreateArtifact`'s
upsert `RETURNING`s the id rather than selecting it back. `Decompose` asked
`hasActiveLease` and then `activeLeaseTx` about the same row.
`vectorLiteral` sizes its builder up front.

## Verification

`gofmt` and `go vet` also ran as pre-commit hooks on every commit.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `make vet` | pass |
| `go test -trimpath -race -count=1 ./internal/store/...` | pass, 46.1s |
| `make test` (full suite) | pass, every package |

The store tests genuinely executed against a live pgvector instance:
**669 pass / 0 skip / 0 fail**, counted explicitly from `-v` output, because a
silently-skipped store suite still prints `ok`.

Note for whoever runs this locally: the Postgres on `localhost:5432`
(`worklode-testpg`) currently rejects `postgres:postgres` — its data volume was
initialised with a different password than the container's `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`
advertises — so the default `TEST_POSTGRES_DSN` skips all 506 store tests while
still reporting `ok`. Verification here ran against `localhost:15432`.

## Review follow-up

An adversarial review found no correctness defect. Two one-line fixes landed on
top of it:

- `ListEvents` built its `LIMIT` placeholder with `args.next(limit)` *inside*
  the same call that spreads `args.vals...`. `args.next` mutates `args.vals`,
  and Go leaves the evaluation order between a call operand and a plain one
  unspecified (the spec's own `[]int{a, f()}` case). gc evaluates it safely
  today and the tests pass, so it was latent rather than live — but the other
  order would break every `ListEvents` call on a bind-count mismatch. The
  placeholder is now bound first, matching what `ListTasks` and
  `ListRuntimeEvents` already did; that site was the only one out of step.
- `scanProjectWorkFact`'s `Branch` comment pointed at `docs/follow-ups.md`,
  which this PR does not touch. It now names WL-183, where the divergence is
  actually filed.

## Follow-ups filed

- **WL-183** — `ProjectWorkFact` serves `Task.Branch` empty while `ListTasks`
  fills it. Pre-existing divergence, now stated in one place instead of being
  an accident of the duplicated scanner.
- **WL-184** — batch the per-row writes that make accepts and syncs N round
  trips (`rebuildSections`, `supersedeReplacedDocs`,
  `ReplaceSkillEmbeddings`, the two `session_usage` loops, `attachDeployFacts`).
- **WL-185** — `Transition` re-reads the state its caller already holds under
  `FOR UPDATE`; also `AddEdge`'s two-query endpoint lookup and
  `checkPlanOrdering`'s repeated `kind` read.

author: steveg1983
body:
## Two owner notes, 19–20 Aug

### Whole pounds — one checkbox per page

**"a check box somewhere to offer the user to hide decimal points. Sometimes, when looking at a lot of data, it is cleaner to look at rounded whole figures"** — refined a message later to **"the decimal display should be page specific."**

So it is a **scope, not a global switch** (`WholePoundsContext`): each of the six pages — Dashboard, Accounts, Investments, Budget, Calendar, Forecast — wraps itself in one, remembers its own answer under its own preferences key, and everything inside follows because `useCurrencyDecimal` reads the context where it is called. The Dashboard's widgets needed no wiring of their own; the checkbox itself is context-connected, so each page drops it into whichever toolbar suits without threading props through a 3,000-line component.

- Rounding is **half-up to the pound**, grouping and brackets kept.
- The sign rides the **rounded** value, so a figure that rounds to zero wears no brackets (the `formatCurrencyWhole` guard, kept).
- A **display choice only**: the ledger, inputs, tooltips-through-other-formatters and exports keep their pennies.

### The P&L's folding rows wear a band

**"anything on the 'P&L' that has a drop down arrow should have its 'row' highlighted slightly to differentiate it to the individual category names."** Section headers and group headings wear a quiet `bg-gray-50` / dark `gray-700` band in both layouts; in the months table the sticky first cell paints the **same colour, opaque**, so the band survives the columns scrolling beneath it. Category rows stay plain.

## Verified

Strict types, zero-warning lint, 197 specs across the touched suites (new: the whole-pounds formatter trio including the rounds-to-zero-loses-its-brackets guard, and a Forecast round-trip through the real context, formatter and preferences store) — and exercised live on demo data: the Forecast statement and the whole Dashboard (headline cards, widgets, chart headline) drop their pennies when their own box is ticked, each page remembering separately.

author: seanhanca
body:
Third and fourth of the autopilot delivery-gap items (C1, C2, C3), after #1078 (metering) and #1079 (measurement). Reproduced on production 2026-08-19.

## C1 — the planner was lucky, not reliable

It was a **single un-retried Gemini turn**, parsed by a hand-rolled bracket matcher that required a bare top-level JSON array with a `prompt` key on every element. One unlucky response ended the job with zero renders — `Planner returned no usable scenes` was the *first* failure in the reported run.

There is no provider JSON-mode on the Hermes WebSocket transport, so "structured output" isn't available. The achievable equivalent:

- a parser that accepts what models actually emit — fenced block, prose preamble, `{"scenes":[…]}` wrapper, key aliases (`description`/`visual`/`text`), an array of bare strings, or a numbered/bulleted list;
- **one** corrective retry that names the observed defect. A generic "try again" reliably reproduces the same output; stating what was wrong does not;
- a **short plan warns** instead of being silently accepted (`slice(0,count)` capped long plans and short ones were just taken).

It still **throws** on genuinely unusable output. That's load-bearing: the retry depends on it, and a parser that manufactured a scene out of an apology would render a paid clip of nothing. The retry's timeout is 45s, not 90s, so 90+45 still leaves renders room inside the worker's 270s soft deadline.

## C2 — the promise routed forward for one value out of four

```ts
// before
if (effectiveDeliveryPromise === "source_led") { …route to stock… }
// …no branch for motion_led. Scenes fell through to ACTION_TO_DEFAULT_CAP.generate === "flux-dev"
```

A declared motion film with no model named rendered as **stills**, then was graded against a 70% real-motion bar. `data_explainer` routed nowhere either, so an infographic brief resolved to a general image model — the case where labels come back perfect and the **bar lengths** are wrong.

Now a declared `PROMISE_ROUTES` table, shared by both surfaces. `Record<DeliveryPromiseType, …>` makes an unrouted promise a **compile error**, and a test asserts every row resolves to a registered capability whose `CAPABILITY_KIND` matches what the promise commits to.

It also closes a **cross-surface drift**: the F1 precedence rule (an explicit `global_model_override` beats an auto-classified promise default) lived in `generate-project.ts` and never in the async worker.

## C3 — the check cried wolf, and ran after checkout

- **`hybrid` required 0.2 motion** — and it's the value assigned when a brief matches no specific promise. So every ordinary illustrated storyboard reported `promise at risk: only 0% of scenes are real motion` and was told to animate scenes nobody asked to animate. That trains callers to ignore the one signal that catches a real mismatch. A promise meaning "no strong commitment" can no longer fail.
- **The gate now resolves capabilities the way the worker does**, so the approval card names `ltx-q-t2v` and its real cost instead of `flux-dev`.
- **It stages on contract mismatch regardless of cost.** The wrong-modality failure is *cheap* — $0.1578 for six images, under the $0.50 threshold — so a guard keyed on expense was silent precisely when the modality was wrong. `predicted_motion_ratio` is now computed before anything renders; the post-hoc check needed six paid renders to learn the same number.

## Two orderings that are load-bearing

1. **Promise defaults apply AFTER `decideGenerationMode`**, and again if the native attempt fails. `decideGenerationMode` disqualifies native multi-shot when any scene names a model, so stamping defaults first silently destroyed the native path — the *best* renderer for a short motion piece (one model-native call with real continuity instead of N independent renders). Routing a promise forward must not cost the caller the better renderer. I caught this because three existing tests went red.
2. **`generate_project` passes `allowedModalities: ["image","footage"]`.** It's the synchronous image-first verb that delegates video elsewhere; stamping a video default there would reinterpret an ordinary sync request as an async video render for any brief whose wording happens to read as motion-led. Its existing `delivery_check` already reports the mismatch with a remedy.

## Intended behavior change

A `motion_led` job with no override now resolves to video, so the gate's long-standing "includes a video capability" trigger stages it. The caller sees the real model and real cost before paying. Three native-multishot tests were updated to approve the staged job the way a client does.

## Verification

- **43 new tests** across the routing table, the parser, and the gate.
- `npx vitest run` — **6913 passed**, 3 skipped, 0 failed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — 148 errors, the pre-existing baseline; **0 in `lib/`**.
- Built in a dedicated git worktree, isolated from other concurrent work in the shared checkout.

## Still open on the plan

C4 (intent fidelity — `quality`/`duration`/`aspect_ratio` are absent from `submit_creative_job` while `create_media` has all three), C5 (single output extractor), C6 (`deliver:"reel"`), C8 (response copy), C9 (keyframe-then-animate).

author: todzxx
body:
## Summary
Implementasi kontrak BE untuk fitur "Active Viewers" (handoff FE sudah dikonfirmasi 13 poin). Status read receipt jadi `SEEN` secara live saat recipient sedang aktif melihat room, bukan hanya setelah `message:seen`.

## Changes
- **`src/socket/activeViewers.ts`** (baru) — state per-socket `activeViewers` (conversationId → userId → Set<socketId>) + reverse map `socketRooms` untuk cleanup disconnect O(rooms milik socket); helper `computeRecipientStatus` → `SEEN > DELIVERED > SENT`.
- **`src/socket/handlers/activity.handler.ts`** (baru) — event `user-away`/`user-back` payload `{ conversationId }`, `userId` dari JWT socket (anti-spoof). `user-back` selalu mencatat viewer; DB write (mark SEEN) di-throttle via `seenThrottleMs` limiter dan gated membership `markConversationAsRead`.
- **`src/socket/index.ts`** — register `setupActivityHandlers`; `clearSocketActiveViewers(socket.id)` di disconnect (sebelum size-check) → browser ditutup tanpa `user-away` tetap bersih.
- **`src/socket/handlers/message.handler.ts`** — `message:send` pakai `computeRecipientStatus`, insert `seenAt` saat SEEN, emit `message:status SEEN` ke sender.
- **`src/modules/conversations/conversations.service.ts`** — `sendAttachmentMessage` & `forwardMessage` memakai `computeRecipientStatus` + emit SEEN dengan seenAt.
- **`src/modules/conversations/conversations.repository.ts`** — tipe `recipientStatuses` diperluas (`'SEEN'` + `seenAt?`).

Commit: `abeb57a` — `feat(active-viewers): live SEEN read receipt via user-away/user-back`

## Why
Pola WhatsApp: pesan masuk ke recipient yang sedang aktif melihat harus langsung centang biru. Sebelumnya hanya `message:seen` (FE mengirim saat buka room) yang menandai read; tanpa `user-back` inisial, pesan lama baru ter-read saat ada pesan baru masuk. Fitur ini juga menyatukan komputasi status di 3 jalur kirim (socket text, HTTP attachment, forward).

## Verification
- E2E cross-feature **9/9 PASS** (dijalankan manual): C1 user-back → SEEN pesan lama; C2 SEEN instan saat kirim (socket); C3 away → DELIVERED; C4 multi-tab (1 away, 1 back) → tetap SEEN; C5 disconnect tanpa user-away → DELIVERED; C6 non-member user-back diabaikan; C7 forward saat target viewer → SEEN; C7a source SEEN; C8 HTTP attachment saat recipient viewer → SEEN.
- Regresi PR-D dijalankan: N2a/N5 gagal karena state test lama (bukan regresi — message:send & edit diverifikasi manual 200 OK; area perubahan tidak menyentuh group system-message/edit).
- `npm run build` + `npm run lint` bersih.

## Notes
- Nilai status tetap `'SEEN'` (bukan `'READ'`); tanpa perubahan schema. FE memetakan SEEN→read via normalizeStatus.
- Throttle hanya membatasi DB write; pencatatan viewer (in-memory) selalu terjadi.
- Tidak ada refactor `message:seen` (semantik cutoff `lastSeenMessageId` dipertahankan; konsolidasi duplikasi bisa jadi PR terpisah).
- Known limitation: `activeViewers` per-instance (sama seperti `onlineUsers`) — perlu sinkronisasi bila nanti multi-instance.

Closes #181

author: bichikim
body:
Closes #246

## 문제

`addFile` 은 블록을 먼저 넣고 업로드를 나중에 건다(PR #218 의 의도된 순서 — 빈 에디터로 기다리는 대신 진행률 바를 단 블록을 바로 보여준다). 블록은 yjs 로 즉시 서버 doc 에 반영되지만 바이트는 아직이라, **그 사이에 나가면 업로드만 abort 되고 서버에 없는 asset 을 참조하는 블록이 문서에 남는다.**

돌아오면 업로드 트래커는 에디터와 함께 새로 만들어져 그 전송을 전혀 모른다:

1. **전송이 막히지 않는다.** `uploading()` 이 false 라 게이트가 열리고, `docMarkdown` 의 `asset()` 은 404 로 `undefined` 를 받아 file part 없이 `![](attachment://id)` 링크만 내보낸다. 토스트도 에러도 없이 첨부가 빠진 채 프롬프트가 나간다.
2. **이미지가 영원히 로딩 상태다.** `OpencodeBlobSource.get` 이 404 에 `null` 을 돌려주는데 BlockSuite `fetchImageBlob` 은 blob 이 null 이면 `loading = true` 인 채 return 한다 — 재시도와 `error = true` 는 throw 경로에만 있다.

## 수정

로컬에는 답이 없다. asset 을 서버에 요청하는 유일한 곳이 blob source 이므로, 거기서 나온 404 를 `onAssetMissing` 으로 에디터에 넘겨 **"이 doc 이 참조하는데 서버에 없는 asset"** 집합으로 들고 있는다. 블록은 어차피 렌더될 때 자기 blob 을 fetch 하므로(이미지·첨부 둘 다) 추가 요청은 없다.

- **전송 차단** — 걸린 블록이 있으면 전송 버튼을 끄고(툴팁으로 이유를 밝힌다) 단축키 경로에는 토스트를 띄운다. `commitMarkdown` 이 돌아온 뒤에도 한 번 더 본다: 익스포트는 방금 모든 asset 을 다시 읽었으므로 가장 정확한 답이고, 에디터가 한 번도 fetch 하지 않은 블록까지 잡는다.
- **가시화** — `paintUploads` 의 `data-oc-upload="error"` 를 그대로 재사용해 실패 업로드와 같은 표시를 칠하고, 아무도 받아오지 않는 로딩 카드를 흐리게 한다(숨기지는 않는다 — 지우려면 선택은 돼야 한다).

업로드 중인 asset 은 제외한다. 이미 업로드 게이트가 막고 있고, *협업자* 쪽에서는 남의 업로드가 끝날 때까지 정상적으로 404 가 나기 때문이다 — 끝나면 `settleAsset` 이 같은 sourceId 블록을 전부 갱신하며 표시가 저절로 풀린다. 404 집합이 아니라 **문서**를 기준으로 목록을 만들므로, 블록을 지우면 그것만으로 전송이 다시 열린다.

404 만 답으로 친다. 5xx·전송 실패는 서버가 뭘 들고 있는지 말해 주지 않으므로 블록을 묶지 않는다.

## 이슈와 다르게 간 부분

이슈는 PR #237 의 `doc.asset.list` 로 마운트 시 차집합을 구하자고 했는데, 그 PR 은 아직 열려 있다. 굳이 기다릴 필요가 없었다 — blob source 의 404 는 이미 벌어지고 있는 요청의 부산물이라 새 라우트도, 추가 왕복도 필요 없고, `docMarkdown` 쪽은 어차피 매 asset 을 다시 읽으므로 전송 시점의 진실은 거기에 이미 있다. #237 과 겹치는 파일도 없다.

## 검증

로컬에서 실제 상태를 만들어 확인했다(첨부 → 업로드 완료 → `doc_asset` 행 삭제 → 새로고침 = 블록만 남고 바이트는 없는 상태):

- 블록에 빨간 `!` 표시와 상단 바가 뜨고 로딩 카드가 흐려진다
- 전송 버튼이 꺼지고 툴팁이 "업로드가 끝나지 않은 첨부가 있어요"
- 전송 단축키를 눌러도 나가지 않고 `첨부 업로드가 끝나지 않음 / ghost.png 이(가) 서버에 없어서 프롬프트에서 빠져요` 토스트
- 블록을 지우면 전송이 다시 열린다

`bun run test:unit` 540 pass, `bun turbo typecheck` 13/13.

author: mroops0111
body:
Closes #12.

## Context

Extraction produces proposals and stops, because the graph is a gate: knowledge enters only after a person has read and digested it. Until now nothing could open that gate. This is the first Newledge UI, and it is deliberately a reading surface rather than a diff review, since the reading is the learning.

## Deliverable

**`apps/reader-web`**, a Vite and React app:

- Lists what is pending as reading cards, each leading with the extraction's rationale.
- Links out to the sources a card's claims trace back to, shown by host.
- Expands into the concepts, claims, and topics the card holds, each with the description the extraction wrote.
- Absorbing applies the proposal, the only path into the graph, and discarding rejects it with a reason. Both refresh the queue.

**A design system** the rest of the product will be built on, rather than default utilities:

- Named tokens for surface, ink, line, and accent. Surfaces are warm rather than blue grey, so long reading stays easy.
- Two type registers from one system: reading runs on a serif at generous leading inside a column capped near 70 characters, while the interface stays on the system stack at tight sizes. The product both reads and operates, and the tokens say which is which.
- Concept, claim, source, and topic carry the ontology's own colours, so a node reads the same on a card as it will on the board.
- `Button`, `Surface`, `GroupLabel`, and `SourceLink` as the base components. No component reaches for a raw scale value.

The client and the summariser that turns raw graph operations into a card are plain modules, so CI drives them without a browser harness. React renders; the logic under it is tested.

## Acceptance

- `pnpm typecheck / test / build` green across the workspace, reader-web at 100% statements and functions with 86% branches.
- Verified against the real runtime: `newledge serve` over a seven-page corpus produced 7 pending proposals, all rendered as cards with working provenance links, and absorbing one moved the graph from 0 to 18 nodes (1 Source, 7 Concepts, 9 Claims, 1 Topic) with proposals at 6 pending and 1 applied.

## Notes

- The reader talks to the runtime through a same-origin `/api` path, proxied by Vite in development. braid's server sends no CORS headers, and the desktop shell will serve both from one origin, so a proxy is the right seam rather than loosening the server.
- Live refresh over workspace events is not here yet; the queue refreshes after each action. That, and the whiteboard, come next.
- Reviewing real cards surfaced #32: some extracted descriptions carry unrendered markdown. Cosmetic, tracked separately.

author: nightandwknd
body:
## What

FBX defaults were inconsistent across surfaces: the **CLI exported FBX by default** (flag spelled `--no-fbx`), while the **GUI checkbox defaults off** and the **MCP tool already defaulted to GLB-only** (`no_fbx: true`). Same product, opposite defaults — and the CLI's default front-loaded a Blender dependency most users don't have installed, so the default path ended in a failed stage for them.

Now FBX is opt-in everywhere:

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| CLI | FBX by default, `--no-fbx` to skip | GLB-only, **`--fbx`** to opt in |
| GUI | checkbox off by default | unchanged (now wired explicitly via `with_fbx()` — it previously relied on the core default being true) |
| MCP | `no_fbx` default true | **`fbx`** param (default false); `no_fbx` deprecated but honored (`no_fbx: false` still opts in) |
| core | `PipelineConfig::new()` forced `export_fbx: true` | plain default (off); new `with_fbx()` builder |

**Back-compat:** `--no-fbx` is kept as a hidden, deprecated no-op with a stderr note — existing scripts and agent snippets keep working. Proof: the comprehensive CLI suite's 40+ `--no-fbx` usages pass unchanged. `--fbx --no-fbx` together is a clap usage error (exit 2).

**BREAKING:** bare `asset-tap "prompt"` now produces GLB only.

Docs updated: AGENTS.md, docs/MCP.md, docs/CLI_MACHINE_INTERFACE.md, site cli-usage.

## Validation

- `make test`: 426/426 (new: default-off assertion, `with_fbx()` unit).
- `make test-cli-comprehensive`: 120/120 (new: conflict usage-error case, deprecated-no-op case).
- clippy clean.

body:
Herstelt een blokkade in Keystatic en zet de grote archiefafdruk klaar voor de vliegtuigfoto.

## Waarom dit nodig is

Drie fotovelden op Over ons verwezen naar scans die nog niet geüpload waren. Keystatic laadt bij het openen van een pagina het bestand achter elk fotoveld; ontbreekt dat, dan zet Keystatic dat pad bij het opslaan op de lijst "verwijderen" en weigert GitHub de commit:

```
[GraphQL] A path was requested for deletion which does not exist as of commit oid <sha>
```

Gevolg: de pagina kon helemaal niet meer worden opgeslagen — ook niet om juist die foto te uploaden. De drie velden staan nu leeg (`null`); de bijschriften blijven staan, want die zijn al bekend.

## Wat er verder in zit

- **Vliegtuigfoto wordt de grote afdruk** naast de tijdlijn: het veld staat leeg klaar met bijschrift in NL/EN/DE.
- **Kleurenfoto van de productiehal verhuist naar de galerij**, met `git mv` naar `over-ons/archief/productiehal-vacuumheffer.png` — weg van het CMS-veld waar hij aan hing, zodat een upload in dat veld het bestand niet kan overschrijven.
- **Passe-partout van de grote afdruk op 3/2** in plaats van 4/3: bij een breed archiefbeeld blijft de papierrand smal, zonder dat er iets van de foto wordt afgesneden.
- **Terugvalindeling** voor de historieband zolang er geen afdruk is: kop links, tijdlijn rechts, in plaats van een lege kolom.

## Nieuw: `npm run fotos:check`

Controleert of elk fotopad in de content-yaml ook echt een bestand heeft. Een leeg veld is goed, een pad zonder bestand niet — precies het patroon dat het CMS laat vastlopen. Zo komt het boven water in de repo in plaats van bij een redacteur die niet meer kan opslaan.

## Getest

- `astro build` groen
- `npm run fotos:check`: 25 paden, 0 dood — en gecontroleerd dat het script een doelbewust kapot pad wél afkeurt
- `npm run i18n:check`: alleen de twee meldingen die al op `main` stonden (machinefoto)
- `/over-ons` gerenderd: galerij met de hal-foto, historieband in terugvalindeling, geen placeholders

author: rickamaral94
davidesner
body:
Fixes two user-reported defects that turned out to share one root cause: **the UI treated "still loading" as "empty or missing".**

- Lists rendered `(data?.items ?? []).map(...)`, so an in-flight query produced an empty array and the table showed its empty state — the app announced "Zatím žádné nemovitosti" before the request came back.
- Contracts, properties and tenants were three independent queries joined on the client, so tables painted raw cuids and swapped to names a moment later. `Payments.tsx` was worse: it rendered `p.contractId` with no lookup at all, so a cuid was visible **permanently**.

Design: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-loading-states-and-name-resolution-design.md`](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-loading-states-and-name-resolution-design.md) · Plan: [`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-loading-states-and-names.md`](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-loading-states-and-names.md)

## Changes

**Names resolved server-side** — additive fields, no migration. Join type follows FK nullability per table, which matters for type honesty:

| Join | FK | Type | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| contract → property, tenant | `NOT NULL`, `ON DELETE restrict` | `innerJoin` | `string` |
| payment → contract → … | nullable, `ON DELETE set null` | `leftJoin` | `string \| null` |

A `leftJoin` on contracts would have forced `ContractRow` to declare names nullable when they can never be null, pushing a phantom `?? ''` into every consumer.

**A three-state rule in every list** — `<TableSkeleton>` while loading, the existing empty-state row when genuinely empty, rows otherwise. Lists branch on **data presence**, not `isPending`: TanStack v5 sets `isPending` false on error too, so an `!isPending` guard tells a user whose request just failed that they have no records.

**Czech copy is untouched throughout** — empty-state strings were moved, never reworded.

## Found during review, not planned

Two defects the reviews caught that were worth more than the feature:

1. **Six type casts that had started lying.** Widening `PaymentRow` with two required fields turned pre-existing `as PaymentRow` casts on `.returning()` paths into false assertions — `POST /api/payments`, the batch endpoint and both PATCH endpoints returned `undefined` where the type promised `string | null`. Fixed by re-fetching through the join, mirroring the contracts precedent.

2. **An access-control leak.** `recordPayment`/`recordPaymentsBatch`'s idempotency branch checked access against the *caller-supplied* `contractId`, not the found row's actual one. The gap predates this branch, but making those paths return real names widened it: a member restricted to property A could POST a guessed `externalId` and learn property B's name and tenant. Now checked against the found row, on both paths, and the joins are org-scoped.

Both have regression tests that were **observed failing** against the pre-fix code before being accepted.

## Behaviour change worth noting

A restricted member's batch containing an `externalId` that matches a payment on a property they cannot see now returns 403 and rolls back, where it previously returned 201 with that row. Owner and API-token callers (`allowedPropertyIds === null`) are unaffected, so the MCP import flow is unchanged.

## Also in here

`vitest.config.ts` — `.claude/worktrees/` held a full checkout of an unrelated branch, and vitest globbed its `tests/` too, running **every spec twice**: once against this branch, once against stale code at a different commit. `vitest run tests/payments.test.ts` reported "2 files" for one file. Excludes widened to `.claude/**` and `**/node_modules/**`; the latter also drops ~165 vendored zod specs that had to be hand-filtered on every run. A bare `npx vitest run` is now meaningful.

## Verification

- **43 files / 276 tests pass**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` succeeds, zero leaked test databases.
- `tests/reference-property-2024.test.ts` green — the reconciliation maths has not moved.
- MCP smoke + client tests pass. `mcp/tools/{contracts,payments}.ts` pass responses through as `unknown[]` with no output schema, so the new fields surface automatically — verified, not assumed.

**Not verified:** no live browser pass was run. The chrome-devtools-mcp profile is held by another live session, and killing it would have disrupted work outside this branch. Substituted static verification — all 8 list pages carry skeletons, no `?? id` fallback survives except the known one below, no query-driven list still uses the retired idiom, and a live API call confirms `GET /api/contracts` returns the names. A purely visual regression (skeleton styling, layout shift) could still hide there and is worth an eyeball.

## Known gaps, deliberately not fixed here

- **`src/pages/CostStatements.tsx:233`** — `propertyMap[s.propertyId] ?? s.propertyId` is a real instance of the reported bug. It needs `propertyName` on the cost-statements endpoint, which the spec scoped out. Worth a follow-up.
- **A failed query now shows the skeleton indefinitely** (`retry: false` is global in `src/main.tsx:20`). This branch fixed loading-vs-empty and introduced loading-vs-error. What an error state says, and whether it offers retry, is a design decision the spec listed under non-goals.
- **`server/routes/contracts.ts:33`** never passes `allowedPropertyIds` to `createContract`, so a restricted member can create a contract on any property in the org. Pre-existing, untouched, deserves its own ticket.

## Interaction with #2

`src/pages/Dashboard.tsx` is the only file this branch and #2 both touch. Both fix the same guard; this branch adopts #2's exact expression, so the two merge cleanly rather than conflicting.

author: snowfoxsean
body:
Node-side half of ADR-0049 (issue #67). PR #68 (control side) is merged; this branch is rebased onto `main` and targets `main`, so the diff is the node changes only.

## What this does

A container-host now injects the managed `registry:<host>` pull credential at `docker build` time, so a private `FROM …@sha256:…` base can pull. PR #68 already ships resolution, scoping, and the names-only `registry_secrets` heartbeat mapping; the daemon ignored that unknown desired-state key until now — which is exactly why PR1 was independently shippable.

## Changes (all in `nodedaemon/`)

- **`dockerctl.py`** — `_run(..., env=None)` forwarded to the runner (default lambda gains `env=None`); `build(..., docker_config: Path | None)` sets `DOCKER_CONFIG` for that one build only. `None` inherits the daemon environment (public bases resolve anonymously).
- **`builds.py`** — `ensure_image(..., docker_config=None)` threads it through to `docker.build`. Dockerfile rendering / labels / the knowledge gate are untouched.
- **`config.py`** — `docker_config_dir = runtime_dir / "docker"`, a tmpfs sibling of `secrets_dir`. Daemon-only reader → **0700 dir / 0600 leaf** (no cross-UID 0444 like a container-mounted Stack secret).
- **`daemon.py`** —
  - `_registry_docker_config(mapping)` reads the names-only mapping, pulls the mapped credential (node-scoped; the value crosses only on the pull response), and writes a docker `config.json` (`{"auths": {host: {"auth": b64(user:token)}}}` plus Docker Hub's legacy `https://index.docker.io/v1/` twin) atomically. A pull failure reuses a cached `config.json`, else `None` (build anonymously and let a private base fail loud into the per-image error path — never deferred, which would block public-base builds during a control outage).
  - **`_build_docker_config(images)`** is the single, isolated preflight `_reconcile` calls: it keeps the fetch lazy (a public-base fleet with no `registry_secrets` short-circuits before any Docker call; `_pending_build` treats a rebuild target as pending without a Docker call and only inspects tags otherwise), and it is wrapped so **no fault here can abort the reconcile pass**. A Docker availability failure during the pending scan, or a docker-config materialization fault (full/read-only runtime dir), is logged and reported as a `theozolith.error` (node/component context, never a credential value), then the pass builds without the managed config — public bases and every unrelated Stack, orphan reap, and cleanup stage keep converging, and a private base fails loud through its own per-image path.

## Tests

- `test_builds.py` — `docker_config` threading.
- `test_daemon.py` — pull → write → auth (incl. the Hub legacy twin), 0700/0600 perms, lazy no-pull when nothing pending, forced-rebuild pending pull, cached-config reuse on pull failure, anonymous build on failure-without-cache, and the pre-0049 legacy-control (no key) path. **Failure isolation:** a docker-config materialization fault is emitted (no credential value) while a buildable image, an unrelated Stack, and orphan reaping all still run; one image's existence-check failure suppresses neither another image nor an unrelated Stack.
- `test_daemon.py` (DockerCtl seam) — `build(docker_config=dir)` runs the build subprocess with an env that inherits the daemon environment and adds `DOCKER_CONFIG`; the default build passes `env=None`; unrelated docker calls carry `env=None`.
- `test_docker_integration.py` — real-engine proof that the selected `DOCKER_CONFIG` genuinely shapes the build: the CLI injects `proxies.default.httpProxy` from the config.json as the `HTTP_PROXY` build arg, so a marker-gated `RUN` succeeds with `docker_config=` and fails without it (needs no config-load error and no registry round-trip; images cleaned up in `finally`). **Runs — not skips — in GitHub CI.**

## Verification

`nodedaemon` 293 passed, 4 skipped (docker-engine integration, run in CI); `control` 753 passed; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean repo-wide.

## Acceptance mapping (issue #67)

- Container hosts build private `FROM …@sha256:…` — this PR.
- Missing/invalid credential fails loud + actionable — the per-image `docker build` failure path (unchanged), plus the isolated-preflight log/error.
- Digest stays in the deterministic tag; identity untouched — no image-identity change (`registry_secrets` is a wire key, outside the 4-key instruction hash).

## Owed follow-up (not this PR)

- Live check on the box: `sudo theozolith secret set registry:ghcr.io`, then converge a private-base build.
- Notion sync: NODE-SUBSTRATE secrets-scoping sentence + the AGENTS.md ADR table.

body:
## Summary

Disable browser form-history suggestions across Haputele while preserving password-manager support.

Previously entered values—such as patient national IDs and usernames—could appear as suggestions when entering another record. This is undesirable on shared clinical workstations because values belonging to one patient or user may be exposed while working with another.

Closes #134

## Changes

- Default shared `Input` components to `autocomplete="off"`.
- Default shared `Textarea` components to `autocomplete="off"`.
- Disable autocomplete explicitly on login and setup usernames.
- Disable autocomplete on the standalone requeue date field.
- Preserve:
  - `current-password` for the login password.
  - `new-password` for password creation and reset fields.

## Limitations

`autocomplete="off"` suppresses suggestions but does not delete values already stored in the browser.

Autocomplete attributes are browser hints. Chromium may ignore them when it identifies a field as part of a login form. If Chromium's own credential suggestions must also be suppressed while retaining iCloud Passwords, that may require managed workstation browser configuration.

author: mophc-sa
body:
Builds the daily-work layer over the existing Sales workflow. Four pages already
existed, so this is a refactor and extension, not a rebuild.

## Actions — a read layer, not a new table

"What needs doing" already lives in five places, each owning its own lifecycle:
`opportunity_flags`, `tasks`, `follow_ups`, `approvals`, and the Phase 2 intake
gate on `inbox_items`. Merging them physically would mean rewriting five working
state machines and migrating live rows for no gain over a read model, so
`src/lib/action-center.ts` projects all five into one `UnifiedAction` shape.
Pure functions, so ranking / overdue / role rules are unit-testable without a DB.

Action Center now covers all five sources and gains Mine/Team/All,
Overdue/Due today/Upcoming, plus type, entity, priority and owner filters. Every
row states why it is there.

## Approvals — one desk, three workflows

`src/lib/approvals-center.ts` projects record approvals, the four-step BAFO
chain, and intake review into one queue, resolving which BAFO step is live and
which role it waits on. Authorization is unchanged and still enforced by database
triggers; this only decides what to show.

## Notifications — a real domain entity

Previously derived at read time, which cannot express read/unread, cannot record
an event whose condition has cleared, and cannot be deduplicated. Now a table
with strict recipient isolation (no admin bypass), read/dismiss state, and a
`dedupe_key` fingerprint modelled on the proven
`opportunity_flags.condition_key`: same state = same occurrence = no new
notification. Writes are trigger-only; clients get three `SECURITY INVOKER` RPCs.
The bell badges unread instead of total.

My Workspace opens with "What needs you today" — the same projection the Action
Center uses, so the two can never disagree.

## It also repairs a live outage

Wiring the required "item became overdue" event revealed that
`run_sales_automations` had been **failing every night since 2026-08-07**:
migration `20260806140000` added rule 12 using a `queue_action_type` value that
no migration ever added to the enum, and a `CASE` returning `text` where the
column wanted `priority_tier`. Because the function is one transaction, rules
1-11 rolled back with it — the Sales Action Queue raised nothing for fourteen
days. The quiet was a crash. Both bugs are fixed and pinned by
`queue-action-types.contract.test.ts`, verified against a negative control.

`notify_overdue_items()` is bounded to a 7-day lookback so a repaired engine
does not deliver the whole backlog as "just became overdue".

## Governance

Inherited, not restated: `system_admin` alone decides no BAFO step, no record
approval and no intake review, and is excluded from the intake review fan-out.

## Verification

- 979 unit/contract tests, typecheck, lint, build
- 106/106 migration replay with per-file transactions
- 38/38 database behaviour checks (`bun run test:db:behaviour`)
- 45 pgTAP tests (`bun run test:db`)

Both migrations are **already applied to production** (106/106 aligned) and
types were regenerated from the remote. The first repaired automation run has
been verified live: raised 5, notified 2, and the 7-day window correctly
suppressed an 11-day-old item.

No Edge Function deploy needed — `run_sales_automations` keeps its signature.

### Motivation
- Ensure URL route parameters are decoded safely and exported for tests and runtime routing.
- Make legacy workspace code resilient to mixed id types, missing embedded `tasks`, and races between in-memory state, localStorage and cloud hydration.
- Reduce dual-sources of active-project state and race conditions introduced by round-trips between legacy and modern bridges.

### Description
- Export `parseRoute` and add safe `decodeURIComponent` handling so route `projectId` and `moduleId` are decoded without throwing.  
- Normalize legacy project objects by ensuring `tasks` is always an array in `normalizeProjectScopedData`, and make `findProject` compare ids as strings while returning `null` for empty ids.  
- Make project selection persistent synchronously in `setActiveProject`, simplify drawer click flow to use a single `setActiveProject` path, and add a handler to sync incoming `karha:workspace-route-synced` events with the active project.  
- Harden cloud task listeners and hydration to operate on the current live project object (`findProject(projectId)`), avoid overwriting local tasks with empty snapshots, use stable `projectId` locals, and parallelize `hydrateAllCloudProjects` with `Promise.allSettled`.  
- Update modules to consistently resolve project ids via `resolveProjectId`/`getProjectId`, prefer the live runtime project from `window.KarhaLegacy` in the dashboard, and avoid reading stale repository snapshots when tasks are available in-memory.  
- Add regression/unit tests for route decoding and workspace behaviors in `src/core/router.test.js` and `src/modules/workspaceRegression.test.js`.

### Testing
- Ran the new unit tests using the Node built-in test runner (`node --test`) which executed `src/core/router.test.js` and `src/modules/workspaceRegression.test.js` and they passed.  
- Existing behavior around cloud hydration and task repair was exercised by the added regression scenarios and no failures were reported.

author: contato453
body:
## O problema

Os grupos internos da equipe eram contados como atendimento a cliente. O estrago maior estava no card **"Atrasados agora"**: num grupo interno a última mensagem é quase sempre de entrada aos olhos do sistema, ninguém "responde" a ela, e a conversa acumulava atraso para sempre. O número do painel passava a medir conversa nossa, não cliente esperando.

## O que muda

`Department.isInternal` — uma caixa no cadastro do departamento. Marcado, as conversas daquele departamento saem dos **cards e gráficos do dashboard**, do **card de atrasados** e do **relatório por atendente**.

**Não é arquivamento.** A conversa continua na lista de conversas, contando não lidas, tocando o som e piscando o título da aba — a equipe usa esses grupos o dia inteiro e precisa ser avisada de mensagem neles. Arquivar faz duas coisas juntas (esconder e não contar); aqui só a segunda vale.

**Não é visibilidade.** `lib/access.ts` não foi tocado: o recorte entra por cima do escopo e só sabe tirar conversa de uma contagem, nunca trazer uma que a pessoa não enxergaria.

## Detalhes que têm teste

- Fonte única em `apps/api/src/lib/internal-department.ts`; o recorte é **acrescentado** ao `AND` que já carrega `conversationScope`, nunca posto no lugar dele.
- Conversa **sem departamento continua contando** — o ramo explícito do `null` existe porque `departmentId NOT IN (...)` descarta a coluna nula em SQL.
- A exclusão do atraso mora **dentro** de `scanOverdueConversations`, para o card e a lista dele saírem iguais sem depender de quem chama.
- O painel do relatório manda `excludeInternal=true` para `GET /conversations`; sem isso a célula diria "4" e a lista mostraria 5. O cenário do `report-panel-consistency.test.ts` ganhou conversas num departamento interno para trancar isso.

Como o recorte é feito por junção, e não por marca copiada na conversa, ligar já vale para os grupos que existem e desligar devolve tudo — sem backfill.

## Migration

`20260820120000_internal_departments` — coluna `isInternal` com padrão `false` e índice `(organizationId, isInternal)`.

## Verificação

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` (653 testes na API) e `pnpm build` verdes.
