author: joepio
body:
Opening a canvas blocked the main thread for **over four seconds** on a 6 KB drawing. All of it was one `getLoroHistory()` call.

Measured on a canvas with 6374 ops:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| First open | 4256 ms | **55 ms** |
| Second open | 4239 ms | **52 ms** |
| Longest blocking task | 4651 ms | 69 ms |
| Checkouts on open | 6374 | 0 |

## The quadratic walk

`getLoroHistory()` walked every op counter in the oplog and materialized each one — a `checkout()` plus a whole-document `toJSON()` plus a `JSON.stringify` — then bucketed by change message and overwrote the bucket each time. Only the last step per bucket survived, so this drawing did **6374 materializations to produce 10 versions** and discarded 6363. A canvas stores one op per stroke point, so the cost scaled with total ink ever drawn.

Bucket winners are now resolved from change metadata first, and only those get materialized: 11 checkouts instead of 6374.

## Why skipping ops needed a dedup fix

`contentSignature` stringified raw `toJSON()` output, whose map key order depends on how the doc reached a version — jumping straight to one yields `{color, path, width}` where replaying every op yields `{width, path, color}`. Identical states compared unequal, so which versions collapsed depended on walking every op. Nested keys are now sorted.

Without this, skipping ops silently changes the output (11 versions instead of 10).

## Opening no longer builds history at all

The mount path wanted one boolean — whether the undo control should be enabled — and paid for the whole walk to get it. `Resource.hasPriorLoroVersions()` answers it from change metadata with no time-travel.

Reconstruction moved to `ensureUndoStack`, on first contact with the undo control: **hovering** it, so the press that follows lands on a stack already built, with press and Ctrl+Z as fallbacks for touch and keyboard.

Trade-off worth knowing: the probe counts version buckets, while `bootstrapUndoSteps` also discards versions matching the current drawing. A canvas whose every prior version equals what's on screen shows an enabled control that greys itself out on first contact. That's the price of not doing the work up front.

## The result was never cached

It re-ran on every open, not once per device. `CanvasHistoryState` now records the attempt, including when it finds nothing — otherwise "found nothing" is indistinguishable from "never ran". Entries written before the flag read as un-bootstrapped, and their non-empty undo stack already short-circuits the guard.

## Verification

- **lib**: 286 tests (+6 from this branch), lint + typecheck clean
- **data-browser**: 602 tests, lint exits 0 with an identical Canvas warning count to develop, typecheck byte-identical to the develop baseline (16 pre-existing errors in test files)
- **e2e**: all 7 canvas specs pass, including *"undo works right after a cold reload of a canvas with history"* — the exact path made lazy
- Each regression test was confirmed to fail without its fix: the op-count test reports `2410 checkouts vs ≤5`, and the key-order test yields `[0,1,1]` instead of `[0,1]` if canonicalization is removed

Verified end-to-end in the running app: open with nothing materialized, hover builds 6 steps in 40 ms, press undoes correctly, and Ctrl+Z without hovering materializes on the keypress.

## Note

While measuring I noticed this 6 KB doc carries **6374 ops across 26 peers**, with nine changes of exactly 546 ops each that look like the same snapshot re-imported per peer. That op amplification is a separate issue — it no longer costs seconds on open, but it's inflating the oplog.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core `Resource` Loro history materialization and canvas undo persistence; behavior changes (lazy bootstrap, possible briefly enabled undo that disables on first use) but is covered by new regression tests and e2e.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Canvas open no longer walks and materializes the full Loro oplog.** On first visit, mount only runs a cheap `hasPriorLoroVersions()` probe (after WASM loads) to decide if undo should look enabled; the expensive `getLoroHistory()` → `bootstrapUndoSteps()` path moved to **`ensureUndoStack`**, triggered on undo-button **hover**, press/scrub, or **Ctrl+Z**, with a persisted **`bootstrapped`** flag so empty results are not recomputed every open.
> 
> **`getLoroHistory()` is cheaper and dedup is stable.** It resolves per-commit bucket winners from oplog metadata first, then **`checkout`/`toJSON` only those steps** (not every stroke-point op). **`contentSignature`** now canonicalizes nested object key order so identical states dedupe regardless of checkout path.
> 
> **Persistence:** `saveCanvasHistory` / `loadCanvasHistory` store **`bootstrapped`**; legacy entries without the flag stay un-bootstrapped. **`ensureUndoStack`** dedupes in-flight work, merges Loro steps with any local undo snapshots from drawing during bootstrap, and records bootstrap even when no steps are found.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e39154ca0af115dffb82f49902d562d86a3080bb. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: frikkern
body:
`webhook-fanout-watch.sh mutation matrix` failed on an unrelated PR with `grep: write error: Broken pipe` and a bogus `FAIL the detector missed a planted continue-on-error`, then passed on a plain re-run. Chasing it found **two** defects in the same predicate, and the second one is not a flake.

## 1. The reported flake: SIGPIPE + pipefail

`uncommented FILE | grep -q PAT`. `grep -q` exits at its **first match** and closes the pipe; the stripping `grep -v` still has bytes to write, takes SIGPIPE (141) or EPIPE (2), and `set -o pipefail` (line 14) reports *that* over grep's success. A successful match is read by the caller as a miss.

Confirmed rather than assumed — the reader matched and the pipeline still failed:

```
128KB file -> pipeline rc=141 PIPESTATUS=141 0   (141=SIGPIPE, 0=reader matched)
```

Forced to 100% by giving the producer any pending write when the reader exits:

```
tiny output + 0.2s gap between writes -> arm reported detector-blind: 20 / 20
input ~ 32032 bytes -> arm reported 'detector blind': 42 / 50
input ~128032 bytes -> arm reported 'detector blind': 50 / 50
```

On a quiet macOS host the real file has ~7 kB of post-match output and never lost the race (0/600, even under 16 CPU hogs) — the margin is scheduling, which is why it only showed up on a loaded runner.

This is **honest-gates D37** (`scripts/cloud-path-escape-check.test.sh:39`). D37 exempts a match made straight against a FILE, and that exemption is how this file kept the bug: `uncommented "$f" | grep -q` *looks* like a file match but is a pipeline whose producer is exactly the writer D37 says must not exist.

## 2. The one that was not flaky at all

The flake direction above was the loud one. The same predicate backs two `there is no continue-on-error here` assertions, where being blinded prints **ok**.

`scripts/webhook-fanout-watch.sh` carries a literal **NUL byte** — the `^@` separator inside the `jq group_by` near its meter. grep classifies the file as binary, so `uncommented "$WATCH"` returned the 38-byte string `Binary file … matches` instead of ~6.4 kB of stripped text. That assertion was searching 38 bytes that can never contain the pattern.

On `origin/main`, with `continue-on-error: true` planted in the script (3 occurrences present):

```
-- ORIGINAL harness (origin/main) --
  ok   no continue-on-error in the script (only the written-down reason it is refused)
   exit = 0
-- FIXED harness --
  FAIL continue-on-error used as a mechanism in the script
   exit = 1
```

A green check over a script with three `continue-on-error` lines in it. `-a` fixes it.

## The fix

- Materialise the stripped text, then match it with a here-string. No reader closes early, and the status read is grep's own, not a pipeline's.
- `grep -a` in both positions, so a NUL cannot silently empty the input.

## Every new arm shown able to fail

| Regression applied | Arm that fires |
|---|---|
| drop `-a` from `uncommented()` | `the script-side predicate missed a planted continue-on-error — … is a false green` |
| restore the `producer \| grep -q` pipeline | `the detector lost a planted continue-on-error to a SIGPIPE race (pipefail read the producer's 141 as 'no match')` |
| rebuild the script fixture with `awk` | `the fixture lost $WATCH's NUL bytes — it no longer tests the condition that blinded this check` |
| plant `continue-on-error` in `shell-harnesses.yml` | `shell-harnesses.yml carries a continue-on-error (a red would launder to a green job)` |
| plant `continue-on-error` in `webhook-fanout-watch.sh` | `continue-on-error used as a mechanism in the script` |

The third row is why the fixture is built with `cat` and not `awk`: **awk silently drops the NUL**, and a fixture without the NUL is a fixture without the property that blinds the real check — the arm would have passed while the real file stayed unreadable.

Plant removed, clean tree: `49 passed, 0 failed`, exit 0. 0 failures in 60 runs under 12 CPU hogs. `shellcheck -S warning` clean. Test-only change; no production script touched.

author: stipsan
body: Switches both React Compiler passes to [`oxc-transform-react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/oxc-transform-react), the native Rust port — one native pass for React Compiler + TypeScript/JSX, no babel in the pipeline. ## Changes - **tsdown build**: [`@sanity/tsdown-config@0.26.0`](https://github.com/sanity-io/pkg-utils/releases/tag/%40sanity%2Ftsdown-config%400.26.0) with `reactCompiler: {target: '19', transform: 'oxc'}` in `packages/react-rx/tsdown.config.ts` - **vitest `react-compiler` project**: [`@vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.0`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react/README.md#rust-react-compiler)'s new oxc-backed `compiler` option (`react({compiler: {target: '19'}})`) replaces the `reactCompilerPreset` + `@rolldown/plugin-babel` setup - **Removed**: `babel-plugin-react-compiler` (devDependency + workspace catalog entry), and `@rolldown/plugin-babel` + `@babel/core`, which only existed to run it - Patch changeset for `react-rx` (published output rebuilt on the new pipeline, functionally unchanged) - pnpm auto-pinned `@vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.0` into `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` (released today, younger than the age gate) ## Before/after build times `pnpm build` wall clock (hyperfine, 2 warmups + 10 runs, Node 22.22.2): | | Mean ± σ | Range | | --- | --- | --- | | babel | 1.730 s ± 0.039 s | 1.672 s … 1.783 s | | oxc | **1.254 s ± 0.034 s** | 1.185 s … 1.307 s | tsdown's own "Build complete" timer — the bundle step where the compiler actually runs (5 samples each): | | Samples | Mean | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | babel | 530, 496, 515, 538, 523 ms | ~520 ms | | | oxc | 156, 150, 150, 140, 145 ms | **~148 ms** | **3.5x faster** | `pnpm test` is flat overall (12.12 s → 12.09 s; jsdom + test execution dominate), but vitest's transform phase dropped from 1.81 s to ~0.7 s. ## Output parity `dist/index.js` built with babel vs oxc differs only in the position of one compiler-generated no-op helper (`function _temp$1() {}` hoisted 13 lines earlier); byte-identical otherwise, same 12.58 kB, both import `c` from `react/compiler-runtime`. A temporary memoization probe (rendering a component twice and comparing callback identity) confirmed the compiler is applied in the `react-compiler` vitest project and not in `default`, exactly like the babel preset: ``` [probe] project=default memoized=false [probe] project=react-compiler memoized=true ``` ## Verification - `pnpm build`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm knip`, `pnpm test` (32 files, 278 passed + 4 expected fail — identical to `current`) all green - `tsc -p packages/react-rx/tsconfig.json` clean (the `satisfies Promise` annotation still holds) - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes - `pnpm peers check` reports the same pre-existing `@emnapi/*` transitive warning as `current` (verified present in the base lockfile) ## Notes - `babel-plugin-react-compiler@1.0.0` still appears in `pnpm-lock.yaml` as a *resolved optional peer* of `@sanity/tsdown-config`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, and `next` — lockfile inertia from the previous direct dependency. No manifest references it; pnpm keeps previously-resolved optional peers through `install`/`dedupe`/`update`, and purging it requires a full lockfile regen (~1,500 lines of unrelated version churn). It will drop out on the next natural lockfile regeneration. `@babel/core`/`@rolldown/plugin-babel` remain transitive dependencies of `@sanity/tsdown-config` itself, which ships the default babel path. - Full benchmark methodology and raw numbers: react_compiler_oxc_build_benchmarks.md

## Summary

Task C of the 4-task "Shared KIS account risk ledger" plan (Tasks A/B
merged: PR #99, PR #100). Implements `SharedKisAccountLedger implements
AccountStateProvider` and wires it into `TradingLoop`'s new 7-arg
constructor and `PaperTradingApp`'s `kis-paper` mode.

- `SharedKisAccountLedger` composes `AccountLedgerLock` + `AccountLedgerStore`
  (both merged, untouched here) into the three `AccountStateProvider`
  methods: `reserveForIntent` (pessimistic reserve, monotonic on repeat,
  honors a tripped reconciliation alarm and a non-positive effective
  price), `confirmReservation` (shrinks to the real approved notional),
  `releaseReservation` (removes entirely) — both tolerate a missing
  reservation as a safe no-op (the reachable case where `reserveForIntent`
  itself skipped creating one).
- `bootstrapOrLoad(ledgerPath, venue, accountId, realBalance)` — the
  one-time bootstrap-from-real-balance-or-reuse-existing step, called
  once in `forKisPaper()` right after `KisPreflight.run(adapter)`
  succeeds, per the governing design's human-approved decision.
- New `PaperTradingApp.resolveAccountLedgerPath(venue, accountId)` —
  `var/live/{venue}-{accountId}-account_ledger.json`, keyed by account
  (not symbol) since the ledger is meant to be shared across every
  `kis-paper` process trading different symbols against the same account.
- New 9-arg `PaperTradingApp` constructor overload (existing 8-arg
  `PriceFeed`-accepting constructor **untouched**, zero test diff on its
  six existing tests) threading `AccountStateProvider` through to
  `TradingLoop`'s new 7-arg constructor.

  (KOSPI200 contract-multiplier gap, disclosed in CLAUDE.md) is
  byte-for-byte unchanged.
- A real **multi-threaded** concurrency test
  (`SharedKisAccountLedgerTest#concurrentTradingLoopsSharingOneLedgerFileNeverExceedAllocatedVirtualCapital`)
  proves combined committed notional across multiple real
  `TradingLoop`+`SharedKisAccountLedger` pairs sharing one ledger file
  never exceeds `allocatedVirtualCapital` under real concurrent access —
  the actual safety property this 3-task effort exists to prove.
  Justification for threads-not-a-second-JVM in the planning doc (Task
  B's own `AccountLedgerLockMultiProcessTest` already proved the
  underlying primitive is cross-process-safe; this task's own new
  composition layer has no in-process/cross-process distinction in its
  locking).
- `simulated`/`bingx-vst` stay a zero diff (their own constructors/tests
  untouched).

Full design rationale, every judgment call (multi-threaded vs
multi-process, why no extra `requireHeld()` call is needed, the equity
floor value, why the regression test is a proxy for the untestable
`forKisPaper()` and why that's disclosed rather than silently assumed,
etc.): `.planning/kis-ledger-c-shared-account-ledger.md`.

body:
`supplies` was read in exactly **one place** in the whole engine:

```
src/composition.ts:340   const supplied = new Set(Object.keys(ch.supplies ?? {}));
```

`Object.keys`. **The keys, never the values.** Compose time confirmed a required slot was filled, then nothing delivered what filled it — `hydration` appeared in no runtime file and no invoker file. The chair's supplied data was write-only.

## The shipped demonstration proved it

CLAUDE.md names bill's carried `structure-conformance` plus the quartet's `structure-builder` chair *"which supplies its house-style slot"* as the working example. `institutions/quartet.json` supplies a real, carefully written house style. bill's skill says:

> *Read the constraints supplied in the `house-style` slot and apply the ones that bear.*

Nothing put it there. So every run landed on the skill's own step 5:

> *Where a slot is unfilled, say so in the output and proceed on the upstream record alone.*

**That is what made it invisible.** The agent politely reports an unfilled slot and carries on — it reads as correct handling of an optional input, not a severed wire. The institution's law was written, validated at compose time, and never read by anyone.

## The fix is two halves, because the bug is a renderer nobody feeds

| half | what |
|---|---|
| **the wire** | the runtime passes the seated chair's `supplies` onto the invocation (`ctx.hydration`) |
| **the render** | `buildPrompt` renders each **declared** slot with its value — institution-bound from the seat, gig-bound from the run's payload — and names an unfilled slot as unfilled rather than omitting it |

Either half alone would pass its own test while the feature stayed dead, which is why the laws come in both shapes.

## What this does NOT reach — stated, not pretended at

An **institutional** chair may also carry `supplies`, and the shipped quartet does exactly that. But neither `composeStandard` nor the runtime is handed the institutions, so nothing can read it. The compose error used to tell authors to supply there; following that advice supplied nothing, so **the message now names only the chair that works.** Threading institutional seatings through compose and dispatch is a real change and is not smuggled in here.

Worth recording: for the only shipped example the dead-slot check **can never fire** — `house-style` isn't `required`, and `target-paths` is gig-bound, which the check deliberately excludes.

## Laws — `tests/the_supplied_slot_reaches_the_seat.test.ts`

| | law |
|---|---|
| W1 | `chair.supplies` reaches `ctx.hydration` — the wire |
| R1 | a supplied slot's **value** appears in the prompt, not merely its name |
| R2 | the value is attributed to its **slot**, so the agent knows which instruction it answers |
| R3 | an unfilled slot is **named as unfilled**, never silently omitted |
| R4 | a slot the agent never declared is **not** rendered — supplies is not a free channel into the prompt |
| R5 | an agent with no hydration renders exactly as before — every buildPrompt fixture stays stable |

R4/R5 are the non-vacuity controls.

Three palette rows (New Agent Lane, New Shell Window, and its `⇧` twin) stopped
appearing off the terminal pages, on every machine with lanes and the windows
room on. That is a visible behaviour change with nothing on the site explaining

npm ci
npm run options:check -- --haus <haus-checkout>   # reference matches merged haus

techluddite
body:
### What this changes

**1. The fourth stat tile no longer leads with the one-year figure.**

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| 39 m, median distance found | 39 m, median distance from the door when found |
| 83%, found outside not in a building | 75%, found within 500 m of where they got out |
| under 2%, found in a shelter | 11%, found shut inside a neighbour's shed or garage |
| **61%, found alive within a year** | **50%, home by day 30, and it keeps climbing after that** |

**2. Finding the escape point is now its own step in the first hour**, in both the site and
`docs/protocol/first-24-hours.md`, with the following steps renumbered.

### Why

The one-year figure is accurate and it is the wrong thing to show someone in the first
thirty seconds. It forces the reader to do the subtraction and land on the 39% who never
came home, at the exact moment they have finished searching the house and realised the cat
is outside. Nothing is gained by it being in a summary tile: it does not change what they do
next.

`50% by day 30` comes from the same recovery curve, is equally true, and argues for the
behaviour that actually matters, which is not giving up after the first week. The full curve
including the one-year figure stays in the evidence section on the page and in
`docs/evidence.md`, and step 8 still uses it where it is framed as a reason to keep going.

The other two tiles were rebalanced while I was there. `83% found outside` and
`under 2% in a shelter` are load-bearing for the project's argument but neither tells an
owner what to do in the next hour. `75% within 500 m` says search close. `11% found in a
neighbour's building` says knock on doors. The shelter figure is still stated inline in step
5, where it is the reason not to spend the first night on the phone.

The second change came out of the same conversation. Everything in the protocol is measured
from the point of escape: the feeding station goes there, the camera goes there, and the
search rings are drawn around it. The document was assuming the owner already knew where
that was, which is not safe. It is now an explicit step, including what to do when you
cannot tell.

### Type of change

- [x] Protocol correction
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Schema / migration
- [ ] Code
- [ ] Other

### If this changes the protocol or a factual claim

No new factual claims. Every figure now shown was already in `docs/evidence.md` and is
unchanged: 39 m median for indoor-only cats, 75% within 500 m, 11% found inside someone
else's building, 50% by day 30 (95% CI 47 to 53).

This is a change of **which** true figures are shown first, not of what is claimed. Worth
being explicit that this is editorial judgement: choosing the most discouraging accurate
number is not more honest than choosing the most actionable one, and the complete curve
remains one scroll away.

- [x] `docs/evidence.md` already carries every figure used; no source changes needed
- [x] Where the evidence is weak the document still says so
- [x] Based on: the same 2018 study, plus field experience of the moment this page is read

Not touched.

- [x] Consistent with `docs/adr/0004`

- [x] No secrets, credentials, real addresses, or real case data in the diff

author: ravik453
body:
Fixes #2720

### Problem

`win32serviceutil.LocatePythonServiceExe()` uses `MoveFileEx()` to move
`pythonservice.exe` from the pywin32 installation directory to
`sys.exec_prefix`.

`MoveFileEx()` cannot move files across different Windows volumes and
returns `ERROR_NOT_SAME_DEVICE` (17). This can occur when Python packages
are installed through a symlink to a different drive.

As a result, service installation fails with:

    The system cannot move the file to a different disk drive.

### Solution

Keep the existing `MoveFileEx()` behavior for normal moves and fall back
to `CopyFile()` followed by `DeleteFile()` when Windows reports
`ERROR_NOT_SAME_DEVICE`.

Other `MoveFileEx()` failures retain the existing behavior.

### Testing

Added a regression test covering the `ERROR_NOT_SAME_DEVICE` path.

Tested with:

    python -m pytest win32\test\test_win32serviceutil.py -v

Result:

    1 passed

body:
## What

Three things existed in this repo but could not be found from the README.

**1. The configuration file had no example.** The guard reads `~/.claude/guard-config.json` — the file that decides where this installation keeps its rules, its hook sources, its dev-mode flag, and which language it speaks. There were examples for `settings.json` and `security-rules.json`, but not for this one. Added as `guard-config.example.json`, every key commented.

**2. The message catalogue was undiscoverable.** `hooks/lang/de.json` ships with the repo and the code reads `language` from the configuration — but the key `language` appeared in **no README, no example file and no document** anywhere in the repo. The only description of how to use it was a comment in the source. Someone finding the German language file had no way to learn what to do with it. Now documented, including that missing keys fall back to English and a half-finished translation still works.

**3. `tools/guard-audit.py` was invisible.** It has a proper `tools/README.md`, but nothing in the main README pointed at it — you had to happen to look in the directory. Added to the audit-log section with its four common invocations, plus the note that the HTML report is sanitized by default and `--full` is not.

While writing it, one correction to my own first draft: `installation.rules` and `installation.hook_source` do **not** both say "load from here". `rules` does both — the hook loads from it *and* the path joins self-protection. `hook_source` only extends self-protection. The example says so now.

- Every option named in the README exists (`--lang`, `--overrides`, `--blocks`, `--html`, `--full` — checked against `--help`).
- "Sanitized by default" checked against the code, not the docs.

body:
## Summary

`_layouts/gallery.html`'s gallery-viewer branch (the fullscreen photo viewer used by every `_voyage`/`_subvoyage` page that isn't in `subgalleries` enumerator mode) opened a **second `<body>` tag three DOM levels deep** inside `<div id="gallery_main"><div class="gallery_view">`, and the file never closed `</html>` at all in either branch. Browsers silently repair this — the stray `<body>`'s classes get merged onto the auto-inserted real `<body>` — so it happened to render correctly, but the source markup is invalid, undermines predictable landmark structure for assistive tech, and is fragile against anything that doesn't do full browser-grade HTML5 error recovery (validators, some SSR/AMP tooling, certain crawlers).

Same branch also skipped heading levels: `h1` (title) → `h4` (subtitle) → `h5` (post-gallery section headers), with nothing at `h2`/`h3` in between except the per-thumbnail `h3` captions — a WCAG 2.4.6-adjacent best-practice violation flagged by axe/Lighthouse-style a11y audits.

This surfaced from a broad tech-debt sweep of the repo (JS modules, gallery viewer, atlas/map, layouts/includes/data, general SCSS) — of everything found, this was the standout: a real correctness + accessibility bug on the site's primary, most-trafficked page type, not just redundant/dead code (which several already-open PRs are handling elsewhere).

### What I surveyed elsewhere (didn't pick, for coverage)
- **JS modules** (`_main.js`, `overlay-opening-scene.js`, `scroll-animations.js`, `subscribe.js`, `masthead-intent.js`, `toc-scroll-spy.js`): a `prefers-reduced-motion`/`QSD_MOTION_OFF` check is triplicated across 4 files, with `masthead-intent.js` missing the `QSD_MOTION_OFF` branch the others have (real latent bug) — strong runner-up, deferred to keep this PR scoped to one subsystem.
- **Atlas/map** (`scripts/geocode-maps.js`, `assets/js/map.js`, `_sass/_map.scss`): the global-atlas and per-parent-atlas GeoJSON builders are near-duplicate loops that have drifted into inconsistent error handling (one lets a bad voyage crash the whole build, the other warns-and-skips) — touches the build pipeline directly, higher regression risk, flagged as a good next candidate.
- **General SCSS** (`_archive.scss`, `_home.scss`, `_page.scss`, `_sidebar.scss`): a 6-layer "deep lift" box-shadow literal is copy-pasted verbatim/near-verbatim across 4 files, unrelated to `$box-shadow-fancy` which already exists as a similar token.
- **Layouts/includes structural dup**: the `page__hero.html` overlay guard and the breadcrumbs guard are byte-identical copy-pastes across 6 and 4 layouts respectively — self-guarding the partials would let callers `{% include %}` unconditionally.
- **`_data/ui-text.yml` drift**: 5 keys referenced by search-related includes don't exist in the data file (silently falls back to hardcoded Liquid defaults); 7 defined keys are never read anywhere.
- **Gallery-viewer CSS**: a dead "focus-pull blur" `@include responsive-reduced-motion` override references a `filter` on `.image img` that no base rule ever sets — leftover from a since-unified crossfade implementation.

## What changed

- `_layouts/gallery.html`:
  - Single `<body>` now emitted once (class list computed via a `body_class` assign — empty for the enumerator branch, `is-loading-1 is-loading-2 gallery-viewer` for the gallery-viewer branch), instead of one real `<body>` in the enumerator branch and one invalid nested `<body>` in the gallery-viewer branch.
  - Added a single explicit `</body></html>` close at the true end of the file (previously neither branch closed `</html>`, and the enumerator branch's `</body>` cut off `random_voyage_anchor.html`'s include, leaving it stray after the close).
  - `#gallery_main` gets `role="main"`, mirroring the enumerator branch's own `<div id="main" role="main">`.
  - Subtitle `h4` → `h2`; the two post-gallery section headers (`Other {{ parent }}`, `Fancy a Markov Chain...?`) `h5` → `h2`. Sequence is now `h1 → h2 → h3 (per-thumbnail) → h2 → h2`, no skipped levels.
- `_sass/_gallery_view.scss`: renamed the `#gallery_main #header` selector from `h4, h5, h6` to `h2, h5, h6` to track the subtitle's new tag — same declared properties (`font-family: "Philosopher"`, `font-weight: 200`, `color: $light-gray`), so zero visual change. The two section-header promotions needed no CSS change — both `.gallery_view .archive h1..h6` and `#thumbnails h1..h6` already style every heading level identically.

## Verification

- `document.body` is read directly by `assets/js/gallery/index.js` (toggling `is-loading-1`/`is-loading-2`) — confirmed it already resolved to the single, real (parser-repaired) body element before this change, so JS behavior is unaffected.
- Built the site (`npm run build:fast`) before and after; diffed rendered `_site/voyage/london/index.html` (gallery-viewer, no subtitle), `_site/voyage/venice/gondola/index.html` (gallery-viewer, has subtitle), and `_site/voyage/rome/index.html` (enumerator/subgalleries) — each now has exactly one `<body>`/`</body>`/`<html>`/`</html>`, correct heading order.
- Screenshotted all three pages at desktop (1440×900) and mobile-small (375×812) before and after via headless Chromium — layout, typography, and spacing are pixel-identical (only the randomly-sampled "related voyages" cards differ between runs, which is expected `sample:` behavior, unrelated to this change).
- `npm test` — 26/26 pass. `scripts/check-responsive-policy.sh` — pass. `scripts/check-single-use-variables.py --all` — clean.

## Impact

Valid, single-body/single-html document structure and a non-skipping heading hierarchy on every voyage/subvoyage gallery page — the site's primary content type — with zero rendered/visual change.

**Risk:** low (verified no visual delta at both breakpoints; JS/tests/mechanical checks all pass; changes are structural markup + a matching CSS selector rename with identical property values).
**Effort:** ~1h.
**Track:** A (implemented; draft PR, not merged).

author: iamcristi
body:
## Summary

Agent Guard now reports the MCP servers it can see at install time and, when
session-start discovery is enabled, at every session start. Hook events identify the
reporting machine by an explicit machine ID rather than by hostname.

## Breaking changes

- **`guard install` now requires `--machine-id`** (or `MACHINE_ID`) and exits 1 without
  it. Existing invocations must be updated. `--control-identifier` is not accepted by
  `guard install`; it remains available only for the legacy control-server blocks used
  by scan, inspect, and evo commands.
- **`X-User.identifier` on hook events is now the machine ID, not the hostname.** The
  POSIX forwarder requires `MACHINE_ID`; the PowerShell forwarder requires either
  `-MachineId` or `MACHINE_ID`. A forwarder from this branch will therefore not run
  against config written by an earlier version unless a machine ID is supplied
  externally.

## New behavior

- New internal subcommand `guard discover --client {claude-code,cursor,codex}
  [--scope {servers,skills,all}]`, with `snyk-agent-guard-discover.sh` / `.ps1`
  trampolines and a new `hook_events.py` that POSTs hook events directly from Python
  (its own User-Agent, `backend_client_session`, transport-only retries).
- `guard install` sends one best-effort `hooksConfiguredServerDiscovery` event through
  the first installed client's endpoint.
- A SessionStart hook sends a best-effort `sessionStartServerDiscovery` event per
  session (`async: true` for Claude and Codex; Cursor's `sessionStart` is
  fire-and-forget by design). It is installed **only when `AGENT_SCAN_COMMAND` is set
  at install time**; otherwise install prints a warning and writes no discovery hook.
- `DiscoveryScope` (`servers` / `skills` / `all`) gates both the `AgentDiscoverer`
  implementations and the well-known-client path.
- Discoverers accept `target_folders` from hook payloads;
  `_project_paths_with_ancestors` becomes `_discovery_paths_with_ancestors` and merges
  recorded project history with the folders named in the request.

## Payload / wire changes

- `hooksConfigured.hooks_script` gains `discover_current_checksum` and
  `discover_new_checksum`.
- `hooksConfiguredServerDiscovery` and `sessionStartServerDiscovery` payloads carry
  `discovery_duration_ms`.
- `snyk-agent-guard.sh` sends the body via `--data-binary @-` on stdin instead of on the
  argv.

## Fixes

- `get_relative_path` home matching is now boundary-aware, so `/home/alicex` no longer
  collapses to `~x`; matching is case-insensitive on Windows.
- `scan` without `--skills` skips the skills glob entirely instead of globbing and
  discarding the result.
- Managed Codex hook commands are escaped as valid TOML basic strings, including
  control characters.

## Refactors (no behavior change)

- `_write_claude/cursor/codex_config` share `_write_config`;
  `_uninstall_claude/cursor/codex` share `_uninstall_hooks`; the three client-specific
  detection wrappers share `_detect_install`; `_run_status` is table-driven.
- POSIX, PowerShell, and argv/environment hook rendering now share a single
  `_HookInvocation` spec.
- `_analysis_client_session` is now the public `backend_client_session`;
  `_RETRYABLE_TRANSPORT_EXCEPTIONS` is public.
- Uninstall's "No X found" message now uses the real filename (for example,
  `managed-settings.json`).

## Verification

- Focused guard/config/discovery unit suite: 1111 passed, 28 skipped
- Guard uv E2E: 3 passed, 3 deselected
- Current GitHub Actions Linux and Linux ARM test jobs: passed
- Current pre-commit job: passed
- Terminal stdin smoke test: returned without hanging

## Known issues / follow-ups

Open on this branch:

- `_compute_hooks_diff` normalizes push keys only, so an upgrade that adds `MACHINE_ID=`
  to the command reports every event as `modified` -- i.e. as customer hook tampering.
- `_servers_discovered_entries` never serializes `skills`, so `--scope skills` posts no
  discovered skill data and the CLI default `all` pays for a skills sweep whose result
  is discarded.
- `--scope` has three defaults: `all` in the CLI, `servers` in the PowerShell trampoline,
  and `servers` hard-coded in the installed hook.
- `_build_discover_hook_command` accepts `tenant_id` and drops it.

Pre-existing, surfaced by this branch's refactor:

- `_render_powershell_command` never emits `TENANT_ID`, so `_parse_command_info` cannot
  recover the tenant on Windows and `guard uninstall` never revokes the push key there.
  The new `_HookInvocation` already carries the field.

Cross-repo:

- agent-monitor PR [#318](https://github.com/snyk/agent-monitor/pull/318) adopts the
  `hooksConfiguredServerDiscovery` and `sessionStartServerDiscovery` event names.
- agent-monitor still needs support for surfaced discovery-entry errors and enforcement
  of the new discovery-script checksums.
- Rollout order remains agent-scan first, then strict per-session matching in
  agent-monitor.
- Reviewers should confirm the discovery event joining the agent's real session context
  has no session-state effects beyond expectation pairing.
- The ADS follow-up ticket still needs filing.

The system compose table maps `<dead_acute> <c>` to ć (Polish c-acute), so US International users get no cedilla from `'c`. [#2979](https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/issues/2979) has drawn people rediscovering the same two-line `~/.XCompose` fix independently between Oct 2025 and Jul 2026.

author: notatallshaw
body:
Reading the METADATA header block directly, instead of handing it to `email.parser.Parser().parsestr(..., headersonly=True)`, takes 4.389% of the instructions off a warm `pip:langchain-ml-course --resolution lowest` resolve: 34,406,223,088 down to 32,896,278,533, or 1,509,944,555 fewer. That count is callgrind under `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and reproduces anywhere; the timings below came off my machine.

Stacked on #938, so the diff and the numbers are against that branch.

`parse_metadata` reads seven header names. The stdlib builds a whole `Message` out of every header, a line at a time, then answers each of the seven with a linear scan that lowercases every name it stored. `_read_header_fields` walks the block once, keeps the seven, and returns a `dict[str, list[str]]`. That is 81,409 ns to 25,409 ns per call over 1,956 documents captured from that resolve (the ones that parse without raising), against the 1,965 calls the resolve makes, so about 0.11 s comes off it.

The 19-scenario canary set sees it on the clock too: locally between about 1% and 5% faster, with a middle estimate near 4%, and CPU between about 2% and 5% lower. Peak memory sits inside about 0.34% either way.

Matching `email` is the risk here:

- `StringIO(text, newline="")` is what `email` splits with. `str.splitlines` is faster and wrong, because it also breaks on `\x0b`, `\x0c`, `\x1c` to `\x1e`, `\x85`, `\u2028` and `\u2029`, so a form feed inside a header value would truncate the read.
- Compared against `email` over 500,000 generated documents and the 64,182 METADATA files in my local cache: no differences.
- One deliberate divergence. CPython changed `Compat32.header_source_parse` in 3.12.8 and 3.13.1, so `Requires-Dist:\n  bar` reads as `"bar"` from those releases on and as `"\n  bar"` on 3.10, 3.11 and the earlier 3.12 and 3.13 patches. The reader takes the newer reading everywhere, which is the one `Requirement` accepts.

author: priyanshup
body:
Tool descriptions and JSON-Schema parameters are sent to the model on every list_tools call, before any tool is actually selected, so a verbose docstring or per-parameter description costs prompt tokens on every turn regardless of whether the tool is ever invoked.

quor/mcp/schema_pruner.py condenses a tool definition's description and its input/output schema parameter descriptions to a short summary line once they cross a length threshold, while leaving required names, types, and property keys untouched. quor/mcp/server.py wires this into list_tools() only -- call_tool() resolves through a separate SDK path that never touches list_tools(), so a direct tool invocation always sees the tool's full, unpruned parameters.

author: stasimus
body:
Fixes #9644.

Blobs pulled from a gRPC remote cache were written to the CAS and synced into the build without re-hashing, so a compromised cache server or plaintext MITM could substitute bytes under the requested digest. Re-hash remote blobs on write and reject on mismatch, and warn when a plaintext grpc:// endpoint is configured.

author: s0okju
body:
## Summary

실제 배치 실행 로그: `openstack-dashboard-django`의 `id` 로케일에서 `423 Locked` (`repository-locked`) 에러 후 Phase 1 덕분에 로그를 남기고 다음 로케일(`en_AU`)로 정상적으로 넘어감 — 격리 자체는 설계대로 동작했다. 실제로 컴포넌트의 lock 상태를 조회해보니 이미 `locked: false`로 풀려 있어서, 이건 몇 초면 풀리는 일시적 잠금이었다.

문제는 `create_translation()`/`create_component()`가 Phase 2에서 고친 `upload_po_file()`과 달리 **재시도를 아예 하지 않는다**는 것 — `raise_error=True`로 첫 실패에 곧바로 프로세스가 죽는(Phase 1이 그걸 잡아서 로그 남기고 넘어가긴 하지만) 구조라, 몇 초 기다리면 풀렸을 잠금 때문에 그 실행에서는 영구적으로 로케일 하나를 건너뛰게 된다.

## 변경 내용
- `is_retryable_status(status_code)` 추가: 5xx, 423(repository-locked), 429(rate limited)는 재시도할 가치가 있고, 그 외 4xx는 서버가 이 요청 자체를 거부한 것이므로 재시도 안 함.
- `create_translation()`/`create_component()`에 `upload_po_file()`과 같은 모양의 재시도(최대 3회, 15초 간격)를 추가. `create_component()`는 zip 버퍼를 매 시도 전에 `seek(0)`으로 되감아야 두 번째 시도에서 빈 파일이 올라가는 걸 피할 수 있어서 그 부분을 신경 써서 처리.
- `upload_po_file()`의 기존 "재시도 안 함" 조건이 `400 <= status < 500`이라 423/429도 거기 포함돼 있었음 — 세 함수 모두 `is_retryable_status()`로 통일.
- `/code-review medium`에서 세 함수의 재시도 루프가 거의 동일하게 반복되고(이 PR 안에서도 그 때문에 하나를 놓칠 뻔함) 있다는 지적을 받아 `_post_with_retry()` 공용 헬퍼로 추출.

## Test plan
- [x] `py_compile`/`flake8` (기존 무관 경고 1건 외 신규 없음)
- [x] `requests.get`/`requests.post` 모킹으로 결정론적 검증 — create_translation(신규 성공/423→성공/400 즉시 실패/이미 존재/423 소진) 5케이스, create_component(423→성공/400 즉시 실패/재시도 시 zip 버퍼가 비어있지 않음 확인) 3케이스, upload_po_file(423→성공/400 즉시 실패/기존 500·200+result:false 회귀 케이스) 5케이스, 총 13개 전부 확인
- [x] 공용 헬퍼로 추출한 뒤 13개 케이스 전부 재검증 (리팩터링 중 회귀 없음 확인)
- [x] `/code-review medium` 2라운드 — 헬퍼 추출 지적 반영, `retry_count=0`일 때의 잠재적 NameError도 assert로 방지

결과 문서: `~/claude-docs/weblate-migration/upload-conflict-blast-radius/phase-4-repository-lock-retry.md`

범위 밖으로 보류: `create_project`/`create_category`/`create_glossary`는 프로젝트당 한 번만 호출돼 같은 잠금 경합 가능성이 낮다고 판단해 제외. Phase 3(근본 원인 - duplicate-key/소스 언어 충돌)은 이번과 무관한 별개 문제로 여전히 미해결.

author: asyrawih
body:
Export pertama berhasil, export **kedua** dengan project yang sama ditolak:

> Project terlalu besar untuk di-render dalam satu jalan: PCM-nya butuh 2.440 MiB, sisa linear memory engine 1.640 MiB

Angkanya yang membongkar penyebabnya:

```
plafon             4.096 MiB
sisa dilaporkan    1.640 MiB
──────────────────────────────
"terpakai"         2.456 MiB  =  2.440 MiB PCM export PERTAMA  +  16 MiB memory awal
```

16 MiB itu persis `MEMORY_INITIAL_PAGES`. Jadi yang dihitung sebagai terpakai adalah PCM export pertama — yang sudah lama dibebaskan.

## Sebabnya

```ts
sisa = plafon − memory.buffer.byteLength
```

Linear memory wasm tidak pernah menyusut: `memory.grow` satu arah, tidak ada `shrink`. Begitu satu export besar pernah jalan, `byteLength` tetap 2,4 GiB walaupun seluruh PCM-nya sudah di-`free()` dan ruangnya siap dipakai ulang oleh alokator. Rumus itu membaca semuanya sebagai terpakai dan menolak export berikutnya **selamanya sampai tab di-reload**.

Yang membuatnya mahal bukan cuma salahnya, tapi bahwa pesannya terdengar masuk akal: ia menyebut angka spesifik dan saran yang wajar ("export per-lane lalu gabungkan"). Yang disalahkan project-nya, bukan penjaganya.

## Perbaikannya

Pisahkan memory yang tumbuh karena **asset** (bisa dipakai ulang) dari yang tumbuh karena hal lain (tidak):

```
bukan-asset = byteLength − puncak asset yang pernah hidup
sisa        = plafon − bukan-asset − asset yang hidup sekarang
```

Kedua angka dilacak di Rust — `LIVE_ASSET_BYTES` dan `PEAK_ASSET_BYTES` di `wasm-bridge/src/bindgen.rs` — karena sisi JS tidak punya cara lain mengetahuinya. Pengurangannya ditaruh di `Drop for OfflineRender`, bukan di `free()`, supaya setiap jalur yang menjatuhkan renderer ikut terhitung termasuk yang gagal di tengah konstruksi.

Untuk project pelapor (4 lane × 27,4 menit, 2.440 MiB): export kedua sekarang dinilai dengan sisa ~4.076 MiB, sama seperti yang pertama.

Arah kesalahannya juga dijaga. Memory yang tumbuh **bukan** karena asset tetap dihitung terpakai, karena PCM memang tidak akan memakainya ulang — penjaga yang terlalu optimis mengembalikan kegagalan ke bentuk `RuntimeError: unreachable executed` di tengah render, dan itu lebih buruk daripada penolakan.

## Verifikasi

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` — bersih
- `pnpm -C web build` (`tsc --noEmit && vite build`) lulus
- `vitest run` — 99 file / **1150 tes** hijau (dari 1147 di `main`; +3)
- `scripts/size-check.sh` — mt 190.188 B gz (limit 307.200)

Tes barunya **diverifikasi menangkap bug ini**: rumus lama dipasang kembali sementara, dan "sisa memori PULIH setelah renderer dibebaskan" langsung merah dengan selisih persis sebesar PCM yang sudah dibebaskan (`expected 4258988032 to be 4293853184`). Tes yang tidak pernah dilihat merah tidak membuktikan apa-apa.

## Yang TIDAK diperbaiki di sini

Temuan bahwa PCM menetap **tiga kali** untuk satu project — `AudioBuffer` cache preview + salinan rata di heap JS + linear memory WASM, ≈7 GiB untuk audio 2,35 GiB — masih berlaku dan masih perlu dikerjakan. Itu tahap 1 dari kerja source-streaming, dan bukan penyebab pesan di atas.

author: dat999zx
body:
`knowl view` was unreadable on a real store. The cause was measurable rather than aesthetic: **589 of 1,070 atoms carry no link at all**. Simulating those with the same forces as the 481 connected ones packed the whole store into one evenly-filled disc, so the structure was buried under its own orphans.

This is a different cause from the hairball fixed earlier by pruning synthetic links — those edges were already correct here, and still invisible, because the nodes they connected were mixed uniformly with the orphans.

## What changed

**Layout.** Unlinked atoms sit on a scattered rim, placed by golden angle with hashed jitter rather than simulated. Golden angle alone draws visible spiral arms, which is a fact about the formula and not about the store, so the jitter is load-bearing. It also drops the repulsion loop from 572k pairs per frame to 115k. `fit()` frames the connected core and lets the rim run off-frame.

**Links** went 0.14 → 0.27 opacity and turned neutral grey. At 0.14 they were not faint, they were invisible — the one thing on the canvas that carries a relationship was the one thing you could not see. Grey rather than brand teal, so the only hues on the stage are the seven that mean a category.

**One fixed-size dot per atom, at every zoom.** Sizing by degree put the largest dots in the densest region, and because radius is drawn in screen space, zooming grew the dots along with the gaps — the crowding was scale-invariant.

**Atoms render as white cores inside category-tinted halos**, blitted from a cached gradient per category rather than drawn with `shadowBlur` (960 blurred arcs a frame is the one thing here that would genuinely cost frames). The gradient peaks at stop 0.30, not 0 — the white core paints over the middle of the tile, so any colour at the centre is thrown away. The first attempt put 0.85 there and the graph came out grey.

**Ambient drift** on two harmonics with per-atom phase, amplitude and tempo, all hashed from the atom id so it is stable across reloads. It lives in `sx()`/`sy()` rather than in the force loop, so the layout still freezes — stable to read and click — while the render never stops moving. Hit-testing goes through the same projection, so clicks follow the drifting dot.

**Labels resolve as the camera comes in** instead of painting ~60 blocks of text over the densest region. The threshold is a multiple of the fit scale, never an absolute: `fit()` picks ~0.35 for a 960-atom store and ~1.4 for a small one, so an absolute cutoff means "zoom in slightly" on one and "zoom in 4x" on another. Collision resolves against the *undrifted* position, so the visible set holds still while each name rides its atom. Halos are stroked, not blurred — the blur smudged every dot a label passed over.

**Clicking an atom flies the camera to it** and holds it centred, biased left by half the inspector, which overlays the canvas rather than shrinking it. Any pan or wheel cancels the flight. `prefers-reduced-motion` jumps straight to the target and pins the pulse steady.

**Chrome.** The stage lost its teal radial gradient, which washed one corner a full step lighter than the other so identical atoms read as different colours depending on where the layout dropped them. Grounds are darker and less blue than the docs site's — that palette carries prose, this one carries a thousand saturated dots — with hue family and every accent token unchanged. Rail narrower and flat, one radius vocabulary across controls, and the list's title column takes the slack instead of stranding Category/Age/Reads against the far edge.

Category colour still renders flat in the rail legend, list rows, tooltip and inspector chip, which is where a precise category read matters. The canvas is where atmosphere does.

## Verification

`typecheck`, `eslint`, `docs:check` and `git diff --check` clean; **344 test files, 3210 passed, 5 skipped**.

Visual and motion claims were measured over CDP rather than asserted, since a single screenshot cannot show motion:

- Two frames from one page session, pixel-diffed over the canvas region: **13.5% of pixels changed** above a 12/255 threshold (6.4% before the amplitude increase).
- **52fps** at 963 atoms with 963 sprite blits, 963 arcs and 789 lines per frame — under headless Chrome with `--disable-gpu`, i.e. software rasterisation, so a GPU-backed browser is above that.

## Risk

Presentation only. No schema, no migration, no tool or command surface, no store behaviour. Everything is in `src/viewer/ui.ts` plus a CHANGELOG entry.

author: andreshernandez-spec
body:
Extends docs/07's outline into a buildable LaTeX project under paper/, per the instruction that the skeleton be clear to both audiences and ready to grow into the full paper.

Conventions, stated in main.tex's header: every section file opens with the claim it must carry and where its evidence lives in the repo; draft prose is plain language first with the technical term in parentheses after (e.g. the estimator explained in one sentence before 'zeroth-order' appears); TODO(andres) marks every point where your judgement or voice is required, including the still-open section 7 lead, where both orders are drafted for you to delete one. Figures include directly from experiments/*/figures, so regenerating a figure updates the paper on the next build.

New assembly scripts: tb1.py (baseline throughput from the m4 runs, both platforms, D=1 primary and D=8 as the what-sharding-adds table, failures rendered as OOM entries) and tb2.py (analytic vs measured communication; its content is the two systematic deviations, A at exactly 2x its naive byte count from the two real gathers and B at its all-reduce plus the same gather riding along). All three table scripts emit LaTeX into paper/generated with --latex, wired into the results section, markdown and LaTeX from one source so they cannot drift. make tables refreshes them; the document compiles clean with pdflatex.

The class is a neutral article until the MLSys CFP lands; swapping in their class file is a one-line change.

author: petrsvihlik
body:
### Motivation

No issue exists — this removes the manual Dependabot treadmill: with several green Dependabot PRs open, merging one makes the rest "out of date" (branch protection requires branches to be up to date), so each needs a manual update + full CI re-run, one by one. Dependabot itself only rebases its PRs **on conflict** (`rebase-strategy: auto`), not when they're merely behind, and GitHub's merge queue isn't available on user-owned repositories — hence a small workflow:

- On every `master` push (typically a just-merged Dependabot PR), plus a daily cron fallback and `workflow_dispatch`, it finds open Dependabot PRs **with auto-merge enabled**, oldest first, and comments `·@·d·ependabot r·ebase` on the first one that is behind its base.
- **One PR per run, deliberately**: rebasing all stale PRs at once would burn CI on branches the very next merge invalidates again. The rebased PR re-runs CI, auto-merges (via the existing Dependabot Auto-Merge workflow), and that merge push triggers this workflow again — the queue drains serially with no human involvement.
- The rebase is requested via comment rather than the update-branch API because pushes made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` don't trigger other workflows — an API-updated branch would sit with its checks never re-running. Dependabot's own force-push retriggers CI normally.
- PRs with auto-merge disabled are skipped: a PR being held back on purpose shouldn't burn CI, and (merging nothing) it would stall the drain.

### Checklist

- [x] Code follows coding conventions held in this repo
- [ ] Automated tests have been added (n/a — workflow-only change)
- [x] Tests are passing
- [ ] Docs have been updated (if applicable) (n/a)
- [x] Temporary settings (e.g. variables used during development and testing) have been reverted to defaults
- [x] Adheres to [.NET Design Guidelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/design-guidelines/) (n/a — no .NET code touched)

### How to test

With ≥2 auto-merging Dependabot PRs open, merge (or let auto-merge land) one of them. The "Dependabot Rebase Queue" run triggered by that push should comment `·@·d·ependabot r·ebase` on the oldest remaining PR; Dependabot reacts with 👍 and force-pushes the rebase, CI re-runs, the PR auto-merges, and the next run picks up the following PR. `workflow_dispatch` allows kicking the drain manually at any time.

author: developer3516
body:
Bounded concurrency is not a bounded rate, and bulk makes that easy to miss. Four workers against an endpoint answering in 10ms issue four hundred requests a second while the concurrency setting does exactly what it promised. Retries do not help either - backoff is what happens after the limiter already rejected you, and the 429 was served, counted and logged against your key.

A token bucket, because that is the shape real limiters use: sustained rate plus a burst, so a caller idle for a minute can send a short burst rather than being throttled to the average by a scheme with no memory. It refills continuously rather than on a timer, since a tick-based refill makes whoever arrives just after a tick wait a full interval for a token already three-quarters earned.

take() re-checks after waking rather than assuming its token survived. Several callers can wait on one bucket and the first to wake takes the token the others were also waiting for.

Where the wait sits matters twice. Before signing, because a request queued behind a slow bucket would otherwise carry a timestamp minted minutes earlier and arrive outside the server's clock tolerance while being perfectly signed. Before the timeout starts, because a request that waited its turn should still get its full budget to run. Both are tested.

Inside the attempt rather than around the retry loop: a retry is another request as far as the server's limiter cares, so three attempts consume three tokens.

Buckets can be shared across clients, which is the only way a shared quota actually holds.

body:
The v1.0 disk image has been rebuilt with the installer window from #60 — same app, byte-identical binary (`shasum` checked against the one extracted from the published image), signed, notarized and stapled again.

The appcast enclosure URL is version-pinned and immutable by design, so reshipping the image means its `edSignature` and `length` move with it. Both are updated here in a single edit. `pubDate` is untouched (the Pro update window is judged by it) and no older item is touched.

- new signature verifies against the rebuilt image
- `SUPublicEDKey` in the shipped 1.0 app matches the signing key, so clients will accept it
- image is 20,586,038 bytes, against 23,266,302 before

body:
Two facts the code already held were kept a second time as prose only a person remembered, and both cost something in 0.11.0.

**The notes were assembled from memory.** The `CHANGELOG` section for a release was written by reading `git log` across three repositories and retelling it. Nothing checked the retelling, and a fix users needed was left out — `release-shelf.yml` copies that section into the GitHub Release verbatim, so what is missing there is missing in public.

`scripts/release-notes-draft.sh` prints the draft. It is told nothing: the previous release tag comes from the tags, and which `core` and `console` versions this release moves through comes from the pins in `Dockerfile.wallet` then and now. Every commit in range is printed, sorted into likely-user-facing and likely-internal, and **nothing is dropped** — a security identifier overrides the prefix, because a fix users want can arrive as `chore(deps)`. The human's job changes from "remember, then add" to "read, then delete on purpose".

It refuses to run under CI: reading the private `core` needs a person's own credentials, and wiring it into a workflow here would put a token for a private repository into a public one. A compare that the API truncated is a refusal, not a short draft.

**The count of version points was written in a sentence.** `tests/version_points.py` declares them once; anything stating how many counts them. The prose keeps its number and is held against the list, the way `test_skill_numbers_do_not_rot` already holds the installer's line count.

Nine hand-typed copies stop being hand-typed: seven byte-exact image strings in the shim harness, the installer tag in the docs guard, and a tag-shape example in `docs/INSTALL.md` that named a version for no reason. The expectations still come from the manifest and never from the artifact under test — point the shim at an older tag with the manifest untouched and six of 165 shim tests go red.

**`smithery.yaml` was eight releases behind**, and nothing looked at it. It was part of the bump once and fell out of the lists. `test_no_image_reference_escapes_the_registry` now sweeps the tree for the *form* of a wallet image reference and requires every occurrence to be the manifest's, declared, or exempt with a reason — and exemptions have to keep earning themselves. The installer-URL form is deliberately not swept: a tag cannot be told from a historical reference without meaning, and that limit is written down rather than papered over.

Measured, not estimated: a real bump taken to green touches 26 version-bearing lines across 12 files. The same command over the last release's prep commit gives 36 across 16 — and two more that nobody edited, which is what `smithery.yaml` was.

`AGENTS.md` says what holds each release point, including the two things held by nothing at all and why.

author: kazuo1970takahashi-sketch
body:
## 何が起きていたか（ステップ別の実測）

同じ commit（PR #917 の `528dd78`）で E2E ジョブの結果が2回とも違いました。`gh api .../actions/jobs/<id>` でステップ別の時刻を取ると、遅かったのは**テストではなくブラウザの導入**でした。

| ステップ | job 96122380273 | job 96369763890 |
|---|---|---|
| Run actions/checkout | 2秒 | 1秒 |
| Setup Node | 5秒 | 7秒 |
| Install dependencies (`npm ci`) | 1秒 | 1秒 |
| **Install Chromium** | **15分05秒 → `cancelled`** | **21秒** |
| Run E2E suites | **skipped** | 3分54秒 |

`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` が15分ぶら下がり、そこでジョブごと打ち切られていました。**E2E スイートは1秒も走っていません。**

同じ症状は #914 でも起きています（2度目）。

## なぜ放置できないか

`Install Chromium` は**外部ネットワークと apt に依存する作業**なのに、**上限も再試行もありませんでした**。

- `cancelled` は「テストが赤」「単に遅い」「外部が詰まった」を区別できない
- `AUTO-MERGE-GATE-001` は conclusion が `SUCCESS` 以外を停止条件にします（P1-2）。`cancelled` はそこに当たるので、**自動マージが外部要因で黙って止まります**

## どう直したか

打ち切りと再試行を**そのステップの中に閉じ込めました**。

- `timeout 240` で括り、最大2回試す。秒数と回数は step の `env` に置き、テストが読み取れる一箇所にまとめた
- 打ち切り（終了コード 124）とそれ以外の失敗（apt のエラー等）を**区別して**ログに出す
- 使い切ったら `::error::` で原因を名指しして落ちる。文面に「E2E は実行していない＝これはテストの赤ではなく、ブラウザ導入の失敗」と書く
- ジョブ上限 15 → 20 分（最悪ケース 2×240＋予備600 = 1080 秒が収まる）

15分の沈黙が「240秒で終わらなかった、やり直す」というログに変わります。

## テスト

新規 `test/test_e2e_install_guard_918.js` … **23 検査**。

- **数字の整合**: `env` とシェル既定値が一致するか、再試行が2回以上か、そして**最悪ケース（回数×秒数＋予備）がジョブ上限に収まるか**を計算で固定します。予備 600 秒は実測（checkout 1 ＋ Setup Node 7 ＋ npm ci 1 ＋ E2E 234 = 243 秒）の倍以上。片方の数字だけ動かすと赤くなります。
- **動作**: workflow から `run` ブロックを抜き出して実際に走らせます。ぶら下がる `npx` ／即失敗する `npx` ／成功する `npx` ／2回目で成功する `npx` の4通りで、終了コード・所要時間・警告の回数・ログの文面を見ます。

★ `timeout` は macOS 既定にありません。無い環境で検査を飛ばすと「守っているつもりで何も検査していない」になります（#914 で `grep -P` を使って実際に踏みました）。ここでは**必ず自前の shim を PATH に置いて**動かし、どの機械でも同じ経路を通します。

`run_tests` **265/0/0**。

### 反証パネル（8本すべて赤を確認）

| # | 入れた欠陥 | 落ちる検査 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `timeout` を外す | A1 / B1 / B2 / B3 / B4 |
| 2 | 再試行をやめる（1回きり） | A7 / A8 |
| 3 | env とシェル既定値を食い違わせる | A6 |
| 4 | 使い切っても落ちない（`exit 1` → `exit 0`） | A3 / B1 / B8 |
| 5 | 再試行を増やして枠を超える（2 → 4） | A7 / **A10** |
| 6 | ジョブ上限を戻す（20 → 15） | **A10** |
| 7 | 打ち切りとそれ以外の失敗を区別しない | A5 / B9 / B9a |
| 8 | 1行 `run` に戻す | 抽出時点で失敗 |

## 進め方の記録（正直なところ）

#918 は最初、「変異チェックが遅いのだろう」という**推測**で選択肢を4つ並べて起票していました。ステップ別の実測を取ったら4つとも的外れで、原因は1つ前のステップでした。測る前に手を動かしていたら丸ごと無駄になっていたので、経緯を issue 本文と changelog に残しています。

## 触っていないもの

`shogi_v4.html` と `app/` は一切変更していません。`test/run_e2e.sh` にも触っていません（**スイート単位のタイムアウトが無い**という別の観察は #918 に残置。今回の原因ではありません）。

Fixes #918

author: olivierfreyssinet
body:
### 📝 Description

Scaffolds the seven ADR Contacts device intents so LWD and LWM can exercise the same register / rename / edit contracts, and documents the file layout they use.

#### Contacts intents

`@features/platform-contacts/device/intents` now exports the seven ADR surfaces: external-address registration, external-contact rename, identifier edit, scope edit, combined external-address edit, Ledger-account registration and Ledger-account rename. Each carries its types, a stub RxJS job emitting `pending` → `awaiting-device-confirmation` → `completed`, and a platform definition. No `ContactsManager` or `device-contacts-kit` wiring yet.

The jobs and platform components are WIP mocks. There are no unit tests for them: the sequences and UI are hardcoded, so a test would only freeze the stub rather than cover real device behaviour.

The debug screens on both apps run the register-external-address intent, so the whole path can be validated end to end against a real device.

#### One definition per intent

Each intent directory holds a single `intentDefinition.ts` binding `./component`, with the renderers split as `component.web.tsx` / `component.native.tsx`:

```ts
import { createIntent } from "@features/platform-device-intent";
import { registerExternalAddressIntentPlatformDefinition } from "@features/platform-contacts/device/intents";

const intent = createIntent(registerExternalAddressIntentPlatformDefinition, input);
```

Rspack resolves `.web` for LWD and Metro resolves `.native` for LWM, so one `IntentPlatformDefinition` covers both platforms — no base-versus-platform definition split, and no `.native` twin of the barrel.

Knip does not apply `moduleSuffixes` in a single run, so it cannot follow `./component` to either renderer. The per-platform knip runs already on `develop` handle that; this branch only adds the intents barrel to both entry lists.

#### DIE docs

The DIE README so far only described the case where an intent's contract lives in a shared lib and each app owns its own renderer plus `intentLWDDefinition` / `intentLWMDefinition`. That split exists because an app is the only place a platform component could live — which no longer holds for an intent owned by a `features/` package, where both renderers sit next to the definition.

A new section documents that layout, recommends it for intents whose job relies purely on DMK and the signer kits, and records the two cases that still require the app/lib split: a dependency on `@ledgerhq/live-common`, or UI leaning heavily on components that still live in the app. It also notes that a DDD intent package using suffix-less `./component` imports must run knip once per platform.

#### Ownership

`features/platform/contacts/src/device/` is now owned by `@ledgerhq/live-devices`. The rest of `@features/platform-contacts` stays with `@ledgerhq/wallet-xp`.

### 🔗 Context

- **JIRA / GitHub issue**: [LIVE-35698](https://ledgerhq.atlassian.net/browse/LIVE-35698)
- **ADR**: [Contacts Device Intents](https://ledgerhq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/WXP/pages/7299039425/ADR+Contacts+Device+Intents)

### Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @features/platform-contacts typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm --filter @features/platform-contacts unimported`
- [x] LWD Developer settings → Device Intent Executor → Contacts mode: register-external-address stub runs and shows the web renderer
- [x] LWM Debug → Device Intent Executor → Contacts validation: same intent shows the native renderer

[LIVE-35698]: https://ledgerhq.atlassian.net/browse/LIVE-35698?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: timtebeek
body:
## What

`org.openrewrite.java.migrate.guava.NoGuavaMapsNewHashMap` throws on Groovy sources:

```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Expected a template that would generate exactly one statement
to replace one statement, but generated 0. Template:
new HashMap<>(__P__.<java.util.Map>/*__p0__*/p())
...
  org.openrewrite.java.migrate.guava.NoGuavaMapsNewHashMap$1.visitMethodInvocation(NoGuavaMapsNewHashMap.java:69)
  org.openrewrite.java.migrate.guava.NoGuavaMapsNewHashMap_1_GroovyVisitor.visitMethodInvocation(...)
```

Found via the Moderne SaaS flagship run of *Java best practices* against the "Netflix + Spring" org, where it puts `Netflix/metacat` into `RepositoryRecipeRunError` on every run. The trigger is `metacat-thrift/src/test/groovy/com/netflix/metacat/thrift/CatalogThriftHiveMetastoreSpec.groovy` — a Spock spec containing `Maps.newHashMap(ImmutableMap.of(...))`, which a sibling recipe in the same composite (`NoGuavaImmutableMapOf`) has already rewritten to `Maps.newHashMap(Map.of(...))` by the time this recipe sees it.

## Why

The templates are marked `.contextSensitive()`. That makes `JavaTemplate` reconstruct and re-parse the *enclosing block* as Java before splicing in the replacement. On a Groovy LST that block routinely contains constructs with no Java equivalent — `def result = ...`, `timer.record(_, _) >> {}`, `registry.createId(_ as String) >> id` — so the reconstructed source does not parse, `parseBlockStatements` returns zero statements, and `maybeReplaceStatement` throws.

None of these templates reference anything from the surrounding scope: they are self-contained expressions (`new HashMap<>(#{any(java.util.Map)})`) whose only external dependency is an import they already declare explicitly. Context sensitivity was never needed here, and dropping it also lets the templates be cached.

- I went with the real fix rather than a language guard (cf. openrewrite/rewrite@e9c478e / rewrite-static-analysis#105, which caught `RecipeRunException` and skipped) — the replacement works correctly on Groovy once the template is context-free, so there is no reason to skip those sources.

## Scope

The same unnecessary `.contextSensitive()` appears across the whole `NoGuava*` collection-factory family, all with the identical latent crash, so they are fixed together:

- `NoGuavaListsNewArrayList`, `NoGuavaListsNewCopyOnWriteArrayList`, `NoGuavaListsNewLinkedList`
- `NoGuavaMapsNewHashMap`, `NoGuavaMapsNewLinkedHashMap`, `NoGuavaMapsNewTreeMap`
- `NoGuavaSetsNewConcurrentHashSet`, `NoGuavaSetsNewHashSet`, `NoGuavaSetsNewLinkedHashSet`

`NoGuavaDirectExecutor` is deliberately left alone — its `Runnable::run` method reference does lose type attribution without context (`MemberReference type is missing or malformed`), so `.contextSensitive()` is load-bearing there.

## Testing

Added `NoGuavaMapsNewHashMapTest#replaceWithNewHashMapWithMapInGroovy`, a `groovy(...)` source spec modelled on the metacat block (Spock `when:`/`then:`, mock interactions, multi-line argument) that reproduces the crash before this change. It needs a `GroovyParser` with Guava on its classpath, and an explicit `testImplementation("org.openrewrite:rewrite-groovy")` so `org.openrewrite.groovy.Assertions` is no longer picked up only transitively.

All 218 tests in `org.openrewrite.java.migrate.guava` pass.

author: stewmac570
body:
## Summary

Closes #421 and #420 — both are window-geometry work in the same files, so they're done together.

**The problem.** The race-day laptop is 1920×1080 at 150% scaling, which gives the app a **1280×688** usable canvas. Both race consoles declared heights taller than that (760 and 800), so their layouts spent every meet getting compressed by `FitToScreen` rather than being designed for the screen they actually run on. Separately, nine windows declared eight different footprints, so every navigation step visibly resized the window — the "3 different sizes" in the meet screenshot.

**Two tiers now:**

| Tier | Windows | Size |
|------|---------|------|
| Workspace | Landing, Setup, Load, Driver Manager, Race Console, Multi-Class | `1180×660`, min `980×620` |
| Utility | Driver Stats, Settings, Live Scoreboard | width `600` |

Moving between workspace windows no longer changes the footprint.

**A second bug found while auditing.** Two windows were *both* taller than the laptop canvas *and* only called `RoundCorners`, so nothing clamped them at all — their docked footer buttons could sit under the taskbar on race day:

- `RaceResultsWindow` 1040×720 → 660, now `FitToScreen`
- `ClassCompletionWindow` 920×700 → 660, now `FitToScreen`
- `LandingWindow` also moved to `FitToScreen` for the same reason

`RaceResultsWindow` is the end-of-night results screen, so this one was worth catching.

**Keeping it true.** `WindowSizingStandardTests` parses the window XAML and fails if any window exceeds 1280×688 (including Min sizes, which are worse than a large default — the window can't be shrunk to fit at all) or if the workspace windows drift apart. The standard is also written into `CLAUDE.md` and the `WindowSizing` doc comment.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet test` — 328 passed, 0 failed, 11 skipped (326 before; +2 new)
- [x] Guard verified to actually fail: temporarily set SetupWindow to 900 tall, both new tests failed; restored
- [x] Launched the app and screenshotted each window at its new size — Landing, Setup, Load, Driver Manager (1180×660), Settings (600×581), Live Scoreboard (600×551). All layouts stretch correctly, nothing clipped, footers visible
- [x] Race console previously verified usable at 1280×672 during the #418 work, which is the same canvas
- [ ] Not visually captured: `RaceResultsWindow` and `ClassCompletionWindow` (need a completed class to open). Both use a star-sized content row between Auto header/footer rows, so the height reduction only shrinks the scroll area — worth a look during review
- [ ] Manual on the actual race-day laptop at 150% scaling

Note for review: Setup and Load were designed at ~780 wide and are now 1180. They stretch fine (screenshots above), but Setup's `Class` column is star-sized and now leaves a wide gap — that's existing DataGrid column sizing, covered by #278 rather than fixed here.

author: cherepoq
body:
### Motivation

- Rebrand the project to RentFlow and prepare it for PWA + Trusted Web Activity (Android) distribution with required metadata and assetlinks support.
- Add server-side encrypted media storage with content validation and optional FFmpeg-based video compression for production use.
- Provide infrastructure and developer UX: Docker / Docker Compose, Caddy reverse proxy, hosting and production checklists, and GitHub Actions for CI and Pages preview. 
- Improve security and production readiness: HTTPS enforcement, security headers, manifest and privacy/account-deletion pages, and example production env variables.

### Description

- Rename/rebrand UI and Android artifacts to `RentFlow` and `app.rentflow.mobile`, update manifest and Android TWA templates. 
- Implement encrypted media subsystem: `MediaAsset` entity, `MediaAssetRepository`, `MediaStorageService` (AES-256-GCM with AAD, signature checks, quota), `VideoCompressionService` (FFmpeg pipeline), and `MediaController` API with token auth.
- Add platform endpoints: `PlatformController` serves `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` and readiness info, and `HttpsSecurityFilter` enforces redirects and common security headers.
- Add client-side secure vault `secure-storage.js` (IndexedDB + Web Crypto) and wire it into service worker and frontend (`theme.js`) to support local encryption and optional server uploads.
- Update infrastructure and ops: `Dockerfile` now installs `ffmpeg`, `docker-compose.yml` runs Postgres, rentflow service and optional Caddy edge proxy, `Caddyfile` with security headers, `.env.production.example`, `HOSTING.md` and `PRODUCTION.md` with deployment/release gates.
- Add developer scripts: `scripts/run_docker.sh`, `scripts/local_preview.sh`, `scripts/static_preview.sh`, `scripts/domain_check.sh`, and Android pre-release checks enhanced in `android/scripts/pre_release_check.sh`.
- Add GitHub Actions: `ci.yml` for lint/tests/build artifact and `pages.yml` to publish static preview to GitHub Pages.
- Update build config: add `postgresql` runtime dependency in `pom.xml` and profile-aware `application.yml` for `prod` profile.

### Testing

- Ran backend unit tests with `mvn --batch-mode test` which executed the new `MediaStorageServiceTest` suite and passed (3 tests: encryption/decryption, signature rejection, AAD tamper-detection).
- Performed frontend static syntax checks with `node --check` on `src/main/resources/static/js/theme.js` and `src/main/resources/static/js/secure-storage.js`, which completed without errors.
- Local smoke runs: `./scripts/static_preview.sh` and `./scripts/run_docker.sh` were used for preview and Docker startup checks (static checks and pre-release scripts executed successfully).
