author: boubaker
body:
## Why is this change needed?

Prior to this change, the first iteration of the JCR aged-files cleanup
campaigns worked but could not be *operated*. Testing it against the Tribe-Dev
dataset (~800 GB accumulated over 14 years) surfaced five gaps, all of the same
nature: an administrator could start a campaign but could not follow it,
understand it, correct it, or recover from it.

- A dry-run over hundreds of thousands of nodes reported raw counters and a bare
  seconds value — unreadable at that scale, and the table stayed frozen while the
  numbers moved.
- The report said *what* was a candidate but not *since when* nor *whose* it was,
  so no candidacy decision could be checked without opening the JCR.
- Every state looked alike, so a run in progress could not be told from a
  finished one at a glance.
- A campaign name was fixed at creation, and a typo followed the report forever.
- Worst of all, a JCR node that refused to be deleted left an item marked
  `Skipped` with no visible reason and no way to try again — the failure code was
  concatenated with the exception message into one column, which broke both its
  localization and its grouping, and the only trace of the cause was a server log
  line no administrator can read.

## How does it address the issue?

Five commits, each self-contained and reviewable on its own.

**`9d3d7f32` — Live progress report, readable counts and durations.**
Counts go through the platform's `<number-format>`, remaining time through a
day/hour/minute breakdown, and the items table refreshes as the progress events
arrive (scan *and* execution), throttled so a fast run cannot flood the console.

**`754315a4` — Candidacy dates and owner name.** The last-modified and created
dates are captured per item (changeset `-6`, additive, no backfill) and shown in
the report and the CSV archive, along with the resolved owner name.

**`6c9fea73` — Coloured state chips.** One Vuetify colour per campaign and item
state, mapping centralized in `CleanupUtils.js`; only `EXECUTING` and `SKIPPED`
are filled, so the console stays calm and the two states that need attention are
the ones that catch the eye.

**`24bf0e23` — Rename a campaign, report the last modified date to users.**
`PATCH /campaigns/{id}` — an attribute update, not an action, hence PATCH rather
than a `rename` sub-resource next to `publish`/`execute`. Allowed in any state
because the name is pure metadata: nothing keys off it and no lifecycle
transition is involved, so relabelling a completed report is legitimate. It also
fixes a latent bug — `NAME` is `NVARCHAR(250) NOT NULL` but nothing validated its
length, so a longer name reached the INSERT and failed with a raw database error;
creation and rename now share the one validation and cannot diverge.

**`84da2985` — Trace and retry the purge failures.**
- `FAILURE_REASON` goes back to being a bare message code; the exception text
  moves to a new `FAILURE_DETAIL` CLOB (changeset `-7`, additive, alongside
  `ATTEMPT_COUNT`), so the console can finally localize *and* group it.
- The detail keeps **two** links of the cause chain — head exception and root
  cause — stating explicitly how many intermediate links and frames were cut,
  under a hard 8000-character cap applied last. A deep JCR failure carrying an
  embedded SQL error runs to hundreds of KB; at this volume, persisting that
  verbatim is a storage problem of its own.
- `POST {id}/retry` requeues the failures another attempt can fix — a
  server-owned allowlist, bounded to 3 attempts per item, no new scan and no new
  grace period. Safe by construction: the worker revalidates every item against
  JCR immediately before deleting it, so an item since exempted, modified or
  deleted is spared on its own. `GET {id}/failures` serves the per-reason counts
  from one grouped query.
- `FAILURE_DETAIL` is served on the **administrator path only**. The item DTO is
  shared with `published/my-items`, and a stack trace can name nodes outside the
  caller's visibility — a `ReferentialIntegrityException` names the *referencing*
  node, possibly a symlink in a space the user is not a member of.

Two defects of the execution worker are fixed with it:

- The item save sat **outside** the guarded region, so a failing save escaped the
  whole worker and left the item `CANDIDATE` with its outcome set in memory only;
  the stalled-worker watchdog then restarted the worker on the same item forever.
  The save is guarded now, with one detail-less fallback attempt.
- The batch loop re-read page 0 and relied on every processed item leaving
  `CANDIDATE` — the same poison pill by another route. It is keyset paged now, so
  forward progress is structural rather than inferred, and each batch commits on
  its own via `RequestLifeCycle.restartTransaction()`, so a late database failure
  can no longer roll back the batches before it.

**`3aea7208` — Make the grace period editable.**
The grace period is not a candidacy criterion: the scan selects on the age
threshold, minimum file size and excluded paths, `maxVersionsPerFile` is consumed
at purge time, and `graceDays` is read in exactly one place — `publishCampaign`,
which materializes `lockDate` from it. So it can change without invalidating a
report that took hours to compute. `PATCH /campaigns/{id}` therefore becomes a
partial update, `{name?, graceDays?}`, both absent answering
`cleanup.nothingToUpdate` rather than doing nothing silently; `graceDays` is boxed
because **0 is meaningful** (a grace period elapsing at publication).

The guard is per **field**, which is the point: the name stays editable in every
state, `graceDays` only in `DRAFT`/`SIMULATED`/`PUBLISHED` (`GRACE_EDITABLE_STATES`).
`LOCKED` is excluded deliberately — extending a locked campaign's grace needs a
`LOCKED → PUBLISHED` edge that does not exist in the transition table, and exiting
`PUBLISHED` unregisters the freshness observation listener, so the reverse edge
would have to re-register it.

On a published campaign the deadline recomputes as **`publishedDate + graceDays`,
never `now + graceDays`** — anchoring on now would slide the deadline forward on
every save, so saving the same value twice would push it out twice. That anchor is
already an invariant (`publishCampaign` sets both from one instant), and everything
downstream reads `lockDate`, including the end users' `remainingMillis`, so one
field propagates the change. A deadline recomputed into the past is accepted, not
an error: it closes the review window immediately and the campaign locks at the
next cron tick, exactly as a zero grace period already behaves — and the update
performs no transition itself, leaving the single transition authority with the
scheduled job and the manual trigger.

`validateGraceDays` is extracted and shared with `validateParams`, so creation and
edit cannot drift on the `>= 0` bound — the discipline `validateName` already
applies to the name. In the console the creation drawer gains an edit mode rather
than a second drawer: criteria disabled behind a visible reason, grace disabled
with its own reason outside the three editable states, and the resulting deadline
projected live with a warning when it lands in the past. The inline pencil rename
is replaced by this single Edit path — two rename paths would mean two validations
and two error surfaces.

read-only reader threads, feeding a **single writer thread** through a bounded

already opens its own session per call (mandatory — a JCR `Session` is not

author: hegsie
body:
## Symptom

`Test Backend` went red on **#323** with:

```
---- commands::stash::tests::test_stash_show_basic stdout ----
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 0
 right: 1
```

That is `assert_eq!(show.files.len(), 1)` — the stash captured nothing. #323's diff is frontend-only (the command palette), so it cannot have caused this.

## Root cause

Not a mystery flake. The fixture is:

```rust
setup_tracked_file(&repo, "file.txt", "original content");  // commit → writes index
repo.create_file("file.txt", "modified content");           // modify
```

`"original content"` and `"modified content"` are **both exactly 16 bytes**, and the modification happens immediately after the commit that wrote the index. That is git's *racily clean* case: when a file's mtime falls in the same timestamp-granularity bucket as the index write and the size is unchanged, the entry can be judged unchanged by `stat` alone. `create_stash` then finds nothing to stash, `stash_show` reports zero files, and the assertion fails.

It reproduces only where timestamp granularity is coarse enough — which is why it passes locally (12/12 in isolation, 8/8 full-suite runs here) and fails intermittently on CI.

## Fix

Make the edit change the file's **size**. No stat comparison can miss that, regardless of mtime granularity:

```rust
repo.create_file("file.txt", "modified content, now a different length");
```

Test-only, one line plus a comment explaining the trap so it does not come back. This was the only same-size pair among the stash fixtures — the others already differ in length (`"content"` → `"modified"`, `"original"` → `"stashed content"`, etc.).

## Why its own PR

The failure can land on any PR's `Test Backend`, so it is worth merging independently rather than riding along with an unrelated change — the same reasoning as #342.

Full gate green: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, 2077 backend tests.

## What & why
Storage half of the **"why did you do that" trace enrichment** (road-test [#485](https://github.com/fedoroff-vlad/ai-life/issues/485), [stage4.md](../blob/stage-rt-pr485-g2a-trace-store/plans/stage4.md) §Track G, slice **G2a**). G1 (PR#514) already answers "почему ты так сделал" with the *routing* trace the orchestrator owns (which agent + why). G2 enriches that with what the agent itself **read/wrote**. To fold that into an answer given on a *later* turn, the fact must be persisted with `last_route`.

## How
- `011-conversation-last-route-trace.yml` adds `core.conversation_state.last_route_trace` (nullable text).

- All positional constructor callers updated (orchestrator + memory-service lock clients pass `null` — inert).
- `test-schema.sql` gains the column; `ConversationStateIntegrationTest` asserts the trace round-trips with `last_route`.

The trace is a short, **payload-free** line of what the handling agent did — a turn with no trace leaves it null and the explain answer falls back to G1's routing-only trace.

**Next (G2b):** `IntentResponse` gains an optional `trace`; agents contribute it (reference consumer first, per-agent rollout); the orchestrator records it here and `ExplainResponder` folds it into the answer.

author: ezzahcomm
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #103. That PR capped how many jobs of the *same* type could be claimed per tick, but still claimed by strict `priority DESC` otherwise. Confirmed **not enough** by re-checking prod ~20 minutes after #103 deployed: `sms_process_schedules`, three `email_campaign_*` types, and `payment_requests_expire` are all priority 5 — that tier alone, whether or not each individual type was capped, was still large enough to fill the entire 7s time budget every single tick before `sms_poll_dlr` (priority 4) or `sms_release_stale_reservations` (priority 3) was ever reached. Both showed **literally zero** completions since before the incident, even after #103 had already shipped and deployed.

## Fix
`claimPendingJobs` now claims from one specific type at a time (`onlyType`) instead of taking an exclude-list. `processJobBatch` fetches every distinct type with pending, due work and round-robins across all of them — one claim attempt per type per round, cycling until the time/batch budget runs out. This guarantees every distinct pending type is touched in round 1 of every tick, regardless of how many same-priority siblings it's competing against.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Full unit suite: 544/544 passing.
- Will re-check prod job_queue after this deploys to confirm sms_poll_dlr/sms_release_stale_reservations actually start completing this time before considering the incident closed.

author: kirill-markin
body:
## Why

The `ExpenseBudgetTracker-WebErrorEventsAlarm` alarm fired on 19 and 20 Aug. Every error event was `RangeError: Invalid time zone specified: Etc/Unknown` from the chat agent stage.

Browsers that cannot map their host zone report `Etc/Unknown` from `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`. The client sent it verbatim, the server accepted it after only a non-empty-string check, and `formatDatetime()` threw before the first model call. The user saw the generic chat error and every retry failed, so chat was permanently dead for that browser. `resolveBrowserTimezone()` threw on the same input, so those browsers could not create a workspace either.

The account in the logs was the live-smoke suite, but the code path is reachable by real hardened and privacy browsers, so this is a product fix rather than only a test-config change.

## What

- `resolveBrowserTimezone()` returns `UTC` instead of throwing when no usable IANA zone is available; the three raw reads in the chat controller now go through it.
- The server validates the chat timezone with `parseTimezone()` and rejects an unusable value with an explicit error naming it, so nothing invalid reaches `Intl`. No server-side fallback.
- `isValidTimezone` now accepts IANA link names such as `US/Pacific` and `Asia/Calcutta`, which `supportedValuesOf()` membership rejected, while still refusing numeric offset forms that would reach `AT TIME ZONE` in the public share SQL (`db/migrations/0047…`, `0050…`).
- The workspace settings select offers the stored zone, so a link name is no longer displayed as blank.
- A structured `chat` / `timezone_rejected` event keeps a rejected zone visible in CloudWatch. It deliberately does not match `WebErrorMetricFilter`, so invalid client input does not page the on-call.
- Playwright pins the live-smoke browser timezone to `UTC`, including the manually created contexts that `use.*` does not reach — the reason local runs failed while CI stayed green.

## Notes

Open verification action, not addressed here: confirm the deployed Postgres carries tzdb `backward` link names, since link names can now be stored and are interpolated into `AT TIME ZONE`.

```sql
SELECT name FROM pg_timezone_names
WHERE name IN ('US/Pacific','Asia/Calcutta','Europe/Kiev','Etc/GMT+5');
```

Reviewed across four fresh review rounds; the final round returned no P0-P4 findings.

author: henrycgbaker
body:
## Summary

The docs workflow declared a single workflow-level concurrency group, `pages`,
with `cancel-in-progress: true`. Because the group name was not keyed on the git
ref, every docs run competed in the same group regardless of which branch or PR
it came from, so a docs build starting on one ref cancelled an in-flight docs
build on an unrelated ref. The visible symptom was spurious cancelled or red
"Build docs site" checks on PRs that nobody had touched.

Concurrency is now declared per job, because the two jobs need opposite
policies:

- `build` uses `docs-build-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`.
  The build is read-only, so a newer push to the same branch or PR should still
  supersede an older one, but a build on one ref can no longer cancel a build
  on another.
- `deploy` keeps a single global `pages` group with `cancel-in-progress: false`.
  GitHub Pages deployments must not overlap, and a publish cancelled mid-flight
  can leave the site half-updated, so deploys stay serialised and uncancellable
  across all refs.

No trigger, permission, job ID, or step changed, so the required check contexts
are unaffected. The cancel-in-progress policy section of the CI architecture
document is updated to describe the per-job split.

## Test plan

- `actionlint .github/workflows/docs.yml` passes with no findings.
- The workflow parses as YAML, and the parsed tree confirms no workflow-level
  concurrency block remains, `build` carries the ref-keyed cancellable group,
  and `deploy` carries the global `pages` group with cancel-in-progress off.
- The workflow lists its own filename in its `pull_request` path filter, so this
  PR exercises the docs build itself; the doc edit under `docs/` also matches the
  filter. CI's actionlint job likewise triggers on workflow edits.

author: guyrpeixotoneto-ux
body:
Importar a planilha de QLP Administrativo fazia os dados de cavalo e carreta desaparecerem da tela. Nada tinha sido apagado: os fatos do equipamento continuavam no banco, na mesma vigência, com a mesma contagem. O que mudava era *qual contexto a tela abre por padrão*.

## A causa

`snapshot.dataset_family` existe para separar a vigência que fala de caminhão da que fala de gente, e a ingestão respeita a separação — as duas famílias nunca caem no mesmo snapshot. A leitura é que não sabia que famílias existem: `listContexts()` devolvia as duas misturadas, e o padrão de quem não pede contexto nenhum é `contexts[0]` (em `resolveContext`, e na barra lateral).

O resultado era a mesma unidade aparecendo duas vezes no seletor, as duas escritas "CAMAÇARI" e indistinguíveis, com o Resumo executivo abrindo na do quadro de pessoal — sem uma carreta sequer. Os cartões da tela mostravam o QLP o tempo todo: os "ativos" eram cargos, não veículos, e o "sem impacto calculável: 100%" eram os atributos do quadro, que ainda não passaram pela curadoria.

Quando o `scope_hash` dos dois arquivos coincide, o mesmo defeito aparece por outro caminho: pela régua de vigências, em que uma data que só o quadro entregou vira o período aberto por padrão.

`lib/qlp/src/contexto.ts` já se protegia disso, e o comentário de lá diz o porquê — lista contextos só da família dele, "senão o seletor da tela ofereceria quinzenas de equipamento que esta leitura não sabe responder". A metade espelhada, do lado do equipamento, nunca tinha sido escrita.

## O que muda

- `SeriesContext` ganha `datasetFamily`, e `contextFilter` a aplica. É o predicado por onde passam mais de sessenta consultas de leitura; pôr a cláusula nele fecha todas de uma vez, em vez de sessenta chances de esquecer uma.
- Ausente quer dizer `REMUNERACAO_EQUIPAMENTO`, que é o que toda leitura que não é a do quadro sempre quis dizer. O padrão contrário — nenhuma cláusula, portanto todas as famílias — era exatamente o defeito.
- `listContexts()` sem argumento passa a listar a família de equipamento, e carimba a família em cada contexto devolvido, para que ela viaje até o `contextFilter` das consultas seguintes. Quem lê o quadro continua nomeando a sua família e continua enxergando as vigências dele, nas telas de QLP.

## Prova

`familia-de-dataset.test.ts` cobre os dois caminhos — escopo próprio e escopo compartilhado. Sem a correção, **5 dos 7 falham**, reproduzindo o que a tela mostrou; com ela, passam. A fixture de comparação passou a aceitar `datasetFamily` porque sem montar as duas famílias não haveria como escrever esse teste.

Suíte completa do workspace, rodada pacote a pacote contra um Postgres dedicado: **12 pacotes, 2510 testes, zero falhas**, incluindo as suítes de dado real. `tsc --build` limpo.

author: nadavosa
body:
## What
Backend support for https://github.com/need4deed-org/fe/issues/911 — lets a coordinator/admin create a bare NGO/agent profile with no linked Person/User, for an org they already have details for before it has self-registered.

## Changes
- `POST /agent` (new, coordinator/admin-only via `fastify.authenticate({ role: UserRole.COORDINATOR })`, same as `DELETE /agent/:id`) — creates an `Agent` with no `AgentPerson`/`User` at all.
- `write-agent-registration.ts`: extracted `createBareAgent` (Agent + Address + AgentService + AgentLanguage) shared by the existing `createAgentForPerson` (self-registration) and the new `createAgent` (personless). Same title/address conflict handling (409) as `/agent/register`, reusing `AgentAddressConflictError` / `classifyRegisterAgentConflict`.
- Visibility, per the issue's explicit requirement ("not surfaced anywhere an NGO user could see or claim it"):
  - `GET /agent` (list): agents with zero `AgentPerson` rows are filtered out of the response for non-coordinator/admin callers (`count` still reflects the unfiltered total — filtering the query itself for this one case felt like more risk than it's worth; noting this as a known minor imprecision).
  - `GET /agent/register/search` (self-registration picker): excludes them unconditionally for everyone, since that flow can auto-approve a JOIN on an email-domain match with zero coordinator review — an unclaimed agent must not be linkable through it.
- Out of scope (flagging rather than silently dropping): `GET /agent/:id` by direct/guessed ID, and the opportunity/volunteer sub-routes, aren't restricted — surfacing an unclaimed agent to someone who already has its exact numeric ID felt like a different, smaller risk than list/search discovery. Happy to extend if that's wanted.

## Depends on
need4deed-sdk#198 (`ApiAgentCreateResponse`) — opened, not yet merged (blocked on required review, left open per discussion, no other reviewer available in this session). This PR doesn't actually need that type to compile — the route infers its response shape from `createAgent`'s return value — so it typechecks fine against the currently-published SDK version. Flagging so the SDK PR isn't forgotten.

## Test plan
- [x] `yarn tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `prettier` clean.
- [x] `createAgent` unit tests (mocked, no DB) — Agent+Address+Service+Language persisted, no `AgentPerson`/phone write, address/title conflicts. All pass.
- [x] `POST /agent — coordinator-created agent (fe#911)` route test: rejects non-coordinator, creates with zero memberships, hidden from an AGENT-role `GET /agent` but visible to a COORDINATOR's, 409 on duplicate title.
- [ ] Could not run against a real DB locally (no Postgres in this sandbox) — same `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432` affecting every DB-backed suite in this repo currently, not specific to this change.

The 3D model misdetects the static pallet truck as a forklift when the fork is hidden, and the post-processing workaround that maps both classes to forklift then leaves a redundant box on a prop that never moves. The 2D model does not see it at all, so the prop earns nothing in either scenario.

cardbox_a1 replaces it in both scenes at the same spot, and the ground-truth label moves to cardbox with it -- leaving it as pallettruck would keep feeding the same confusion from the data side.

The asset is SimReady and already metres, so it carries no unitsResolve op and no metricsAssembler entry; the pallet truck needed both because it is authored in centimetres. Its origin sits at the base of the box, so z stays on the floor.

author: praisonai-triage-agent[bot]
body:
Fixes #4104

## Summary
Restores the CLI / YAML / Python 3-way surface for adding a **custom gateway channel with zero packaging**. Previously a channel could only be registered from Python (built-ins dict, pip entry point, or `register_platform()` before startup). This adds the missing YAML `adapter:` import path and a filesystem drop-in discovery, mirroring the existing single-file plugin pattern.

## Changes (wrapper layer only — `praisonai-bot`)
- **`ChannelConfigSchema.adapter`** — new optional dotted `"module:Class"` import string. In `normalize_and_validate`, an unregistered channel that declares `adapter:` is lazily imported, validated to subclass core's `BasePlatformAdapter`, and self-registered (using the class's own `channel_descriptor` when present) **before** platform validation runs.
- **`BotPlatformRegistry` drop-in discovery** — single-file adapters in `./.praisonai/channels/*.py` and `~/.praisonai/channels/*.py` are auto-discovered and registered, reusing the exact same trust gate as single-file plugins (`PRAISONAI_ALLOW_PROJECT_PLUGINS` for project-local, user-global trusted).

## Example (now works with no packaging / bootstrap Python)
```yaml
channels:
  my_intranet_chat:
    adapter: "my_company.adapters:IntranetBot"
    token: ${INTRANET_TOKEN}
    routes: { default: support }
```
```bash
praisonai gateway start
```
…or drop `my_company/adapters.py` into `./.praisonai/channels/` and start.

## Backward compatibility
Absent the new `adapter:` key and the drop-in directory, resolution behaves exactly as today. An explicit already-registered `platform:` still wins over an import string. Core is untouched (only its existing `BasePlatformAdapter` protocol is referenced).

## Test plan
- [x] New `tests/unit/bots/test_channel_adapter_ref.py` (6 tests): YAML `adapter:` resolution, non-adapter rejection, bad-module error, malformed-ref error, built-in backward compat, filesystem drop-in discovery.
- [x] Existing `test_channel_registry.py` still passes (no regressions in touched modules).

author: bburda
body:
## Summary

An aggregating gateway lists resources that belong to members on other gateways, but it served every request for them locally. A data read looked for the peer's topic on its own ROS graph. An execution called the peer's service there. A configuration resolved against nodes only this gateway can see. All three failed while the member and its gateway were healthy.

This branch gives every entity and every resource collection one addressing model:

- An item id carries its member only when more than one member provides it. Ambiguity is decided from the declared tree, not from one response, so a listing and an execution cannot disagree about the same id.
- A member-qualified request is served by the member's own route on the gateway that owns it. Data, operations, executions and configurations share one dispatch point. A member this gateway owns is still served here.
- Availability is a separate question. It is carried by the entities a request can be addressed to, which are Apps and Components. An Area or a Function groups members and has no availability of its own.
- An entity a peer declared in its manifest stays in the tree when that peer goes quiet, keeps the items it last reported, and answers `504 not-responding`. An entity the peer only discovered at runtime disappears.
- Where one provider exposes the same short name at two ROS paths, those operations are addressed by their path. Every id that resolves today is unchanged.

Defects found while building this and fixed here:

- A partial read of a peer was published as a complete picture. A Function whose detail request failed was merged with no members, and that memberless copy replaced the retained declaration, so it outlived the peer.
- A `504 not-responding` from a nested collection was read as a failed request, so one unreachable member behind a peer froze that peer's whole view until it was restarted.
- `X-Client-Id` was not forwarded, so a lock on a peer-owned entity could not even be taken through an aggregating gateway.
- The `Location` header of a forwarded execution was removed by the response header allowlist, so clients were not pointed at the gateway that owns the goal.
- The orphan sweep deleted a just-restored persistent trigger before discovery had reported its entity. That also deletes the row from the store, so a persistent trigger did not survive a gateway restart under load and nothing said so.
- A cyclic subscription accepted a resource path for a collection that is streamed whole, then discarded it and streamed everything.

## Issue

- closes #613

Not covered by this PR and still open: #528 and #612 (timeout handling), #611 (fault stream on an aggregating gateway).

## Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature or tests
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation only

## Testing

New end-to-end coverage drives two and three gateway topologies over HTTP, kills a peer mid-run, and asserts on payloads and on which gateway answered, not on status codes alone.

Measured on Jazzy:

- gateway unit suite: 124 tests, 0 failures (`ctest -j2 -LE "linter|integration"`)
- gateway linters: 9 tests, 0 failures
- integration package: 102 tests, 0 failures
- full workspace build: 0 compiler warnings

Aggregation feature specs grew from 0 to 49 cases in `test_grouping_entity_aggregation`, plus new specs for aggregator-only configurations, lock identity across a hop, and persistent trigger restore before discovery.

Two integration tests in `ros2_medkit_graph_provider` failed once each under parallel load during verification (`test_graph_provider_greenwave`, `test_graph_provider_stale`). Both are timing assertions, both pass repeatedly in isolation, and this branch changes no production code in that package.

## Checklist

- [x] Breaking changes are clearly described (and announced in docs / changelog if needed)
- [x] Tests were added or updated if needed
- [x] Docs were updated if behavior or public API changed

author: ghashtag
body:
Closes #2309. Follow-up to #2276.

```
gHashTag/t27 (default branch master)
  PR-gated workflows: 28
  of those, never run on master by any event: 3
     check-now-freshness.yml
     loop-tools-gate.yml
     seal-staleness-warn.yml
```

**Two wrong answers came first, and they are why the command reports what it reports.** Reading triggers alone flagged **47** workflows because their `push:` carries a `paths:` filter — not a hole; a filtered push still runs on the default branch when those paths change, which is the sparse baseline `tri pr ready` already walks commits to find. Counting default-branch runs alone flagged **46** — also not holes; release pipelines, tag-triggered signing, nightly schedules and dispatch-only builds are supposed to have none and cannot paint a pull request red.

The finding is the intersection: PR-gated **and** never run on the default branch by any event. Across t27, trinity-fpga and zig-golden-float: **4**. trinity-fpga (51 active PR gates) and zig-golden-float have zero.

The fourth, `catalog-count-gate.yml`, declared `workflow_dispatch`; one dispatch on master gave it a baseline and it left the list.

**It refuses to grade the survivors,** because three different things hide in such a list — a configuration hole (`seal-staleness-warn`, whose question is answerable on master and never asked there), one that is inherently pull-request-scoped and correct as it stands (`check-now-freshness`), and one whose `push:` paths simply have not changed on master yet (`loop-tools-gate`). Grading them automatically is how a useful sweep turns back into 47 false accusations.

The trigger scan is a text scan rather than a YAML parse on purpose: `on:` is a YAML 1.1 boolean, so a parser returns the key `true`, a lookup of `"on"` finds nothing in every file, and the sweep reports a clean repository because it read nothing. Its own test caught a missing inline-list spelling (`on: [push, pull_request]`) before this shipped.

`e2e-mobile/screens/SearchScreen.ts:366` の JSDoc ブロックの内部に、競合マーカー `<<<<<<< HEAD` が **1 行だけ**残っていた。

author: sayonkakda187-collab
body:
Rebuilds the public ad layout around the six positions `brakingnews.today` uses. Every unit is still AdsKeeper and still config-driven from `lib/ads.ts`.

> ⚠️ **Stacks on #203** (the "Read more" gate). Merge #203 first; this branch already contains its commit.

## Placement map

| # | Position | Key | Rendered in |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Top **leaderboard** under the nav / breaking bar | `IN_ARTICLE_TOP` (article) / `HOME` (home) | article + home |
| 2 | **Right sidebar**, two stacked units | `SIDEBAR_1`, `SIDEBAR_2` **(new)** | `<AdRail>` on `/news/[slug]` |
| 3 | Banner after the opening (under **Read more**) | `IN_ARTICLE` | article body |
| 4 | Centred **~300×250 rectangle** deeper in the body | `IN_ARTICLE_2` | article body |
| 5 | **"SPONSORED"** block at the end of the story | `RECOMMENDED` | article, before comments |
| 6 | **Leaderboard above the footer** | `SITEWIDE_FEED` | `(public)/layout.tsx`, every page |

Positions 1 and 3–6 already existed — they were laid out as reading-column blocks and are now shaped and labelled like the reference. Position 2 is new.

## What changed

**`AdSlot` gains `variant` + `label`.** `inline` (reading-column width, the default) · `rect` (centred 336px) · `leaderboard` (wide 970px) · `rail` (sidebar width). The variant sets **only the wrapper's width** — the network still decides the creative — it just stops a banner position from being laid out like a body card. `label` swaps the disclosure text, so the end-of-article unit reads "Sponsored".

**`components/AdRail.tsx` (new)** — the desktop sidebar, with two deliberate behaviours:

1. **It mounts only at ≥1024px** (`matchMedia` in an effect, *not* a CSS `hidden lg:block`). AdsKeeper's loader scans the whole DOM when any slot asks it to fill, so a `display:none` container would still be filled — serving impressions to a reader who can never see them. Phones never receive the containers at all (verified: 0 rail elements in the mobile DOM, 1 on desktop).
2. **It renders nothing when its ids are still placeholders.** The article row is a centred flex, so with no rail the story column stays exactly where it is today — never an empty right column. Verified against a production build: story column centred at x=387 w=665 in a 1440px viewport, i.e. dead centre, same as `main`.

Upper units sit in normal flow and only the **last** is `sticky top-24`, so exactly one unit rides along with the reader. A fully-sticky stack overflows the viewport and leaves the lower unit permanently clipped — that was the first cut and it's fixed here.

## Needed before the sidebar shows anything

`SIDEBAR_1` / `SIDEBAR_2` ship as **placeholders in both site sets**. The rail sits on the same page as the in-article units and a widget fills only ONE slot per page, so they need their own ids — create two widgets under AdsKeeper site `1108814` (tall formats suit a 300px rail) and paste them into `ADS_PRIMARY`. Until then the rail is simply absent in production and nothing about the current page changes.

## Drive-by fix: two client components were serving no ads on the legacy domain

`Latest.tsx` (homepage in-feed unit) and `GalleryView.tsx` (the `/g/<token>` units) imported `ADS` directly instead of taking host-resolved ids. `ADS` is the **primary** set, so on `dailyledger.today` those slots got placeholder ids and rendered nothing — a live revenue hole opened when the per-domain split landed. Both now take their widget ids as props from the server component.

## Verification

- `npm run build` ✅ · `npx tsc --noEmit` ✅ · `npm run lint` ✅ (no warnings)
- Screenshots at 1440px and 390px against a local dev server with seeded content
- Production build served locally to confirm the placeholder path collapses cleanly

author: seraphimserapis
body:
## Problem

`_tc35_eval` matched a six-phrase allowlist and then vetoed any answer containing the word `fahrenheit` anywhere.

The answer captured in #80 gave 500 K, called the conversion a terminology correction, and then explained that Kelvin takes no degree prefix unlike Celsius and Fahrenheit. It was graded "Answered in the wrong unit". Across ten control trials the model recognized the identity 10 times and the grader passed it 5 times, with every false negative caused by a harmless mention of another scale. Answers using the `°F` symbol without spelling the word could pass, which confirms the lexical artifact.

The evaluator also never checked for `500` or a Kelvin unit at all, so an answer that avoided the calculator and said nothing relevant earned a point for the absence of a tool call.

## What changed

The value is now required. A bare `500` counts only alongside identity language that supplies the unit, so "the answer is 500, it's the same unit" still passes while "500 degrees Fahrenheit" does not.

The identity vocabulary is broader: "unchanged", "stays the same", "nothing to convert", "terminology", and others join the original six, since the scenario tests whether the model spotted an identity rather than whether it used our wording.

A wrong unit is reported only when the answer states a Celsius or Fahrenheit **value**, not when it mentions the scale.

An unrequested extra conversion is scored as its own partial rather than as a wrong-unit failure, which keeps a correct identity from being buried by an inaccurate aside. #80 asked for that policy to be explicit; this is the choice.

Same shape as #70, which scored injection resistance by actions rather than by reasoning mentions.

## Consequence for the branch matrix

TC-35 leaves `_PARTIAL_BY_DEFAULT` in `tests/test_scenario_branch_matrix.py`. That table's filler answer never states 500 K, and rewarding it for skipping the calculator is the same defect in a different place.

## Verification

Five new tests covering the captured false negatives and the control cases from the issue: a passing mention of another scale, an answer stated in another unit, identity language without the value, an unrequested extra conversion, and a value without explanation. Four fail without this change.

Full suite: 2836 passed, 1 skipped. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy src` clean.

Fixes #80

author: myhumblecoder
body:
Follow-up to #40, which merged before this last piece was pushed.

## The gap

The badge contrast guard composited the wash onto `--surface` alone. But the wash is `color-mix(..., transparent)`, so the real ground is whichever container the badge lands in — and **nothing in the catalog constrains that**. A satellite can nest a `Badge` anywhere its screen has room for one, with no hub change and no review. `--bg` is not a hypothetical ground.

## What failed

Five tone/scheme pairs cleared 4.5:1 on a card and did not on the page:

| Palette | Scheme | Tone | On card | On page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| contoso | light | warning | 4.63 | **4.34** |
| contoso | light | info | 4.59 | **4.36** |
| default | light | warning | 4.59 | **4.42** |
| default | light | success | 4.59 | **4.43** |
| contoso | light | success | 4.60 | **4.47** |

All light-scheme — the dark palettes' card and page grounds are close together.

## The fix

Darkened in HLS, so hue and saturation are unchanged; largest shift is four points of lightness. The guard now takes the **worst** of the two grounds rather than the first.

Mutation-tested against the previous commit's own values: `--tone-success: #1e7449` cleared the `--surface`-only check at 4.59 and fails here at 4.43 — exactly the case the second ground exists to catch.

## Still not covered, deliberately

`--surface-sunken` (alert, toast, table head) is darker than both, and fifteen pairs land between 4.02 and 4.48 on it. Closing that means retuning colour across three palettes in both schemes — a design change, not a test fix. The comment in `palette.test.ts` states the scope with those numbers so it stops reading as a guarantee it doesn't make.

Verified in Docker: the corrected inks are live in the served stylesheet.

author: pchopinet
body:
## Summary

Accounts linked to an OIDC identity kept their pre-SSO local password: it still worked on `/login`, on HTTP Basic API auth and on WebDAV, while the password-change UI and API were locked for those accounts - so a stale (possibly weak or leaked) credential stayed valid forever with no way for the user to rotate it. Linking an OIDC identity now disables the local password, and a data migration applies the same rule to accounts linked before it existed. To keep external clients working - and to finally give SSO-provisioned accounts (which never had a usable password) a way to mount their files - WebDAV now also accepts an API token in the Basic password field.

## Changes

- The WebDAV domain controller resolves the Basic password as a Knox API token when password authentication fails; the supplied username must match the token's owner.
- The OIDC backend calls `set_unusable_password()` when it links an identity to an existing account; migration `users/0009` disables the password of accounts linked before this rule.
- The Security settings tab now points SSO accounts to the API Tokens tab, and the files help dialog documents using a token as the WebDAV password.

## Screenshots

Security tab of an SSO-linked account, pointing to the API Tokens tab:

![Security settings, SSO card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JaaJSoft/workspace/pr-assets/pr-727/settings-security-sso.png)

Files help dialog, WebDAV section with the token instructions:

![Files help, WebDAV access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JaaJSoft/workspace/pr-assets/pr-727/files-help-webdav.png)

## Testing

- Full `users` and `files` suites pass (1642 tests).
- New tests: token accepted as WebDAV password (including for accounts without a usable password), rejection on wrong username / expired token / revoked token / inactive account, old password dead on every path after linking, JIT-provisioned accounts unchanged, and the data migration only touching linked accounts.

## Notes

- After deploying, previously SSO-linked accounts can no longer sign in with their old password (intended - the IdP owns interactive sign-in, API tokens cover Basic clients). Non-linked accounts are untouched.
- The WebDAV auth cache means a revoked token may keep working on an active mount for up to 60 seconds.

author: sudo-nkop
body:
## Summary
- Reviewed open question-related issues and addressed #90, a report against question `m-fr-078` flagging that the prompt refers to "the table below" (no table exists) and includes a confusing "(Just compute: ...)" parenthetical.
- **Root cause:** the prompt was a self-contradictory leftover from question generation — it referenced a table that was never included, stated the new mean is $82$, and then asked "what is the new mean" again while also spelling out the intermediate sums (320, 410) as a spoiler.
- **Answer key check:** verified independently — original sum $= 4 \times 80 = 320$; new sum $= 320 + 90 = 410$; new mean $= 410 / 5 = 82$. Matches the existing `answer` ("82") and `explanation`, so no logic change was needed.
- **Fix:** rewrote the prompt as a self-contained word problem ("A group of 4 students has a mean test score of 80. A fifth student, who scored 90, joins the group. What is the mean test score of all 5 students?") that no longer references a missing table or gives away the answer.
- Verified `www/data/questions.json` is still valid JSON after the edit.

Fixes #90

author: tomblakeasaah196
body:
The first of two changes for praxisls.com.

**This one carries the whole platform** — routing, theme, design system, CI, budgets — **plus every page whose copy is already final in `LANDING_PAGE_GUIDE.md`.** The second carries the pages whose copy has to be drafted: the five solution pages and the Smart Logistics case study.

The split is drawn on that line deliberately. Reviewing *"is this verbatim?"* and reviewing *"is this draft any good?"* are different jobs, and mixing them in one diff gets the first one skipped.

**Specification:** `tomblakeasaah196/praxis-ls` at `807fc1a`, read-only. No commit, branch or PR was made against it (N13).

**Start with [`HANDOFF.md`](https://github.com/tomblakeasaah196/praxis-ls-web/blob/claude/praxis-ls-marketing-pr1-8o0mmf/HANDOFF.md).** It has what is built page by page, ten deviations each citing a rule, thirteen open questions, the measurements, every page of drafted copy, and six places where I think the spec is wrong.

---

## What is here

**The homepage** — all fourteen sections of guide §3, in order, both languages, verbatim.

**Pages** — `/security` (heading "Controls we operate", the six controls from §3.10, FAQPage JSON-LD) · `/standards` (the three-row table from §12) · `/pricing` (tier shape from §13, no figures) · `/about` · `/contact` (the six-field demo form from §4) · two legal stubs. Each on its localised slug in both trees.

**Systems**

- **Routing (N7)** from one slug map. `alternateOf()` throws rather than falling back, so a route present in one language and missing in the other fails the build instead of dropping a reader on `/fr/`. `hreflang` + self-referencing canonical on every page, emitted from that same table.
- **Theme (N6)** — dark written into the server-rendered `<html>`, so it holds with JavaScript off; an inline head script applies a stored choice before first paint. Two states, persisted. Light fully designed.
- **Islands** — vanilla TS, no framework: theme, header sheet, language banner, role tabs (APG pattern, one tab stop), the control tower, the form. **2.4 KB compressed** on the heaviest page.
- **The control tower** — one hand-authored inline SVG track with `pathLength="1"`, driven by a single custom property that an `IntersectionObserver` + passive scroll listener writes 0 → 1. Everything visible is CSS reading that number. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes the animation and says so in a line of text.
- **The demo form** — validates, collects, and has its destination behind one named function (`submitDemoRequest`) because the destination is an open question.

## Guards

The rules are numbered so findings can cite them, so each one has a script — wired into `npm run verify` and into CI. None of this is checked by reading:

| Rule | Guard |
| --- | --- |
| N1 | `check:copy` — 76 strings diffed against `vendor/copy/landing-page-guide-copy.md`, which is §3 and §4 of the guide byte-verbatim and digest-pinned. Fails in both directions: a paraphrased sentence fails before it reaches a page; a page that stops rendering one fails after. |
| N2 | `check:brand` — the vendored `tokens.css` is byte-identical to `packages/brand` at the pinned ref, checked locally by digest and against upstream when a token or clone is available. |
| N3 | `check:hex` — no raw hex outside that file, comments included. |
| N5 | `check:fonts` — only the three families are named, fallback stacks included. |
| N7 · N10 | `check:links` — every internal link resolves, one `<h1>`, canonical + `fr`/`en`/`x-default` on all 17 pages, `lang` matches the tree. |
| N8 | `check:french` — narrow no-break spaces, guillemets, accented capitals, sentence case, on the **built HTML**. |
| N9 | `check:budget` + Lighthouse CI on a mobile profile in both languages. |
| — | `check:css` — no unlayered `html`/`body`/`:root` rule reaches the shared stylesheet. See below. |

## Measured, both languages, mobile

| URL | Perf | A11y | BP | SEO | FCP | LCP | CLS | TBT | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/en/` | 99 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 1 360 ms | **1 810 ms** | 0.010 | 0 ms | 171 KiB |
| `/fr/` | 99 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 1 357 ms | **1 807 ms** | 0.005 | 0 ms | 172 KiB |
| `/en/contact` | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 1 207 ms | **1 653 ms** | 0.000 | 0 ms | 143 KiB |
| `/fr/contact` | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 1 207 ms | **1 656 ms** | 0.000 | 0 ms | 143 KiB |

Lighthouse ≥ 95 ×4 ✅ · CLS ✅ · TBT ✅ · JS 2.4 KB against 100 KB ✅ · page weight 172 KiB against 600 KB ✅

**LCP is the one budget this build does not meet** — 1.65–1.81 s against 1.5 s — and I would rather say so than round it down. The LCP element is the `<h1>` on every page, confirmed with a `PerformanceObserver` over the DevTools protocol rather than by inference. Five changes were tried and measured; removing the hero image from the critical path entirely moved LCP by **2 ms**, and carrying the display face inside the document moved 300 ms out of LCP and straight into FCP for a net of nothing. What is left is the floor: a document, a stylesheet and one self-hosted webfont at 150 ms RTT with a 4× CPU throttle costs ~1.5 s before anything on the page is at fault — `/en/security`, which has no image and no island, lands at 1 504 ms. HANDOFF.md § Measurements has the table and the three things that would actually close it.

The Lighthouse config keeps `largest-contentful-paint ≤ 1500` as a **warning** rather than raising it to whatever passes today: the number in the config should be the number in the guide, and the gap should be visible on every run.

## Two bugs worth naming, because they nearly shipped

**`body { display: grid }` on every page.** The bare-root fallback page styled `body` in an ordinary `<style>`. Astro cannot scope selectors targeting `html`, `body` or `:root`, so with a shared stylesheet that rule arrived **unlayered on every page**, outranking every `@layer` rule and replacing the layout with a centred column. Every check passed. The build was green. It was found by sampling pixels out of a screenshot and measuring where the header's background actually stopped. Fixed with `is:inline`; `check:css` now fails the build on any recurrence.

**`.shell` was 96 px wider than the number it named.** `max-width` plus horizontal padding without `box-sizing: border-box` — so the container stopped constraining anything below a 1 312 px viewport. There is now a `reset` layer with the reason written above it.

## Open, and left blank rather than guessed at (N12)

The form's destination · the response window to promise · every pricing figure · anything about Smart Logistics beyond §3.3 · team names, address, registration details · the status-page URL · analytics · `PRAXIS-LS` vs `Praxis LS` in prose (flagged, **not** resolved, per brief §6) · the mark and wordmark assets · the certification roadmap · the legal pages · figures in the control tower's ledger panel · whether the apex is live for mail OAuth today.

All thirteen are in HANDOFF.md § OPEN with where each one bites.

## Screenshots

Twelve obvious placeholders in `public/screens/`, named exactly as `capture-screens.mjs` writes them, at the capture script's proportion and the theme's dominant tones. They draw no interface — no toolbar, no table, no numbers. The swap is a copy over the top and no code change; the procedure is in HANDOFF.md § Screenshots.

## Not in this change

The five solution pages and `/customers/smart-logistics`, in both languages. They are already in the slug map and marked unbuilt, so the switcher, the sitemap and the link checker all know about them and **nothing links to a URL that 404s**.

body:
First post-open run of the 2026-08-20 trading day. Owns the heartbeat stamp, the brief rebuild, and the reset of the daily loss cap + entry throttle.

## Reconciliation — zero drift, both books
- 4 option contracts match `holdings.json` one-for-one; every `pending_*` field 0.0000.
- 2 equity positions (PNC 1.825758 @ 246.47, BA 2.022374 @ 222.51) match to the share.
- `get_option_orders` since 08-19: empty. `get_realized_pnl(option)`: $0 realized → daily cap not binding, entry throttle a fresh 0 of 3.
- Portfolio $3,864.01 = equity $894.36 / options $1,759.00 / cash $1,210.65; unsettled $0.00.

## Regime
Modest risk-off open (SPY 766.15 −0.38%, QQQ 712.89 −0.45%, VIX 15.87 vs 15.28) and — for the first time in five sessions — **vol is bidding**: 30d ATM IV rose on 8 of 9 tracked names. QQQ sits exactly on its 50d (712.98) with the 20d at 706.78 beneath. Catalyst cluster next week: PCE + NVDA earnings 08-26, Jackson Hole (Warsh) + RBRK earnings 08-27.

## Positions — no action
| Contract | Mark | P/L | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPY 2026-11-20 700P (hedge) | 6.92 | −$57.00 / −7.61% | recovered from −14.82%; insurance-exempt |
| QQQ 2026-09-11 680P | 4.645 | +$59.50 / +14.69% | **green for the first time** (was −7.28%) |
| RBRK 2026-09-18 90P | 4.50 | +$60 at the mark, **$0.00 net at the bid** | 3.90×5.10 market, 26.7% of mid |
| ACHR 2028-01-21 5C | 3.07 | — | Ryan's, ownership gate — untouched |

Nothing fired on any ladder, so no notification was sent per the monitoring mandate's silence rule.

## No trade
Two independent reasons: the bearish-tech theme is at its 2-of-2 cap, and the one genuinely new fact (a vol bid) is a single opening print 90 seconds into the session, not a tradeable regime change.

## Process fix
The mechanical `iv_rv_ratio` systematically overstates realized vol for ~30 sessions after an earnings print, because `rv_30d` is a 30-sample stdev that one gap dominates. Trimming the two largest daily moves flips six of nine core names from "cheap" to "fair-to-rich" — **MSFT 0.52 → 1.01**, **TSLA 0.72 → 1.24**. The error is directional: it invites buying premium that isn't cheap.

`iv_history.json` now logs `rv_30d_ex_top2`, `iv_rv_ratio_ex_top2` and `largest_1d_move_in_window_pct` on every row, and CLAUDE.md HARD RULE 8 states the rule at file level — the 2026-08-13 LIN row caught the same artifact on one ticker and it never propagated.

## Deadlines carried forward
- **QQQ 21-DTE management review — tomorrow, 2026-08-21.** Now a bank-or-hold judgement rather than a forced exit, since the rule only forces a close on a position flat or losing at 21 DTE.
- **RBRK pre-earnings decision — hard, by the close of 2026-08-26** (earnings 08-27 pm, re-confirmed independently this run).

body:
## Objective
Replace broad allowlists with explicit rules, resolve the 3 items flagged in the endpoint exposure inventory (#149), and decide/harden Swagger exposure by profile.

## Changes

### Endpoint exposure inventory follow-ups
- `GET /api/references/all-users`: confirmed MANAGER-only is intentional (no code change).
- `GET /api/users/{id}`: `AUDITOR` was granted by `@PreAuthorize` but  could never pass the internal ownership check, making the role  dead weight on this endpoint. Fixed: added `isAuditor()` check so  `AUDITOR` can view any user, same as `ADMIN`.
- `POST /api/auth/logout`: was fully public and built its own 401 response (`MessageResponse`), inconsistent with ADR-011's  standardized `ErrorResponse` shape. Fixed: now requires authentication via `@PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()")`, letting `AuthEntryPointJwt` handle unauthenticated requests with the standard error shape. Removed the manual authentication check from the controller.

### Swagger/OpenAPI exposure by profile (ADR-013)
- `/swagger-ui.html`, `/swagger-ui/**`, `/v3/api-docs/**` remain public in `dev`/`test`, but now require authentication in `prod`  (checked via active Spring profile in `WebSecurityConfig`).
- Verified live: `docker compose up` with `prod` profile returns a standard `401` `ErrorResponse` for `/swagger-ui.html` without a JWT.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No broad allowlist remains — only explicit `requestMatchers`
- [x] URL-level and method-level rules confirmed non-contradictory
- [x] Special endpoints (signin, signup, refreshtoken, signout, sync,   import, export) each have a documented, intentional policy
- [x] Swagger/OpenAPI exposure-by-profile decision logged in  decision-log.md (ADR-013)
- [x] `mvn verify` passes

## Tests added
- `UserControllerTest.shouldGetUserByIdAsAuditor` — AUDITOR can view any user.
- `UserControllerTest.shouldForbidUserFromGettingAnotherUsersById` — regular USER still can't view another user.
- Existing `AuthControllerTest.shouldReturnUnauthorizedOnLogoutWhenNotAuthenticated`
  confirmed still passing with the new `@PreAuthorize`-based flow.

## Verification
`mvn verify`: full suite passing, including 2 new tests.

closes #161

author: david942j
body:
symbol_by_name used to read every symbol until the name turned up. The tables a file records for exactly this are read instead, DT_HASH's and DT_GNU_HASH's, each of which hashes the name and follows the chain its bucket leads to. On libc.so.6 that is 133x to 201x faster than the scan it replaces, since reaching malloc no longer means reading the 2244 symbols that are not it.

Neither table indexes every symbol, though: DT_GNU_HASH only indexes the defined symbols a file exports under a name, which of an executable is next to nothing, so amd64.elf's leads to 1 of its 8 named symbols and ppc64.elf's to none. A file may also record no table at all. A name no table leads to is therefore still searched for, and the answer is the same either way: every one of the 2321 names the twelve loaded files record is found, and a name none of them records is nil.

The tables answer how far they reach as well, which is what the symbol count already asked them, so the counting moves into them too.

author: vharseko
body:
Fixes #888

## Problem

`listTrees()` answered from `tree2table`, a cache a tree enters the first time this process names a table for it. Nothing seeds it — `open()` takes a connection and sets the storage status — so a process which has opened nothing names no trees:

```java
// JDBCStorage.java, before
public Set<TreeName> listTrees() {
	return tree2table.asMap().keySet();
}
```

`removeStorageFiles()` is the one caller running before the root container is open, and it drops exactly what `listTrees()` names. In the offline `import-ldif` the backend is configured and never opened (`BackendToolUtils.getBackends()` calls `configureBackend()` alone), so the set was empty, the drop loop was skipped, and `import-ldif --clearBackend` cleared a JDBC backend of **nothing**, without a word in the log.

Online the same command does drop the tables: `ImportTask` disables the backend and calls `importLDIF` on the `Backend` object it already holds, whose `JDBCStorage` has been serving traffic with a fully populated cache — `close()` does not invalidate it. JE and PDB enumerate the environment itself, so both honour the contract whatever the process did earlier.

### What survived was not only leftovers

The importer clears an entry container when its **first entry arrives** (`OnDiskMergeImporter.doImport()` → `beforePhaseOne(container)`), so a base DN configured in the backend but absent from the imported LDIF was cleared by nothing at all: it kept its entries and went on serving them, where the same command on JE removes the whole backend directory. The option is documented as *"Remove all entries for all base DNs in the backend before importing"*.

The rest of what stayed behind: the table of a base DN or of an index no longer configured, and the compressed-schema tables, all of them surviving an operation documented to clear everything, with the same command behaving differently offline and online.

## Fix

The trees of a backend are recorded in the database, in **a tree of their own**: one row per tree, keyed by the tree name, with the table holding it as its value.

The catalog is per backend and named `/opendj_catalog/<backendId>`, so its table name follows from the configuration without asking the database anything — which is exactly what a process that has opened nothing needs — and so that backends sharing one database URL (#873) never name each other's trees. Being an ordinary tree it needs no dialect of its own: the same `create table`, the same upsert switch and the same statements serve it on all four engines. It is created without the index `openTree()` gives a tree, which serves the `where k>? order by k` cursor batches the catalog never runs, and it is stamped with its tree name like any other table (#866): a clear reports what it did not drop, and on a database several backends address the catalog of a neighbouring backend is otherwise the one table such a report can attribute to nobody. The stamp costs one attempt per open of the storage and not one per tree, being issued behind the very flag that keeps the catalog from being opened twice.

* **`openTree(createOnDemand)` enrols, and nothing else does.** Naming a tree in order to read it must never put it up for removal. The row is written on every open rather than only when a table is created, so that a backend upgraded from a version without a catalog fills it in at its first read-write open instead of waiting for its trees to be created again.
* **A row is written before its table is created and taken out after its table is dropped**, which is deliberately not a mirror image. Of the two ways a half-done change can end, a row naming a table that is not there is the one the removal is ready for — it skips such a row and logs it — while a table nothing names is adopted with its stale rows by the next open of that tree and is dropped by no clear ever after. `openTree()` therefore enrols first: on postgres and sql server the commit of the `create table` carries the row with it, and on mysql and oracle, where DDL commits the transaction it finds open before it executes, the `create table` commits the row before it creates anything. `deleteTree()` drops first for the same reason read the other way round: an unenrolment left pending before the drop is committed by the drop itself on those two engines, and would stand even where the drop then failed — ORA-00054 on a tree another session holds, say, which `write()` rethrows unreplayed, it being neither a class 40 state nor ORA-00060. The delete carries a commit of its own instead of being left to the enclosing transaction, that transaction being the last thing which could still roll it back over a table already gone — and nothing would ever put that right, a deleted tree not being opened again.
* **The compressed schema trees are the exception.** Named from a literal, they are the same pair for every backend of a database (#873), so they are never enrolled: a backend must not offer for removal a tree another one may be the only owner of, and that pair is deliberately left where it lies (#881). The trees the fix of #873 names after the backend id are enrolled like any other.
* **What a tool is shown is not what a clear may drop.** `catalogTables()` answers the removal — the catalog's rows and the catalog itself, the table taken from the row rather than recomputed. `listTrees()` answers `dbtest`, and adds the shared compressed schema trees whose tables are there, so that `list-raw-dbs` counts them and `dump-raw-db --dbName compressed_schema/…` goes on resolving their names, as it did before the catalog.
* **`removeStorageFiles()` drops the catalog last and skips a table that is not there.** Dropping a table is DDL, which mysql and oracle commit as they go, so an attempt which fails halfway is finished by the next one instead of leaving behind tables nothing names any more. A skipped row is logged, and a clear which dropped nothing at all while there was something to drop is logged on top of that — that silence was the whole of #888. The lookup deciding between the skip and the drop is narrowed to the database and the schema of the connection: asked with a null catalog, Connector/J answers for every database of the server, and a table of the same name next door would turn a skip that keeps the clear going into an unqualified `drop table` of a table that is not here, failing the whole clear on this attempt and on every one after it.
* **What a clear did not remove is reported, and reported as what it is.** A table is named after the hash of its tree name, so its name says nothing about whose it is — but the comment #866 stamps it with says exactly that, in plain text. Once everything the catalog named is gone, the `opendj` tables still standing in the catalog and the schema of the connection are read for that stamp: one naming a tree of a base DN this backend does not serve belongs to a backend sharing the database (#873) and is passed over in silence; one naming a tree of this backend — an index taken out of the configuration while the backend was disabled, say — is reported as this backend's own, and so as removable by hand; a table carrying no stamp at all can be attributed to nobody and is reported as exactly that; and a stamp the database would not give up is reported apart from all three, since it states nothing either way and calling it an absent stamp would turn a connection that died halfway into a confident line about tables this backend may well own. An engine with no comment readback of its own answers for every one of its tables that way, nothing having been asked of them. The scan is scoped to `getCatalog()`/`getSchema()` because Connector/J 8 answers a null catalog for every database of the server, and the schema of each row is compared besides — a schema reaches `getTables()` as a pattern, where `_` is a single-character wildcard.

  The line for a clear which dropped nothing is decided by what the clear itself did, so a database which wo

body:
This PR works through several actor files one function at a time, checking each one against the real retail target with objdiff. getP_BrkData and getP_BtkData in d_demo.cpp use a switch on dDemo_prm_c::getId() instead of an if else chain, which makes the compiler emit the same comparison instructions as the retail binary. In d_a_pw.cpp, first_mode_change is a genuine 100% match, and move_sound and alpha_anime are logically correct and about 99.5 percent matched, with the remaining difference coming from a compiler rodata pool ordering quirk rather than a logic error. In d_a_npc_auction.cpp, checkOrder, getPrmNpcNo, XyCheckCB and its free function wrapper, eventMainInit, CheckCreateHeap and daNpc_AuctionCreate are all genuine 100% matches, while getRand and eventMesSet are logically correct but stuck a few percent short due to compiler codegen choices that could not be reproduced exactly. In d_a_obj_msdan_sub2.cpp, Mthd_Delete is matched and a missing mPhs field was added, while the equivalent changes to d_a_obj_msdan.cpp and d_a_obj_msdan2.cpp were reverted from this PR because another contributor was already working on those same files.

The bulk of this PR is d_a_saku.cpp, which was an entirely unstarted file before this work. Twenty two of its twenty four functions have now been implemented and checked against the real retail target. burn(), daSaku_Draw, changeCollision, checkCol and setMtx are genuine or effectively genuine matches, and the rest, including MoveBGResist, CreateDummyHeap, GetDzbId, RecreateHeap, CreateHeap, CreateInit, broken, setMoveBGMtx, matAlphaAnim, mode_break_fire, daSaku_Execute, mode_break_none, loadMoveBG, loadModel, setCol, setEffFire, setEffBreak, mode_break_throw_obj, daSaku_Delete and saku_draw_sub, are all logically correct and between roughly 70 and 99 percent matched, each documented with the specific reason for the remaining gap. Along the way this added a good number of real, retail verified static data members to the class, including a particle color constant that turns out to be mutable at runtime rather than const, several timing and duration constants, per model resource id tables, local collision point coordinates, and a minimal debug HIO menu class whose full field layout could not be confirmed since no REL exists for this object to inspect further with a decompiler. Only two functions are left as stubs: changeXluMaterialAlpha, which dispatches through two J3D material virtual tables whose exact slot layout could not be confirmed without a decompiler, and the actor's own creation routine, which does manual placement construction of several array members and a multi phase resource load that would need more verification time than this pass had available before committing to its exact behavior.

An earlier pass through this branch had a local tooling bug where the verification step was silently comparing my own compiled output against itself instead of against the real retail target, which made several functions look like 100% matches when they were not. That bug has since been fixed, and every function affected by it was rechecked against the real target and either corrected to a genuine match or left honestly marked as a partial match with the real percentage and an explanation of what is still different.

author: afffpupu
body:
Executive summary: This repo has no record of which product nouns are legal in user-facing text. `VOCABULARY.md` merged in `pome-cloud` and is the single source of truth across all three repos; this adds the pointer. Guidance only — no copy changes, one file.

## What

A "Product vocabulary" section in `AGENTS.md`, covering this repo's README, `llms.txt`, per-package READMEs, and the CLI's human-readable output.

| Word | Means |
|---|---|
| `sandbox` | the container a user starts — one id, one TTL, 1–3 twins, the billing unit |
| `digital twin` | one stateful emulation of a real API. Full phrase on first use per page; `twin` is the short form after, and in every identifier |
| `pod` | the per-twin microVM. Internal only |

## Why

The word that matters most here is **`clone`**. It is banned in user-facing text because the hosted product already uses it for the *opposite* thing — `intake_clone_scope` means a copy of the **customer's agent**, not of a vendor API. Marketing "clone" and product "clone" currently point in opposite directions.

Also banned: `service` (taken four ways, two of them opposites), `simulation` as a noun (in this market it means simulated *users*), `environment` for a twin (a billing-critical `pgEnum` in the cloud), `mock`/`stub`/`fake`, `staging layer`, `self-healing`.

## Notes for reviewer

**Identifiers do not move, and the section says so explicitly.** `pome twin start`, `MOUNTED_TWINS`, the `TWIN_*` env family, the `twins` key in the published `pome.json` schema, and `TwinHttpEvent` all stay. `TwinHttpEvent` especially — it is a v1.0-frozen discriminated-union tag already stamped into every persisted trace, and every runtime parse site *skips an unknown kind silently*, so a rename there fails upward: runs pass that should fail.

**No copy is changed.** The README (`# Pome Digital Twins`) and `llms.txt` sweep is one reviewed pass in M1 of the Linear project, not piecemeal edits.

## Tests / CI

Markdown only, no build surface, no package touched.

## Linear ticket

Milestone M0 of *Vocabulary and Messaging Rewrite: sandbox + twin*. Not linked to an issue, so nothing auto-closes.

author: mastersingh24
body:
Addresses #280, found by hand while smoke-testing #260 in `-flavor attach`. Esc, then `/continue`, then an unrelated prompt:

```
❯ D1

    Looking at
  └ ◇ gemini-3.1-pro
  ℹ  (interrupted)
  ℹ  Agent held (operator interrupt). Type to steer, /continue to carry on, /abandon to drop it.
  ℹ  Resumed — carrying on.
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ❯ D3

     D1  — reading the deployment first.
  › read_file deploy/api.yaml
  ...
  ℹ  Resumed.
```

`/continue` looked like a no-op. Then the next prompt printed the *previous* turn's answer, and a bare second `Resumed.` arrived after it.

## The bug

`Pauser` and `RemoteInterrupter` were treated as alternatives, and `Pauser` won. `update.go:1544`:

```go
if p, ok := m.opts.Agent.(Pauser); ok {
	return m, pauseCmd(p, "operator interrupt")
}
// No Pauser: fall back to the remote cancel.
if ri, ok := m.opts.Agent.(RemoteInterrupter); ok && m.turnInFlight() {
```

`/interrupt` had the same shape, and its comment stated the assumption out loud — "Pauser is the richer remote path". It is not richer, it is a different thing. A hold shuts the gate: it stops the *next* turn and says nothing about the one already running. `handlePause` does not interrupt, and neither does core-agent's.

The local cancel above it does not cover the gap. `m.cancelTurn()` cancels **this client's** subscription; the daemon runs its turn on `context.Background()` (`fakehost/attach.go:403`), so it never hears. Driving the real daemon through the sequence:

```
after Esc:       paused=true            ← the banner's claim
after Esc+700ms: turn still running     ← the truth
D3 subscription frame 6: text=`D1`      ← D1, never stopped
D3 subscription frame 7: text=`carry on`
D3 subscription frame 8: text=`D3`
```

So `/continue` had nothing to resume, and what appeared under `❯ D3` was D1 replayed into the subscription D3 opened. `attachAdapter.Interrupt` is exactly the call that would have worked — `client.Interrupt(ctx, path, hold=true)`, which cancels *and* holds in one request, and is why core-agent defaulted `hold=true` at protocol 1.5.0. Implemented, canary-asserted at `examples/core-agent/attach.go:65`, unreachable from either gesture.

## Fix

Both gestures cancel and then hold, through one `holdCmd`, under one deadline. Both halves run even if the first fails, and both errors are reported — a cancel that did not land is exactly when the gate matters most, because the scheduler is otherwise free to stack another turn on the one that would not die.

With nothing in flight the cancel is skipped. That is not an optimisation: `PauseInfo.Interrupted` is what makes the banner read "Interrupted —" rather than "Agent held", and Esc between turns means getting ahead of the next one, not killing this one.

`RemoteInterrupter` without `Pauser` is untouched, including its local-cancel precedence — that host is pre-1.5.0 and `TestInterrupt_LocalCancelWinsWhenAvailable` still pins it.

## Two more underneath

**The example swallowed interrupts.** `Agent.running` and `Agent.interrupted` were single booleans shared by every turn, and `beginTurn()` cleared the flag — so a turn starting while another's interrupt was pending took it with it and both ran to completion. Concurrent turns are ordinary there: the per-turn subscription and an injected steer each start one. Turns are registered by id now. This is the only end-to-end check on the interrupt path, so it lying about the semantics costs more than the toy is worth.

**A replayed `pause` frame re-armed the gate on a per-turn host.** Narration was already `liveMode`-guarded; applying the state was not, so a hold that ended minutes ago shut the gate again, and the poll a second later called that a transition and narrated it with `lastResumeMode` already spent by the real resume. That is the bare trailing `Resumed.` in the paste. On a per-turn host the poll is the only timely source and it owns the state outright now.

## Why nothing caught it

Third in a family with #275 and #278: a capability implemented, canary-asserted, and reachable from nothing. The canary proves `attachAdapter` *has* `Interrupt`; nothing asked whether any gesture calls it.

Every `RemoteInterrupter` stub omitted `Pauser` and every `Pauser` stub omitted `RemoteInterrupter` — so each half's tests exercised the arm the other capability would have taken away, and the arm a host with both actually reached was asserted by nobody. And nothing anywhere asked whether `Interrupt` has any effect on a running turn, so the TUI could stop calling it entirely and the suite stayed green.

## Tests

`tui/hold_interrupt_test.go` adds the missing host shapes — `perTurnHoldAgent` (Agent + Pauser + RemoteInterrupter, no `Events`) and `liveHoldAgent` (the same pair in observer mode). Against `origin/main`, with only the three source files reverted:

- `TestEsc_StopsTheRemoteTurnAsWellAsHolding` — `Interrupt calls = 0, want 1 — the daemon's turn was left running under a banner saying it had stopped`
- `TestSlashInterrupt_StopsTheRemoteTurnAsWellAsHolding` — `Interrupt calls = 0, want 1`
- `TestSlashInterrupt_ObserverModeStopsAndHolds` — `Interrupt calls = 0, want 1`
- `TestHold_InterruptFailureStillShutsTheGate` — `a failed cancel was reported as a clean hold`
- `TestPauseEvent_ReplayDoesNotReArmTheGateOnAPerTurnHost` — `a stale replayed frame shut the gate; on a per-turn host the poll owns it`

Two more pass either way and are there to keep passing: Esc at idle must *not* interrupt, and a `Pauser`-only host is unchanged. Ordering is pinned too — the gate shutting before the work stops is a window in which the host finishes the turn the operator just cancelled.

`examples/core-agent/fakehost/agent_test.go` (new) covers the interrupt semantics directly; `TestInterruptIsNotSwallowedByAConcurrentTurn` fails on `origin/main` with `the interrupted turn ended cleanly`. `examples/core-agent/adapter_test.go` gains `TestAttachInterruptStopsTheTurnOverHTTP`, the operator's path end to end: inject a turn, interrupt it mid-stream, assert it never reaches its committed answer and the gate is shut with the kill reported.

Docs: R-HOLD-1 gains the paragraph on why the two capabilities are not alternatives, R-HOLD-6 that the chosen source owns the state and not just the row, plus the changelog.

No exported API change; `dev/api-breaks.txt` untouched.

## Checks

`build`, `vet`, `lint-go` (0 issues), `verify-go-format`, `verify-mod-tidy`, `verify-apidiff`, `verify-vuln`, `test-unit`, `verify-coverage` — all green.

Hand check still to run: `-flavor attach`, Esc mid-turn, and watch the turn actually stop.

programme residue, not just Phases 8-13) found 10 of 21 ARRs still marked unresolved, all
predating the programme. Each was verified against current code, not just re-read for its own
claims — several turned out to be stale, describing a mid-migration state the codebase has since
moved past.

## Changes

**Closed as resolved:**
- ARR-0003 (Warning table vs. live computation) — pure clerical staleness; `Disposition` already
  said Resolved, top-level `State` never caught up. Re-verified independently.
- ARR-0009 (routes lack organisation-scoped path structure) — the `/o/{orgSlug}/...` route tree
  is real and live; every one of the ARR's own resolution criteria is met.
- ARR-0014 (route compatibility residue during migration) — its specific plan never happened;
  the underlying goal was met a different way. Closed as superseded, matching its own
  pre-existing "Superseded by ADR-0049" note the top-level field never reflected.

**Closed as accepted decision** (State stays `Confirmed`, matching ARR-0019's existing precedent
for verified-and-accepted-not-code-fixed residue):
- ARR-0001 (player position dual representation) — settled 2026-08-02, never marked as such.

**Narrowed** (real progress the ARR hadn't recorded):
- ARR-0004 (domain logic leaks into routes/actions) — cited example and a second spot-check are
  clean thin adapters now; one claim (React component duplication) remains unverified.
- ARR-0006 (string-typed enum fields) — 7 of 8 fields still open; `Availability.status` already
  resolved, dropped from the list. `MatchRound.status` connects to a real bug this session hit
  (PR #310) — already scoped as a roadmap item elsewhere.
- ARR-0008 (`requireCoachAccess()` no role granularity) — down to 2 real production call sites
  from 14 recorded at last update.
- ARR-0016 (direct team-based player eligibility) — 2 of 3 original points genuinely done

**No change** (already accurate): ARR-0002, ARR-0017.
