author: lukaswodka
body:
Part of the **backend#1979** wave. `backend#1680` closes on this landing.

## What changes

`.github/workflows/stale-backlog.yml` — a byte-identical copy of an `actions/stale`
config carried in 16 repos — becomes a thin caller of the reusable that `.github#288`
landed, following the `-caller.yml` convention already used by `fr-gate-caller.yml`,
`code-quality-caller.yml` and `fr-pass-comment-caller.yml`.

```yaml
jobs:
  stale:
    uses: tracebloc/.github/.github/workflows/stale-backlog.yml@main
    secrets: inherit
```

## Why it is not just deduplication

The copy called `actions/stale`, which is **column-blind**: it can see labels and
dates, not the board. So it would close a `North Stars` epic, or anything already in
the pipeline, on the same 6-week/8-week timer as a forgotten `Backlog` item — the
defect behind backend#1597 item 1.

Board awareness needs a script, and a script cannot be maintained as sixteen
byte-identical copies. The reusable's eligibility is exactly `Backlog`, and it
**fails toward skipping**, because the destructive direction here is closing.

## No inputs passed, on purpose

Every input the callee declares is defaulted (`project-number: 2`, `dry-run: false`,
`strict: false`, `script-ref: main`). A caller may only pass inputs the `@main`
callee declares — passing one it lacks kills the run at `startup_failure`, which is
exactly why the callee had to reach `main` before any caller could be armed.

`permissions: contents: read` only: the sweep's writes go through the App token
minted inside the reusable, and asking for more here than the callee needs fails the
run at startup with no jobs.

## DRAFT — and what un-drafts it

**This cannot merge yet, and draft is the mechanical guarantee of that.** Callers pin
`@main`, and `.github/main` still carries the old 1174-byte copy — the reusable is on
`.github/develop`, 4 commits ahead. Merging this first would leave a scheduled
workflow that fails at startup every Monday.

Order, per the note carried in `repo-inventory.yml`:

1. `.github` promotes `develop → staging → main`, carrying the reusable
2. **these 16 callers merge**
3. one final `.github` PR adds `.github`'s own caller *and* flips all 17 inventory
   entries from `exempt` to `required`

Step 3 is last for a stated reason: flipping to `required` before a repo's caller
lands would redden the org audit for every repo still waiting — the drift window made
to look permanent. And `.github`'s caller ships *with* the flip rather than before it,
because `exempt` plus a caller on the audited branch is itself a finding
(`caller-drift.py:2260`).

body:
Reported from the viewer: the Agents / Skills / Prompts pages showed descriptions in Spanish while the UI was in English, and some cards had no description at all — just a `>`. Four separate defects behind that one symptom. ## 1. Descriptions were never translated Agent and skill cards rendered the raw frontmatter: ```js `

${escapeHtml(agent.description)}

` // no t() ``` Prompts already went through `t()` (which is why only they looked right). Agents and skills now do too, so the dictionary applies to them like every other string in the viewer. ## 2. `description: >` rendered as a literal `>` The parser took whatever followed `description:` on the same line: ```js /^description:\s*(.+)$/m.exec(block)?.[1]?.trim() ``` For a YAML folded block scalar that is the `>` itself. Two skills use that form — `sdd-data-schemas` and `sdd-file-structure` — and both showed `>` as their entire description. Block scalars (`>`, `|`, with or without chomping) are folded now. The first attempt used a negative lookahead on the inline branch, which backtracked over the whitespace and matched anyway; detecting the block form first is what actually works. The skill view carried **its own copy** of the parser, so fixing `parseAgentFrontmatter` alone left the skills page broken — both share `parseFrontmatterDescription` now. ## 3. Two prompts had no description `hermes-resume` and `sdd-steward` were missing from the viewer's fallback catalog, so `enrichPromptManifest` gave them `description: ''`. Added with label, description and trigger. ## 4. The kit mixed languages `sdd-reviewer`'s skill frontmatter was in English while the other 18 were in Spanish — that is the "Sdd: Reviewer" card reading differently from its neighbours. Normalized to Spanish, the kit's source language, keeping the frontmatter single-language because it is what the agents read to decide when to invoke a skill. ## Coverage All 27 kit descriptions (8 agents + 19 skills) plus the 6 prompt entries now have English translations. Verified by parsing every frontmatter with the fixed parser and asserting a dictionary hit for each: **27 translated, 0 missing.** Checked in a real generated workspace, both languages, on all three pages: 0 empty descriptions, no Spanish leaking into EN, no English leaking into ES. `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm test` (81/81) · `pnpm build`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: mudream4869
body:
Introduces the `textnorm` package to support content-based similarity detection by normalizing text layout variations and providing reproducible hashing.

## Summary

This adds a new internal package `textnorm` that handles two critical operations for PlainShelf's similarity detection:

1. **Text normalization** — reduces text to its content by applying NFKC Unicode normalization and stripping layout characters (whitespace, punctuation, symbols, separators)
2. **Reproducible hashing** — provides xxHash64-based hashing with a fixed seed to ensure consistent fingerprints across machines and builds

## Key changes

- **`normalize.go`** — Implements `Normalize()` which strips layout variations so that reflowed paragraphs, different quote styles, and indentation differences all reduce to the same string. Deliberately preserves traditional/simplified Chinese distinctions and runs Latin words together (a necessary cost of making CJK reflowing invisible).

- **`hash64.go`** — Implements `Hash64()` and `Hash64String()` using xxHash64 with a fixed seed. The fixed seed is essential: a per-process seed would cause the same book to hash differently on different machines, breaking cross-shelf similarity detection.

- **`normalize_test.go`** — Comprehensive test suite covering:
  - Layout independence (same text wrapped four different ways)
  - Quote and punctuation style variations
  - NFKC compatibility folding (fullwidth Latin, ligatures, etc.)
  - Latin word spacing collisions (documented as an accepted cost)
  - Chinese variant preservation
  - Format rune handling (known limitation)
  - Idempotence property (required for caching)

- **`hash64_test.go`** — Golden hash tests pinning known inputs to known outputs, plus stability and collision detection tests. These golden tests are the only reliable way to catch algorithm substitutions that would silently break cross-machine fingerprint matching.

- **`doc.go`** — Package documentation explaining the versioning contract: both `NormalizeVersion` and `Hash64Version` must be included in any cache's algo block, and must change whenever the rules change.

- **`go.mod`** — Adds `github.com/cespare/xxhash/v2` dependency for the hash implementation.

## Notable implementation details

- Both `Normalize` and `Hash64` are versioned constants that must be bumped whenever their output can change for any input. A mixed cache is worse than no cache.
- The `isLayout()` helper uses `unicode.IsSpace()` (which covers separators and ASCII line-ending controls) plus Unicode categories P (punctuation), S (symbols), and Z (separators).
- Hash64 uses xxHash64's default seed (0) explicitly to ensure determinism across all machines and builds — this is non-negotiable for a shared shelf.
- Normalize is idempotent: running it twice on the same input produces the same result, which is required for cache correctness.

author: oddharsh
body:
Two small additions now that the toolchain is bun.

## `deps:dedupe`, in CI

`bun dedupe --check` joins the `validate` job right after the frozen-lockfile install. All 239 packages are currently deduplicated, so it lands green and starts failing the day a duplicate arrives. It sits inside `validate` because that is the one required check on `main`.

## `check:fast`, local only

`bun run --parallel lint typecheck test` runs the three independent read-only gates concurrently, in roughly 1.6 to 1.9 seconds against about 4 seconds sequential.

CI keeps them as named sequential steps, since a parallel run collapses three failures into one log. `package.json` carries a `comment:check-fast` key recording that split and the rule for what may join it: nothing that touches `.build` and nothing pinned to node, which rules out build, routes, lens and perf.

author: klangenk
body:
## Motivation

Every node's `main.py` repeats the same twenty lines — read `UVICORN_RELOAD`, build the settings, construct the node, call `uvicorn.run`. There are eight copies across the three node repositories, and they have drifted: `dfine_node` parses settings with configargparse so each one is both a flag and an environment variable, while `yolov5_node` and `classification_node` hand-roll `os.getenv` with `assert`s and hardcode the host and port.

This puts it in one place, so a new node's entry point is the two lines that are actually its own.

**Stacked on #89**; review that one first.

## Implementation

- Add `helpers/entrypoint.py` with `node_parser(description=, legacy_env_prefix=)` and `run_node(app, args)`
- A setting is named after its flag: `--conf-threshold` reads `CONF_THRESHOLD`. One declaration yields a flag, an environment variable, and a `--help` entry.
- `legacy_env_prefix` accepts a prefix an earlier version of a node required, with a warning naming the replacement, so adopting this breaks no deployment
- Add `configargparse` to the runtime dependencies
- Nine tests in `tests/unit`

## Why unprefixed names

`dfine_node` required a `DFINE_TRAINER_` / `DFINE_DETECTOR_` prefix; the other two read bare names. Bare wins here because **`yolov5_node` is the widely deployed one and `dfine_node` is still in beta** — so the repositories running in the field keep every variable they already set, and the one repository that has to move is the one where moving is cheap. `dfine_node` passes `legacy_env_prefix` so its beta deployments keep working meanwhile.

## `--host` and `--port` are the exception

They read `NODE_HOST` and `NODE_PORT`, not the names their flags imply. The bare `HOST` already means **the loop's address** — every deployment sets it, `face_detection`'s compose file sets `HOST=preview.learning-loop.ai` — and a node adopting it would hand that to uvicorn and fail to bind. There is a test asserting exactly this.

## Note

`logging.basicConfig(...)` in the trainers is deliberately not reproduced. `helpers/log_conf.py` configures the root logger at import, so `basicConfig` has been returning without doing anything — verified, not assumed.

author: leggetter
body:
A fourth Outpost scenario, and the second that discriminates on something an agent has to notice rather than look up.

## The scenario

Acme stopped receiving order events. Their endpoint had a bad deploy and has since been fixed. Nothing is arriving.

The destination was disabled after repeated failures. Three events are held against it, the endpoint is now healthy, and nothing recovers on its own. An agent that checks the endpoint finds it fine; an agent that republishes finds the new events held too. The only route through is noticing the destination's state.

This shape was chosen deliberately over "endpoint broke and healed", which self-heals under Outpost's exponential backoff — the defect that had to be repaired in `resolve-002`.

## Verified, not inferred

Retry against a disabled destination answers `400 "Destination is disabled"`, checked against the live API. So re-enabling *then* retrying is an ordering the product enforces, not one the scenario invented.

## Scored on outcome

Any enabled destination counts, not the first one listed, and attempts are summed across the tenant. An agent that makes Acme receive again by adding a destination has reached the end state, and reading `[0]` would decide that on list order. This is the `alerting-001` lesson — that scorer asked *who created* an alert and failed the agent that repaired a broken one.

A second tenant is seeded and delivering normally. Recovery scoped too widely is the failure mode that turns a fix into a second incident.

## Both directions checked

`score-only` gains `--no-solution`. A scorer shown to accept a correct answer has not been shown to reject a wrong one, and a scorer that passes unconditionally does the first perfectly.

- with `SOLUTION.ts`: **3/3 pass**, stable
- unsolved: **0/2 pass** — the two intended checks fail with useful notes, and the negative check correctly passes

## Three traps this cost, now in AGENTS.md

1. **Publishing is synchronous, delivery is not.** `after` disabled the destination before Outpost had attempted anything, so the failed attempts the scenario is built on were never created. It looked like a working seed only because a previous run's tenant had survived and had been delivering while it sat there. `applyOutpostSeed` now waits for attempts before running `after` — the same trap `applySeed` already fixes for the gateway.
2. **Tenant create is idempotent, destination create is not.** Seeding onto a leftover tenant appended a second destination rather than replacing the first: one carrying the seeded history, one empty. The seed now deletes the tenant first, so it does not depend on the previous run having exited cleanly.
3. **`/events`, `/attempts` and `/retry` are top-level**, not tenant-scoped, and a wrong path returns an HTML 404 that reads like a broken deployment rather than a wrong path.

Also worth knowing: Outpost event history outlives the tenant. A freshly recreated `acme` listed 38 events against the 3 that run published, still bound to destinations that no longer exist.

author: quangvdao
body:
## Summary

- Add a dependency-light `akita-error` crate as the single owner of `AkitaError`.
- Add `akita_error::checked` as the single owner of reusable exact `usize` formulas.
- Replace copied `checked_product`, `checked_mul3`, `checked_mul4`, range, alignment, ceiling-division, power-of-two, and exact-division helpers across the workspace.
- Move every direct protocol error consumer to `akita_error::AkitaError`. Keep only the intentional `akita-pcs` umbrella reexport.
- Add repository tests that reject duplicate generic helpers, duplicate error definitions, old field aliases, and new non-umbrella reexports.
- Remove the now-unused `akita-field` dependencies from `akita-planner` and `akita-schedules`.

## Why this PR comes first

PR #307 combines the error extraction with the much larger and now outdated `akita-field` to `jolt-field` cutover. This PR lands the independent lower layer now. The field consolidation can rebase later and add any `jolt_field::FieldError` conversion at this boundary without owning or duplicating the Akita protocol error.

This change does not depend on Jolt or on the contributor branch behind #307.

## Checked arithmetic contract

The new module contains small, pure operations:

| Function | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `checked::product(iter)` | Exact product for fixed arrays or dynamic iterators. The helper does not allocate or collect. Fixed arrays and borrowed slice iterators are allocation free. |
| `checked::sum(iter)` | Exact sum, including dynamic claim and layout counts. |
| `checked::mul_add(a, b, c)` | Exact `a * b + c` for flattened indices. |
| `checked::pow2(exponent)` | Exact `2^exponent` with checked exponent conversion and shift. |
| `checked::ceil_log2(value)` | Exact padded Boolean-domain variable count. Rejects zero and unrepresentable padding. |
| `checked::range(start, len)` | Exact half-open range with a checked endpoint. |
| `checked::align_up(value, alignment)` | Exact power-of-two alignment with validation and overflow rejection. |
| `checked::div_ceil(value, divisor)` | Ceiling division without the overflow-prone `value + divisor - 1` formula. |
| `checked::exact_div(value, divisor)` | Division only when the divisor is nonzero and the result is exact. |

These functions return `Option` because the arithmetic layer cannot know whether failure means invalid input, setup, or proof. Callers map failure once at the semantic boundary. They never wrap, saturate, or panic.

Direct standard library `checked_*` calls remain appropriate for one local operation. The central module owns formulas that were being copied into generic helpers.

## Behavior and compatibility

- No proof format, transcript, verifier acceptance rule, field arithmetic, or serialization behavior changes.
- Overflow and malformed geometry continue to return `AkitaError` or `SerializationError` at their existing boundaries.
- Some power-of-two calculations are stricter: oversized exponents can no longer truncate through an integer cast, and verifier-reachable padding no longer uses panicking `next_power_of_two` calls in the migrated paths.
- This is a breaking source change. `akita-field` and `akita-algebra` no longer export `AkitaError`; direct consumers must import `akita_error::AkitaError`. The broad `akita-pcs` package still reexports it intentionally.

## Enforcement

`scripts/tests/test_checked_arithmetic_ownership.py` checks that:

- `AkitaError` has exactly one definition;
- old `akita_field::AkitaError` paths do not return;
- only `akita-pcs` may provide the umbrella reexport; and
- removed generic helper families, including any future `checked_mulN`, are not redefined outside `akita_error::checked`.

The architecture chapter, crate graph, verifier contract, contributor rules, and documentation blast-radius map record the same ownership boundary.

## Reviewer map

- `crates/akita-error/`: canonical error and checked arithmetic API, documentation, and edge-case tests.
- `crates/*/Cargo.toml`, workspace lockfiles, and direct imports: mechanical ownership cutover.
- `akita-types`, `akita-algebra`, `akita-planner`, and `akita-prover`: removal of copied arithmetic helpers and migration to the shared formulas.
- `scripts/tests/test_checked_arithmetic_ownership.py`: static ownership enforcement.
- `README.md`, `book/src/how/architecture.md`, `book/src/how/verification.md`, and `docs/`: durable architecture and no-panic contract.

## Validation

- Deterministic schedule regeneration completed successfully.
- Repository preflight passed: formatting, Taplo, Rust file limits, 75 Python tests, dependency hygiene, `cargo machete`, typos, and documentation guardrails.
- All four CI Clippy feature graphs passed with warnings denied.
- Exact unsharded CI Nextest command passed: 1,654 tests across 51 binaries.
- `akita-field` with `jolt-compat` passed: 154 tests.
- Rust documentation built with warnings denied.
- The recursion profile workspace compiled across all targets.
- The fuzz workspace compiled and its independent lockfile was updated.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Follow-up

After this lands, #307 can rebase onto the new ownership boundary, drop its duplicate `akita-error` extraction, and focus only on the field implementation and Jolt integration cutover.

## Note

Replaces #421 (opened from `quangvdao` fork). Same commits, same-repo branch so org CodeQL default setup can run.

body: ## Problem `release` had `needs: [build, build-wasm]`. A single red native matrix cell (e.g. `windows-x86_64`) fails the whole `build` job, which **skips** publish even when `build-wasm` already succeeded. That leaves `wit_snapshot.wasm` off the GitHub release. ## Fix (smallest change) Only touches `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `scripts/check_release_workflows.sh`. 1. **`release` job** keeps `needs: [build, build-wasm]` but adds: ```yaml if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build-wasm.result == 'success' }} ``` so a failed native cell does not skip publish. 2. **Native artifact download** uses `if-no-files-found: ignore` for `dist-*` — missing cells are skipped downloads, not publish failures. 3. **Checksums** hash only archives that exist (`nullglob` + `natives=(wit-*.tar.gz wit-*.zip)`), always require `wit_snapshot.wasm`, and still `grep` it into `wit-checksums.txt`. 4. **`fail_on_unmatched_files: false`** unchanged on `softprops/action-gh-release`. 5. **Guard script** asserts the split: publish must not gate on `needs.build.result`; wasm attach + checksum still required. ## Out of scope Windows flake, new tags, npm/Cloudflare, renaming assets, second workflow. ## Reviewer check With this change, a red `windows-x86_64` cell still attaches `wit_snapshot.wasm` and lists it in `wit-checksums.txt`.

author: aashishbhanawat
body:
💡 What: Replaced $O(N^2)$ inline list comprehensions with $O(N \log N)$ cumulative sums and binary search (`bisect`) in the `_get_realized_and_unrealized_cash_flows` function in `crud_analytics.py`.
🎯 Why: The original nested list comprehensions iterated through potentially thousands of transactions to determine valid buys/sells relative to an income event's date, causing a severe performance bottleneck scaling quadratically.
📊 Impact: Reduced calculation time for an artificial scenario with 14,000 transactions from ~33.7s to ~0.024s.
🔬 Measurement: Verify via code review or running standalone benchmark script comparing list comprehensions vs bisect array approaches.

author: pnotarysvcs-bit
body:
### Motivation

- Turn Pay Period into a cash-flow allocation workspace for two regular monthly paychecks plus variable notary income.
- Let bills be assigned to Paycheck 1 (13th) or Paycheck 2 (27th) independently of their contractual due date.
- Keep Bills as the monthly source of truth while using Pay Period for funding decisions.
- Establish a measurable path toward being one month ahead on bills.

### Description

- Reworked `/pay-period` from a read-only 14-day due-date view into a semi-monthly paycheck allocation workspace.
- Uses the existing `ledger_bills.pay_period` field so moving a bill changes only its paycheck assignment; the bill due date remains unchanged in Bills.
- Shows all monthly bills: current-paycheck Personal/TCU, Business/TCUB, Other, bills assigned to the other paycheck, and Unassigned bills.
- Added editable cash-plan inputs for regular paycheck income (default $2,992), variable notary income, and the amount intentionally allocated toward next month.
- Added a One Month Ahead progress indicator showing funded dollars, next-month planned expenses, and funded percentage.
- Added `ledger_pay_period_finances` persistence for regular income, notary income, one-month-ahead contributions, and target month; RLS is enabled and the app accesses it server-side through the existing service-role pattern.
- Retained the information tooltip explaining the Pay Period, Bills, and Savings architecture.
- Added server actions for paycheck assignment and cash-plan persistence.
- Updated unit tests for the 13th/27th semi-monthly cycle, editable paycheck allocation independent of due dates, notary income, and unassigned bill visibility.

### Business rules now covered

- Regular paycheck baseline defaults to $2,992 but is editable per paycheck.
- Notary income is supplemental and editable per paycheck.
- A bill can be moved between Paycheck 1 and Paycheck 2 without changing its actual due date.
- Submitted, partial, and unpaid bills remain part of the allocation model.
- Newly added active bills appear in the monthly Pay Period workspace and remain visible as Unassigned until allocated.
- Archived/inactive bills do not appear because the existing Bills Master data layer remains the source of truth.
- One Month Ahead funding is tracked separately from ordinary bill expense totals.
- Emergency Fund wiring remains out of scope for this PR; that tracker stays on Bills for a later enhancement.

### Validation

- Existing CI previously passed before this expansion.
- A new CI run is executing against the semi-monthly allocation implementation and updated tests.

Fifteen pairs of segment files over one two-contig reference: an exact match,
breakpoints shifted past the padding and the same pair with the padding widened,
a normal that is neutral everywhere, a match on the second contig, a normal
region strictly containing a tumour segment, a reciprocal overlap at three
thresholds, another call column name, and five refusals.

The tagging is an OR of two tests taken over two different lists: the breakpoint
search runs over the unmerged tumour segments, the reciprocal overlap over the
merged ones. The `shifted` row tags through the overlap even though its
breakpoints are out of reach of the padding, and `reciprocal-default` shows the
same pair failing when the threshold is the default.

The per-segment filter is a third test again, and its intersection comparison is
strict (`>`) where the reciprocal one is not (`>=`).

author: lukaswodka
body:
Part of the **backend#1979** wave. `backend#1680` closes on this landing.

## What changes

`.github/workflows/stale-backlog.yml` — a byte-identical copy of an `actions/stale`
config carried in 16 repos — becomes a thin caller of the reusable that `.github#288`
landed, following the `-caller.yml` convention already used by `fr-gate-caller.yml`,
`code-quality-caller.yml` and `fr-pass-comment-caller.yml`.

```yaml
jobs:
  stale:
    uses: tracebloc/.github/.github/workflows/stale-backlog.yml@main
    secrets: inherit
```

## Why it is not just deduplication

The copy called `actions/stale`, which is **column-blind**: it can see labels and
dates, not the board. So it would close a `North Stars` epic, or anything already in
the pipeline, on the same 6-week/8-week timer as a forgotten `Backlog` item — the
defect behind backend#1597 item 1.

Board awareness needs a script, and a script cannot be maintained as sixteen
byte-identical copies. The reusable's eligibility is exactly `Backlog`, and it
**fails toward skipping**, because the destructive direction here is closing.

## No inputs passed, on purpose

Every input the callee declares is defaulted (`project-number: 2`, `dry-run: false`,
`strict: false`, `script-ref: main`). A caller may only pass inputs the `@main`
callee declares — passing one it lacks kills the run at `startup_failure`, which is
exactly why the callee had to reach `main` before any caller could be armed.

`permissions: contents: read` only: the sweep's writes go through the App token
minted inside the reusable, and asking for more here than the callee needs fails the
run at startup with no jobs.

## DRAFT — and what un-drafts it

**This cannot merge yet, and draft is the mechanical guarantee of that.** Callers pin
`@main`, and `.github/main` still carries the old 1174-byte copy — the reusable is on
`.github/develop`, 4 commits ahead. Merging this first would leave a scheduled
workflow that fails at startup every Monday.

Order, per the note carried in `repo-inventory.yml`:

1. `.github` promotes `develop → staging → main`, carrying the reusable
2. **these 16 callers merge**
3. one final `.github` PR adds `.github`'s own caller *and* flips all 17 inventory
   entries from `exempt` to `required`

Step 3 is last for a stated reason: flipping to `required` before a repo's caller
lands would redden the org audit for every repo still waiting — the drift window made
to look permanent. And `.github`'s caller ships *with* the flip rather than before it,
because `exempt` plus a caller on the audited branch is itself a finding
(`caller-drift.py:2260`).

author: vincentkoc
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/1488

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reusing an SSH workspace could see a retained run abort after an acquire or renewal response was lost, even when the remote ownership mutation had succeeded.

Native Windows also needs the witnessed process tree to stop before the workspace is reused when its published supervisor record is removed or changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Acquire retries are bounded by the configured ownership wait and use same-token idempotence to reconcile a lost success response. Renewal retries are bounded by the last confirmed ownership TTL; mismatch and expiry remain terminal.

Native Windows keeps the identity-checked Job Object supervisor and revalidates its exact PID/start-time record on every poll, closing the job on record loss or mismatch. Linux, macOS, and WSL2 retain the current two-line direct-child PID/start-identity witness. This PR makes no POSIX descendant-containment claim; kernel-owned POSIX containment is tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/1488.

No configuration, protocol action, readiness behavior, or secret handling changes.

## User Impact

Brief response loss no longer aborts a retained run while ownership is still provably within its deadline. Native Windows descendants are terminated before inspection and reuse after supervisor-record loss or tampering. POSIX completion and direct-child ownership behavior remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `bdd59ba9805b8e172fdbcccb344d8fa4b62ed997`
- Base: `0364ddb5c4d2462a152db4d232f74f4f7604681b`
- Focused owner and cleanup tests: pass
- Focused race: pass
- `go vet ./internal/cli/...`: pass
- `go build -trimpath ./cmd/crabbox`: pass
- Windows amd64 test-binary cross-compile: pass
- `gofmt` and `git diff --check`: pass
- Hosted exact-head CI: all required checks pass
- Exact-head ClawSweeper re-review: reviewed `bdd59ba9805b`; no source-code finding, but proof remains blocked on the native Windows authority boundary and a complete WSL2 lifecycle
- Fresh POSIX SSH proof: pass. The retained workload acquired ownership, ran for 17 seconds across renewal, preserved stdout/stderr markers, exited 0, released the owner and lease, and left `owner=0 child=0 run=0 launcher=0 tmp=0` with zero local spools.
- Fresh native Windows proof: infrastructure-blocked before the changed Job Object supervisor path. Direct Windows OpenSSH remained available, but owner renewal/staging failed closed before the workload. Exact task processes and eight private stdin files were mapped and removed; final `owner=0 child=0 run=0 witness=0 tmp=0`, zero local spools, lease released. The earlier combined-head proof covered record removal/tampering and descendant termination, but it is not substituted for fresh exact-head final-effect proof.
- Fresh Windows-to-WSL2 proof: infrastructure-blocked before workload execution. Warmup completed; direct Windows OpenSSH and direct `wsl.exe` controls both passed. The exact owner acquire stayed ambiguous for 168 seconds while broker heartbeats timed out, then failed closed. Three exact task wrappers were mapped and stopped; final `owner=0 child=0 run=0 launcher=0 tmp=0`, zero local spools, lease released and absent.
- Production implementation: `+158/-40`, net `+118` lines, justified by bounded reconciliation and the native Windows security boundary
- Tests: `+467/-5`; docs and changelog: `+11/-3`

## Current Blocker

Do not merge until a maintainer resolves ClawSweeper's exact-head proof hold. Fresh native Windows record-tamper final-effect proof and a successful Windows-to-WSL2 acquire/renew/workload/release lifecycle remain unavailable; all exact task leases, processes, remote residue, and local spools are cleaned.

author: danielhanchen
body:
### The bug

`carried_forward_items` in `studio/backend/core/inference/checkpoint.py` reserves the OLDEST evicted turn ahead of every newer one, so the slot cap drops the turn immediately after it. That turn is exactly where an early change of direction lives, so the block carries the abandoned request and hides the correction to it.

On current main:

```python
from core.inference.checkpoint import carried_forward_items
turns = lambda *t: [{"role": "user", "content": x} for x in t]

carried_forward_items(turns("Build Flappy Bird", "Actually build Tetris instead", "Add music"), max_items = 2)
# ['Build Flappy Bird', 'Add music']

carried_forward_items(
    turns("Build Flappy Bird", "Actually build Tetris instead", *[f"Add feature {i}" for i in range(1, 8)]),
    max_items = 8,
)
# ['Build Flappy Bird', 'Add feature 1', ... 'Add feature 7']
```

Both blocks tell the model to build the game the user walked away from, and then apply every later increment to it. A wrong statement of the current task is the failure the reservation was added to prevent, and the reservation is what produces it.

With this PR:

```
['Actually build Tetris instead', 'Add music']
['Build Flappy Bird', 'Actually build Tetris instead', 'Add feature 2', ... 'Add feature 7']
```

The case the reservation exists for is unchanged. A task stated once at the front followed by nineteen increments, at `max_items = 8`, still carries `Build a Flappy Bird game` first and `increment 19` last.

### The rule

The opening turn is reserved together with the next evicted instruction turn, both or neither, so the block can never show an opening request without what the user said next about it.

The pair is slotted in behind the newest turn that can actually be taken, exactly as the single reservation was, and it costs one more slot, paid by the oldest turn the newest-first walk would otherwise have taken. If the pair does not fit whole (a cap of one or two slots, or the budget already spent), the reservation is abandoned and the newest-first walk decides WITHOUT the opening turn: leaving it in the fallback simply picked it up again whenever it was the cheaper of the two, which is the same wrong statement of the task by another route.

One exception, and it is the boundary of the rule: when the successor costs more than the whole budget, no ordering carries it and there was never a pair to take. Dropping the opening then buys nothing, because on those threads the opening is the only affordable turn. The campaign's headline case is exactly that shape, a 43-token standing instruction followed by eight 160-token sections under a 100-token budget, and excluding the opening sends the block out empty, which is the failure the whole pass exists to stop. Nothing but the English separates that thread from an unaffordable correction, so both keep the opening.

Rendering position is read off the transcript rather than off the walk, for the same reason the header's later-wins rule exists: the reserved pair can fill the slot cap before the walk reaches a newer copy of a restated instruction, and the surviving copy then rendered at the position of the older one.

It needs no reading of the English. It does not ask which turn is a task statement and which is a correction; it only guarantees that a correction sitting immediately after the opening request cannot be hidden behind it.

Boundary: the pair needs two slots behind the newest usable turn, so three slots is where it starts fitting. `["Build Flappy Bird", "Actually build Tetris instead", "Add feature 1", "Add feature 2"]` gives `['Add feature 1', 'Add feature 2']` at `max_items = 2` (nothing wrong, only missing) and `['Build Flappy Bird', 'Actually build Tetris instead', 'Add feature 2']` at 3. The same rule applies against the token cap: a budget with room for the newest turn and one of the two opening turns now buys the correction, not the abandoned request.

### Alternatives rejected

**Drop the reservation entirely.** It regresses the case the reservation was added for, which is the ordinary shape of a real session: the task is stated once at the front and every later turn is an increment ("add music", "now the score", "fix the pipes"). A plain newest-first walk then carries eight ways to change a game it never names. `test_the_opening_task_still_survives_a_run_of_short_increments` is that case.

**Reserve the newest task-establishing turn instead of the oldest.** This needs a classifier for "task-establishing", and there is no structural signal for it. Nothing separates "Actually make it Tetris" from "fix it" except the English, and the file already records the cost of guessing at phrasing: the 80-character floor was a guess of exactly this kind and dropped "Create a Flappy Bird game in HTML" (33 chars) on a live session. A rule that cannot be stated without reading the words is a rule that cannot be tested at its boundary.

**Keep the reservation but never let it displace a newer turn.** Every turn in the walk is newer than the reserved one, so the reservation only ever displaces newer turns. The condition is unsatisfiable, and the rule degenerates to dropping the reservation, with the regression above. A weaker reading, "abandon the reservation whenever the walk cannot also reach the turn after the opening", is the same regression: on a task plus nineteen increments at eight slots the walk reaches the thirteenth turn, nowhere near the second, so the reservation is abandoned and the task statement goes with it. Promoting the successor alongside the opening is what makes the condition satisfiable, which is why the fix is a pair rather than a veto.

### Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_checkpoint_compaction.py` gains nine tests: both repro cases above, the long run of increments with no correction, the both-or-neither boundary at two slots versus three, the same rule against the token cap, an opening turn that nothing follows (still reserved, since nothing can be hidden behind it), the fallback that must not re-select the opening, the unaffordable-successor boundary where it must, and a restatement that has to outrank its own older copy even when the pair fills the cap.

```
python -m pytest tests/test_checkpoint_compaction.py -q     85 passed
python -m pytest tests/test_context_overflow_truncation.py tests/test_llama_cpp_context_fit.py \
  tests/test_conversation_recall_injection.py tests/test_llama_cpp_tool_loop.py \
  tests/test_chat_history_routes.py -q                      427 passed (all six suites)
```

No existing test changed.

author: nedseb
body:
## Ce que fait cette PR

Elle **tranche le dernier point mesurable** du spike de captation, et la réponse est de ne rien
construire.

La page recommandait un bassin de tampons rendus par le scribe après écriture, pour éviter d'allouer
une toile neuve à chaque image. La mesure dit que ce n'est pas justifié.

## Vérification

On a poussé la cadence jusqu'à faire bouger le compteur d'images perdues, sur
`ParcoursNavigationE2ETest`.

| Cadence | Images écrites | Images perdues |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 img/s (nominale) | 212 | **0** |
| 25 img/s | 417 | **0** |
| 50 img/s | 710 | **0** |
| 50 img/s, file étranglée de 60 à 1 | 703 | **0** |

**Comment on saurait que c'est cassé.** Quatre zéros consécutifs peuvent signifier « rien ne se
perd » ou « le compteur est mort ». Il a donc été éprouvé : en ralentissant le scribe de 120 ms par
image, il rapporte **45 pertes**. Les zéros ci-dessus sont des zéros mesurés, pas des zéros par
défaut.

| Épreuve | Résultat |
|---|---|
| `./mvnw test` sur les cinq classes du paquet | 23 tests, 0 échec |
| `./mvnw -Pquality-gate pmd:pmd pmd:check` | BUILD SUCCESS |

## Chemins sensibles

- [x] **sans objet** : cette PR ne touche aucun des chemins ci-dessous
- [ ] `db/migration/**`
- [ ] `ServiceSauvegarde` / restauration
- [ ] `.github/workflows/**`

---

## Pourquoi ne pas le faire quand même

Un bassin coûterait cher en risque pour un gain nul : il faudrait que le scribe **rende** chaque
tampon, et un tampon rendu trop tôt réécrirait une image encore en attente. Le film serait alors
faux **sans être plus court**, donc sans aucun signe.

Le piège reste documenté au-dessus de `composer()`, parce que la tentation, elle, reviendra.

## Ce qui change dans le code

Une ligne : la cadence devient pilotable par `-Drecette.film.cadence`, comme la taille l'était déjà
par `recette.film.taille`. Elle est réglable parce qu'elle a **servi à éprouver le dispositif** :
sans elle, on ne pouvait pas le pousser à cinq fois sa valeur nominale.

## Ce qui reste ouvert

Le pipeline logiciel Prism SW, seul point du spike encore non tranché, et sans conséquence attendue
pour un film de recette.

L'ancienne rubrique 4 de la page, qui recommandait le bassin, est retirée : la laisser aurait fait
dire à deux sections du même document l'inverse l'une de l'autre.

author: srg-kostyrko
body:
## What and why

The months of a `calendar-timeline` block in `quarter` or `calendar` mode rendered at different sizes from each other — reported from a Q3 grid where August's cells were 51% wider than July's, September's rows were shorter than both, and September was cut off at the edge of the note.

`useCellDecorations` computed its shared padding reservation from the cells that **matched** in that call, and `NotesMonthView` calls it once per instance. Each month therefore reserved padding from its own notes alone: the month holding a decoration with an inline-placed mark reserved horizontal room its siblings did not. `repeat(3, 1fr)` carries a min-content auto minimum, so that month's track grew to its min-content (300px measured), the other two were pinned at theirs (203px), and the row overflowed a 700px note by 38px — clipping the last month. The same drift hit the stacked-month surfaces (`TimelineMonth.vue`, `MonthCalendarBlock.vue`) as row heights that did not match between months.

Two changes:

- **`use-cell-padding.ts` (new)** — the reservation now comes from the decorations the scope can *draw* rather than the ones that currently match. Surfaces over the same journals size their cells identically whatever their own cells hold, and a note gaining a decoration no longer reflows the grid around it. Trade-off: a cell reserves space for a decoration even when nothing in view uses it, so grids are marginally roomier than before.
- **`TimelineQuarter.vue` / `TimelineCalendar.vue`** — the row sizes its columns around that same reservation (`--month-min`) through `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(…))`, so decorated months wrap onto another row instead of clipping. The hardcoded 420px/630px container queries go with it; a `(100% - 2·gap)/3` floor keeps three months per row as the maximum, and for undecorated months the new thresholds land within ~30px of the old ones.

Both regression tests were watched failing first:

- `use-cell-decorations.test.ts` — a surface whose cells match nothing reserved `max(0.1em, 2px)` against the matching surface's `max(0.6em, 2px)`; now equal.
- `code-blocks.e2e.ts` — with the test in place and `src/` at baseline, the quarter grid reports **2 distinct month widths**; with the fix, **1**, and no overflow. Layout is invisible to the unit suite, which is why nothing caught this.

## Test-ordering fix (81ce655d)

The first push failed e2e on all three OSes with two condition-decoration tests: `has-open-task decoration did not render on the week cell` and `all-tasks-completed decoration did not render on the month header`. **This was caused by this PR, not by the local environment** — the earlier note in this description attributing it to a local artifact was wrong.

Mocha runs a suite's own tests before its nested suites, and `assertDecorationMatrix(timelineCalendar)` is a `describe` factory that reads like a plain statement. The new quarter-sizing `it()` was registered beside it, so it ran **first** and swapped the month timeline the suite's `before` had staged (`blocks/timeline-matrix.md`) for a quarter one. `calendarSurface.periodCell` is `$()` — first match — and `NotesMonthView.vue` emits `header-month`/`week-number-cell` per month view, three to a quarter, so the matrix then read *July's* header and first week instead of the seeded current ones. `header-quarter` still matched (every month in Q3 carries the same quarter period) and the day cells are pinned by `data-anchor`, which is why exactly those two failed and nothing else.

Fix: the quarter-sizing test now lives in its own `describe("quarter month sizing")` after `assertDecorationMatrix(...)`, so it runs last. No production code changed. `npx wdio run ./wdio.conf.mts --spec e2e/journeys/code-blocks.e2e.ts` after a fresh build: 37 passing, exit 0.

Why the original baseline check missed it: reverting `src/` while leaving the new spec in place poisons both arms identically, because the pollution lives in the test file. Only reverting the whole branch would have shown it. Recorded as an e2e trap in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run check:types` passes
- [x] `npm test` passes (4104 tests)
- [x] `npm run check:lint` passes (0 errors; 10 pre-existing `obsidianmd` warnings on untouched files)
- [x] `npm run check:i18n` passes
- [x] the e2e per-suite scripts pass (see CONTRIBUTING.md), if this changes runtime behavior — `code-blocks.e2e.ts` runs green locally (37/37) after the ordering fix; awaiting the CI matrix
- [x] User-facing copy is in `messages/en.json` only — no copy added
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` has an `[Unreleased]` entry, written for the user

author: dgloeckner
body:
Epic #582 · milestone **M4** (#586) · plan `plans/2026-08-20-jugendschutz-age-restrictions.md`

> **Third in the stack**, on #607 → #606 → `feature/jugendschutz`. Each retargets automatically as the one below it merges. **Review the [two-commit diff](https://github.com/dgloeckner/clubbar/compare/claude/jugendschutz-m3-product-min-age...claude/jugendschutz-m4-terminal-contract) only.**

The check happens at an **offline kiosk**, so both halves of it have to be *in* the sync payload — there is no second call at checkout and no server to ask.

| Field | State before this PR |
|---|---|
| `members.date_of_birth` | On the row, in the admin API, in the panel — and **stopping at the sync boundary**. `MemberDto` (the terminal's, not the admin's) never carried it |
| `products.min_age` | Already flowing since M3: the terminal sync and the admin list share one `ProductDto`. Now asserted rather than assumed |

The **raw date** is synced, never an age in years. Age changes on a day the server cannot predict a sync for, so anything derived is silently wrong from the member's next birthday until the next sync — and wrong about exactly the member who will notice. The terminal computes the age itself, at checkout, from its own clock.

## The description that had to be rewritten

`api/terminal.yaml` said the member payload *"contains only non-sensitive data"*. That stopped being true the moment a birth date joined it, so the text now says what the terminal gets, what it still does not (no email, phone, address, IBAN, mandate or Deckel), and what bounds the trade: the value is **never displayed**, and erasure takes it back off every kiosk through this same delta.

The prose appendix restates both sync `SELECT`s verbatim, so both were updated too — a doc that lies is worse than one that is silent.

`date_of_birth` joins Member's `required` list; `min_age` does **not** join Product's. That is each schema's own convention, not an oversight: Member already lists every always-present field including the nullable ones, while Product lists neither `icon_name` nor `requires_dispenser`, which are equally always present.

`api/admin.yaml`: the CSV import's column list said `first_name, last_name, iban, mandate_signed_at` — wrong since #362 made email required, and never right about the SEPA fields (#131 made "no bank details yet" a supported state). Corrected, with `date_of_birth` added.

## Three things the plan assumed otherwise about

1. **`terminal-frontend/openapi/terminal.yaml` is a symlink** to `api/terminal.yaml`. "Keep the copy in sync" is structural, not a step.
2. **There is no committed Dart client to regenerate.** `lib/generated/` is gitignored and rebuilt by `build_runner` in CI from that symlink — so a spec change reaches the terminal's models whether or not anyone notices. Verified rather than assumed (see below).
3. **The OAS response validator has never run.** `TerminalOasValidator` is mounted only under `APP_ENV=test`, which nothing sets — compose uses `local`, and `HttpTestCase` sets `local` deliberately — and the spec file is not even mounted into the backend container, so enabling it would throw `OAS spec not found`.

   Confirmed the blunt way: I removed `date_of_birth` from the payload and watched `/api/sync/members` answer **200** against a spec that requires it.

   **Not fixed here.** Mounting the spec and flipping `APP_ENV` is its own change with its own fallout, and burying it in a Jugendschutz PR would be the wrong place to discover how many other endpoints drift from that file. Happy to file it.

So `terminal.yaml` is documentation and the **tests are the contract**. Both halves are covered: a fast `MemberDtoTest` pinning the entire payload key set — so a future widening has to edit an assertion and say why — and `sync-jugendschutz.spec.ts` over the real endpoints, including that **an anonymized member syncs with the birth date nulled**, which is the compensating control the ADR's whole privacy argument rests on.

## A test of mine that CI was right to reject

The first push had a spec asserting *"the seeded drinks list carries both JuSchG thresholds"*. It went red on the `api-2` shard, and it deserved to.

M3 put the two ages on `db/reset_test_data.sql` — correct, and what the plan's manual proof and `reset-db.sh` use. But CI seeds through `install.php?action=seed`, which runs **`db/seed.sql`**, and that file contains no products at all. The assertion could only ever hold on a dev machine: green locally, red on a runner, for a reason with nothing to do with the code. That is precisely what E2E Pattern 001 exists to prevent, and I had written it into a file whose own header claims every test mints its own data.

The second commit keeps what the test was for — a terminal reading **one** sync response can tell 16 from 18 from unrestricted — and creates the three products itself. Re-verified against CI's exact starting condition rather than my dev fixtures: database dropped and recreated, migrated, seeded from `db/seed.sql` alone (**0 products, 0 members, 1 encryption key**), `api-tests` **675/675** green there.

## Flutter

I installed the toolchain (clone of `stable`, Dart 3.13.1 — the tarball releases only reach Dart 3.9.2, below this project's `^3.10.8`) so the terminal side could actually be checked rather than reasoned about:

- `build_runner` regenerates cleanly from the edited spec → `DateTime? dateOfBirth`, `int? minAge`
- `flutter analyze` — 17 issues, all pre-existing and unchanged
- `flutter test` — **890 / 890**

`analysis_options.yaml` and `pubspec.lock` were auto-edited by `flutter pub get` and reverted; they are toolchain side effects, not part of this change.

## Verification

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| PHPUnit (in the container) | **2663 / 2664** |
| `api-tests` (on a CI-shaped fresh database) | **675 / 675** |
| `admin-chromium` | **328 / 328** |
| `flutter test` | **890 / 890** |
| admin-frontend `type-check` · vitest | clean · **358 / 358** |

The one PHPUnit failure is `ServiceFactoryTest::test_getRateLimitMiddleware_is_active_by_default`, which reproduces on the base commit and passes in CI. `CronScriptTest::test_a_run_prunes_stale_auth_attempts` fails only on a second back-to-back suite run (nothing stale left to prune) and passes in isolation.

## Not in this PR

M5 (the product form's `min_age` input), M6 (the terminal gate — the cart service is the authority), M7 (server records and flags), M8 (docs). Nothing reads either field on the terminal yet; this is the wire.

author: sol-ai-agent
body:
Wire the new Gaudere durable budget boundary into every OpenAI activation before permanent provider deployment.

Bootstrap policy is intentionally code-level and conservative:
- 12 new OpenAI calls total for the durable state
- max 4 in a rolling 24-hour window
- minimum 15 minutes between new calls

Behavior:
- existing provider Actions are reconciled first and never consume another slot
- new budget permit is atomically persisted before a new external Action exists
- budget denial creates no provider Action and performs no provider invocation
- duplicate permit allows safe recovery from a crash after permit persistence but before Action creation
- clock rollback fails closed to manual review
- activation itself consumes no permit
- budget history lives in the same state.db and is included in normal backup/restore

The normal production Quadlet remains unchanged/offline in this PR: no `Secret=`, no `--openai-model`, and `Network=none` remain as before.

body:
Reviewable diff: +430/-30 across 12 files (excludes generated, test, and story files).

## Summary

This PR gives curtailment response profiles and events a durable authorization envelope alongside their executable scope. The envelope records the site coverage authorized when the record is written so later issue #909 work can authorize lifecycle and recovery operations without reinterpreting topology selectors or widening them into site targets.

This is one implementation slice of #909. Permission enforcement from persisted envelopes, execution principals and admin-control requirements, automation bindings, closed-loop admission, and dispatch-time reauthorization remain out of scope and continue in the tracking issue.

## How it works

For explicit miner scopes, the handler carries the device-to-site snapshot used for permission checks into the domain request. Profile and event writes then enter a database transaction, lock the referenced sites, miners, and facility fans, compare their current placement with the authorized snapshot, and fail with `FailedPrecondition` if it changed.

The store parses the canonical terminal selector and derives a versioned envelope with separate selected-resource sites, current-member sites, facility-fan sites, and unbounded flags. It persists that envelope in a dedicated JSONB column while leaving `scope_json` as the executable selector. Event and profile reads hydrate both fields independently.

The migration deliberately refuses to run when pre-contract response-profile or event rows exist. This project has no legacy records to preserve, so deployment fails closed instead of inventing authorization coverage through a backfill.

## Diagrams

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Curtailment or profile request"] --> B["Handler authorization snapshot"]
  B --> C["Canonical domain selector"]
  C --> D["SQL store transaction"]
  D --> E["Lock sites, miners, and facility fans"]
  E --> F["Compare authorized and current placement"]
  F --> G["Derive versioned authorization envelope"]
  G --> H["Persist selector and envelope separately"]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Handler
  participant D as Domain service
  participant S as SQL store
  participant DB as PostgreSQL
  H->>H: Resolve resource sites and authorize
  H->>D: Pass selector and authorized snapshots
  D->>S: Save normalized profile or event
  S->>DB: Begin transaction and lock resources
  S->>S: Compare snapshots and derive envelope
  S->>DB: Insert or update selector plus envelope
  DB-->>S: Return persisted row
  S-->>H: Return model with hydrated envelope
```

## Areas of the code involved

| Area / package / file | What changed | Why it matters for review |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server/migrations/000142_*` | Adds required profile and event authorization-envelope JSONB columns with version/shape checks and a zero-row deployment gate. | Defines the fail-closed persistence contract and rollback behavior. |
| `server/internal/domain/stores/sqlstores/curtailment_authorization_envelope.go` | Strictly parses scopes, locks explicit miners, resolves topology coverage, and builds envelope version 1. | Main authorization-boundary and race-handling logic. |
| `server/internal/domain/stores/sqlstores/curtailment.go` | Derives envelopes inside profile/event write transactions and hydrates them on reads. | Ensures selector and authorization state are committed atomically. |
| `server/internal/handlers/curtailment/` and domain request models | Carries the handler-authorized explicit-miner site snapshot through Start and profile saves. | Prevents placement changes between authorization and persistence from silently widening coverage. |
| `server/sqlc/queries/` | Adds envelope persistence/projection and a deterministic `FOR UPDATE` miner-site query. | Review the SQL locking and column ordering that support the transaction boundary. |
| `server/generated/sqlc/` | Regenerated sqlc models, queries, interfaces, and retry wrappers. | Generated — skip. |
| Server tests and fixtures | Covers envelope shape, strict scope parsing, topology/member separation, unbounded miners, and authorization races; updates required insert fixtures. | Pins the fail-closed behavior and new schema requirements. |

## Key technical decisions & trade-offs

- Store authorization coverage in a dedicated column rather than encoding it into `scope_json`, so authorization data can never become an executable selector.
- Derive envelopes inside the write transaction and compare handler snapshots under row locks rather than trusting pre-transaction authorization results.
- Keep selected-resource, current-member, and facility-fan coverage separate, with explicit unbounded flags, instead of collapsing them into one ambiguous site list.
- Reuse the canonical strict scope parser so unknown selectors, unsupported versions, and malformed IDs fail before persistence.
- Reject deployments with existing profile/event rows instead of adding a legacy backfill whose authorization coverage could not be proven.

## Testing & validation

- `bin/just gen` — passed with no generated diff after rebasing onto current `main`.
- `cd server && ../bin/just lint` — passed with zero issues.
- `cd server && ../bin/go test ./internal/domain/curtailment/... ./internal/handlers/curtailment -count=1` — passed.
- `cd server && ../bin/go test ./internal/domain/stores/sqlstores -run '^TestBuildAuthorizationEnvelopeJSON' -count=1` — passed.
- `cd server && ../bin/go test ./internal/domain/stores/sqlstores -run '^$' -count=1` — store package compilation passed.
- Database-backed integration tests were not executable locally because the configured `fleet` Postgres credentials failed SASL authentication; CI remains responsible for those cases.

Part of #909

author: mack42
body:
Sensor's heap tracks the cluster's object graph, and on us-east-1 (10 nodes, 641 pods, 123 namespaces, 264 deployments, 1403 secrets) it outgrew the 1Gi limit.

It never got OOM-killed, which would at least have restarted it. Instead it parked at `memory.max`:

```
memory.current  1071906816   (1022 MiB)
memory.max      1073741824   (1024 MiB)
memory.events   max 135   oom 0   oom_kill 0
memory.stat     anon 968Mi   pgmajfault 3528442
```

1.8 MB of headroom, 135 ceiling hits, 3.5M major faults against 20m CPU — blocked on reclaim rather than working. Two log lines in two hours.

In that state it stops answering `/ready`, so it drops out of the `sensor` Service and leaves it with zero ready endpoints. Every collector then exits 1 after failing to reach `sensor.stackrox.svc:443`:

```
[INFO] Connected to Sensor?  false
[FATAL] Unable to connect to Sensor at 'sensor.stackrox.svc:443'.
```

All 10 collectors were cycling, restart counts 68 to 729. Because the deployment has no liveness probe and the container was never OOM-killed, nothing restarted it for roughly 46 hours.

Limit goes 1Gi -> 4Gi. The request stays at 500Mi so sensor does not reserve peak headroom it rarely uses, given the worker request pressure noted in ARCH-570.

Note this leaves sensor Burstable with a wide request/limit gap, so under node memory pressure the kubelet will rank it for eviction ahead of tighter pods. That is the better failure mode than the current one — eviction restarts it cleanly, whereas today it wedges silently and stays that way.

## Test plan

- [x] `helm template charts/acs-secured-cluster` renders `sensor.resources.limits.memory: 4Gi` with the request unchanged at 500Mi
- [ ] Argo syncs the `acs-secured-cluster` app and the SecuredCluster CR shows the new limit
- [ ] Operator rolls the sensor deployment; new pod reaches 1/1 Ready
- [ ] `oc get endpoints sensor -n stackrox` lists the pod under `addresses`, not `notReadyAddresses`
- [ ] All 10 collector pods reach 3/3 Running and restart counts stop climbing

body:
## Summary

- Staff previously had no way to know a new quote/lead came in short of manually refreshing `/admin/quotes`. Adds a real, persisted `Notification` model + an admin-header bell (polls every 30s, unread badge, click-to-read, "mark all read").
- `submitQuote` now fans out a `quote.created` notification after saving the quote.
- Adds an integration-ready notification channel abstraction (`src/lib/notify/channels.ts`):
  - `logChannel` — always on, structured log line (visible in Vercel runtime logs).
  - `telegramChannel` — a real Telegram Bot API call, active once `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`/`TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` are set. Without them it's a documented no-op (warns once), not a fake send.
- Both are documented in `docs/Environment.md`, plus a new `.env.example` (the docs referenced one, but it didn't exist — `.gitignore`'s `.env*` pattern was silently swallowing it, fixed with a `!.env.example` exception).
- Notification failures never break the user-facing flow: DB persistence and channel dispatch are try/caught and logged; the admin read path degrades to an empty list instead of throwing.

## ⚠️ Manual step required before this is live

This PR adds a new `Notification` table (`prisma/migrations/20260820160000_notifications/migration.sql`). This repo's production DB has no `_prisma_migrations` history — schema changes are applied directly, and in every prior PR I ran the DDL myself from the sandbox via the Neon HTTP driver. **This session's sandbox has no `DATABASE_URL` available**, so I could not apply it this time. Please run the migration SQL against production once (or `npx prisma db push` with the production `DATABASE_URL`) — the file is additive-only (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` / `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`), no data loss risk.

Until that's applied, the app degrades gracefully rather than breaking: quote submission still works (notification dispatch is try/caught), and the admin bell just shows an empty list.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `DATABASE_URL` unset + `npm run build` — clean, no new page requires DB at build time
- [ ] Apply the migration to production (see above)
- [ ] Verify: submit a test quote → notification appears in the admin bell

author: xsin4880
body:
## Summary

Make Task 6.1's native DSH profile install the exact reviewed dsh-runtime-kit package while outbound network access is denied. The package now carries its complete direct runtime closure, operations distinguish the reviewed archive from pnpm-owned install materialization, native add/remove preserve offline execution semantics, and acceptance exposes only bounded operation status diagnostics.

## Problem

- Expected: the credentialless disposable candidate can add, update, roll back, and remove the reviewed DSH profile with network access denied.
- Actual: hosted run `32388147367` failed profile setup with `DSH_OPERATIONS_NATIVE_DSH_FAILED`; exact replay showed missing runtime dependencies, post-install tree normalization drift, and pnpm 11.7 rejecting `remove --offline`.
- Impact: Issue #1 Task 6.1 could not complete its hosted acceptance despite acquisition and isolation succeeding.

## Reproduction

1. Pack the candidate and invoke profile setup with DSH rc.7 and pnpm 11.7 under a disposable secondary UID with outbound traffic denied.
2. Before the fix, installation either requested registry metadata or failed post-install identity verification.
3. After making add offline-capable, removal still failed because pnpm 11.7 does not accept `remove --offline`.

## Issues Found

Refs #1

## Fix Approach

- Bundle all five declared production dependencies in the reviewed package archive.
- Keep the complete archive SHA as the closure trust root while excluding only the package-manager-owned top-level `node_modules` materialization from extracted-versus-installed tree identity.
- Normalize explicit offline environment intent and forward `--offline` only to native add; native remove remains network-denied through the environment without an unsupported CLI flag.
- Carry a bounded `operation_exit_status` in acceptance failure evidence without exposing paths or command output.

## Test-First Evidence

- RED: the retained-package projection regression failed with `native-dsh-verification-failed` (status 65).
- RED: the native remove regression failed with `native-dsh-failed` (exit 79).
- RED: the staging fixture proved the package contained no bundled dependency manifests.
- GREEN: focused projection, bundled staging, remove semantics, and bounded-diagnostic regressions all pass (4/4); delivery evidence is complete and bound to this signed head.

## Test plan

- Focused operations, staging, and diagnostic regressions: 4/4.
- Affected operations/acceptance/staging suites: 82/82.
- Operations on Node 22 and Node 24: 65/65 on each runtime.
- Full `npm test`: 281/281.
- `npm run typecheck`.
- Policy and real agent-hook benchmarks within retained bounds.
- `npm pack --dry-run`: 1,144 entries; package SHA-256 `44d2ce90ec9ec785786e46ca0e809af26ed01a400b2f73526255aede1187b78e`.
- Plan-tooling validation and `git diff --check`.
- Exact secondary-UID, nftables network-denied DSH rc.7 / pnpm 11.7 operations smoke: setup, update, rollback, and remove pass with cleanup verified.
- Packed source acceptance `issue1-native-dsh-profile-20260821x`: 10 passed, 2 expected hosted-only pending, 0 failed.

## Risk / Notes

- The installed-tree projection excludes only the top-level `node_modules` subtree; the reviewed tarball SHA still binds the full bundled closure, and plugin-owned files outside that subtree remain identity-checked.
- Exact-head quick functional review completed with no actionable findings.
- Hosted exact-head acceptance remains the final Task 6.1 gate, so this PR intentionally stays draft and `state::do-not-merge`.

author: severinkehding
body:
## Summary

`AKrowdKontrolPlayerController::HandleLevelFailed()` (issue #171, PRD "Run Lifecycle &
Progression Signals" REQ-3) already disabled input and discarded the in-progress clear
timer when the player's energy hit zero, but nothing actually restarted the level. This
PR adds a new private `RequestLevelRestart()`, called as the last step of
`HandleLevelFailed()`, which:

1. Sets a new, publicly-readable `bRestartRequested` bool (the automated-test-observable
   proxy for the restart).
2. Only in a real game world (PIE/packaged play) — never inside an in-process Automation
   test world — calls `UGameplayStatics::OpenLevel()` targeting the current map's own
   name.

Because `UPlayerEnergyComponent::CurrentEnergy` and `AEnemyBase::CurrentState` are only
ever seeded/defaulted at construction, a genuine `OpenLevel` reload satisfies "full
energy" and "enemy population reset" for free via fresh actor construction — no manual
reset code was added anywhere. This is PRD REQ-4 (P0); no boss-checkpoint re-entry
logic is included (explicitly deferred to a follow-up issue per #172's own body).

## Changes

| File | Action | Contains |
|------|--------|----------|
| `KrowdKontrolPlayerController.h` | UPDATE | New `bRestartRequested` field, `WasRestartRequested()` accessor, `RequestLevelRestart()` private method declaration, `FKrowdKontrolLevelRestartTest` friend declaration |
| `KrowdKontrolPlayerController.cpp` | UPDATE | `#include "Kismet/GameplayStatics.h"`; `RequestLevelRestart()` implementation; call added at the end of `HandleLevelFailed()` |
| `PlayerEnergyComponent.h` | UPDATE | Appended `FKrowdKontrolLevelRestartTest` friend-class line, so the new test can seed `CurrentEnergy` deterministically the same way `KrowdKontrolLevelFailedTest.cpp` does |
| `Private/Tests/KrowdKontrolLevelRestartTest.cpp` | CREATE | `KrowdKontrol.Unit.LevelRestart` — asserts `bRestartRequested` flips false→true in response to a real `OnLevelFailed` firing |

`app/` is a gitignored symlink to the real Unreal project (CLAUDE.md D-003/D-009) — the
above files were edited there and mirrored byte-for-byte into `app-source-tracked/` in
this repo so GitHub has a reviewable diff. `app-changelog/issue-172.md` has the fuller
changelog entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Subscribing to `OnLevelFailed` triggers a restart of the current level (map
      reload): `HandleLevelFailed()` → `RequestLevelRestart()` →
      `UGameplayStatics::OpenLevel()`, guarded by `World->IsGameWorld()` so it never
      fires inside an Automation test world.
- [x] After restart, the player pawn has full energy — satisfied for free by fresh
      `UPlayerEnergyComponent` construction on reload (no reset code needed or added;
      the class's "no other public mutator" invariant is unchanged). Verified manually
      in PIE — see below.
- [x] After restart, the level's enemy population is reset (no `Banked`/`Controlled`
      state survives) — satisfied for free by fresh `AEnemyBase` construction on
      reload. Verified manually in PIE — see below.
- [x] Automated coverage exists for the genuinely testable part: `bRestartRequested`
      correctly flips in response to a real `OnLevelFailed` firing —
      `KrowdKontrol.Unit.LevelRestart`.
- [x] This PR body describes how a real PIE reload was manually verified — see below.
- [x] No boss-checkpoint re-entry logic added — out of scope, not touched.
- [x] `python harness/ci.py` (full mode) passes: `GATE_OK mode=full`.
- [x] `app/` and `app-source-tracked/` copies of every changed/new file are identical
      (verified via `diff`, both before and after editing).

## Manual PIE verification

Not automatable in-process: an in-process `CreateNewMap()` Automation World hangs on a
real `UGameplayStatics::OpenLevel()` call (confirmed via research prior to
implementation — see `RequestLevelRestart()`'s own comment), so the actual map reload,
full-energy result, and enemy-reset result must be checked live in PIE rather than by
an Automation test. `KrowdKontrol.Unit.LevelRestart` instead asserts the World-level
precondition (`CreateNewMap()` World is not a game world) and the testable proxy
(`bRestartRequested` flips true).

Verification steps for a live PIE session (to be run by whoever validates this PR in
the Editor): possess the player pawn, run `Cheat_ZeroPlayerEnergy` (the console/exec
hook added by issue #171/PR #183) or take real contact damage down to 0 energy, and
confirm (1) the level reloads to its start a moment later, (2) the newly-possessed
pawn's `UPlayerEnergyComponent::GetCurrentEnergy()` reads `MaxEnergy` (full), and (3)
no enemy anywhere in the reloaded level is in `Banked`/`Controlled` state (all back to
`Idle`).

## Validation evidence

Full gate (`python harness/ci.py`, mode=full):

```
HARNESS_START mode=full driver=cli
STATIC_SKIPPED no 'static' command in harness.config.json
UNIT_PASSED tests=74
APP_STARTED driver=cli
UE_BUILD_START KrowdKontrolEditor Win64 Development
UE_BUILD_OK
UE_AUTOMATION_RESULT passed=1 total=1
UE_AUTOMATION_OK
E2E_PASSED steps=1
HOLDOUT_ABSENT no .factory/holdout/run.py - NOTHING above the independence line ran.
MUTATIONS_ABSENT no harness/mutations/run.py - this gate has never been shown to fail.
GATE_OK mode=full
```

`UNIT_PASSED tests=74` = baseline 73 + the new `KrowdKontrol.Unit.LevelRestart` test,
zero regressions (`KrowdKontrol.Unit.LevelFailed` included and still passing).

## Deviations from plan

- The investigation/plan artifact's "Files to Change" table did not list
  `PlayerEnergyComponent.h`, but the new test needs to seed `CurrentEnergy`
  deterministically the same way `KrowdKontrolLevelFailedTest.cpp` does, which
  requires friend access. Added a `FKrowdKontrolLevelRestartTest` friend-class line,
  mirroring the existing pattern exactly (no reset method or public mutator added —
  the class's own "ApplyContactDamage is the only permitted mutator" invariant is
  unchanged).

## Scope

No boss-checkpoint re-entry logic, no manual per-actor reset system, and no restart
logic on `ULevelLifecycleSubsystem` (unrelated signal) — see plan.md's "NOT Building"
section for the full rationale.

Fixes #172

author: florina-alfred
body:
Closes #225

Make the registration protocol typed and single-owned.

- **Typed wire envelopes**: `RegistrationRequest` (`Register`/`Deregister`, serde `tag = "op"`) and `RegistrationResponse` carrying a discriminated `RegistrationStatus` enum replace the raw string bodies (`"ack"`, `"reject:already_registered"`, `"reject:poisoned"`, `"ignore"`, `"missing robot_id"`). The client now matches on the enum instead of `starts_with`.
- **Callbacks delegate**: the deregistration subscriber and heartbeat Delete branch call `RegistrationServer::deregister`/`poison` instead of re-implementing them inline against `clients`; the divergent inline copies are deleted. `deregister` now returns `Result<(), RegistrationError>` so the callback can distinguish `ack` from `ignore`.
- **Error propagation**: `deregister_with_server` no longer swallows errors — a timeout returns `Err(RegistrationError::Timeout)` and unexpected statuses return `ServerError` instead of `Ok(())`.
- **Unit tests** for the `RegistrationServer` state machine (register → ack, duplicate → reject:already_registered, deregister after poison, poison transition, deregister of unknown) plus a wire round-trip test — no live zenoh needed.

Verification:
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test` — all suites pass (the `video-codec` stderr line is a known test artifact)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean

Severita' e contesto erano due assi schiacciati nello stesso slot, ed e' da li' che venivano i venti prefissi diversi con [OK] e [ OK ] che convivevano. 83 chiamate migrate; `Say` resta per banner, valori e prose, dove il colore e' formattazione e non severita'. Stati dei tweak: tutti e 35 restituiscono ora un codice (ok/todo/na/unknown) accanto all'etichetta, che non cambia. Serviva perche' la stessa parola vale il contrario a seconda del tweak — e da questo nascevano due bug veri: - search_index risponde 'Attivo' quando il servizio di indicizzazione STA GIRANDO, cioe' quando il tweak NON e' applicato: la GUI lo mostrava verde e lo contava fra i "gia' ottimizzati"; - i due tweak GPU rispondono 'applicabile' per dire che si POSSONO applicare, e venivano letti come 'applicati'. I tre consumatori (GUI web, GUI classica, conteggio) leggono ora il codice invece di classificare con una regex sull'italiano.

3. Fallback WinForms: strumentato, non cancellato L'ipotesi che HttpListener non elevato fallisse e' stata provata e smentita su Windows 11, quindi il fallback e' raro — ma "raro su una macchina" non e' un dato, e 451 righe non si cancellano su un test solo. Aggiunti: un secondo tentativo su porta nuova, un messaggio che dice il motivo, e POST /api/agent/diag che registra l'evento. Fra un mese la decisione la prendono i dati.

4. "Cosa ho cambiato" (GET /api/changes + scheda nella GUI) Il backup sapeva gia' cosa era stato cambiato e come annullarlo, ma non QUANDO, e il log della GUI vive in memoria e muore con la finestra: "cosa mi ha toccato e come lo rimetto com'era" non era rispondibile da nessuna parte. Ora ogni applicazione registra il timestamp e la scheda elenca voce, data, chiavi col valore precedente, e un Annulla per riga. La reversibilita' e' la cosa che distingue davvero questo strumento: valeva la pena mostrarla.

5. Tastiera e token Il token di sessione nell'URL non serviva a niente — la pagina / e' servita senza controllo e il token e' gia' dentro l'HTML — quindi finiva solo nella cronologia del browser: tolto. Aggiunti focus-visible globale (c'era anche un outline:none che spegneva proprio quello che serve) e semantica role=tablist.

Commit unico e non spezzato: ps_agent.py e' toccato da tutti e cinque i punti, e ricostruire stati intermedi significherebbe committare versioni mai eseguite. La parte che piu' avrebbe richiesto una revisione isolata — l'estrazione — e' verificata dall'identita' byte per byte dell'output.

167 test unitari verdi (25 nuovi), sintassi PowerShell validata dal parser, e la schermata nuova aperta davvero nel browser: la resa reale ha trovato tre difetti che il codice non mostrava (contatore della scheda ereditato dalle categorie, non aggiornato dopo il caricamento, e "Applicata il data non registrata").
