author: teunp
body:
## Why

I got this wrong in practice, which is why it is worth writing down.

Handing #993's new `E_DOSE_ATTR_DOUBLE_USE` behaviour to the ferxtranslate maintainer, I told them "`25b5f473` is the commit a translator engine-CI pin should target". There is no such knob on their side. ferxtranslate pins **ferx-r** at a commit, and that ferx-r commit's `src/rust/Cargo.lock` pins ferx-core. They caught it and measured the actual chain:

```
ferx-r@7889719 (their CI pin)  -> ferx-core 6c0f317f   (2026-08-07)
ferx-r origin/main             -> ferx-core 59065317   (2026-08-20 16:46)
#1003 merge                    -> ferx-core 25b5f473   (2026-08-20 21:54)
```

Verified both lock revs myself before writing this. Both predate the merge, so the new diagnostic is not live downstream and will not become live on its own — it needs two bumps in order: ferx-r's lock, then their ferx-r pin.

## What this changes

CLAUDE.md already carried the lock-is-the-pin rule, but addressed only to someone working *inside* ferx-r — "a ferx-r PR that needs a new ferx-core commit must bump that lock". It said nothing to a third repo consuming ferx-r transitively, which is precisely the reader who gets it wrong. That is the gap I reasoned from when I gave the bad advice.

Adds, under **Sibling repositories**:

- the two-step bump, in order;
- "do not tell a downstream maintainer to pin ferx-core at `<sha>`";
- the trap — reading `ferx-r/src/rust/Cargo.toml` alone shows `branch = "main"` and reads as *unpinned*;
- a one-line check for the current lock rev, run as written rather than composed from memory:

```bash
git -C ../ferx-r show origin/main:src/rust/Cargo.lock | grep -A2 'name = "ferx-core"'
```

## Cross-repo dependency

| Repo | PR | Status | Must merge |
|------|----|--------|------------|
| ferx (R) | — | not needed | — |

## Breaking changes
- [ ] `.ferx` model file format
- [ ] `FitResult` / sdtab fields changed
- [ ] Public Rust API (`api.rs` / `types.rs`)
- [x] None

## Numerical validation
- [ ] Warfarin example converges and estimates are within tolerance of prior run
- [ ] Compared against: NONMEM / nlmixr2 / prior ferx commit
- [ ] Reference values
- [x] Not applicable — documentation only

## Performance
- [x] No significant impact expected — no code touched.

## Tests
- [ ] Unit test(s) added in the same module
- [ ] Regression test added that fails without this fix
- [x] No new tests needed — CLAUDE.md is guidance, not code. The one factual claim it makes (the shape of the lock entry) was verified by running the documented command.

## Example
- [ ] Example added to `examples/`
- [x] Inline below

<details>
<summary>Example</summary>

```
$ git -C ../ferx-r show origin/main:src/rust/Cargo.lock | grep -A2 'name = "ferx-core"'
name = "ferx-core"
version = "0.3.0"
source = "git+https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core?branch=main#59065317b265c0eb978cce3b5b9e257333f5c140"
```

</details>

## Docs
- [ ] `docs/` updated for user-visible changes
- [ ] New pages linked in `docs/_quarto.yml`
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry added
- [x] No user-visible change — contributor/agent guidance only, so no CHANGELOG entry (CLAUDE.md rule: internal-only changes need none).

## Checklist

author: elkaix
body:
## What this is

**No functional changes.** `git diff v0.4.0..main -- skills/` is empty — the cleaners, detectors, CLI flags, and API surface are identical to 0.4.0. This release exists to move the last manual release step into CI and to exercise the tag-triggered path end to end on a release where a failure costs nothing. The notes say so plainly rather than dressing it up as a feature release.

## Changes

- **Version bump to 0.5.0** in `pyproject.toml`.
- **`docs/release-notes/v0.5.0.md`** — merged before the tag is pushed, which is the ordering the new automation depends on and this is its first live test.
- **`workflow_dispatch` removed from both release workflows.** It was non-functional from the UI default: every step derives the version from the tag, so a branch dispatch hit `test -f dist/watermark_remover-main.tar.gz` or the `^v[0-9]` ref regex and failed closed. Dispatching from a tag ref already worked and still does; the stanza only ever produced a confusing failure.

### Considered and rejected

Adding a `tag` input and using `${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}`. It would have put user-supplied free text into `actions/checkout`'s `ref:`, letting an arbitrary ref publish to PyPI and GHCR, and it would have required weakening the `count(...) == 2` assertions in `test_release_image_tags_validate_ref_from_environment` — editing a security guard to accommodate the change it guards against. Deleting the stanza touches no test.

## Verification

- `make check` green: lint, format-check, compile, 982 passed / 1 skipped, smoke ok.
- `python -m build` produces `watermark_remover-0.5.0.tar.gz`, so the workflow's `test -f "dist/watermark_remover-${TAG#v}.tar.gz"` check will pass for `v0.5.0`.
- Both workflows parse; triggers are now exactly `{'push': {'tags': ['v*']}}`.
- The notes file satisfies the job's own title guard (`v0.5.0 — automated releases` starts with the tag at a non-alphanumeric boundary), and `0.5.0` matches the stable `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` pattern, so the release publishes with `--latest` rather than as a prerelease.

## After merge

Tagging `v0.5.0` will be the first execution of the `github-release` job from an actual tag trigger, closing the "unverified until v0.5.0" caveat from #21. I'll confirm the job took the notes-file branch rather than the `--generate-notes` fallback.

- **Release**

  - Releases now publish automatically when a version tag is created; manual release triggering is no longer available.
  - Supports explicit prerelease handling and safe retries without duplicate releases.
  - Package publishing, GitHub releases, and container image builds follow a consistent tag-based process.

- **Documentation**
  - Added release notes covering the publishing process, contribution guidance, project principles, and complete changelog.

author: paranoa-dev
body:
# Fail-fast configuration validation + standalone `typecheck` script (#230)

Resolves **AnchorNet-Org/AnchorNet-Backend#230** (GrantFox OSS / Third Campaign).

## Summary

`package.json` had no standalone `typecheck` — types were only checked as a
side effect of `build`. More importantly, configuration failures degraded
silently: `src/middleware/apiKeyAuth.ts` makes the auth middleware a **no-op
(open access)** whenever `API_KEY` is unset, so a missing environment variable
changed the service's security posture instead of refusing to start.

This PR adds a fail-fast configuration contract (`validateConfig`) that runs at
startup **before the port binds**, a `typecheck` script wired into CI as a step
distinct from `build`, the full configuration inventory, and tests for the
required-value failure path.

## Configuration inventory

| Variable | Default | Required? | Absent behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | `3001` | optional | binds to `3001` |
| `FEE_BPS` | `10` | optional | 10 bps; validated `0–10000` |
| `API_KEY` | unset | **required in `production`**; optional in dev/test | dev/test: open access (historical). `production`: **refuses to start** naming `API_KEY` |
| `CORS_ORIGIN` | unset | optional | all origins permitted (historical default) |
| `BODY_LIMIT` | `"100kb"` | optional | 100kb JSON limit |
| `MAINTENANCE_MODE` | `false` | optional | writes allowed |
| `NODE_ENV` | `"development"` | optional | drives env-specific behaviour |
| `METRICS_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS` | unset | optional | no snapshots |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_MS` | `86_400_000` | optional | 24h window |
| `RATE_LIMIT_MAX` | `30` | optional | 30/window |
| `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` | `60_000` | optional | 60s window |
| `TRUST_PROXY` | `false` | optional | proxy not trusted |

(Full reasoning in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.)

## Required-vs-optional classification

- **`API_KEY` → required in `production` only.** Its absence silently disables
  auth on every mutating endpoint — a security-relevant fail-open — so it must
  be present in production. In `development`/`test` the historical open access
  is preserved (no secret needed for local runs).
- **Everything else → optional** with a safe default; none alter a security
  control when absent. `FEE_BPS` is range-validated but still optional.

## Environment-sensitivity policy

Requirements are `NODE_ENV`-driven, never an unset variable: `production` ⇒
`API_KEY` mandatory; `development`/`test` ⇒ `API_KEY` optional. The mechanism
is explicit and centralised in `validateConfig`.

## Validation approach

**Hand-written checks in `src/config.ts` — no new dependency.** The service
ships exactly three runtime deps; a schema-validation library would be
unjustified for a twelve-value config that already has parsing helpers.
`validateConfig` is invoked from `loadConfig`, so it runs once at startup
before the server binds a port. Failures are actionable: the thrown
`ConfigValidationError` names the offending variable and explains the fix.

## Deliberate fail-open closure (called out)

The only behaviour change vs. the previous release: a `production` deployment
without `API_KEY` now **refuses to start** instead of running with open
mutating endpoints. No default was changed.

## Coordination with the `apiKeyAuth` issue

This issue owns the **general configuration contract** (fail fast on a missing
required value). The concrete authentication **policy** (when/how `API_KEY` is
enforced on routes) is owned by the separate `apiKeyAuth` issue.

## Evidence — fail-fast at startup

```text
$ NODE_ENV=production node dist/index.js
AnchorNet API failed to start: API_KEY is required when NODE_ENV=production.
Without it, mutating endpoints are open to unauthenticated access
(see src/middleware/apiKeyAuth.ts). Set API_KEY to a secret value, or run
with NODE_ENV=development for local open access.
$ echo $?
1

$ NODE_ENV=production API_KEY=secret node dist/index.js
AnchorNet API listening on http://localhost:3001   # starts normally
```

## What changed

- `src/config.ts` — added `validateConfig()` + `ConfigValidationError`; called
  from `loadConfig` so validation runs before the port binds.
- `src/index.ts` — wraps startup so an invalid configuration exits non-zero
  with a clear message before binding; keeps the default `app` export for
  tests.
- `src/config.test.ts` — added `validateConfig` tests: production-without-API_KEY
  throws (`ConfigValidationError`, names `API_KEY`), blank key treated as unset,
  dev/test allow missing key, production-with-key passes.
- `package.json` — added `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — added a distinct **Type check** step (runs
  before `build`).
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` — full inventory, classification, and policy.

## Acceptance criteria (from #230)

- [x] PR contains the full configuration inventory with defaults and absent-value behaviour.
- [x] Each value is classified required/optional, with reasoning.
- [x] Missing required configuration causes a non-zero exit with a message naming the variable, before the port binds.
- [x] A test covers each required-value failure path.
- [x] A `typecheck` script exists and runs in CI as a separate step from `build`.
- [x] No default changed except the deliberate fail-open closure (called out).
- [x] `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `npm test` all pass (494 tests, 42 suites).

## Verification

```bash
npm ci
npm run typecheck
npm run lint && npm run build && npm test
NODE_ENV=production node dist/index.js   # expect non-zero exit + clear message
NODE_ENV=production API_KEY=secret node dist/index.js   # expect it to listen
```

Closes #230.

author: sve-nnn
body:
Las descripciones ya están escritas en producción (29 de 30, ver abajo). Esta PR trae el script que las escribió y el arreglo de una ruta del validador.

## Qué pasaba

La plantilla de post ya cae al `excerpt` cuando falta `meta.description`, así que estas trece entradas no tenían ni una cosa ni la otra: salían sin `<meta name="description">` y Google armaba el snippet solo. Las dos categorías (`development`, `general`) tenían `categories.description` vacía, que alimenta la meta y el subtítulo visible.

La home ya estaba en 148 caracteres, así que ese punto del issue estaba resuelto de antes.

## Las descripciones

Treinta, escritas una por una leyendo cada artículo, en los dos idiomas, todas entre 120 y 155 caracteres. El script se niega a escribir si alguna se sale del rango. No se generan truncando el intro: un corte a 155 deja frases a la mitad y repite el título.

`que-es-css` es la única URL del dominio que rankea algo hoy (`css`, posición 23-26 en Ecuador y Colombia), así que es la que más pesa.

## Una salteada, a propósito

`en que-es-css` quedó sin escribir: ese post no tiene fila en inglés, así que la página sirve el español por fallback. Ponerle una meta description en inglés rotularía como traducida una página que no lo está. Es del issue #7.

La primera corrida murió justamente ahí, con `ValidationError: Content > Title, Content > Content`: Payload valida los campos requeridos al escribir, y `find` había devuelto el texto español por el fallback de idioma, así que el post parecía traducido. Ahora consulta con `fallbackLocale: false` y saltea los que no tienen título propio, listándolos al final.

## Validador

`que-es-css` se movió a `/blog/development/que-es-css` con la recategorización del blog, y el validador seguía pidiendo la URL vieja, que 308ea. `fetch` no sigue redirects, así que leía un cuerpo vacío y reportaba "0 caracteres" para una página que sí tenía descripción.

## Estado en vivo

`./scripts/seo/validate.sh 8` → **16/16**.

Refs #8

author: pmquang87
body:
## Scope

`*ELEMENT_SPH` (+ `_VOLUME`) → `/SPHCEL/<part_ID>`, `*SECTION_SPH` (+ `_TITLE` /
`_ELLIPSE` / `_TENSOR` / `_INTERACTION` / `_USER`) → `/PROP/SPH` (TYPE34),
`*CONTROL_SPH` `NMNEIGH` → `/SPHGLO`, `*DATABASE_HISTORY_SPH[_SET]` →
`/TH/SPHCEL`, `*DATABASE_SPHOUT` → the engine `/TFILE` frequency.

Before this branch the whole family landed in `skipped_keywords`, and for an
element keyword that is not a soft failure. Measured on master for
`Ryan_Lee_Examples/W11_SETUP_SPH_BirdStrike.k`: `SKIPPED: ['CONTROL_SPH',
'ELEMENT_SPH', 'SECTION_SPH']`, a bare `/PART/2` on a placeholder
`/PROP/SHELL/2`, and **0 of 18 795 particles emitted — 1.82 mass units, 100 % of
the projectile, with no `MESH LOSS:` warning**, because the orphan census can
only report elements that were parsed and none were. Worse than an absent bird:
those 18 795 nodes were still emitted, still carried `*INITIAL_VELOCITY_NODE`,
and were still the secondary side of two converted eroding `/INTER/TYPE25`
contacts — massless free nodes flying into a contact that reported itself
healthy. Same shape on all ten independent r14 SPH decks.

## The defining decision: where the mass lives

Radioss offers exactly two places for a particle's mass and they are mutually
exclusive, because the one that carries the mass also decides the smoothing
length (`spinih.F:85-109`, `spinit3.F:139-153`):

| where | particle mass | smoothing length `h` |
|---|---|---|
| `/SPHCEL` `Flag = 1/2`, `MASS` set | exact per particle | Radioss DERIVES `(√2·m/ρ)^(1/3)`; the property's `h` is **ignored** |
| `/SPHCEL` MASS blank (`Flag = 0`) | `Mp` from `/PROP/SPH` | the property's `h`, verbatim |

k2rad states the mass **once on the property** when the section's particles all
carry the identical value and the deck gives a usable `h` — exact total *and*
the deck's own `h` — and **per cell** otherwise, reporting in numbers what the
second route costs. Radioss's `√2` is the FCC packing factor, so its derived
support is 0.9354× LS-DYNA's on a simple-cubic fill and 0.8333× on close
packing; that is why the route is chosen rather than defaulted. This is the one
place the batch deliberately outranks dyna2rad's "copy the cell mass and move
on".

## d2r fidelity notes

Seven deliberate divergences from dyna2rad, each a measured defect on its side:

1. **`Mp` is always positive.** dyna2rad never sets the field, so
   `hm_read_prop34.F:235-239` raises `WARNING 138` on every deck it converts and
   forces `MP = 1` *in the deck's mass unit* — measured, four blank-mass
   particles gave `TOTAL MASS = 4.000000000000`. A zero-mass cell is written
   `Flag = 0`, never `1`: an explicit `Flag = 1` with a blank MASS keeps
   `TYPE = 1` and `spinit3.F:142` computes `VOL = 0/ρ` — `TOTAL MASS =
   0.000000000000` with no diagnostic at all.
2. **The LS-DYNA card defaults are applied by the parser** (`CSLH = 1.2`,
   `HMIN = 0.2`, `HMAX = 2.0`, `DEATH = 1e20`). The CFG declares them and the SDI
   read path does not apply them, so dyna2rad sees a blank `CSLH` as 0 and takes
   the `else` of `lsdCSLH > 0` — turning the commonest deck there is into a
   CONSTANT smoothing length with `SPHINI` discarded.
3. **`h_1D = 3` and `hmin`/`hmax`/`hcst` are NEVER emitted.** They live on a
   `radioss2026`-only third card that a `/BEGIN 2022` reader discards SILENTLY —
   measured, `0.37 / 3.77 / 1.77` echoed as the hard-coded `0.2 / 2.0 / 1.2`,
   `0 ERROR(S)` — while `h_1D = 3` on card 1 IS accepted, i.e. bounded dilatation
   with bounds nobody chose. dyna2rad writes exactly that combination, and
   targets `"hcst"`, which is not an attribute of the property at all.
4. **`Order` stays 0.** dyna2rad maps `SPHKERN == 2 → ORDER = 2`; Radioss's
   `Order` is the renormalisation CORRECTION order and `spcompl.F:107-118`
   dispatches on `-1/0/1` only, so such a particle gets no kernel correction.
5. **`*HOURGLASS` / `*CONTROL_HOURGLASS` never reach `h`.** dyna2rad copies
   `QM`/`QH` into the `/PROP/SPH` field named `"h"` — a dimensionless viscosity
   into a LENGTH. Measured: `QM = 0.13` with `SPHINI = 0.5` echoed
   `SMOOTHING LENGTH = 0.13`, and a global `QH` **zeroed it outright**.
6. **`MASS < 0` is a VOLUME, and `_VOLUME` means the same** → `/SPHCEL` Type 2.
   dyna2rad honours neither: `TOTAL MASS = 8.0` instead of `0.016`, and a
   `_VOLUME` block wrong by exactly ρ.
7. **`NEND` is expanded.** Neither dyna2rad nor OpenRadioss's own native `.k`
   reader does it — measured `NUMSPH = 1` where the card asks for a cloud.

Plus two things dyna2rad has no equivalent for: `/TH/SPHCEL` is screened the
#106 way (its SPH branch is the only element branch in
`converttimehistory.cxx` with no `FindRadElement` filter, so a dangling id
converts "successfully" and then is starter `ERROR 69`), and the `/SPHCEL` id
column is offset with `IDNOFF` at conversion time — dyna2rad emits a
`//SUBMODEL` and the id column is a plain `INT` with no entity type, so the
submodel machinery leaves it alone while `/NODE` moves (measured: four
`ERROR 78` and `TOTAL MASS = 0`).

## Test counts and corpus

|  | `origin/master` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| pytest | 3061 passed, 2 skipped, 888 subtests | **3202 passed, 2 skipped, 922 subtests** |
| new | — | `tests/test_sph.py`, 141 tests + 34 subtests |
| ruff | clean | clean |

One existing test changed: `test_optt_on_a_solid_only_part_is_reported_as_inert`
— the OPTT warning now reads "SOLID **or SPH** elements only", because SPH
joined that bucket (there is no `NUMSPH` loop in `i7sti3.F` either).

**Corpus**, 415 deduped decks (73 repo-side including all 40
`Ryan_Lee_Examples`, plus 342 under `dynaexamples_r14_ton-mm-s`), both `_0000`
and `_0001` SHA256'd, `origin/master` vs this branch:

* **401 byte-identical, 14 moved, 0 conversion errors on either side**;
* every mover carries an SPH keyword, established by an independent grep
  following `*INCLUDE` one level — **no mover without one, and no SPH-carrying
  deck that failed to move**;
* **zero warning-count changes on the 401 byte-identical decks**, so the new
  deck-wide duplicate-`/PROP` scan adds no noise.

The review round itself moved 7 of those 14: bar1/bar2 (the LAW2 clone) and
five decks whose particle masses need more than seven significant digits —
e.g. r14 `taylor1.k`, whose `/PROP/SPH` `Mp` went from `2.025177E-09` to the
deck's own `2.0251772E-09`.

**Every SPH arm is mutation-verified**: 30 of 30 — removing the arm makes the
full suite fail. Two controls behaved (dropping `abs()` in `_sph_flag_and_mass`
and `sqrt(2)` in `_radioss_h` both fail), so the harness is sound.

## Validation

**Mass.** r14 `foam.k` → `NUMSPH = 1000`, `PARTICLES MASS =
2.2640880000000E-07`, per-part echo `Mass 2.26408800E-04` = 1000 ×
2.264088e-07 to every printed digit, **no `WARNING 138`**. `W11_SETUP_SPH_
BirdStrike.k` (18 795 particles): emitted total 1.819999917 vs the deck's
1.819999917, deviation 2.1e-11 %; part KE = 1518.79 = ½·1.82·(38²+15²) exactly,
so the projectile is moving. `W11_Multi` (three per-particle masses on one
section, per-cell route): 1.850173002 vs 1.850173002. Purpose-built lattice
decks: hand value `m = ρ·d³ = 8.0e-09`, N = 1000 → starter `TOTAL MASS =
7.9999999999999E-06` (1.3e-12 %, double-precision summation), `Ixx =
5.28000000E-04` = M·2·33 exactly, CoM (9,9,9) exact.

**Free particles (the #120 shape).** Explicit deck: the only `/BCS` is the
four anchor-plate nodes, **zero** of the 1000 SPH nodes. Implicit deck: the only
`/BCS` is the synthesized inert probe. Counterfactual — adding one genuinely
free orphan node makes the guard fire on exactly that node, so the arm is live
and discriminates. Physically: free-fall over 16 606 cycles, worst
`|d_z − ½gt²|` = **1.459e-05 %**, particle-to-particle spread **0.000e+00 mm**
at every sample, `Z_MOMENTUM` vs `M·g·t` to 2.6e-06 %, `IE` exactly 0.

**Smoothing length is consumed, not inert.** `dt = h/(c·(qb+√(qb²+1)))` is
exactly linear in `h` (`mdtsph.F:132`), so three decks differing ONLY in `h`
pin it: `SPHINI 2.0` → mea

author: mateuskasuya
body:
Irmão de [`tech-lamjav/analytics-engineering#100`](https://github.com/tech-lamjav/analytics-engineering/pull/100) (issue AE #95), que cria o mart `fact_value_funnel`.

Os workflows enumeram modelo a modelo, então **modelo fora da lista nasce parado**: a tabela
existiria no repositório e nunca seria construída no agendado. O `fact_value_funnel` entra
**antes** do `fact_value_opportunities` nas quatro listas — `dbt run` e o recovery com
`--full-refresh`, nos dois workflows.

A ordem importa porque a guarda de paridade compara as duas tabelas na mesma execução: funil
construído **depois** do board compararia a foto de agora com a de quinze minutos atrás.

Cada arquivo mantém o seu próprio estilo de `--select` — o `workflow_futebol.yml` repete a
flag, o `workflow_futebol_odds.yml` lista os alvos como argumentos de um `--select` só.

## ⚠️ Mergear não basta, e a ordem é o contrário do que parece

Editar o YML **não muda o workflow vivo**: precisa de `gcloud workflows deploy`.

E este deploy vai **antes** do `./build-and-push.sh dbt_futebol` do PR irmão. As guardas do
funil viajam na imagem e o agendado as roda por `tag:guarda`; o modelo só é construído se
estiver no selector do workflow **vivo**. Imagem nova + workflow velho = duas guardas vermelhas
sobre uma tabela que não existe.

A ordem inversa é inócua, e foi verificada: um `--select` que nomeia modelo ausente da imagem é
**aviso** do dbt, exit 0 — o workflow novo simplesmente ignora o `fact_value_funnel` enquanto a
imagem velha estiver rodando.

author: apholmes7-bot
body:
## What this does

The owner asked for two things on 2026-08-20: *"a couple fuel pumps at NMC wharf which charge a higher
price, then there's a full gas station at the end of the wharf road intersection with Route 91."*
#610 priced both sites; #612/#613 baked the kit and built its 23 Defs and prefabs. This is the ground
they stand on.

**Site A — the wharf.** Two `dispenser_sDock` pedestals on the apron's seaward face, gas and diesel.
**Site B — Route 91.** The full forecourt at the T where Wharf Road dead-ends on the through-road:
island, two multi-product machines, a two-bay canopy, the pylon sign, the C-store with its seamless
sales floor, and the tanker fill cluster.

Plus the whole-scene reach pass the kit's own README says is owed, and the forecourt's paving.

---

## The layout is the rig's, not mine

`StationIso.plan()` was run in the standalone V8 harness on the committed `gasStationRig.js`, in the
registered load order (`deckIsoSolid → fuel → gasStation → stationInterior`). Every offset in
`NineMileCreekStation.Route91Layout()` is that call's output, with the cfg recorded beside it.

**The harness was controlled first.** `StationIso.gameplayAll({grades:['gas','diesel','mixed']})`
reproduced the committed sidecar **byte-for-byte at 83,650 bytes** (against the git blob, not the
working tree — `core.autocrlf` inflates it to 88,726). That is what proves the load order and the
grade list before any number was read off the rig.

The facing rule was measured the same way, through the rig's own `project()`, un-squashing the 40°
elevation so the reading is a ground bearing:

* local **+Y** bears **45°·d** — cell 0 north, cell 2 east. This is `AzimuthConvention.Clockwise`.
* local **+X** bears **45°·d + 90°**.

⚠️ **A dispenser's business axis is +X, not +Y**, so `FacingForHeading(seaward)` points a dock
pedestal's hose *along* the wall instead of over it — a quarter turn wrong that draws perfectly.
`StationCatalog.FacingForLocalDirection` exists for that, derived from the piece's own published
nozzle position, and a test fails if the two helpers ever start agreeing for this piece.

---

## Where the two sites are, and why

### Site A — the apron, south of the brow

`NineMileCreekMainland`'s float note has said since Phase A that *"the west wall is the service end
(the fuel pump and the oil tank are both on it)"*. Nothing had built it. This is that sentence taken
literally — and it is also the only answer the yard allows: the spit is full (the fish market misses
its own site by 0.38 m), so a fuel island ashore was never on the table.

Everything is derived, nothing typed:

| | derivation | value |
|---|---|---|
| standback from the lip | nozzle reach 1.06 + body 0.22 + half the quay wall 0.175 + clearance 0.30 | **1.755 m** |
| north pedestal | `GangwayShoreEnd.y − 4` | (90.245, **66**) gas |
| south pedestal | north − 4 (twice the pump's own 2 m reach) | (90.245, **62**) diesel |

Measured and pinned by tests: both clear the brow, the ladder, all 14 berths and the slipway band;
both stand on ground that is dry at spring high; the standing spot clears the #609 quay wall by
exactly the 0.30 m the constant asks for; and **a hull lying half a beam off this face at either
pedestal is inside the dredged channel at spring low** — which matters, because the basin bares and
"alongside the wharf" is not everywhere a wet berth here.

### Site B — the south-west corner of the junction, 16.6 m out

Wharf Road **dead-ends** on the through-road, so the junction is a T and this corner is straight
ahead as you drive up off the wharf. Chosen by the max-min-slack search `NineMileCreekShops` used for
the restaurant — all four corners × all four orientations, against the road corridors, the nine town
lots at `TownLotRadius`, their yard polygons (#604) and the truck park, with the front edge held
within 1.5 m of Route 91's corridor so the apron *meets* the carriageway.

* **3.48 m** to the nearest thing (House South's dooryard) — the binding clearance
* **3.51 m** to Wharf Road's corridor
* **1.33 m** from the front edge to Route 91's corridor

⚠️ The runner-up scored 0.08 m better and was **rejected on reading, not on numbers**: it puts the
C-store between the pumps and the highway, which is a station with its back to the road. The corner
across the junction to the north scored 2.35 m.

The forecourt's road side faces **east**, so the island lies parallel to the highway and a vehicle
pulls in off it.

---

## ⭐⭐ The whole-scene reach pass, and the gap a positive control found

Every `reach_point` in this kit was tested at bake time — but **scoped to one piece**. The Def says so
(`ReachTestedAgainstThisPieceOnly`) and the README repeats it. `StationReachAudit` runs the rig's own
march (body 0.22 m, arm 1.20/1.90 m, 6 cm steps, as-asked → flipped → four axes) over the whole
forecourt plus whatever the region says is in the way.

**32 fittings across both sites, 0 with nowhere to stand.**

⚠️ **That green is only worth something because a control found a real gap first.** With the wall and
road tests alone, a pedestal set at the apron's very lip **PASSED** — its standing spot is 1.06 m out
over the basin, inside no blocker and nowhere a body can be. The pass was asking *"is this inside a
solid"* and never *"is there anything to stand on"*. `SceneObstructions` now asks the authored terrain
whether the ground floods at spring high, and the control fails as it should. Three positive controls
ship as tests:

1. a pedestal at the lip → caught (its spot marches 1.71 m)
2. one piece stood on another's standing spot → caught, and it names the piece
3. the forecourt shoved 8 m into Route 91 → the clearance sweep goes negative

---

## The wiring

Both sites' pumps point at their `FuelStationDef` (#610) and charge through the region's existing
`PersistentWalletProxy` — **found**, not made, which is why this runs after the wharf economy.

### ⚠️⚠️ One hose per dispenser side, and that is a finding rather than a choice

Measured off the shipped Defs: a multi-product machine's three nozzles publish the **same ground reach
point** (`sMpd` a0/a1/a2 are all `(1.21, −0.34)`) and differ only in Z. Three `FuelPump`s there would
be three candidates at one `WorldPosition`, and `InteractResolver`'s total order — priority, then
distance, then **lowest id** — hands every press to the same one forever. Two of the three grades
would be drawn on the machine and unreachable.

So a side carries exactly one hose, its grade named in the offer label before the press. Route 91's
four faces carry **gas · diesel · mixed · gas**. Giving a pump a grade *choice* is a change to the
interact seam (`HiddenHarbours.Economy`), not to placement, and is left to that lane. A test pins the
coincident reach points so the day that stops being true, this can be revisited.

---

## Also in here

* **The forecourt is paved.** One row in `NineMileCreekRoads.Pads()`, concrete, covering the driving
  half only (storefront's front face out to the road edge). It does a second job:
  `NineMileCreekFields.IsGrassGround` steps off any pad, so the meadow stops at the concrete instead
  of growing up between the pumps.
* **Colliders turn; sprites do not.** Baked iso art contains the camera, so the facing *is* the
  rotation. The sidecar's footprints are the ground the piece covers, stated in the piece's own frame,
  so at any cell but 0 they are turned — the blocker children carry that rotation and the root stays
  at identity (which is also what `PropertyBoundary` requires of a host).
* **Hit-testing happens in each blocker's own frame.** The rig inflates an axis-aligned bbox rather
  than offsetting the polygon; in world at a diagonal facing that would over-block by up to 41%.

---

## ⚠️ What is NOT wired, and it is logged on every build

1. **Boat tanks — this moved under the slice, so it is stated by PR number rather than as a flat
   claim.** The economy lane is landing the tank in a five-PR stack. **Merged:** #618 (tank as d

author: albanandrieu
body:
## Summary

Reduces unnecessary CI executions and makes the runtime version deterministic.

### Changes
- Pin Node to `>=24.11.0 <25` and npm to `>=11.6.2 <12` to prevent automatic major upgrades on Vercel.
- Replace broad CI `paths-ignore` with an application-focused `paths` allowlist.
- Restrict Playwright to `master` PRs and runtime/E2E-relevant files.
- Keep existing Chromium and Next.js caches and failure-only artifacts.
- Reduce Playwright timeout from 60 to 45 minutes.

### Expected impact
- Documentation/CV/Docker-only PRs no longer start application CI or Playwright unnecessarily.
- Fewer GitHub Actions minutes and fewer redundant Next.js builds.
- Node 25/26 cannot silently become the Vercel runtime through the package engine range.

### Follow-up

author: frankii91
body:
## Summary

- keep encrypted job bundles and launch credentials out of automatically generated `JOB_*` variables
- preserve manager-computed `job_env`, `BASE_URL`, and `BASE_APP_URL` for remote jobs without mutating the shared configuration object
- prevent Docker, Kubernetes, SSH, and SSHX transport credentials from crossing into their child container, pod, local shell, or remote bootstrap environments
- stop logging the complete child environment and invalid Kubernetes config contents
- retain the existing public runtime contract, including user runtime secrets, `JOB_ARG` for Docker/Kubernetes, public `JOB_*` metadata, and credential-free `DOCKER_HOST`

## Boundary details

- Docker keeps connection-only credentials and credential-bearing `DOCKER_HOST` references in the wrapper, while preserving credential-free endpoints for compatible nested Docker clients.
- Kubernetes keeps `KUBE_CONFIG` in the wrapper and no longer prints invalid configuration content; `JOB_ARG` remains ordinary pod runtime input.
- SSH local execution removes the selected host/reference plus password, key, and passphrase from the spawned shell environment.
- SSHX removes the selected `SSH_HOST`/`JOB_ARG` transport value, its reference, and SSH credentials from the generated remote export script.
- URI detection covers password and username-only userinfo plus normalized token/secret/password query-key variants.

This PR intentionally does not change browser status payloads, completed-job storage, retry queues, email/webhook payloads, or manager-worker protocol state.

## Validation

- `npm test` — 101/101 tests, 384 assertions, 3 suites
- focused plugin boundary suite — 8/8
- real wrapper entrypoints exercised with captured Docker `Env`, Kubernetes pod manifest, SSH local process environment, and SSHX bootstrap script
- remote-manager launch regression verifies `job_env` copy semantics and manager `BASE_URL`
- `node --check` for all changed JavaScript/MJS sources
- `git diff --check`

## Review provenance

The issues and initial patches were proposed by a Codex Ultra security review (fork PRs [frankii91/cronicle-edge#15](https://github.com/frankii91/cronicle-edge/pull/15) and [frankii91/cronicle-edge#52](https://github.com/frankii91/cronicle-edge/pull/52)). This version was manually re-analyzed across all four transport plugins, expanded to the complete connection-credential boundary, tested against the real wrapper entrypoints, independently reviewed by three reviewers, and is submitted for maintainer review in line with our prior discussion.

author: robhunterclaude
body:
## What was wrong

`faviconState` treated `services.cron.installed` as "cron will fire". Turning cron off comments the wake line out and leaves the file installed with the daemon alive, so a switched-off agent kept a stopwatch on its tab forever. `lib/cron.js` already computed the fact that settles it — `enabled` — and `/api/status` dropped it before serving.

Second gap: a live schedule whose cycles keep failing looked exactly like a healthy one. `fleethd-reviewer` sat behind a stopwatch through four consecutive dead cycles this morning while its sandcat egress was blacked out.

## What this does

- `/api/status` forwards `services.cron.enabled`, and `faviconState` returns `idle` (grey ring) for it. Only an explicit `false` counts, so a payload from an older portal — which has no `enabled` field — does not turn every agent grey.
- Adds a fifth state, `degraded`: a filled triangle in `#d29922`, which is Flenderson's `.status-dot.partial`. Same yellow, same meaning, dashboard and tab strip.
- `/api/status` gains `lastCycleErrored`. It walks back to the newest `cycle_start` and reports whether an `error` beat it there — the harness logs `error` and then still logs `cycle_end`, so the newest event alone says nothing about whether the work landed. `null` when there is no history to judge.
- `lib/cron.js`: the comment test was anchored at column 0, so an indented `# … wake.sh` read as a live schedule.

Precedence is `running > idle (off) > broken (dead daemon) > degraded > scheduled`. Off-on-purpose outranks any complaint about a schedule nobody asked to keep; a dead daemon outranks a failed cycle, because "nothing will fire" is more useful than "the last one did not land".

## Verification

`npm test` — 586 node tests, 0 fail; shell suites pass.

Booted a real portal on fixture agent dirs and read the state the browser half picks:

| scenario | cron payload | faviconState |
|---|---|---|
| wake line commented out | `installed=T daemon=T enabled=F` | `idle` |
| commented out, indented | `installed=T daemon=T enabled=F` | `idle` |
| live schedule, clean history | `installed=T daemon=T enabled=T` | `scheduled` |
| live schedule, errored cycle | `installed=T daemon=T enabled=T` | `degraded` |
| no cron file | `installed=F` | `idle` |

Then in a real headless browser against that portal, reading `#favicon` after the status poll: cron-off → `title="idle"`, grey ring `#9e9e9e`; errored → `title="degraded"`, triangle `#d29922`.

Rasterised all five at 16px and measured ink distribution — silhouettes are distinct (filled disc / top-heavy stopwatch / bottom-heavy triangle / ring), except `idle` and `broken`, which differ by colour by design and are pinned by an existing test.

## Not in scope

`lib/ui/styles.js` still uses `#ff9800` for the sidebar `.status-yellow` dot, against Flenderson's `#d29922`. Left alone — this PR only settles what the tab icon does.

body:
## Problema

Quando o acesso era recusado, a tela de entrada mostrava **"Sessão não autenticada. Entre novamente no VybeChat."** — que não diz à pessoa o que ela precisa saber: que o código está errado.

O cliente dispara `channel:join`, `direct:list` e `decision:list` no mesmo instante do `presence:join`. Com o acesso negado, os quatro voltam com erro, e os três genéricos sobrescreviam justamente a mensagem específica que chegou primeiro.

Verificado em produção depois do deploy anterior: digitando um código errado, aparecia a mensagem genérica.

## Correção

- O cliente passa a preservar o **primeiro** erro de autenticação. `submitProfile` já limpa o estado antes de cada nova tentativa, então uma segunda tentativa mostra o erro novo normalmente.
- Acentuação das três mensagens do Worker corrigida (`Sessão`, `não`, `código`, `possível`).

## Verificação

Contra o Worker rodando em `wrangler dev`, com a build de produção do cliente:

- Código errado → **"O código de acesso da equipe não foi aceito."**, na tela de entrada, sem erro no console.
- Matriz de administradores, com os slugs reais configurados (`paulo,vinicius,ewerton,deivid`) — 10/10:

| Nome digitado | userId gerado | Papel |
|---|---|---|
| Paulo | `paulo-...` | admin |
| Vinicius | `vinicius-...` | admin |
| Ewerton | `ewerton-...` | admin |
| Deivid | `deivid-...` | admin |
| Vinícius (com acento) | `vinicius-...` | admin |
| PAULO (maiúsculas) | `paulo-...` | admin |
| Paulo Silva (nome completo) | `paulo-silva-...` | admin |
| Estagiario | `estagiario-...` | member |
| Paulinho | `paulinho-...` | member |
| Deividson | `deividson-...` | member |

Os dois últimos confirmam que o casamento por prefixo não pega nomes parecidos: exige o slug exato ou o slug seguido de hífen.

- Suíte do repositório: 75/76. A única falha é `realtime-worker-url`, que exige `VITE_REALTIME_WORKER_URL` no ambiente e passa quando a variável está definida.

## Estado dos secrets

Ambos já estão ativos em produção: `VYBECHAT_WORKSPACE_CODE` e `VYBECHAT_ADMIN_SLUGS` (`paulo,vinicius,ewerton,deivid`).

## Nota operacional

Todo push de branch dispara o Workers Builds e cria uma **versão do Worker que não é implantada**. Enquanto ela existir, a Cloudflare recusa editar secrets (`Secret edit failed... the latest version of your Worker isn't currently deployed`). Se precisar mexer em secret, implante antes — ou use `wrangler versions secret put`.

author: thegspiro
body:
### Motivation

- Ensure approving a shift swap validates the live state of offering/requested shifts, participating users, and assignments immediately before mutating data to avoid stale approvals.  
- Remove duplicated assignment checks by reusing the same validation logic as `create_assignment` so rules for overlap, leave, eligibility, driver qualification, finalization, and capacity stay consistent.  
- Prevent race conditions where concurrent approvals bypass capacity/duplicate checks by locking affected rows or using equivalent transactional control and only marking a request approved after all validations and changes succeed.  

### Description

- Introduced a reusable validator `._validate_assignment_candidate(...)` that encapsulates duplicate-assignment, overlap, leave-of-absence, position availability/capacity, position eligibility, driver qualification, and mutable/future-shift checks.  
- Updated `create_assignment` to call `._validate_assignment_candidate` instead of duplicating those checks.  
- Reworked `review_swap_request` to acquire row-level locks on the swap request, involved shifts, and affected assignments (via `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` / ordered selects), revalidate live state under lock, and only apply mutations after all validations succeed.  
- Defined explicit swap semantics: two-person exchanges swap `user_id` values while keeping positions attached to shift seats, and one-way moves transfer the assignment (keeping the member’s position with them).  
- Added clear, actionable business errors for stale conditions (e.g. offering/requested shift cancelled or finalized, offering/requested assignment removed, position filled after request submission, member no longer eligible or on leave).  
- Rollback-on-reject behavior is used so a rejected approval leaves the DB unchanged and releases locks predictably.  

### Testing

- Ran formatting and static checks: `python -m black --check app/services/scheduling_service.py` which passed.  
- Verified bytecode/compilation with `python -m compileall -q app/services/scheduling_service.py` which passed.  
- Commit hooks (including `black`, `flake8`, and `isort` checks executed during commit) completed successfully.  
- Attempted unit tests: ran `pytest` for the affected scheduling assignment and swap tests, but the test run was blocked by the local test database not being reachable (MySQL connection to `localhost:3306` failed), so integration-style tests could not complete in this environment.

author: shlsdhrth16dev
body:
Fixes #37638.

When a guardrail was configured with `additional_provider_specific_params.secrets.config.mode: block`, it correctly blocked on `/chat/completions` but silently downgraded to `redact` on provider-native passthrough routes (e.g. Gemini `generateContent`, Vertex AI) because `LlmPassthroughRouteHandler` returned early without invoking the guardrail at all.

## Root cause
`_get_provider_handlers()` only contained an entry for `"bedrock"`. For every other provider, both `process_input_messages` and `process_output_response` returned the original data unchanged — the guardrail never ran, so `resolve_check_mode()` fell back to the guardrail's built-in default (`redact`).

## Fix
Added `_generic_passthrough_handler()` which returns a `PassThroughEndpointHandler` instance — the same generic fallback `BedrockPassthroughGuardrailHandler` already uses for its own non-Converse (invoke) routes. Unknown providers now delegate to it instead of returning early.

This fixes the issue for Gemini, Vertex AI, and all future passthrough providers automatically, with no new provider-specific code needed.

## Tests
9 new unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/llms/pass_through/guardrail_translation/test_llm_passthrough_route_handler.py`:
- Gemini input blocking (`mode=block` raises)
- Vertex AI input blocking raises
- Gemini output blocking raises
- Unknown provider falls back to generic handler (not skipped)
- Bedrock still routes to its dedicated handler (regression guard)
- Non-dict responses pass through unchanged

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added and all 9 pass
- [x] No existing behaviour changed (bedrock still uses its dedicated handler)
- [x] Inline comments explain the two-tier dispatch architecture

author: krzyssikora
body:
## The problem

Add a callout (or spoiler) with text but no nested children, save, and the editor shows:

> This callout shows its text above. Add an element below to nest content inside it.

**Text above what?** Neither container renders its body in the editor row. The row shows only the type tag and the label — `el.title`, else `element_summary`, which for a callout is `display_heading` (`courses/templatetags/courses_manage_extras.py:157`). The body is never painted there.

The "above" the copy meant is the **published page**: `templates/courses/elements/calloutelement.html` renders `callout__body` and then `callout__children`, so the text genuinely does sit above nested content *there*. But the very next clause — "Add an element **below**" — points at the editor's add-menu. One sentence, two different frames of reference. That's the incoherence.

## The fix

`templates/courses/manage/editor/_element_row.html`, two `{% trans %}` strings (`:198`, `:300`). No markup, no logic, no CSS.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Spoiler, has body | This spoiler shows its text above. Add an element below to nest **more** content. | This spoiler has text, but nothing nested inside it yet. Add an element to nest content inside it. |
| Callout, has body | This callout shows its text above. Add an element below to nest content inside it. | This callout has text, but nothing nested inside it yet. Add an element to nest content inside it. |

`"more"` is gone from the spoiler string for the same reason `"above"` is — it implied something was already nested, and by definition nothing is. That also makes both second sentences identical.

The `{% else %}` branches (`This spoiler is empty.` / `This callout is empty.`) were already accurate and are untouched.

## The fuzzy trap fired

`makemessages` marked both new entries `#, fuzzy` and — because the two msgids are now near-identical — pre-filled **both** with the *callout's* old Polish text. The spoiler entry silently became `"Ta ramka pokazuje tekst powyżej…"`: wrong element, wrong wording. Flag and msgstr cleared on both.

New Polish:

- spoiler → `Ta rozwijana treść ma tekst, ale nie ma jeszcze nic zagnieżdżonego. Dodaj element, aby zagnieździć w niej treść.`
- callout → `Ta ramka ma tekst, ale nie ma jeszcze nic zagnieżdżonego. Dodaj element, aby zagnieździć w niej treść.`

`locale/en` keeps empty `msgstr` per the existing convention (falls back to the msgid). Both `.mo` recompiled.

## Verification

author: pacu
body:
Closes #2190. Linear: MOB-1757

## Why

The `zodl-slipstream` crate is licensed **AGPL-3.0-only**, while every artifact this repository publishes carries an MIT POM. Since 3.0.0 the `zcash-android-sdk` AAR has shipped the Slipstream engine (`com.zodl.slipstream.*`) and `libzcashwalletsdk.so` has linked that crate. This PR removes the engine end to end so the SDK runs solely on the classic `SdkSynchronizer` over `CompactBlockProcessor` (spend-before-sync), and adds a licence gate so a copyleft crate cannot re-enter the native dependency graph unnoticed.

Three commits, each buildable on its own:

1. **Remove the Slipstream sync engine and its AGPL dependency** — Rust module + Cargo feature/deps, the `com.zodl.slipstream` Kotlin package and its tests, the public API that existed only for it, `WalletCoordinator` wiring, ProGuard rules, and the CI credential plumbing for the former private repository.
2. **Gate the native library on a permissive-licence allowlist** — `backend-lib/deny.toml`, `make deny-rust`, a `deny` stage in `scripts/ci-local.sh`, and a `check_native_licenses` job.
3. **Run the licence gate with a pinned cargo-deny binary** — replaces the third-party action in that job with a checksummed release download.

After this branch, `git grep -i -E 'slipstream|zodl'` matches only `CHANGELOG.md` (the new `[Unreleased]` entry and the immutable 3.0.x history). Git history retains the removed sources; no history rewrite is intended.

## Consumer-visible changes (see CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`)

- **Removed:** the `com.zodl.slipstream` package (`SlipstreamSynchronizer` and its 14 public model/exception types), the `Java_com_zodl_slipstream_*` JNI exports, and the consumer ProGuard rules for them.
- **Changed (breaking):** `Synchronizer.broadcaster` is abstract (no `UnavailableBroadcaster` default); `Synchronizer.syncBurst` / `syncToTip` / `restartSyncSession` / `SyncBurstResult` are gone; `CloseableSynchronizer.pause()` / `resume()` are gone; `WalletCoordinator` loses the `isSyncBlocked` and `isSlipstreamEnabled` constructor parameters. All of these were inert on `SdkSynchronizer`.
- **Licensing:** the native library links no AGPL code; all published artifacts are MIT throughout with only permissively licensed dependencies.

## CI changes

- The GitHub App credential steps (`SLIPSTREAM_APP_ID` / `SLIPSTREAM_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `create-github-app-token`, the `insteadOf` rewrite, `CARGO_NET_GIT_FETCH_WITH_CLI`) are removed from `.github/actions/setup` and all workflows. The remaining git-sourced crates are the public KeystoneHQ repos, so **pull requests from forks can now run the Rust jobs**.
- Rust cache key bumped `rust-v3` → `rust-v4` and `~/.cargo/git` is cached again (its exclusion only existed to keep the private clone out of fork-restorable caches). Expect one cold `Setup` after merge.
- New `check_native_licenses` job: installs the cargo-deny 0.20.2 release binary (SHA-256 verified; the third-party `cargo-deny-action` is not resolvable under this repository's Actions policy, which made the workflow fail at startup on the first push) and runs `make deny-rust` — `cargo deny check licenses sources` against `backend-lib/deny.toml`. It is not yet in the branch ruleset's required checks — an admin should add it.

## Verification (local, on this branch)

- `./scripts/ci-local.sh quick` ✅ — shell tests, detekt, ktlint, `cargo test --all-features` (60 passed), `cargo deny`, `./gradlew test` (includes the 4-ABI native build)
- `./scripts/ci-local.sh lint` ✅, `make check-format-rust` ✅, `make lint-rust` (clippy `-D warnings`) ✅
- `llvm-nm -D --defined-only libzcashwalletsdk.so | grep -c Java_com_zodl` → **0** on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86, x86_64 (121 `Java_cash_z_*` exports remain)
- `sdk-lib-release.aar`: no `com/zodl` classes, no engine ProGuard rules; POM declares `The MIT License`
- `Cargo.lock` regenerated by `cargo check` (never `cargo update`): only `zodl-slipstream`, `tracing-android`, `android_log-sys` dropped, no version changes
- **Negative control** — the new `deny.toml` applied to the untouched `maint/v3.0.x` tree fails exactly as intended:
  ```
error[rejected]: failed to satisfy license requirements
31 │ license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
   ├ AGPL-3.0-only - GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 only:
   ├ zodl-slipstream v0.2.0
licenses FAILED, sources ok
  ```
  and passes on this branch (`licenses ok, sources ok`).

## Test plan

- [x] `./scripts/ci-local.sh quick` and `lint` green
- [x] Native libraries export no `Java_com_zodl_*` symbols (all four ABIs)
- [x] Release AAR/POM contain no engine classes, rules, or references
- [x] `cargo deny` fails on base, passes on branch
- [ ] Demo app on testnet: create wallet → sync → send, on the classic engine (`WalletCoordinator` now always calls `Synchronizer.new`)
- [ ] A device that ran 3.0.x: confirm the wallet database opens and syncs after upgrade

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Forward-merge to `main`, where the `:slipstream-lib` module extraction and the `IS_SLIPSTREAM_ENABLED` flag must be undone as well.
- Delete the `SLIPSTREAM_APP_ID` / `SLIPSTREAM_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` repository secrets and uninstall the GitHub App from the `zodl-inc` organisation.
- Add `check_native_licenses` to the required status checks.
- The next release from this line removes public API; the version number is the release manager's call (`LIBRARY_VERSION` is untouched here).

author: eshton
body:
Sharing **airooster.dev** on LinkedIn showed *"Cannot display preview. You can post as is, or try another link."*

## Cause

The marketing head had `og:title` / `og:description` but **no `og:image`** (and no `og:url`). LinkedIn (and Slack, Facebook, X) can't build a preview card without an image, so it gives up.

## Fix

Added the full Open Graph + Twitter large-image card set to the `Base` layout (applies to every page), with **absolute URLs** derived from the configured `site` (`https://airooster.dev`):

- `og:url`, `og:site_name`, `og:image` (+ `width`/`height`/`alt`), `<link rel="canonical">`.
- `twitter:card=summary_large_image` + title/description/image.

The preview image is the dashboard screenshot (`/screenshots/overview.png`) — real and on-brand. Verified the tags render with absolute URLs in the built `dist/index.html`.

## After you deploy

LinkedIn **caches** the "no preview" result. Re-scrape the URL once in the [LinkedIn Post Inspector](https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/) (paste `https://airooster.dev`, hit inspect) — it'll refetch and the card will appear. Same idea for Slack/X if needed.

## Follow-up (optional)

A dashboard screenshot works, but a **dedicated 1200×630 branded OG image** (logo + tagline) reads better as a social card. Happy to add one if you can drop a PNG in — I can't generate raster images here.

author: arshad0126
body:
The three commits that missed #23. That PR was merged at `eddeb68`, which carried only the icon set, palette and Match Analysis redesign — everything below landed after the merge and never reached `main`, which is why the player chips and the reworked breaker control weren't on the live site.

## Preset players

Awais / Suraj / Arshad as one-tap chips on the Player Names step. Nothing is pre-selected — tap to fill the next free slot, tap again to remove. Add Player still works for anyone else. Blank names fall back to "Player N" rather than blocking Next.

## Breaker control

The row showed a "Breaks Off" badge **and** a button whose ternary returned `'Breaker'` on both branches — two controls saying the same thing in a row with no space for either, which is what was overflowing.

The whole row is the control now: tap a player to give them the break. Selected row gets an accent border, filled seat number and one "Breaks off" chip. Reorder arrows sit at the end and stop propagation. Disabled arrows go 0.15 → 0.35 opacity (they were effectively invisible). Row is a radio in a radiogroup and takes Enter/Space.

## Frame rotation

Two faults made this invisible for 3+ players.

The engine rotated the wrong thing — `newStartIndex = frameNumber % turnOrder.length` moved the entry point into the order while leaving the order itself untouched, so the sequence of play never changed. The order is now rebuilt each frame from a new `baseTurnOrder`: the breaker moves to the front, everyone else keeps their configured sequence.

```
frame 1 -> 1, 2, 3
frame 2 -> 2, 1, 3
frame 3 -> 3, 1, 2
frame 4 -> 1, 2, 3   (wraps)
```

Deliberately not cyclic rotation, which gives 2,3,1 for frame 2 — the point is that each player follows a different opponent each frame. Verified by driving the real reducer through five frames.

The scoring screen then mapped `state.players`, pinning cards to setup positions, so even a correct rotation wouldn't have shown. It now walks `turnOrder`.

## Century and half-century

Counted when a break **finalises** (miss, foul, concede, frame end), not as the score crosses a threshold — a run on 48 may still become a century. A break counts once at its highest tier: a 104 is one century, not also a fifty.

Adds `matchHighestBreak`, tracked separately because `highestBreak` resets each frame and was being saved as the match figure — discarding every break before the final frame. That's why Match Analysis showed MAX BREAK 8 while Frame 2 had 11.

Fixes the milestone chime, which tested `[25, 50, 100].includes(next)` and so only fired on an exact landing — 48 → 51 on a blue skipped the fifty.

## Battery

Removes the 1 Hz `setInterval` that dispatched `UPDATE_TIMER`, re-running the reducer and re-rendering the scoring screen 60 times a minute for a whole match to repaint a clock. Durations now derive from timestamps, banked when they actually change.

Fixes two bugs for free: backgrounding no longer loses time (iOS suspended the old counter), and undo can no longer rewind the clocks.

Still outstanding, not in this PR: infinite CSS animations (`pulse`, `bounce`, `ballFloat`), 27 `backdrop-filter` rules, and an AudioContext that is never suspended.

## Theme

`tokens.css` keyed its dark block off `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` while every other sheet keys off `body.light-theme`. With the phone in light mode and the app set to dark, the two disagreed — `index.css` painted the page dark while tokens stayed light, so token-styled surfaces rendered as white cards with pale text. Now `body:not(.light-theme)`. (Issue #13.)

Light-mode primary gradient started at `#A4D8FF` under white text — 1.5:1, the washed-out Next Step / Start Match buttons. New stops are 4.8:1 and 8.9:1. Retires 9 leftover emerald `rgba(5,176,100)` tints from the old palette.

## Match length

1/3/5 only. An even best-of can end level with no defined outcome (#10).

## Verification

- `npm run build` — 0 errors
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors (4 pre-existing warnings in untouched files)
- Rotation verified by executing the reducer

**Not verified on device.** The sandbox proxy blocks `*.vercel.app`, so none of this has been seen rendered.

body:
## Status
Ready for review.

## Mission Control
- Plan: `organizations/HumanAndMachine-ai_GEN3/mission-control/db/data/mission-control/plans/2026/08/DEV-6439-lazurio-runtime-contract.yaml`
- Task lane: `task-2026-08-12-008` (cross-platform lifecycle and process-tree supervision)

## Motivation
Astro 7.2.2 detects Codex and other AI-agent environments and automatically backgrounds its dev server. Launchpad expects the runtime command it starts to remain attached, so it interpreted the clean launcher exit as a crash, repeatedly reclaimed the healthy listener, and eventually reported `desired_restart_exhausted` even though the website was available.

## Target state
Launchpad remains the sole runtime supervisor. Astro dev and preview commands started by Launchpad take Astro's supervised-child path, stay in the managed process group, and no longer trigger a false restart loop.

## Scope
- Pass Astro's internal supervised-child markers to runtime start processes.
- Assert both markers in the runtime lifecycle fixture.
- No Organization manifest, website source, public deployment, port allocation, or production behavior changes.

## Validation
- `bun test launchpad/src/runtime-lib.test.mjs`: 91 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run --cwd launchpad check`: 737 pass, 13 platform-only skips, 0 fail.
- `bun run check`: PASS, including the complete root and Launchpad suites.
- `bun run doctor`: exit 0; expected feature-worktree/update warning and missing worktree-local Guide dependencies only.
- Real BNO & LJ smoke: the fixed worktree Launchpad reclaimed the detached Astro PID, started Website Lyžák jinak with a persistent managed launcher/process group, kept desired state active without restart entries, and `http://127.0.0.1:24905/` returned HTTP 200.

## Risks and rollout
The markers are Astro-specific and inert for other runtimes. They are forced only for Launchpad-managed start processes, matching the single-server runtime ownership contract. The change takes effect after merge and the normal Lazurio update/restart flow; it does not deploy the public Lyžák jinak website.

author: jobordu
body:
**DEV1.** ARCHITECT's ruling on **#164 item 1** made checkable, and then applied to this repository.

> **ARCHITECT (#341):** *"name a caller whose INPUTS YOU DID NOT CHOOSE"* is criterion 5's population leg applied to a control. A `--self-test` over author-chosen fixtures satisfies criteria 3 and 4 and **fails** it.

## The finding

```
at bb7e6fe, 37 indexed instruments — 28 carry a --self-test

  DRAWN         22    the control consulted nothing but its own fixtures
  UNDRAWN        6    it consulted something it did not create
  NO-SELF-TEST   9    (not counted — a missing control is criteria 3/4's territory, not 5's)
```

⛔ **#26 and criterion 5 are different demands, and satisfying one does nothing for the other:**

| rule | what it demands of the control's population |
|---|---|
| **#26** | drawn from **outside** the measured population — else repairing the subject silences the control |
| **criterion 5** | **not chosen by the author** — else the control re-runs the author's model |

★ A synthetic fixture satisfies #26 **perfectly** and fails 5 **completely.** Several tools here cite #26 in their docstrings as evidence of rigour — mine among them. The credit is real and it is **partial**, and nothing said so.

## How it is measured — behaviour, never source

Every instrument here derives its root from `__file__`. ⇒ Copying one into a barren temp tree makes the repository unreachable **without editing a byte of it.** Run `--self-test` in both places; identical exit code and identical output means the control consulted nothing but itself.

⚠ **The masking is the method.** Both runs print their own absolute paths, so an unmasked diff calls every tool UNDRAWN and the instrument becomes a machine for agreeing with itself. Controlled directly: *with masking disabled, a fixture that merely prints its own path must stop reading DRAWN.*

## ⛔ Three corrections, all forced by running it, all recorded rather than quietly fixed

Each was wrong in the direction that would have been **believed**.

**1 — Under-masking.** I masked *this module's* `ROOT` rather than the *measured tool's* root. In production they coincide, so the bug is invisible on the real population; the self-test caught it only because its fixtures live outside the repo. ⚠ And both symlink forms of every root must be masked — macOS hands out `/var/…` while a tool resolving its own `__file__` reports `/private/var/…`.

**2 — The first live run credited seven tools falsely.** 7 of 35 came back `UNDRAWN-BY-CRASH` on **one shared cause**: `ModuleNotFoundError` on a sibling import broken by relocation — an artifact of my method. Every one was scored as **having** a population leg.

> ★ A missed finding is worse than a false one. A false finding gets argued with; a missed one is indistinguishable from an absent defect.

Sibling **source** now travels on demand; repository **content** still does not. The seven moved into the finding.

**3 — The verdict was non-deterministic and I was reporting a coin flip.**

```
fleet-identity.py, three consecutive readings, identical bytes:
  run 1: DRAWN
  run 2: UNDRAWN
  run 3: DRAWN
```

A differential attributes its difference to the one variable it changed. **That attribution is void if the tool disagrees with itself.** ⇒ Two in-place runs first; if they differ, `NON-DETERMINISTIC` — establishes nothing, neither a finding nor a clean bill.

⚠ **And that guard is a sample, not a proof** — printed on every run, not buried here. Two agreeing in-place runs establish only that the tool *did not disagree twice*. On a later run `fleet-identity.py`'s two samples agreed and it scored UNDRAWN. **`NON-DETERMINISTIC` is a positive detection; its absence is not a clean bill, and every DRAWN/UNDRAWN row inherits that uncertainty.**

## What this does NOT establish

- ⚠ **`UNDRAWN` means a population leg exists, not that it is a good one.** A self-test that reads a real file and asserts nothing interesting lands there too.
- ⚠ **`DRAWN` is not a defect in the tool.** It is a statement about its **control**. Where an undrawn population is genuinely unaffordable — `verdict-census` cannot exercise its classifier without running the real instruments, the ~4-minute cost that made #2 unreadable to begin with — the right answer is a **stated exception with a reason**, not a forced fix. ⛔ This PR proposes no fixes to anyone's tool.
- It reads no source and judges no assertion. Whether a control checks anything *worth* checking is outside it.

★ **Its own control is `DRAWN`, and it reports itself by name rather than skipping the row.** A tool that measured this property and exempted itself would be the joke version of itself. Its population leg is the live run over `tools/`, whose contents it did not choose.

**8 controls passing.**

Refs #26, #164, #2 · rules on #341 — DEV1

author: pushery
body:
**The settings screen now distinguishes "you never accepted this" from "a new version is waiting
for you"** — the two positions that looked identical on the one screen where the subject could
still act voluntarily, before the gate compels them. Around that: the registration listener says
when it records a consent no form ever validated, the tamper-evidence chain refuses a value it
cannot hash instead of folding it onto the empty string, and the README badge row follows the
fleet canon.

Nothing here changes an existing hash or an existing consent row. One behavior changes for code
that hands the chain an Eloquent model instead of a database row — see `UPGRADE.md`.

### Added

- **The settings screen now says which rows are asking for something.** A row the subject has not
  accepted looked identical whether nothing was pending or a new major version was waiting for
  them — and only the second one ends at a gate that compels. The screen where it could have been
  done voluntarily was the one that did not say so.

  Each row of `ConsentPresenter::settingsFor()` carries `outstanding`, computed exactly as
  `Consent::statusFor()` computes it, so the screen and the status map cannot disagree. A
  voluntary consent is never outstanding however long it goes ungiven — demanding one would be
  Art. 7(4). All four shipped views render it as *Action required*, translated in every locale.

  Additive: a new key breaks no consumer that does not read it.

- **The registration listener now says when it records a consent no form ever validated.** Way B
  fires on the standard `Registered` event. A contract or an acknowledgement is accepted there
  unconditionally — correct while a form ran, because `RegistrationRules` made the box required and
  validation already happened. Sign people in through an external provider and no form runs, so the
  row whose entire purpose is to prove a human acted gets written without one having.

  Recording a mandatory document whose `legal_<key>` field is **absent from the request** now logs a
  warning naming the keys, the subject type and the method, plus what to do instead.

  That is an observation about the request rather than a guess about your application: the input
  either carried the field or it did not. Asking the router whether a registration form exists
  cannot be made reliable, because an application may name that route anything.

  It warns and still records. Refusing would break every application whose form names the fields
  differently — that is a decision about your data, so the package reports and leaves it to you.

### Documentation

- **The README badge row follows the fleet canon: identity first, all of it read from Packagist,
  then what the gate enforces.** The license badge already resolved from Packagist rather than
  being hardcoded — the drift that started the fleet-wide review — but the row was single-line and
  carried no test, coverage or type-coverage badge at all, and the license sat in the middle of the
  quality badges instead of closing the identity row.

  Added: Pest 5, coverage 100%, type coverage 100%, and *tested on PostgreSQL + MySQL*. No Livewire
  badge — it is a `require-dev` dependency here, and badging it would tell a reader that installing
  this package pulls Livewire into their application.

  **No mutation badge, deliberately.** A static badge may state exactly what the gate enforces and
  no more; the enforced floor is `--min=67` over Unit and Feature only. Next to two 100% badges that
  reads worse than the package is, and raising the floor is real work with a real proof behind it
  rather than a number edited into a README.

  `ReadmeBadgeClaimTest` now holds the one thing that can silently stop being true: a percentage on
  the page against the `--min=` the composer script enforces.

### Fixed

- **The tamper-evidence chain no longer folds a value it cannot hash onto the empty string.**
  `LedgerHashChain` serializes each proof field as `N` for null, else `S<byte-length>:<value>`, and
  the class promised that two distinct rows always produce distinct canonical strings. That held
  only for values with a lossless string form. An array, an object and a bool `false` all cast to
  `''` — which is itself a legitimate value of `source` — so four different rows shared one hash.

  The point where this becomes concrete is an **Eloquent model**. `hashRow()` accepts any object,
  and `LegalConsent` casts `document_type`, `action`, `method` and `accepted_at` to enums and a
  date object. Hashing a model therefore left four of the eighteen proof fields empty — including
  which document, which act and when — producing a link the verifier, reading the same row raw,
  can never reproduce. `legal-consent:verify-ledger` would later report tampering on rows nobody
  touched.

  Such a value is now refused with `UnhashableProofFieldException` naming the field and the type.
  Encoding it distinctly was the other option and is the worse half: it keeps the mistake silent
  and still hashes the model differently from the row.

  **No existing hash changes, and that is the acceptance criterion rather than a hope.** Null,
  string, int and float encode byte-for-byte as they always did, pinned against hashes measured
  before the change. Both shipped call sites pass raw database rows, so nothing shipped was ever
  affected — what was missing is the guard for the obvious override, since `latestChainedRow()`
  is `protected` and an application returning a model from it would break every chain in its own
  system, silently.

author: assafkip
body:
A voice checker asks whether a draft **sounds** like the author. Nothing here asked what **shape** it is.

That gap cost twelve drafts and four rejections of one post's opening line before anyone measured that the author's own median opener is nine words, while every draft opened with twenty to thirty. Nothing could see it, so nobody could say it.

## What's added

**`config/slop-shapes.json`** — four templated sentence shapes with measured reach penalties, blocking by default. Each violation names its replacement, because a prohibition with no alternative just moves the problem.

| shape | instead |
|---|---|
| "That is not a branding question. It is a system question." | a definitive statement |
| "Records were missing. The result? Deals slipped through." | causal linking |
| "Here is what nobody tells you about X." | a data-anchored premise |
| "Stop chasing likes. Start solving problems." | a direct operational directive |

**`scripts/check-slop-shapes-against-corpus.py`** — sweep the patterns over your own writing *before* trusting them. A blocking word-pattern that matches its own author is the classic failure of this category of tool. The shipped defaults scored zero hits across a real 103-post corpus before they were made blocking, and a looser contrast-bridge variant scored one hit on that same corpus and was rejected for it.

**`config/post-form.json`** — off by default. Point it at your own posts and it derives your bands for total length, opener length, and sentences per paragraph at run time. No median ships as a number: a hardcoded one is a second source of truth that goes stale the day you write another post.

## Verification

- All four shapes confirmed firing through the real lint, not by reading the diff.
- A clean sentence passes.
- The sweep script run against a real corpus reports zero hits.
- Checked for author/client data in every new file: none. The kit gets the mechanism, never the data.

**Caught while wiring:** the config loaded but was never returned from `load_config()`, so the check would have shipped inert. Found by running it end to end.

body:
Fixes the mirror image of #89497: bot DMs stuck on a stale provider pin.

## Summary

Bot-Mode canonical chats (the ONE forever DM per bot) and room plumbing sessions are plugin-owned scratch conversations. They are now created with an explicit `follow_profile_config` contract, persisted in the session row's `model_config`, so `session.resume` rebuilds from the member profile's **CURRENT** config instead of restoring the stored model/provider pin from an old row.

That stale pin is what left bot DMs stuck on a dead provider (e.g. "out of Nous credits" after the profile was switched to ollama-cloud) while the same bot worked fine in rooms — the mirror image of the room-plumbing bug (#89497 class). Normal 1:1 user chats keep the stored-runtime restore: opening an older chat must show the model it actually used.

## How to Test

1. Configure a bot profile with model A (e.g. a paid Nous model), open its Bot Chat DM, send a message.
2. Switch the profile to model B (e.g. ollama-cloud/glm-5.1).
3. Reopen the DM. Before this fix: resume restores the stored model A pin → "out of Nous credits" / HTTP 404. After: resume uses the profile's current model B.

## Verification

- Backend: `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` returns `{}` for rows carrying the marker (dict and JSON `model_config` shapes); unmarked rows still restore stored runtime; `_ensure_session_db_row` persists the marker only when the contract is set.

author: senguidanos
body:
## What Changed

- Pipeline-authored fix commits now derive their subject from the configured title format when that format reads a token from the branch name, so a branch on the exfresso style gets `[sc-1234] Description` instead of `no-mistakes(review): description`.
- Every other style keeps `commit.fix_message` exactly as it was, which is what upstream configures and what a repository on Conventional Commits needs: there the subject has to carry a type and scope that a bare summary cannot supply.

## Why

Fix commits were the one place the repository's commit convention did not reach. PR titles already run through the title format, so an Exfresso branch gets `[sc-1234] Description`; fix commits went through `commit.fix_message`, whose default is `no-mistakes({{.Step}}): {{.Summary}}`. The result was Conventional Commits shaped subjects landing on branches whose every other commit is `[sc-<number>] <description>`.

`commit.fix_message` cannot express that format on its own. It exposes `{{.Step}}` and `{{.Summary}}` and nothing else, while the story number has to come from the branch name — which is exactly what the title format already reads, and already declines to invent when the branch carries no token. Rather than add a second way to spell the same convention, `fixCommitSubject` reuses the one that exists.

## Verified

Built and tested against upstream 1.55.1 (this branch sits on a `main` freshly rebased onto it). `go test ./internal/...` shows the same 22 failures before and after the rebase — all process-reaping and worktree-sweeping tests that require host PID semantics the build container does not provide — so no regressions. The title and commit-format suites pass in full, including `TestPRStep_ExfressoStylePrefixesTitleFromBranchToken` and `TestPRStep_ExfressoStyleWithoutBranchTokenLeavesTitleUnprefixed`.

Observed end to end before the rebase, on a real Exfresso branch: the first pipeline-authored commit after installing this came out as `[sc-51834] Resolve zone once in toZone, bound Intl caches, deflake offset test`, with the story number taken from the branch name and no hand-editing.

author: franciscpd
body:
## What & why

ACP providers can emit hundreds of state-equivalent updates for one tool call. Those duplicates could fill the active prompt's bounded event channel, stall delivery, and disconnect an otherwise healthy provider.

This change keeps one canonical projection per tool call during the active prompt. It suppresses only redundant nonterminal updates while preserving new title, name, kind, input, or prechecked state, plus terminal results and prompt completion in order.

### Release notes

#### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Prevent repeated ACP tool updates from overflowing active prompts while retaining meaningful metadata and terminal results.

## How you verified it

- `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./internal/acp -count=1` passed.
- `make gate-full` passed with current fingerprint `30cbf15585f325c8a17d58b4c427baeed5765eac`. Commit and tag signing were disabled only inside the test process so temporary Git repositories did not inherit the operator's global signing settings.
- Public runtime QA sent 1,100 identical in-progress updates, then a terminal update. Both the initial prompt and a follow-up prompt completed with one canonical call/result pair and no provider disconnect.
- Francisross validated the signed branch build in the installed runtime and confirmed normal behavior. Codex implemented and verified the change.

### QA

**Final status:** PASS — the repeated update burst completed twice through the public session surface with no duplicate durable events or provider disconnect.

**Coverage:** Ada walked J-15 through the CLI, UDS, ACP subprocess, persistence, and follow-up prompt paths using a deterministic provider.
