author: y3owk1n
body:
## What changed for a user

**A Merchant can now say where each part of an Order has got to, and a Shopper can read it
back.** A Fulfilment is marked **dispatched** with a tracking reference, marked **delivered**,
or **cancelled** when it cannot be delivered — per Fulfilment and never on the Order — and
`GET /store/orders/{id}` reports each Fulfilment's state, so a mixed Order shows each part
separately and a downloaded file is not waiting on a posted one.

An invalid transition is refused with a named `reason`, and the Admin's Order screen gains
per-Fulfilment Dispatch, Mark delivered and Cancel controls behind `ActionButton`, so a
Merchant whose Role cannot move one is told which word to ask for.

**This is where [ADR-0014](https://github.com/y3owk1n/kobai/blob/main/docs/adr/0014-fulfilment-strategies-are-an-open-set-and-fulfilment-is-its-own-entity.md)'s
central claim gets tested rather than merely made.** `core_order` gains no status column, and a
schema-seam sweep fails naming **any** column on it that looks like a lifecycle — not just one
called `status`, because the cheap answer arrives spelled `fulfilment_status` at least as often.

## The decisions

**The legal transitions are written down, in `packages/core/src/fulfilment/lifecycle.ts`, and
nothing else decides one.**

```
  pending ──dispatch──▶ dispatched ──deliver──▶ delivered
     │                       │
     └────────cancel─────────┴──────cancel────▶ cancelled
```

Two of those edges are decisions rather than obvious, and both are argued at the line:

- **Delivering takes a dispatch first.** Something handed over the counter was still dispatched,
  so recording it is one extra request — where `pending → delivered` would leave an Order whose
  record cannot say when it left, and no later request could put that back.
- **Cancelling is allowed from `dispatched`.** A parcel lost in transit is exactly the part that
  cannot be delivered. It is **not** a refund and not a Return — that is spec 9.

`delivered` and `cancelled` are terminal, so `cancelled → dispatched` is refused, which is the
one #211 names by hand.

**The refusals *are* the states**, which is what makes them exhaustive by construction rather
than by care: `FULFILMENT_REFUSALS` is a `Record` over the state union, so every state has a
word and there is nowhere for a default branch to live. A move is refused by *where the record
already is*, which is the whole answer. **409**, on `cart-placed`'s distinction — the record
conflicts, rather than the Store's configuration disagreeing with a well-formed body.

**Three action routes, never a `PATCH`** (ADR-0062): a `PATCH` accepting `state: "dispatched"`
would let any state be set from any other, which is every refusal above made unreachable.

**`fulfilment:write`, appended last in `PERMISSIONS` with a `--custom` migration granting it to
`owner`. There is no `fulfilment:read`** — a Fulfilment is read through its Order, which
`order:read` already covers.

## Worth a close look

- **The one statement, and the fourth concurrent test.** The check and the write are one
  `update … where state in (<the legal predecessors>)`, so two Merchants dispatching at once
  produce one 200 and one refusal rather than two 200s and a lost tracking reference.
  `the-fulfilment-dispatched-twice.test.ts` was **watched failing** against the select-then-update
  shape at twenty of twenty-four requests answered 200 — and its constant departs from the
  Reservation tests' rule on purpose, dispatching *more* than the connection pool rather than
  fewer, because at eight the broken build passed.
- **The migration.** `state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` plus a `CHECK`, in one generated
  migration rather than ADR-0038's three: nothing could move a Fulfilment before this column
  existed, so `pending` is the fact that was never recorded rather than a guess at one, *and* it
  is right for every row after — which is exactly when a default is a default. The `CHECK`
  arrives at rows the statement before it has already given a value.
- **Two kinds of assertion about the transitions, and it takes both.** A twelve-case sweep holds
  the *implementation* to the table; hand-written cases hold the *table* to the decision. The
  sweep reads the same source the code does — ADR-0049's trap — so a table changed by hand would
  take it along. Both halves were watched failing, in opposite directions.
- **The Admin holds no copy of the transition table.** It offers all three controls on every
  Fulfilment and renders kobai's refusal, because the legal moves are Core's and are **not
  published on the wire** — a table there would go stale in silence rather than reddening the
  build the way a closed `reason` set does.

## Deliberately not here

**Nothing is emitted.** ADR-0085 decided the events surface and #322 builds it, with a dispatch
as its first consumer. No shipping either — that is #321, which is what `seedTestMixedOrder`
was built to be reusable for.

Closes #320

author: ianmeyer
body:
### Describe what this PR is addressing
Stacked on #471. Capture Android ANRs for SDK diagnostics so a prior-session hang can be reported with the same schema as crash (`analytics.anr` counter + event, `report` property).

### Describe the solution
Two catchers behind `createAnrCatcher()`:
* **API 30+:** `ApplicationExitInfo` unread `REASON_ANR` exits, claimed once under a process-wide mutex so concurrent Amplitude instances do not double-count.
* **Pre-30:** main-thread watchdog that pings every 2s and persists if a ping is unanswered for 5s.

Watchers are installed in `initWatchers()` next to crash capture. Consume is suspend I/O on the storage dispatcher at the call site; persist on the watchdog stays synchronous. A pending legacy report after an OS upgrade to 11+ is not drained (one-off).

### Steps to verify the change
* `./gradlew :android:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.amplitude.android.anr.*`
* Sample app **ANR** button (`Thread.sleep(10_000)` on main) on an API 29 emulator, then relaunch and confirm `analytics.anr` in diagnostics when sampled in.
* On API 31+, force an ANR, relaunch, confirm AEI-backed report.

### Useful links and documentation (optional)
Depends on #471.

### Checklist
* [x] Does your PR title have the correct [title format](https://github.com/amplitude/Amplitude-Kotlin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-commit-title-conventions)?
* [x] Does your PR have a breaking change?

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces a process-wide background watchdog and startup I/O on all API levels; reports can contain stack traces, similar to existing crash diagnostics but with extra runtime overhead on pre-Android 11.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **prior-session ANR reporting** to the Android SDK, wired like existing crash capture: an `AnrCatcher` is started in `initWatchers()`, reports are consumed during `buildInternal()`, and each is sent via `diagnosticsClient.recordAnr` as an **`analytics.anr`** counter plus event with a **`report`** property.
> 
> **API 30+** uses `ApplicationExitInfo` (`REASON_ANR`), tracks the last consumed exit timestamp so each ANR is reported once (mutex for concurrent Amplitude instances), and includes bounded trace text. **Below API 30**, a process-wide main-thread watchdog pings every 2s and synchronously persists a truncated thread dump after ~5s of no response; the legacy file is read on the next launch.
> 
> `detachWatchers()` now tears down the legacy watchdog when the owning instance retires. The sample app gains an **ANR** button that blocks the main thread for manual testing.
>

author: nibsbin
body:
A section heading opened on the column its fields start on, so the row naming a section began where the section's contents began, and the vertical bracketed the two alike. Nothing in the figure said which held which. Measured from the card's border: the rail at 12, its fields at 24, the chevron's ink at 29 — inside the column it was supposed to head.

Three changes, each derived rather than dialled.

**The heading rides its vertical at `--_qm-space`.** Not a chosen rung: the header's own block padding is the whole air a heading keeps under the payload's top rule, a rule insets no further, and WCAG 2.5.8's 24×24 floor pins that padding. Any tighter inline inset squares that corner on one axis alone. The fields keep the full nesting step, so the heading stands a step out from them.

**A rule is drawn on the edge of the box it faces, and the air is that box's own.** Each rule then stands off the ink beside it by the inset that squares its corner — `--_qm-nest` for a field row, `--_qm-space` for a heading, each the rung that ink already keeps off a vertical inline. Two headings closing the payload's two ends stand the same distance off their rules, where the lower one stood three rungs against the upper one's one. Where the last section is open, the box carries the longer rung as real padding, so its vertical ends *on* the rule at every frame of a fold rather than only at the two ends of one.

**A disclosure row stands off the next by the two headers' own block padding and nothing else.** The accordion spent a rung of gap besides, calibrated as the distance the fields keep between their rows — a label over a well, which reads as a float between two lines of text. A run of shut headings read as separate items rather than as the list of sections it is. The rows tile now, and their tap targets with them. A section's vertical caps its free end at `--_qm-space`, the rung a subform's own vertical already caps at, which is what keeps the stroke ending where it did against the heading below it, and what makes the two figures cap alike.

## Verified

Every end measured against the live DOM in the built playground, both accordion states:

| end | facing | air | vertical lands |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| top · section open | heading | 4 | yes → 4 × 4 |
| top · section shut | heading | 4 | — |
| top · ungrouped | field row | 12 | — |
| bottom · section open | field row | 12 | yes → 12 × 12 |
| bottom · section shut | heading | 4 | — |
| bottom · ungrouped | field row | 12 | — |

Motion is read off `document.getAnimations()` at the instant a toggle creates them. Ten transitions; the three that move geometry — both panel tracks and the box's own bottom padding — are one duration on one curve, created in one style pass. Toggling any section but the last runs five, and none of them a padding. Under `.qm-instant` the group's transitions read `0s` and return, so a reveal moves the accordion whole and the landing measures a target that has stopped. `prefers-reduced-motion` collapses the rung in the derivation, so nothing here needs its own guard.

Full gate green: lint, four `check` passes, docs, style, deps, build, bundle, 858 tests.

## Left to judge

The payload now carries two rhythms: rows inside the accordion tile, and the ungrouped block stands a rung further off the first heading, being a boundary between two kinds of section rather than two rows of one run. Deliberate, and the thing to look at first.

author: hobbyiq
body:
> Replaces #1159, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch (`refactor/remove-ch-delta-poll`) was deleted on merge of #1158. Same commit, rebuilt on current main. Full discussion is on #1159.

Every `start*Job()` in `server.ts` arms its `setInterval` (and usually a first-run `setTimeout`) **inside the API process**. App Service runs `numberOfWorkers=2`, so every one of those timers exists twice and every scheduled cycle ran **twice, concurrently, on the same data**.

## The measurement

`hobbyiq-insights`, 3h window, log lines grouped by tag:

| job | lines | `dcount(cloud_RoleInstance)` |
|---|---|---|
| `[price.alert.evaluator]` | 19 | **2** |
| `[portfolio.reprice.job]` | 7 | **2** |
| `[advanced.alert.evaluator]` | 7 | **2** |
| `[buyeriq.deal.scanner]` | 6 | **2** |
| `[ebay.order.poll.job]` | 6 | **2** |
| `[ebay.finances.enrichment]` | 5 | **2** |

Consequences range from wasteful to user-visible: **`price.alert.evaluator` evaluating every alert twice is how one price move becomes two push notifications**, and `portfolio.reprice` reprices every holding twice.

This surfaced through the CardHedge delta poll, whose vendor calls made the duplication visible in *request* telemetry. That job is now deleted (#1158) — but the pattern had nothing to do with CardHedge, and fixing only the job that happened to be measurable would have left nine behind.

## What changed

New `src/jobs/_singleFlight.ts`. `runSingleFlight(jobKey, intervalMs, cycle)` takes a Redis `SET NX EX` lock and runs the cycle only if it wins. All ten jobs call their cycle through it, at **both** the first-run and interval sites:

```
dailyiq                  ebay.order.poll           portfolio.reprice
buyeriq.deal.scanner     ebay.purchase.sync        price.alert.evaluator
advanced.alert.evaluator ebay.finances.enrichment
matched-cohort           subscriptions.safety.net
```

**Error handling is untouched.** `runSingleFlight` returns the cycle's promise, so every existing `.catch(err => console.error(...))` still fires. There's a test for exactly that, because it would be an easy thing to break silently.

**TTL** is one minute under each job's own interval — long enough to lock out the sibling worker firing milliseconds later, short enough to always expire before the next cycle, so a worker dying mid-cycle costs one skipped run rather than wedging the job forever.

**Failure modes, deliberate in both directions:**

| condition | behaviour | why |
|---|---|---|
| no `REDIS_HOST` | memory map is per-process, every worker acquires | exactly today's behaviour — duplicated, never stopped |
| Redis throws | proceed and run | a blip must not silently halt every job on every worker; duplicate work is recoverable, a fleet of quietly stopped jobs is not |

## Verification

Re-run against current main after #1157 and #1158 landed:

```
npx tsc --noEmit    clean
full suite          503 files, 6,711 passed | 1 skipped
new tests           6 cases
```

Cases pin: the cycle runs when the lock is free; **two concurrent callers run it exactly once**; locks are keyed per job; cycle errors still propagate to the caller's `.catch`; a lock failure runs rather than skips; and the TTL sits below the interval but above one cycle.

## Method note

The first transform attempt was wrong and I caught it before it shipped. I assumed indentation made the first-run and interval call sites unique anchors — but `"      FN().catch("` *contains* `"    FN().catch("`, so the 4-space pattern matched both sites in all 8 files. The script also wrote files despite failed pairs. Fixed by anchoring each pattern to a preceding newline and refusing to write a half-transformed file.

⚠️ **Touches `backend/src` — requires a "Daily 5AM ET Refresh & Deploy" dispatch after merge.**

## Summary
- `Customer` sealed interface (`Individual`/`Company`) per `ARCHITECTURE.md` §4, plus real CPF/CNPJ check-digit validators (weighted-sum mod-11, not just length checks — both share the same algorithm, parameterized by weights) and e-mail format validation.
- `CustomerValidator`: combines the format validators with a repository-backed duplicate-document check, returning `Result<Unit>` with a `CustomerValidationError` (`InvalidCpf`/`InvalidCnpj`/`InvalidEmail`/`DuplicateDocument`).
- `CustomerRepositoryImpl` → `CustomerLocalDataSource` (**interface**, implemented by `CustomerLocalDataSourceImpl`) → SQLDelight, with `CustomerMapper` as the only file that imports a SQLDelight-generated type. Seed data (2 Individual + 2 Company, real valid CPF/CNPJ) inserted on first access.
- 27 unit tests: both validators, e-mail, `CustomerValidator` (incl. duplicate-document rejection), the mapper (direct, not just through fakes), the repository (fakes), and the seeding path itself (real in-memory driver).

## Real findings during implementation
- `Dispatchers.IO` doesn't compile from `commonMain` — it's JVM/Android-only in kotlinx.coroutines' stable public API (`internal` on Kotlin/Native). Switched to `Dispatchers.Default` and corrected `ARCHITECTURE.md` §5 to match.
- `Address.id` changed from `TEXT PRIMARY KEY` to `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` — the domain `Address` has no identity of its own, so auto-increment (same pattern as `ProductPrice`) avoids inventing UUID-generation logic for a value object.
- The Phase 1 round-trip tests moved from a persistent-file driver to in-memory (`inMemory = true` / `name = null`) — the `Address` schema change broke the iOS test against a stale on-disk database from a previous run. In-memory is the correct practice for tests regardless of this specific bug.
- Extracted `CustomerLocalDataSource` as an interface (was a concrete class) — `ARCHITECTURE.md` §2/§10 already called for this (DataSource as an interface, repositories tested with in-memory fakes), the initial implementation just hadn't matched it yet.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest` — 27 new tests pass, 0 failures

- [x] `./gradlew ktlintCheck` passes clean

author: camerontredoux
body:
Follow-up to #70. That PR tied **both** the access level and the window duration to the roster `paid` flag, which was too narrow — the correction was pushed after the merge went through, so it never landed.

## The problem

Only one org sets `paid` at all:

| org | free-tier | dancer rows | paid rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| prodigy | ✅ | 947 | 134 |
| dance-team-night | — | 284 | **0** |
| summit | — | 160 | **0** |
| core | — | 2 | **0** |

Measuring the window from paid rows alone froze the expiry for most org dancers. A `limited` dancer uploaded to next season's roster kept a window dated from her first event, and orgs that never touch the column got nothing at all from the extend logic.

## The fix

Separate the two concepts:

- **Duration ← the roster.** Being uploaded to another event means she is still attending, so her window runs from that event — paid or not, in every org.
- **Level ← the paid flag.** Paid → `standard`; unpaid → whatever level she already had.

| Scenario | #70 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `limited` dancer added to next season's roster | ❌ frozen | ✅ extended, still `limited` |
| Org that never sets `paid` | ❌ frozen | ✅ extended |
| Already `standard`, later unpaid event | ❌ frozen | ✅ extended |
| Already `limited`, later marked paid | ✅ upgraded | ✅ upgraded |
| Window already reaching further | ✅ untouched | ✅ untouched |

Downgrades remain impossible. An unpaid dancer keeps her level, and an account with no tier still gets none — `limited` is *more* restrictive than null, since it blocks the photo upload a plain free account has. Explicit revocation stays with `SetRosterPaidService`.

## Verification

| | Tests | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (post-#70) | 270 | 258 | 12 |
| This branch | 272 | 260 | **12** |

+2 tests; the 12 failures are identical to `main`'s and pre-existing. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean.

One test from #70 asserted the opposite behavior ("an unpaid later event does not stretch paid access") — that was my earlier design rather than a requirement, so it is inverted here, alongside new cases for the `limited` return visit and the no-paid-flag org.

## Production data

Already reconciled under this rule: 9 further accounts extended (6 Prodigy dancers, 3 in `s2s-test`), extend-only, verified 0 remaining. Notably `samantharoselaster@yahoo.com` — paid at Tempe, then attended Chicago unpaid — now correctly runs to 2026-11-16 off the Chicago event.

author: ricardotemporal
body:
## Problema

**1. Segundo clique em "Sou veterinário".** Quem clicava na carteira pública era mandado para o login com `{ redirectTo, acessoVet }`, mas o login navegava de volta **sem repassar o estado** — a carteira não sabia que o acesso já tinha sido pedido e esperava um novo clique. O cadastro era pior: não lia o redirecionamento, então quem criava conta a partir da carteira caía no dashboard e precisava escanear o QR de novo.

**2. Aviso de CRMV sem saída.** O botão "Verificar meu CRMV" só existia na tela do pet. No dashboard o aviso era um parágrafo solto — e vinha do estado de navegação do cadastro, então sumia ao recarregar e nunca aparecia para quem entrou por login. Na carteira pública, o 403 virava texto de erro.

## Mudanças

- `vetAuthRedirect.ts`: o estado (`redirectTo`, `acessoVet`) que atravessa login e cadastro. Os links entre as duas telas repassam.
- `CrmvAviso`: aviso acionável reutilizado nos três lugares — dashboard, carteira pública e prontuário.
- Dashboard: o aviso passa a vir de `GET /veterinarios/me/crmv`, não do estado de navegação.
- `AuthContext.register` deixa de devolver `crmv_verificado` — quem precisa da situação consulta a API, que é a fonte única.

## Testes

103 passando; cobertura 85,8 / 82,4 / 74,1 / 85,8, acima da catraca (84/80/73/84).

Três casos novos, todos ligados a regra de negócio (ADR-006): login preserva `acessoVet`, cadastro devolve à carteira do QR, e o `CrmvAviso` destrava a tela quando o registro é aprovado / mostra a situação quando é recusado. O teste do login foi conferido revertendo a correção — falha sem ela.

Sem mudança na API.

author: jpcontreras
body:
Follow-up to #48. The security reviewer died in `Step 2.5` with a bare
`exit 1` and no message, on the very first PR that actually reached it
(`Voltop-SAS/g4c-web-app#22`).

## Cause

`collect_security_context` builds an inventory of every API route and the guard
helper it uses. For each route it greps for guard tokens. Under
`set -euo pipefail` a grep that matches nothing exits 1, `pipefail` propagates
it, and `set -e` kills the script — so **a route with no guard helper aborts the
whole review instead of being reported as such.**

The route that triggered it is `api/donations/webhook/route.ts`. It
authenticates by signature rather than by session, so it matches no guard token
by design. The collector died on precisely the row it exists to surface, and
that route is the most security-critical one in the application — the only
source of truth for donation state.

```
=== Step 2.5: Collecting security context ===
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

## Fix

Both greps now tolerate an empty match.

Verified against all 41 routes with `set -euo pipefail`:

```
Security context collected (50 lines)
rutas: 41/41
- `src/app/api/donations/webhook/route.ts` | POST | NO GUARD HELPER DETECTED
```

Audited every other command substitution in both scripts for the same hazard —
the streaming parse lines already carried `|| true`.

## Why the earlier local test missed it

The test harness ran the function with `set -uo pipefail` but **without `-e`**,
which is exactly the flag that turns an empty grep into a fatal error. The
harness did not reproduce the CI shell. Re-verified with the real flags.

## Status of the rest of the pipeline

The same run proved the quality reviewer end to end against the live API for the
first time — streaming, text extraction past the thinking block, score parsing,
comment posting, check run:

```
Model: claude-sonnet-5   Max output tokens: 32000   Effort: medium   Streaming: true
Decision: APPROVE        Scores: Arch=10, Quality=10, Testing=10
Quality Gate: PASSED
```

The security reviewer still has **not** completed a run against the live API.
That is what merging this unblocks.

## Note

`g4c-web-app` sparse-checkouts these scripts from `main`, so re-running #22 only
picks the fix up once this is merged.

body:
## What

All 38 utils packages declare `"license": "ISC"` and publish to npm, but **37 of them shipped no license file**. Consumers got a license identifier in the metadata and no terms in the tarball — which is exactly what compliance tooling and most corporate review processes look for.

Also adds a `LICENSE` at the repository root, which had none.

## Why no manifest change is needed

npm always includes `LICENSE` in the tarball regardless of the `files` field. Verified rather than assumed — `npm pack --dry-run` against acp-llm-cli, whose `files` is `["dist"]`:

```
npm notice Tarball Contents
npm notice 752B  LICENSE
npm notice 11.1kB README.md
```

## One thing for you to decide

`@simpill-env.utils` already had a LICENSE and is **left untouched**. It carries a different holder line from the only other package that had one:

| package | holder |
|---|---|
| `@simpill-env.utils` | `Copyright (c) 2024 @SkinnnyJay` |
| `@simpill-acp-llm-cli.utils` | `Copyright (c) 2026 @simpill contributors` |

The 37 new files follow the acp-llm-cli wording as the more recent precedent. Reconciling the two is a judgement call, so I've left it to you rather than silently rewriting an existing license header.

## Risk

None — no source, build, or test changes. Every package's pre-commit format and lint hooks pass.

author: evanpelle
body:
## Summary

Adds **zbin** (`zbin/` at the repo top level): a self-contained library that gives zod schemas a compact binary wire format. **Library only** — no game schemas or transport code are touched; wiring the game websocket onto it lands in a follow-up PR.

Motivation (from the design investigation): the game socket sends uncompressed JSON at 10 Hz per client. Replaying real archived game `P8XsSiP8` (70 players, 30 min) through this codec measured **1,577 KB → 213 KB per client (86.5%)**, ~108 MB → ~15 MB of egress for one game.

### Design

- **Zod stays the single source of truth.** Every `zb.*` builder returns a *real zod schema* (`z.infer`, `.extend()`, JSON paths all unchanged) with its binary codec registered in a WeakMap side table; root builders attach `serialize` / `parseBytes` / `decodeBytes`. Most plain zod auto-derives — only int-vs-float numbers, dictionary-mapped ids, JSON-escaped subtrees, and intersections over discriminated unions (`zb.stamped`) need explicit builders.
- **Encoding:** LEB128/zigzag varints, bit-exact float64 (sim determinism), bigint varints, presence-bit object headers (optional/nullable flags and boolean *values* are bits), zero-byte literal tags, ~1-byte union tags.
- **Dictionary contexts:** `ctx.mapping("clientId", { max })` + `zb.mapped("clientId")` encodes repeated ids as one byte, with an inline escape for unmapped values. No on-wire learning — peers seed identical tables from shared data, so decoding is stateless per message.
- **Error contract:** `parseBytes` = decode + full zod validation (untrusted input); `decodeBytes` skips validation for trusted hot paths. All corrupt input — truncation, trailing bytes, bad ordinals/flags, unknown dictionary indexes, oversized collection counts, invalid embedded JSON — surfaces as `ZbDecodeError`, never a raw `RangeError`/`SyntaxError`.

Library docs: `zbin/README.md`. The only change outside `zbin/` and `tests/zbin/` is one tsconfig include entry.

### Testing (63 tests, `tests/zbin/`)

- **`zbin.test.ts`** — primitives across the full safe-integer range, presence-bit packing (incl. multi-byte headers), containers/unions/tuples/records, defaults, `zb.custom`, and the context contract (boundary index 254, overflow-to-inline, duplicate/undeclared mapping errors).
- **`protocol.test.ts`** — a realistic stamped-intent turn protocol: cross-peer round-trips of every variant, JSON-path equivalence, escape-path ids, mis-seeded peers failing loudly, byte budgets (empty turn ≤ 7 bytes, ~12-byte attack intent, ≥5× smaller than JSON), determinism, truncation at every byte boundary.
- **`fuzz.test.ts`** — 2,500+ generative round-trips over a composite schema checked against zod's own JSON path; byte-stability of encode∘decode∘encode; adversarial fuzzing (5,000 random byte strings, 1,000 bit-flipped payloads) proving the decoder only ever throws its documented error types. This fuzzing caught and fixed a real bug pre-merge (corrupt varint count → raw `RangeError` from `new Array(2^50)`).

Full repo suite (3,656 tests), lint, and typecheck pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest tests/zbin --run`
- [x] `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`

author: marc-gavanier
body:
Follow-up to #192, which recorded the 08-21 audit while its headline finding was
still wrong.

That run reported that no LAN address had queried Pi-hole since 08-08, and read
it as a resolver nobody uses any more — ad-blocking silently off for the whole
LAN, with the cause somewhere in the router. Every fact was correct and had been
re-measured independently. The reading was not.

**2026-08-08 is the day the operator left on holiday.** The devices went with
them, and the VPN peers that kept querying throughout are the same people from
elsewhere. Nothing broke; the house emptied.

The entry is rewritten rather than deleted, because the correction is the part
worth keeping:

- No further measurement on either machine could have separated the two
  readings. One question to the operator did.
- A disappearance is not an event until something identifies the disappearing
  side. Traffic that stops in a band of a few hours on a single day describes
  people at least as well as machinery.
- The apparent instrument gap — Kuma asserts the resolver answers, never that
  anyone asks it — is real and deliberately left open. "No LAN client is
  querying" is true every time the house is empty for a week, so a monitor
  asserting it would fire on holidays and train everyone to ignore it.

One dated, manual follow-up is kept: after the return, check that LAN clients
reappear in the query log. If they come back and stay silent, the finding is real
after all.

The row is removed from the still-open table. #188 to #191 are unaffected — they
came from a different pass and were verified on their own evidence.

author: fletcherreaves-cloud
body:
Docs only. Amends dispatch #48's INV-004 section.

## The blocker wasn't real

INV-004 was deferred on *"no day-part sales denominator identified."* `qsr_daily_activity` carries `net_sales`, `product_sales` and `transactions` per `(loc, dt, hour_slot)` — an **hourly** denominator, pulled daily, finer than day-part. Sum hour slots into day-parts and the plan's "waste per sales dollar" is directly computable.

Same failure shape as `manOverringQty`: a reasonable-sounding "we don't have X" that one look at the schema refutes. Recorded as a standing instruction — **check the schema before deferring on a missing-data premise.**

## Owner directive on the boundary

> *"build it the same way as we have in place. it is universal."*

The 4:00am → 4:00am business day is a first-class fact about this data, not a per-rule decision. Do not invent a convention for this rule, and do not re-derive the cutover inline — `businessDate()` / `lastClosedBusinessDay()` (`src/utils/date.js:101,117`) already implement it, and re-deriving it inline has recurred **five separate times** in this repo.

## The concrete risk is double-shifting, not mis-shifting

Both legs look *already* aligned:

- DAR's `hour_slot` runs `05:00 → 28:00` — measured, 24 slots covering 04:00→04:00 (`dar-vs-ops-reconciliation.md`)
- `qsr_waste`'s date column is named **`busn_dt`** — a *business* date, suggesting QSRSoft already applied the shift

Calling `businessDate()` on top of an already-shifted date moves a whole day's waste onto the wrong day. **One query settles it:** do any `qsr_waste` rows carry a `busn_tm` in 00:00–03:59, and which `busn_dt` do they have? If those rows carry the *previous* calendar date, the shift is already applied — join directly, add nothing.

## Verification

Docs only — no code, no tests affected. Memory index drift check clean.

author: vvolam
body:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Enable `platform_tests/test_power_off_reboot.py` on SmartSwitch platforms. The
test was silently skipped on SmartSwitch because `reboot()` routed every
SmartSwitch reboot through `reboot_smartswitch()`, which only handled the
command-based reboots in `reboot_ss_ctrl_dict` (cold / watchdog) and skipped
everything else. A power-off reboot is not a DUT command — it is driven by the
PDU physically cutting power via `reboot_helper` — so it was skipped even though
the operation is completely platform-agnostic.

This PR adds `REBOOT_TYPE_POWEROFF` to `reboot_ss_ctrl_dict` and dispatches it in
`reboot_smartswitch()` through the PDU `reboot_helper`, the same mechanism
`perform_reboot()` uses on non-SmartSwitch platforms. Warm / fast reboots continue
to skip on SmartSwitch as intended by #19617.

Fixes: ADO 39345689

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement

### Back port request

- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [ ] 202605

Tracking issue/work item for backport/cherry-pick request (GitHub issue or Microsoft ADO): ADO 39345689
Failure type: day-one issue (power-off reboot never dispatched correctly on SmartSwitch since the `reboot_smartswitch()` dispatch was introduced in #19617)

### Tested branch

- [x] master
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [x] 202605

### Test result

- master: 20260510.10 (SmartSwitch Mellanox-SN4280) — `platform_tests/test_power_off_reboot.py` **2 passed** (`power_off_delay` = 5 and 15). Both parametrizations ran the full power-off flow (3 PSU power-on sequences each = 6 real PDU power-cycles), the DUT lost power and recovered on every cycle, and `show reboot-cause` reported **"Power Loss"** for all 6 cycles.

### Approach

#### What is the motivation for this PR?

`test_power_off_reboot.py` was being skipped on SmartSwitch, leaving power-loss /
power-cycle recovery completely unvalidated on that platform. The root cause was
in the framework: `reboot()` unconditionally sent SmartSwitch reboots to
`reboot_smartswitch()`, which only knows about the command-based reboot types and
skips the rest — including power-off, which is inherently a PDU operation and not
a DUT command.

#### How did you do it?

In `tests/common/reboot.py`:

1. Add a `REBOOT_TYPE_POWEROFF` entry to `reboot_ss_ctrl_dict` so it is recognized
   as a supported SmartSwitch reboot type (no `command` key — power-off is not a
   DUT command).
2. Teach `reboot_smartswitch()` to accept `reboot_helper` / `reboot_kwargs` and,
   for `REBOOT_TYPE_POWEROFF`, dispatch through the PDU `reboot_helper`
   (`reboot_helper(reboot_kwargs, power_on_event)`) — the same mechanism
   `perform_reboot()` uses on non-SmartSwitch platforms. All other SmartSwitch
   reboot types still run their DUT command as before.
3. Pass `reboot_helper` / `reboot_kwargs` into `reboot_smartswitch()` from
   `reboot()`.

No other reboot type is affected; warm / fast reboots still skip on SmartSwitch
per #19617.

#### How did you verify/test it?

Ran `platform_tests/test_power_off_reboot.py` against a SmartSwitch DUT
(Mellanox-SN4280, image 20260510.10) with two PDU-controlled PSUs. The power-off
dispatch to the PDU `reboot_helper` was exercised end-to-end:

- Both `power_off_delay` parametrizations (5 and 15) **passed** (2 passed).
- `reboot_smartswitch()` dispatched `REBOOT_TYPE_POWEROFF` to the PDU
  `_power_off_reboot_helper`, which turned both PSUs off (SSH dropped → DUT
  powered off) and back on (DUT recovered).
- All 6 power-cycles recovered and the reboot cause was correctly reported as
  **"Power Loss"** on each.

#### Any platform specific information?

Applies to SmartSwitch (DPU-based) platforms. The change only adds the power-off
reboot type to the SmartSwitch dispatch; the underlying power-off logic is
platform-agnostic and unchanged. Requires PDU/PSU control for the DUT, as the
power-off test already does on every platform.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?

Not a new test case — this enables an existing test on SmartSwitch. It runs on
SmartSwitch topologies whose DUT PSUs are controlled by a reachable PDU.

### Documentation

N/A

Você pediu a base local em vez da API paga — está pronta.

## Por quê
A API do OpenSanctions (PR #30) não é de graça para uso pessoal continuado: 30 dias de teste e depois cobra por consulta; a chave permanente só é concedida a jornalismo/ONG/academia. Mas os **dados em massa são livres para uso não-comercial** (CC BY-NC 4.0) — só é preciso baixar e indexar.

## O que foi construído
- **`holmes/opensanctions_bulk.py`** — baixa `targets.simple.csv` (~400 MB, só as entidades sinalizadas: sanção/PEP/crime) em streaming (nunca carrega tudo na memória) e monta um **índice SQLite por nome**, com o mesmo cuidado anti-homônimo que o resto do motor já usa (nome completo bate = confirmado; só primeiro+último sobrenome bate = provável, com aviso).
- **CLI**: `python -m holmes.opensanctions_bulk --update` — pensado para um Railway Cron semanal (mesmo padrão do `holmes.monitor` que já existe).
- **Botão na UI** (aba Investigar → Avançado): baixa e indexa direto da página, para quem não quer configurar Cron agora. Mostra status (baixado? quantos registros? quando?).
- **`holmes/sanctions.py` atualizado**: agora tenta o **índice local primeiro** (grátis, sem rede na hora da consulta) e só cai para a API paga se o índice ainda não foi baixado — a chave da API virou reserva, não o caminho principal.
- Conector nunca falha em silêncio: se não tem índice nem chave, aparece como "pulado" explicando exatamente o comando para resolver.
- Atribuição da licença (CC BY-NC 4.0) visível na própria UI.

13 testes novos, tudo sem rede (CSV de exemplo pequeno, build+busca reais no SQLite temporário). Suíte total: **236 testes passando** (era 225).

## Depois do merge
Rode uma vez (pode ser local ou no Railway):
```
python -m holmes.opensanctions_bulk --update
```
ou clique em **Baixar/atualizar agora** na aba Investigar → Avançado. Aponte `HOLMES_OPENSANCTIONS_DIR` para o Volume persistente do Railway, senão o índice se perde a cada deploy.

author: xzawed
body:
`.claude/rules/go.md`는 **"`Roles.Update`에 `role.Name = &name`을 주입하면 rename이 조용한 no-op이 된다"**를 길게 경고한다. 그런데 그것을 잡을 테스트가 없었다.

| | 실측 |
|---|---|
| `admin_test.go`의 Update 테스트 | **0건** |
| E2E의 `Roles.Update` | 경로 `"e2e-role"` · body `Name: "e2e-role"` — **같은 이름** |

즉 **주입해도 E2E는 그대로 통과한다**. 실제로 rename을 태우는 것은 `Groups.Update` 하나뿐이고, Rust는 같은 위험에 전용 wiremock 테스트를 이미 갖고 있다.

Users·Clients·Groups는 반대로 body에 식별자를 **주입해야** 하므로, 그 관용을 Roles에 복사하는 것이 **실제로 일어나는 회귀**다.

## 변이검증 3요건

| | 조작 | 결과 |
|---|---|---|
| (a) | `role.Name = &name` 주입 | **FAIL** — `body는 **새 이름**을 날라야 한다 … got old-role` |
| (b) | 복원 | PASS · go 전체 51개 통과 |
| (c) | 주입한 채 **body 단언만 무력화** | **PASS (exit=0)** |

**(c)가 핵심이다.** 경로 단언만으로는 공허하다 — gocloak이 `name` 인자를 경로에 이미 싣기 때문에 **경로는 절대 어긋나지 않는다**. 주입이 깨뜨리는 것은 body뿐이다. 이 대조군이 없으면 "경로를 확인했으니 됐다"로 끝났을 것이다.

## 하네스가 가벼운 이유

로그인 왕복이 **필요 없다** — `UpdateRealmRole`이 베어러 **문자열**을 인자로 받으므로, `AdminClient`를 같은 패키지에서 직접 세우고 스텁 `TokenProvider`를 꽂으면 된다. 핸들러 기본값은 **404**다: 아무 2xx나 돌려주면 경로가 틀려도 통과한다.

## 무효 측정을 하나 잡았다

대조군을 처음엔 슬라이싱으로 만들었다가 파일을 깨뜨려 **컴파일 실패를 "잡았다"로 읽을 뻔했다**. 정밀 치환으로 다시 쟀고 위 (c)가 그 값이다.

## 검증

```
go test -count=1 ./...  3회      전부 51개 통과
go vet                            exit 0
gofmt (LF 사본 28개)              지적 0건
check-docs --strict               통과
scripts/test/*.sh 전종             ALL GREEN
```

body:
…a del índice

Los tres seguían declarando «para evaluación, ninguna modificación aplicada» después de aplicados, ninguno tenía su sección «Cómo se resolvió», y el índice se contradecía: la tabla de desenlaces daba el 13 por resuelto en 9.19 y la sección del 12 lo seguía listando abierto.

La causa no es el olvido. La regla del índice está atada al acto de emitir —«quien agrega un reporte, agrega su fila»— y el estado lo cambia el acto de resolver, que ocurre en otro repositorio: una intervención sobre el framework publica, y nadie del lado de acá lo ve pasar. Es el mecanismo que el propio reporte 14 describe.

Cada uno cierra ahora con el veredicto de sus criterios de aceptación uno por uno, que es lo que la comprobación 13 del framework (SDD 11.1) obliga a producir en la nota de coherencia de toda intervención. El 14 lleva las dos versiones que hicieron falta y declara su criterio 4 incumplido en 10.0.

Se restituye además la fila 1.12 del control de cambios, que faltaba: la intervención anterior subió la cabecera y no escribió la fila.

author: ancheetah
body:
The `.env.example` template was missing the `VITE_SDK_CONFIG` variable (a JSON string) which allows one to configure the application solely through the `.env` without the use of unified JSON. This PR replaces it with `VITE_SDK_<NAME>` variables and additionally rewrites the creation of the configuration object(s) in `constants.js` to be more explicit in order to demonstrate _both_ configuration options and showcase some of the options available. This helps developers better understand what exactly goes into configuring clients.

Previously, we demonstrated that both the oidc and journey clients can be initialized with the same config. While that is still true, I opted to create two separate config objects for each client because now with the unified SDK config additional properties relevant to only one client or the other can be present. So it is possible that the configurations are different (even though the clients currently ignore most of these properties).

This change has only been done in the journey sample app to get initial feedback before applying the same changes to the DaVinci and OIDC sample apps.

**[Old] Config with VITE_SDK_CONFIG (JSON string):**
```
VITE_SDK_CONFIG='{"oidc":{"clientId":"WebOAuthClient","discoveryEndpoint":"https://openam-sdks.forgeblocks.com/am/
  oauth2/alpha/.well-known/openid-configuration","scopes":["openid","profile","email"],"redirectUri":"http://localho/
  st:8443/callback.html"}}'
  ```
  
**[New] Config with standard variables:**
```
VITE_SDK_CLIENT_ID=WebOAuthClient
VITE_SDK_DISCOVERY_ENDPOINT=https://openam-sdks.forgeblocks.com/am/oauth2/alpha/.well-known/openid-configuration
VITE_SDK_SCOPE='openid profile email'
```

author: crowlkats
body:
Stacked on #69 (base branch is `click-passthrough`; retarget to `main` once that merges).

Adds a `set_click_passthrough_forward` / `is_click_passthrough_forward` pair to the backend C ABI (**API version 33 → 34**) — the counterpart of Electron's `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })`. While a window is passthrough, forwarding keeps its mouse events (moves, clicks, wheel) flowing to the embedder's registered `on_mouse_move` / `on_mouse_click` / `on_wheel` handlers, even though the OS delivers every event to whatever is beneath the window.

**Observation only, by design**: hit-testing is decided by the OS before any handler runs, so a forwarded event cannot be consumed. The intended use is the standard interactive-overlay pattern — watch forwarded mouse moves and toggle `set_click_passthrough(false)` just-in-time when the cursor enters an interactive region, re-enable on leave.

```rust
let overlay = Window::new_with_options(400, 300,
  WindowOptions { frameless: true, transparent: true, ..Default::default() })
  .always_on_top(true)
  .click_passthrough(true)
  .click_passthrough_forward(true)
  .on_mouse_move(|ev| { /* toggle passthrough off over interactive regions */ })
  .load("overlay.html");
```

## Implementation (v1: macOS, WebView + CEF backends)

A passthrough window's events are delivered to *other* applications, which is exactly what `NSEvent` **global** monitors observe — so both backends install global monitors for click/move/wheel masks, lazily when the first window enables forwarding and removed when the last one disables it. The handler hit-tests `[NSApp orderedWindows]` front-to-back for a visible window with passthrough **and** forwarding active whose frame contains the screen point, converts to window-local coordinates (`convertPointFromScreen:` + the same `contentLayoutRect` y-flip the local monitors use), and re-dispatches through the existing `DispatchMouseClick/Move/Wheel` paths. Notes:

- Mouse observation via global monitors needs **no macOS permission** (unlike keyboard).
- Global monitors never fire for the app's own events, so there is no double dispatch with the existing local monitors. The flip side (documented): if an event lands on another *non-passthrough window of the same app* overlapping the overlay, the overlay's handlers don't fire for it.
- Forwarding without passthrough is deliberately inert — normal per-window delivery already fires the handlers, and dispatching global events for a window that isn't passthrough would report events that actually hit an occluding window.

**Not implemented yet** (flag ignored, getter reports `false`): Windows (`WH_MOUSE_LL` hook), Linux/X11 (XInput2 raw events — the CEF backend already has that monitor connection to build on), winit. Linux/Wayland cannot support it (no global input observation). All documented in `docs/window-management.md`.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p laufey`: 45 tests pass; webview + CEF backends build cleanly.
- New capability-probed `set_click_passthrough_forward round-trips` in the `native_e2e` battery: **PASS** under WebView and CEF on macOS (overall PASS), **N/A** under winit as expected.
- What is machine-verified is the flag round-trip, monitor install/remove, and builds; *actual* event forwarding needs real OS input (synthetic `CGEventPost` requires an Accessibility grant), so that part needs a quick manual check: run an overlay with forwarding on, hover it, and confirm `on_mouse_move` fires while clicks land in the window beneath.

author: acehack
body:
**METERED.** Every line is a command run against the YubiHSM 2 physically attached to the
maintainer's Mac Studio, with verbatim output. **No credential was read, printed or handled, and
no authenticated session was opened.**

Closes the metering gap on `081M0B230NW…` — *"frost-hardware-probe could not see a YubiHSM 2 at
all, and paired any module with any device"*. That bug was fixed in the same PR that filed it,
and the workitem says plainly: *"No hardware was touched: the device was never plugged in."* So
the fix was **implemented and unmetered.** It has now met the device.

## The trap found on the way in

```
$ system_profiler SPUSBDataType          # 0 bytes, exit 0
$ system_profiler SPHardwareDataType     # 514 bytes, exit 0   ← control: the tool works
```

**`SPUSBDataType` returns empty with exit 0 under an agent sandbox.** A check that *could not
run* is indistinguishable at the call site from one that ran and found nothing — **the same
sentence the closed workitem used about its own bug, now recurring one layer up in the
environment rather than in the code.** `ioreg` is unaffected and is what the fixed probe
actually uses.

> Standing consequence: on macOS, `system_profiler` is not a dependable enumerator inside an
> agent context, and any future detection route reaching for it inherits this **silently**.

The device is there — `YubiHSM`, `idVendor 4176 / idProduct 48`, serial `0039160506`, behind two
VIA Labs hubs on an Anker dock (recorded because a probe walking only the root hub would miss it).

## Both halves of the closed bug confirmed against hardware

```
  YubiHSM 2:          ATTACHED (bulk USB — invisible to the reader/ykman probes above)
  PKCS#11 module:     Not found
  PKCS#11 pair:       …/yubihsm_pkcs11.dylib drives YubiHSM 2
  Device present:     YES
  Honourable tiers:   hardware-pkcs11
```

The HSM is no longer invisible; and the module is **matched** to the device rather than merely
co-present — under the old `someModule && someDevice` logic those middle two lines **could not
coexist**. The forcing case the workitem described is exactly the state of this desk.

And the line worth keeping for its own sake:

```
  TPM 2.0: UNAVAILABLE (THE CHECK DID NOT RUN) … This is "not asked", not "no TPM".
```

The discipline is carried in the device layer's **own output string**, where a reader who never
opens the source still cannot mistake a gap for a finding.

## Connector reachability is the real perimeter — measured, not argued

```
status=OK   serial=*   version=3.0.7   pid=14449   port=12345
```

A connector **is already listening**, and **`serial=*` — it is not pinned to a device.** Live
confirmation of `081M0DJQ7BP…`: the 16-domain bitmask is enforced by the hardware **against a
session**, but the path *to* the hardware is an unpinned localhost TCP daemon. **Domain
separation is not reachability control, and only one of the two is currently constrained.** The
cheap narrowing (pin to the serial) is **named rather than performed** — it changes a running
service.

## Device facts re-measured rather than quoted

`get-device-info`, unauthenticated, **agrees** with `hsm-domain-map.ts` on firmware 2.4.1 and
serial 39160506 — the file's facts survive re-measurement. **`eck256` is secp256k1**, so the
wallet/x402 path has a real on-device curve. Brainpool and the full RSA range are present and
were not in the file's list, which **widens rather than contradicts** it (the file said "observed
subset"). **Still absent: any FROST-capable mechanism** — threshold signing remains software
FROST over HSM-sealed shares.

## What this deliberately does NOT claim

**Domain separation enforcing per-AI isolation is not metered and must not be read as such.**
`hsm-domain-map.ts` states it at the claim: the **decision** is enforced and tested, the
**separation** is not — nothing stops a caller that already holds an authenticated session from
using any key that session's domains reach, and the gate is one a caller can simply decline to
call. **A probe reporting `Honourable tiers: hardware-pkcs11` is not evidence for it.**

Also still unrun: the Linux TPM 2.0 probe (`081M00VN9P1…`) needs an x86 node; this is Apple
silicon, and the darwin path correctly declines to guess.

author: ftechspace
body:
All three scheduled reports ran monthly, on whatever weekday the company had picked for its **Top Insights brief**. Neither half of that was asked for. A competitive or market sweep is a quarterly exercise — running it twelve times a year re-buys a multi-minute web sweep to report on a category that has barely moved — while 3P feedback genuinely is monthly. And expressing a report's cadence as "the first configured brief weekday" tied it to an unrelated surface, so changing the brief day silently moved the reports.

## The calendar

| Report | Cadence | Opens |
|---|---|---|
| Competitive intelligence | quarterly — 1 Jan / Apr / Jul / Oct | **08:00** local |
| Market intelligence | quarterly | **11:00** local |
| 3P feedback | monthly — the 1st | **15:00** local |

The stagger is **load control, not taste**: the tick walks companies sequentially and one report costs roughly 25 minutes of sweep plus extraction, so three reports opening at the same instant would queue a tenant's whole set behind one another and pile every paid sweep into one window. `test_the_report_hours_are_distinct` fails if two specs ever drift onto the same hour.

## The period is now the window

`should_run_brief`, `FREQ_MONTHLY` and `REPORT_DUE_WINDOW` are **deleted**. A company is due from the moment its quarter or month opens until a saved `reports` row closes it. Only the opening day is gated on the clock — any later day is due at any hour, or the stagger would become the 24h cliff this replaced, where whoever sorted last got nothing at all.

**The join run falls out of that**, with no hook and no backfill job. A tenant that finishes onboarding on 12 February has no report for February, so the next tick finds it due and runs each report once. Same check that backfills a tenant the scheduler never reached.

Worth being precise: it is a **poll on the hourly tick, not an event trigger**. A new company waits up to an hour rather than seeing reports the moment onboarding completes. If first-visit experience matters, that wants a `kickoff`-style hook in `post_onboarding_complete` — deliberately not in this PR.

## Vendored skills — and what that quietly changed

Adds `SKILL.md` for **competitive-intelligence-review** and **public-feedback-report**. The engines have named these since #1180 with nothing behind the name: `_build_method_prefix` tolerates an id matching no directory, so both ran METHOD-LESS with `+bare` in `prompt_version`.

A live A/B on one tenant, same competitor set — the skilled CIR run added a Direct/Entrant classification, **discovered a competitor outside the configured set**, and defended its scope with a "considered and excluded" section. PF went from declining outright to a 20-post report that graded its own source quality ("*most records came from competitor comparison blogs… a step removed from direct user voice*").

⚠️ **Vendoring a skill re-methods every call site that names it.** `research/market.py` binds `public-feedback-report`, and `research/competitor.py` binds `competitive-intelligence-review` at three call sites. All four were decision-log labels with nothing behind them and now carry 20k / 24k characters of method. **Two tests asserted exactly that absence** — they are flipped to pin the new behaviour rather than deleted, so the change is recorded instead of silent. Reviewers should decide whether the market-research binding is the method they want there.

The competitor path also passes `skill_module=` per stage while the vendored skill ships **no modules**. That is safe only because `call_with_web_search` tolerates an unknown module where `graph.gateway._build_method_prefix` raises `KeyError` — that asymmetry is now pinned in a test, so moving those calls onto the gateway fails loudly instead of at runtime.

Also renames the PF skill's `reference/` → `references/`, which is what the loader reads. Its 12k-char `capture-spec.md` had never once reached the capture pass.

## What was verified

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_monthly_reports.py`, `test_kg_ingest_monthly_report.py`, `test_scheduler_brief.py`, `test_brief_schedule.py`, `test_skills_loader.py`, `test_competitive_intel.py`, `test_public_feedback.py`, `test_runtime_compat.py` | **307 passed** |

Both skill directories were scanned against the 205-entry customer-name denylist before committing — **no hits**.

## Deliberately left out

- **No onboarding trigger.** The poll covers the join case; an event hook needs its own guard against racing the tick into two sweeps.
- **No concurrency across tenants.** The stagger separates the three reports, not the 40 companies — the tick is still sequential.
- **The skill directories carry `examples/`, `state/`, `README.md` and a PDF** that the loader never reads (only `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `assets/`). Kept as authored rather than pruned.

## Heads-up on merging

The first tick after deploy makes **every company due at once** — none has a Q3 or August report. That is 40 × 3 sequential runs and a real one-time spend. `MONTHLY_REPORTS_ENABLED=0` is the reports-only kill switch if you want to stage it.

## Current exact-head status (2026-08-20)

Exact head: `55a5eaadae2206bb6e2b7def08e52fe13ecb6cfc`, rebased onto current `origin/develop`.

The approval-standing ambiguity is resolved explicitly: owner/co-parent/current-partner bindings have intrinsic standing while caregiver/professional identities require an active, child-scoped `schedule.approve` grant; both roles may receive that independently revocable scope. The real-PGlite coordination file passes 27/27, including denial without the caregiver grant and success after issuance. Changed-file Biome and default-pack lint are clean. Package typecheck could not be qualified in this isolated install because many unchanged workspace packages lacked built declaration artifacts; the focused real-database lane is green.

This PR remains draft because the authoritative #17178 delivery ledger still lacks real multi-principal connector delivery/reply logs and warning-UI evidence. No live-evidence claim is made.

---

Refs #17178 (non-closing: live multi-principal connector evidence still pending on the issue)

## Why

The AC-by-AC review on #17178 identified one codeable deviation: AC2 requires that grants distinguish free/busy, event detail, **propose**, **approve**, mutate, and **export** scopes, but `HOUSEHOLD_ACCESS_SCOPES` carried only four members — propose/approve were enforced implicitly through `calendar.mutate` and the approval workflow, and export was not a grant scope at all. This PR closes that deviation in code rather than by amending the criterion.

## What changed

- **Scope enum**: `HOUSEHOLD_ACCESS_SCOPES` gains `schedule.propose`, `schedule.approve`, `household.export`. All six authorities named by AC2 are now distinguishable inside the grant enum, each with the existing expiry/revocation semantics of `HouseholdAccessGrant`.
- **Implication lattice** (`expandGrantScopes`, `types.ts`): one closure used at both grant issuance and check time — `calendar.mutate ⇒ schedule.propose ⇒ calendar.freebusy`, `schedule.approve ⇒ calendar.details`, `household.export ⇒ household.visibility`. Persisted grants written before these scopes existed keep working without migration.
- **Propose distinguished from mutate**: proposal creation and cross-creator revision now require `schedule.propose` instead of full `calendar.mutate`, so a caregiver or professional can be delegated proposal authority (role limits extended accordingly) without mutation authority. Proposals still only land through the affected-adult approval workflow.
- **Approve is revocable after routing**: `respondToProposal` re-verifies standing at response time — an active non-child role binding covering every affected child, or an active `schedule.approve` grant (role-limited to owner/co-parent/current-partner). Previously, narrowing or retiring a party after their approval request was routed left the request actionable.
- **Export distinguished from visibility**: the export audit/decision trail is withheld from principals whose effective scopes lack `household.export`, and the user-facing export action requires the scope for non-self principals. Scoped schedule views keep degrading by calendar scopes exactly as before (retired/narrowed access still renders as a visibly empty export, not an error).

## Verification

- `src/lifeops/household/` real-PGlite suites: **39/39 passed** on the rebased head (26 coordination incl. 3 new contract tests, plus boundaries/inbound-approval/discord-route suites).
- New tests: caregiver proposing via `schedule.propose` without mutate (and denied without it); standing removal blocking `respondToProposal` then restored coverage re-enabling it; audit-trail withheld without `household.export` and restored with it (including grant revocation in between).
- Wider lanes: `src/lifeops/household/ + parenting/ + family-communications/` integration configs: 69/69 passed. Turbo `typecheck --filter=@elizaos/plugin-personal-assistant`: 67/67 tasks green. Biome clean on changed files.
- Plugin unit lane (`vitest.config.ts`): 13 failures in brief/translation-harness/connector-fuzz/relationships-encoding suites — none import the household module and this branch touches only the five household files, so they are pre-existing on develop.

## Remainder (human-only)

The live multi-principal connector evidence the delivery-ledger row waits on (real co-parent identity, delivery/reply proof over live connectors) cannot be produced from an offline lane and remains the closing condition tracked on the issue.

author: josephfinlayson
body:
## Description

Multi-project contexts can already load models from independently configured projects into one graph and shared state store. However, a model without an explicit `gateway` currently inherits the one context-selected gateway, so every model in a secondary project must repeat the same `gateway` property.

This adds `model_defaults.gateway` as a project-level default for managed SQL, Python, and seed models:

```yaml
model_defaults:
  dialect: duckdb
  gateway: project_gateway
```

The default is resolved before model name qualification, so the model receives the selected gateway's default catalog and gateway variables. An explicit `gateway` in a SQL `MODEL` block or Python decorator still takes precedence.

Plain Python decorator gateway strings are treated as literal gateway names, including names with characters such as hyphens. Macro-prefixed Python gateway values retain blueprint rendering, as do SQL `MODEL` gateway expressions.

External models intentionally remain gateway-neutral unless their YAML row specifies a gateway. For external models, gateway selects an alternate source definition rather than an execution default.

No behavior changes when `model_defaults.gateway` is omitted.

## Prior art

This builds on:

- #3394, which introduced model-level multi-engine routing.
- #3888, which introduced gateway-specific model defaults.
- #4101, which introduced gateway-managed virtual layers.
- #4996, which discusses broader default scoping but not project-level gateway routing.

## Test plan

- Added SQL model coverage for project defaults, explicit overrides, gateway variables, gateway-specific default catalogs, and hyphenated gateway names.
- Added Python model and blueprint coverage, including literal hyphenated gateways and macro-prefixed blueprint gateways.
- Added external-model regression coverage.
- Added a two-project Context integration test proving each project uses its own default gateway, catalog, and variables while explicit overrides still win.
- `make style`
- `make fast-test` (2,777 passed across the fast, isolated, registry-isolation, and dialect-isolation phases)
- Focused model/config/schema-loader plus new slow integration test (412 passed)

## Checklist

- [x] I have run `make style` and fixed any issues.
- [x] I have added tests for my changes.
- [x] All existing tests pass (`make fast-test`).
- [x] My commits are signed off per the DCO.

body: ## What Makes the walk strip on the Issue page status-aware. Each stage now renders a status glyph: **Check** for done, **Minus** for skipped, **filled Circle** for active, **outline Circle** for pending. One file changed: `app/issues/[id]/walk-strip.tsx`. No redesign — the stage-name pills stay; only the visible ` · now` status text is dropped in favor of the glyph. ## Why Today every stage renders the same way whether done, skipped, running, or pending. `docs/design-system.md` (Walk Strip section) prescribes checkmarks for completed, dashes for skipped, and an accent highlight for active. This is the smallest change that satisfies that, without touching sibling panels. ## Marker mapping (glyph primary, color strictly secondary) | Status | Glyph (lucide-react) | Color (existing repo token) | aria word | |---|---|---|---| | done | `CheckIcon` | `text-emerald-300` | completed | | skipped | `MinusIcon` | `text-neutral-600` | skipped | | active | `CircleIcon` (filled, `fill="currentColor"`) | `text-primary` | in progress | | pending | `CircleIcon` (outline, default) | `text-neutral-600` | pending | Status is conveyed by the glyph, not by color alone — `skipped` and `pending` intentionally share `text-neutral-600` and are distinguished by Minus vs outline-Circle. No animation/pulse on the active marker (a distinct filled glyph conveys it). ## Token substitutions recorded (AC6) `docs/design-system.md` is the design-token file and was followed verbatim for the Walk Strip (completed → checkmark, skipped → dash, active → accent highlight). The named color tokens below are **not wired as usable tokens** in `app/globals.css`, so per the spec's substitution rule each was replaced with the closest existing repo token: - **success / positive (done)** — no `--success` token exists; the design-doc value `oklch(0.7 0.15 145)` is documented but not wired. Substituted with `text-emerald-300`, the repo's existing dark-theme positive green (`agent-message.tsx`). - **accent (active)** — the design-doc primary accent (indigo `oklch(0.65 0.15 260)`) is not wired as a text token; `--accent` in `globals.css` is a gray *surface* (`oklch(0.2 0 0)`), not indigo. Per the spec rule "missing accent → primary", used `text-primary` (white `oklch(0.985 0 0)`), which also matches the existing `stageTone("active")` of `text-neutral-50` (≈ white). - **muted (skipped)** — wired `--muted-foreground` is `oklch(0.7)` (brighter than the strip's established muted treatment). Substituted with `text-neutral-600`, the repo's existing skipped/pending muted color in `stageTone` (closest to the design-doc quaternary `oklch(0.5)`). - **base/border (pending)** — `--border` (`oklch(1 0 0 / 14%)`) is a border utility, not a text/icon token, and would be near-invisible on black. Substituted with `text-neutral-600`, the repo's existing pending/base treatment in `stageTone`. No new design tokens were introduced. No new packages (lucide-react, Tailwind, class-variance-authority only). ## Behavior notes - **`blocked` clamps to `pending`.** The real `StageStatus` enum (`lib/foundry/types.ts`) is `"pending" | "active" | "blocked" | "skipped" | "done"`. `blocked` is outside the spec's four states, so it is rendered as an outline Circle with aria-label `: pending` and emits `console.warn("[foundry:walk-strip] unrecognized stage status \"blocked\"; clamping to pending")` so the mismatch is visible rather than silent. If a distinct *blocked* marker is wanted, that's a follow-up Issue (it would also need a `stageTone` color decision, which is out of scope here). - **No reflow on state transitions.** Every stage always renders a fixed `w-4 h-4` flex-centered box with a `size-3` glyph, so a stage moving pending → active changes no widths. Removing ` · now` (which previously widened only the active stage) actually fixes the one place the old strip did reflow. - **Accessibility.** Each marker `` carries `aria-label=": "` (completed / skipped / in progress / pending), with a `Stage N` positional fallback if a name is ever missing. The inner glyph is `aria-hidden`. The visible stage-name label is preserved for sighted identity, so a screen reader may read the stage name twice (once from the marker's aria-label, once from the visible label) — this is an accepted, minor consequence of the spec requiring the name to live in the marker's aria-label while the pill labels are kept (no redesign). No visible status text, no hover tooltips. - **Scope.** Only `app/issues/[id]/walk-strip.tsx` is modified. `stage-hero`, `mid-walk-panel`, `late-walk-panel`, and `lib/foundry/copy.ts` (`stageTone`/`STAGE_LABEL`) are unchanged. ## Verification - `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — passes (exit 0). - `npx vitest run` — 33/33 tests pass (5 suites); no regressions. - Confirmed `lucide-react@1.16.0` exports `CheckIcon`, `MinusIcon`, `CircleIcon` (matches the repo's existing `...Icon` import convention in `dropdown-menu.tsx`/`select.tsx`). - `git diff --stat` shows exactly one file changed (`app/issues/[id]/walk-strip.tsx`, +56 / −6); sibling panels untouched. ## Acceptance checklist - [x] Only `walk-strip.tsx` modified; `stage-hero`, `mid-walk-panel`, `late-walk-panel` unchanged. - [x] Done → Check; skipped → Minus; active → filled Circle; pending → outline Circle. - [x] Every marker in one fixed-size flex-centered box (`h-4 w-4`) at a consistent `size-3`; no reflow on state transitions; issue-page layout unchanged across states/viewports. - [x] Each marker carries `aria-label` = `: ` (completed/skipped/in progress/pending), with `Stage N` positional fallback. - [x] Glyph is the primary signal; color strictly secondary; status not color-only. - [x] Color uses only existing repo tokens; design-token file followed verbatim; all substitutions recorded above. - [x] No new tokens, no new packages (lucide-react + Tailwind only). - [x] Unrecognized status (`blocked`) clamps to `pending` + `console.warn`. - [x] No animation/pulse on the active marker. - [x] No visible text labels added (the old ` · now` was removed); no hover tooltips. --- ## Summary by cubic Makes the Issue page walk strip status-aware and removes the " · now" text. Previously all stages looked the same; now each stage shows a glyph: Check for done, Minus for skipped, filled Circle for active, outline Circle for pending, improving clarity and matching the design spec. - One file changed: `app/issues/[id]/walk-strip.tsx`; stage-name pills are unchanged. - Markers render in a fixed 16×16 box to prevent layout reflow on status changes. - Each marker carries aria-label ": "; glyphs are aria-hidden; visible labels remain. - Unknown statuses (e.g., blocked) clamp to pending and log a console warning. - Uses `lucide-react` icons and existing color tokens; no new tokens or packages. Written for commit bad424eac093506f1260b658f7915e0cb41d8b90. Summary will update on new commits.

author: deepakvish001
body:
## Why

`/api/auth/login` accepted **unlimited password attempts**. The validation in #9 stopped a body with no email from testing a guess against an arbitrary account — but a caller who names an address could still try passwords as fast as the network allowed.

## Limits

| Route | Budget | Counts |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/auth/login` | 10 / 15 min | failures only |
| `POST /api/auth/signup` | 5 / hour | all requests |

`skipSuccessfulRequests` is on for login so an office or campus NAT sharing one address doesn't lock itself out through ordinary use — only failed attempts consume the budget. Responses use draft-7 `RateLimit` headers and the same `{ success, message }` shape as the rest of the API.

## `trust proxy` — the part that makes it actually work

`vercel.json` routes this API through Vercel's proxy, so `req.ip` is **the proxy's address** unless `X-Forwarded-For` is honoured. Without it, both limiters would bucket every client into one counter and throttle all of them at once — the limiter would look configured and be worse than useless.

Set to `1`, not `true`: trusting the whole chain lets a caller spoof their own address by sending the header themselves.

## Test-environment guard

The middleware stands down under `NODE_ENV=test`, and the test script now **sets** `NODE_ENV=test` so that guard is actually in effect.

Worth flagging: it wasn't before. `NODE_ENV` was unset during `npm test`, and the only reason the existing tests passed is that they call the controllers directly rather than through the router. A future router-level test would have hit the limiter and been very confusing.

## Tests — 7 added

They load the module with the flag **cleared**, so they prove the limit fires rather than trusting the configuration:

- 11th login attempt → `429`
- 6th signup attempt → `429`
- 429 body names the wait (`/15 minutes/`)
- draft-7 `RateLimit` header present, legacy `X-RateLimit-*` absent
- 25 consecutive requests all pass under `NODE_ENV=test`

The handler under test always returns 401, so `skipSuccessfulRequests` can't quietly mask the count.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Suite | 27 | **34**, all passing |
| `node --check` sweep | clean | clean |

---
